edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 and Gate5 / M1, M5 (NK-evasion cloak on cells that may retain pluripotency vs iCasp9 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: Same-day purified NK transfer prevented teratomas from unedited hiPSCs (0/17 versus 10/12 NSG; O3), whereas week-6 NK transfer left 7/8 established teratomas detectable at week 8 (O8), supporting a timing/target-state boundary in this model. This raises a Gate3/Gate5 safety qualification for residual PSCs, but neither HLA-E/CD47 cloaking nor iCasp9 was tested; Blueprint §7 already addresses residual clonogenic-cell safety, while incorporation of this specific NK-surveillance boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK missing-self cytotoxicity against HLA-I-low cells)
edges.claim_summary: Unedited HLA-I-low hiPSCs were susceptible to human NK attack (O3, O5), consistent with the missing-self threat explicitly addressed by Blueprint §1.2 Gate3. This link is limited to that general threat: activating ligands and HLA-I were not causally separated, and the serum-associated HLA-I increase (O9) does not establish efficacy of the engineered HLA-E/CD47 construct.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allogeneic adaptive-rejection threat; recognition route not isolated)
edges.claim_summary: Allogeneic NK-depleted PBMCs were associated with 0/7 teratomas versus 7/7 with autologous NK-depleted PBMCs (O2), while Hu-BLT allogeneic rejection remained incomplete at 8 weeks (O7). This supports the allogeneic adaptive threat already addressed by Blueprint §1.2 and §4.1-4.2; the study did not test B2M/CIITA edits, isolate direct versus indirect presentation, or study SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 clonogenic suicide switch, Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 state that a knock-in iC9 switch drives efficient apoptosis of human iPSCs in vitro and eradicated AML-iPSC-derived malignant cells in mouse models, supporting the iCasp9 fail-safe concept the cheatsheet already lists for Gate5. Evidence is abstract-only, undifferentiated iPSCs and leukemia cells rather than SC-islet grafts, and O3 notes unspecified limitations, so no escape rate or threshold can be derived.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (in vivo graft and oxygenation: cluster-size diffusion limit and 72-hour oxygen bridge); Gate4 (hypoxic stress context)
edges.claim_summary: In immunosuppressed recipients of culture-surviving primary intraportal islets, size was not independently associated with 3-month graft function after adjustment (O8); this underpowered observational result does not show equivalence or establish culture-mediated hypoxia protection. Blueprint §1.2 Gate5 and §4.5 retain the ≤120 µm SC-islet size/oxygen constraint; transfer to that engineered extravascular product or relaxation of its 72-hour bridge is unvalidated, and incorporation of this specific clinical boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide clinical benchmark and dose-dependence of early graft function)
edges.claim_summary: Primary-islet clinical reference under alemtuzumab/tacrolimus/mycophenolate: at ≥5000 IEq/kg, Results reports mean 3-month stimulated C-peptide 624 ± 524 pmol/L, lower insulin requirement (O1-O2, with unresolved change arithmetic), and stronger C-peptide association with number/kg than total IEq (O5, O12). This bounded endocrine comparator can inform Gate1/M4 context; primary-nonfunction exclusion, unspecified analyzed n and product/site differences prevent SC-islet qualification, and claim-specific Blueprint incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(a) / M3, M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge in a prevascularized bed; Gate4 hypoxia survival)
edges.claim_summary: Raising subcutaneous oxygen tension from 45 to 140 mm Hg (O1) reduced central necrosis and raised insulin release in vitro (O2), and a 3-day postoperative oxygen course on a prevascularized bed was needed for six hundred syngeneic islets to reverse diabetes (O3). This supports an acute oxygen bridge of about 3 days; the bridge is by systemic inhalation in syngeneic rats rather than a PDMS-CaO2 device with hPSC-islets, and only abstract-level qualitative evidence is available.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; high-density encapsulation diffusion limits)
edges.claim_summary: In primary human islets, 12 h of high-density ischemia lowered OCR/DNA (O1, O3) and FDA/PI viability (O2: 8.8 +/- 5.5% vs 87.3 +/- 1.0%) and abolished the glucose-stimulated insulin response (O5, O8), supporting the need for the oxygen bridge. Primary adult islets at ambient O2 are a bridge, not SC-islets in a PDMS-CaO2 slab, and the cheatsheet states no such quantitative 12 h damage figure.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant hypoxia and inflammatory stress resilience; HMOX1)
edges.claim_summary: Ischemic human islets upregulated IL6, IL8, CCL3 and CXCL3 (O10), hypoxia and nutrient-deprivation genes including HMOX1 (O12) and HIF-1α and AP-1 pathways (O13), and downregulated KCNJ3 and SLC38A4 (O11), supporting Gate4's premise of hypoxia plus cytokine stress. The cheatsheet does not state this ischemia-induced transcript program; the data are from primary islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell identity and GSIS function versus immune resistance)
edges.claim_summary: In NOD mice the immune-resistant Btm subpopulation was also the functionally impaired one: reduced identity genes including Pdx1 and Mafa (O5), no response to high glucose (O2) and higher Neurog3 (O6). This qualifies natural immune-resistance as a template for Gate2B/Gate4 protection because it comes at the cost of Gate1 function; extrapolation to hPSC-derived grafts is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (resistance to cytokine and immune-cell killing, intrinsic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: Sorted Btm beta cells resisted death from IL-1beta, IFN-gamma and IL-6 (O16) and showed a decreased apoptosis pathway (O4, exploratory IPA) with unchanged ER stress genes (O9), supporting that intrinsic cytoprotection can protect beta cells under inflammatory stress. This was seen in native mouse NOD cells without an identified protective gene, so it gives no gene-level target for the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 clonogenic suicide switch, in vivo ablation of iPSC-derived tumors)
edges.claim_summary: A lentiviral iC9 switch plus systemic CID cleared iPSC-NS/PC-derived tumors in NOD/SCID mice (O7, O9, O11, O13) with no luminescence re-increase (O8, O10), supporting the cheatsheet's iCasp9 fail-safe concept for Gate5. The grafts were neural-lineage tumors in the spinal cord, not SC-islet grafts, and O12 reports 'a major portion' rather than all cells cleared in one group.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (<1e-6 escape threshold; promoter silencing with EF-1alpha/UbC lentiviral iC9)
edges.claim_summary: Randomly integrated lentiviral EF-1alpha/UbC iC9 gave about 95% apoptosis in iPSCs (O1) and >93% in iPSC-NS/PCs (O3), far short of the cheatsheet's <1e-6 escape benchmark, and the authors flag incomplete killing and possible silencing as unresolved (O18); they propose a safe-harbor locus (not tested here). This qualifies short-term bulk-kill assays as evidence for the escape threshold rather than contradicting the AAVS1 design.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(a) and Gate1 / M3, M2 (oxygen-providing subcutaneous macro-encapsulation device carrying hESC-derived progenitors)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(b) / M5 (genomic and oncology safety layers around hPSC grafts)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: macro-encapsulation may add a physical containment layer for residual pluripotent cells, since encapsulated undifferentiated hESCs did not form teratoma and died (O1). The abstract gives no incidence, n or mechanism (the device had limited capability to sustain undifferentiated cells), so it cannot replace the iCasp9 fail-safe and is untested with SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (innate attack beyond NK and macrophage: neutrophils, coagulation and complement in the first 48 h)
edges.claim_summary: In a human whole blood model, native human islets met early coagulation and platelet activation (O1), steadily rising sC5b-9 (O2) and a massive neutrophil infiltration (O3). The cheatsheet defines Gate3 around NK and macrophage axes (HLA-E, CD47), so neutrophil-driven and coagulation-driven early loss is a scope limit of that gate; the model used unedited islets and exocrine tissue, not SC-islets or edited cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 and early cytokine exposure)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (FAS effector pressure on islet cells; FADD-dependent extrinsic death)
edges.claim_summary: FAS ligand killed human islet cells in a FADD-dependent manner (O2), consistent with the cheatsheet naming FAS effector pressure within Gate2B's scope. Evidence is abstract-only, in primary adult islet cells and islet-derived progenitors in vitro with exogenous FAS ligand, not SC-islet grafts under T-cell attack.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (candidate FAS-pathway protection node: FADD rather than BID)
edges.claim_summary: BID knockdown did not protect human islet cells or progenitors from FAS ligand (O1, O3) while FADD knockdown reduced death (O2), suggesting a FADD-level FAS block as a candidate addition to the cheatsheet's SERPINB9 + PD-L1 Gate2B protection, and that mouse BID-deficiency data should not be transferred (O4). This is a hypothesis from siRNA knockdowns with no effect sizes; FADD loss effects on other pathways and in SC-islets are untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (dsRNA/IFN-driven beta-cell apoptosis; TYK2 as a candidate cytoprotection node)
edges.claim_summary: TYK2 inhibition prevented PIC-induced human beta-cell apoptosis (O5) and lowered type I IFN signaling (O1), MHC class I (O4) and IFN-alpha/CXCL10 output (O2, O3), suggesting TYK2 knockdown or inhibition as a candidate Gate4/Gate2A protective edit not listed in the cheatsheet's Gate4 elements. Abstract-only evidence from PIC-exposed human beta-cells in vitro; the line, effect sizes, SC-islets and T-cell killing are untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: TYK2-silenced beta-cells made less CXCL10 after PIC (O3), indicating beta-cell CXCL10 output depends on TYK2-supported IFN signaling, so any TYK2 edit could weaken a CXCL10-promoter-driven circuit. This is an inference: the CXCL10 promoter, IFN-gamma/TNF triggers and SC-islets were not tested, and the cheatsheet does not say whether this dependency is already considered.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (neopeptide / minor-antigen T-cell responses to hiPSC-derived cells)
edges.claim_summary: In Hu-mice with an autologous immune system, hiPSC derivatives were rejected in a cell-type-dependent way (SMCs immunogenic, RPEs tolerated; O3, O4, O5), the infiltrating T cells were oligoclonal (O6), and aberrant Zg16 expression was sufficient to make RPEs rejected (O7, O9). This supports Gate2B's premise that neoantigen-driven T-cell responses can arise even without allogeneic mismatch; the cells are SMCs and RPEs, not islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1, M3 (reprogramming-induced aberrant antigen expression as a release-criterion check)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: screen hiPSC-derived islet cells for aberrantly expressed immunogenic antigens (the paper names Zg16 and Hormad1 in SMCs) before graft release, because ectopic Zg16 alone turned a tolerated cell type into a rejected one (O8, O9). Zg16 and Hormad1 were not examined in islet cells here, and tolerance of RPEs was not due to lack of HLA expression (O10).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4, M3 (clinical benchmark: stimulated C-peptide and functional engraftment of a device-contained product)
edges.claim_summary: This registry record has no results, but it shows a Phase 1/2 trial with 19.0 enrolled (O1) using C-peptide change at Month 6 as a primary outcome (O3) that was terminated for insufficient functional product engraftment (O4). It scopes any clinical C-peptide benchmark at Gate1/M4 by showing that an early-phase device-based product did not reach functional engraftment; the cause is not stated and the product composition is not described in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (static GSIR stimulation index as a potency and release criterion; clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: In 13 human islet allotransplants, static GSIR stimulation index did not separate insulin independent from insulin dependent recipients (O4, O7) even though all products met release criteria (O1). This qualifies reliance on a GSIS stimulation-index threshold alone as a predictor of clinical function, with the caveat that the assay is static, the product is primary islets not SC-islets, and n is small.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 and Gate5 / M7 (viable-dose release metric based on oxygen consumption rate)
edges.claim_summary: OCR dose (OCR/DNA multiplied by IE dose per kg) separated insulin independent from insulin dependent recipients with AUC 1.00 versus 0.98 for IE dose (O2, O3, O6), suggesting a hypothesis that an OCR-based viable dose could complement GSIS in SC-islet release criteria. Evidence is primary human islets in 13 recipients; no SC-islet data are given.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1-[CpG-core]-EEF1A1-core-iCasp9 anti-methylation insulation)
edges.claim_summary: The study supports the failure-mode rationale for Locus 4 insulation: lentiviral 1,176 bp EF1alpha-driven iCasp9-hDeltaCD19 lost expression during EB/MSC/teratoma differentiation, with higher promoter CpG methylation and partial 5-azacytidine rescue (O10-O14). Frozen Blueprint section 4.4 already addresses methylation risk, but this mouse/rhesus cassette does not test the human 230 bp EEF1A1-core at AAVS1 or establish anti-silencing function of the HNRNPA2B1-proximal 455-bp CpG-core candidate and engineered cHS4 boundaries.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 fail-safe efficacy and Section 7 clonogenic safety model)
edges.claim_summary: In these mouse/rhesus lentiviral iPSC models, AP1903 delayed teratoma progression without general tumor ablation; treatment after palpable subcutaneous/intramuscular tumors showed no apparent growth inhibition, and low-expressing differentiated MSC survived AP1903 (O5, O6, O9, O10, O12). This qualifies efficacy by model, timing and retained expression; the IV delayed-start day remains unresolved (O7/A12). The bounded failure-mode claim is already addressed by frozen Blueprint section 7 and ranker common-mode/debulking and retrieval gates; M0121 supplies no exact-product SC-islet clonogenic escape rate or qualification of those gates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (EEF1A1-core promoter choice for iCasp9 in Locus 4)
edges.claim_summary: Undifferentiated miPSC carrying the tested lentiviral 1,176 bp EF1alpha promoter showed stronger reporter expression and AP1903 killing than EOS-C(3+) or CMV (O1-O3). This supports a promoter-family rationale consistent with the EEF1A1-core choice already present in frozen Blueprint section 4.4, but transfer to its 230 bp core and human AAVS1 cassette is unvalidated; the tested EF1alpha cassette itself lost expression with differentiation (O10-O14).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation toward adult beta-cell function)
edges.claim_summary: hPSC-derived INS+ cells from three lines were mutually similar (O1) but closer to fetal than adult beta cells (O2), supporting the need for the Stage-6/7 maturation and function benchmarks listed for Gate1. This abstract-only transcriptome result applies to the differentiation protocol of its publication year, so it does not show whether current Stage-6/7 products remain fetal-like.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation, MAFA, GSIS benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: A seven-stage hESC protocol gave S7 cells expressing MAFA (O1) with static GSIS similar to human islets (O2) but with notable differences in dynamic and single-cell assays (O3), consistent with the cheatsheet's Stage-6/7 maturation and dynamic perifusion benchmarks for Gate1. Abstract-only: no stimulation indices are given, so the cheatsheet's stimulation-index benchmark cannot be checked.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo functional graft benchmark)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (oxygenated immune-isolating chamber; oxygen-support component only)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract describes one human-islet chamber recipient followed for 10 mo (O1) and reports persistent graft function without immunosuppression (O2). This is qualitative clinical precedent for a combined oxygenated immune-isolating chamber, without an oxygen-only comparator, oxygen measurements, or quantitative survival data; it does not establish causal benefit from oxygenation, the Blueprint 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/catalase bridge, vascularization, or clonogenic fail-safe performance. Incorporation of this specific case is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (qualitative clinical islet-function benchmark without immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: The single-recipient abstract reports regulated insulin secretion and preserved islet morphology/function without immunosuppression (O2), alongside 10-mo follow-up (O1). This is a qualitative benchmark in encapsulated human islets; no C-peptide, insulin-independence, GSIS kinetics, or glycemic-control values are provided. O3 is an overlapping system-design assertion, not independent evidence, and transfer to genetically edited SC-islets remains unestablished. Incorporation of this specific case is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive memory T cells, IGRP; recurrent autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: In diabetic NOD hosts, IGRP-reactive CD8+ T cells accumulated in IGRP+ grafts (18.2% +/- 4.7%) but were undetectable in IGRP-/- grafts (O4), and recurrence occurred in all four combinations within 2 weeks (O3), supporting Gate2B's premise that primed autoreactive memory T cells drive recurrence. Mouse syngeneic kidney-capsule grafts, so the bridge to hPSC grafts rests on conserved cognate pMHC recruitment; the cheatsheet does not state this antigen-dependence finding.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (single-autoantigen removal as a protective strategy)
edges.claim_summary: Deleting one epitope (IGRP206-214) from the graft delayed recurrence only by a few days (12.7 vs 5.9 days, O1) and did not prevent graft loss in any host-donor combination (O3), so protection by removing a single autoantigen would be insufficient; other memory specificities such as InsB15-23 may fill the niche (O13, not significant). The cheatsheet lists several autoantigens but does not say whether this single-epitope boundary is already considered.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (GRAVEYARD_006: base-editor sequence and structural genotoxicity hazard)
edges.claim_summary: O5–O8 and O11 support the generic hazard that nickase-based cytosine editing can coexist with off-target sequence changes and translocations. That mechanism is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §5 GRAVEYARD_006 and its precautionary non-islet evidence basis. These single-Unc13d-locus mouse primary-cell data do not validate multiplex hPSC/islet risk, a numerical manufacturing penalty, or a zero-risk single-base-edit threshold; their exact rates are contextual, and O6 preserves the unresolved abstract/Results structural-variant wording.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (cell-, platform- and time-specific genomic-safety transfer limits)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O9, O11 and O14 qualify transfer: CAST-Seq aberration signals and their persistence vary by cell type, CBE sequence editing correlates poorly with translocation hits, and editor activity in a reporter or other cell context does not establish endogenous primary-cell activity. General genomic QC is specified in the Blueprint, but incorporation of these particular cell/time/editor boundaries is not established. No matched hPSC-derived islet evidence or clinically acceptable mutation threshold follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (complementary sequence and structural genomic-safety surveillance)
edges.claim_summary: O9–O10 support complementary sequence and structural surveillance: persistent sequence edits and late CAST-Seq nondetection are different endpoints, and rare-clone sensitivity is limited. The general multimodal principle is already present in frozen Blueprint §2 Stage 4 (duplex sequencing, long-read LOH and CAST-Seq) and GRAVEYARD_006 supporting records (WGS/optical mapping/CAST-Seq); it is not a wholly novel upgrade. The particular nominated-site assay coverage, longitudinal design and final-islet performance remain unqualified; O12–O13 preclude treating this study as a disease-free safety proof.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety: baseline hiPSC culture drift and attribution of structural variants)
edges.claim_summary: Unedited, undifferentiated hiPSC cultures acquired karyotypic and sequence changes over P10-P50, including trisomy 12 (O2-O3), chr20 duplication (O4) and translocations (O11-O13). This supports using passage-matched unedited cultures when attributing lesions to genome editing, but does not quantify an editing-attributable rate or validate safety in SC-islet products. Blueprint §8 row 4 already recognizes TP53/20q clonal selection; specific incorporation of this baseline-control requirement and these longitudinal observations is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (complementary genomic QC assays and line-specific passage qualification)
edges.claim_summary: The observed assay complementarity (O2/O8 aneuploidy timing, source-conflicted CNVs O9, low-VAF OGM event O13 with orthogonal validation O21, and coding mutations O16-O20) motivates evaluating broader WES-based variant annotation and line-specific passage limits alongside existing QC. The frozen Blueprint §8 row 4, ranker longitudinal TP53/PPM1D/BCOR QC and karyotype/OGM gate, and GY-006 already incorporate structural-variant surveillance; OGM or longitudinal QC alone is not claimed as a new upgrade. Exact adoption of broader WES and a passage-cap policy is unknown. No universal safe passage threshold, clinical safety, or multiplex-editing penalty is calibrated by this three-line unedited study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 EEF1A1-core-iCasp9; lineage-specific anti-silencing qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 provide a cross-lineage hPSC expression warning: promoter/WPRE configurations can prevent silencing, while unnamed chromatin insulators have less impact in the abstract-described comparisons. The bounded qualification that anti-silencing architecture requires lineage-specific testing is already explicit in frozen Blueprint sections 4.4 and 9.1 (AAVS1 methylation risk; exact 455-bp candidate anti-silencing function pending). This classification does not assert incorporation of TK4 or its component comparison, failure of the Blueprint insulators, or SC-islet/iCasp9 qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (research comparators for Locus 4 promoter/regulatory-element and safe-harbor selection)

The neuronal/microglial abstract does not establish SC-islet expression durability, iCasp9/AP1903 killing, genomic safety or superiority to the frozen AAVS1 design; exact construct architectures, novel-locus identities and follow-up are unresolved. Study-specific incorporation is unknown: the current Blueprint describes EEF1A1 with cHS4/455-bp candidate elements and an AAVS1 plus GAPDH contingency, which does not establish adoption or evaluation of this TK4 hypothesis.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A (Scenario B HLA-C-retained design; matched HLA-C requirement)
edges.claim_summary: In iPSC-derived iNKT cells, compatible re-expressed HLA-C was associated with a smaller increase in T-cell killing in vitro, and the matched in vivo condition showed greater day-27 dual HLA-C/E persistence than WT and B2M-KO (O3, O5). The abstract reports reduced residence time with incompatible HLA-C (O9). This supports the existing recipient-matched HLA-C premise for Scenario B as a mechanistic bridge; it does not qualify an SC-islet product or prove a direct matched-versus-mismatched effect size. R8 preserves separately a nonsignificant and a significant day-27 B2M-KO-versus-dual comparison without recoverable donor/condition mapping (O7, O8); neither is selected as the universal mismatch effect.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate immune cloak; limits of humanized-mouse NK qualification)
edges.claim_summary: The authors explicitly qualify the humanized-mouse observations because human NK function is incompletely recapitulated and interpret in vivo rejection as T-cell dominated (O10). This reinforces the frozen Blueprint/ranker requirement for separate primary human NK-subset assays (O1, O2 provide only iNKT-cell evidence); graft residence alone cannot qualify an SC-islet innate cloak. The independent NK-assay requirement is already present in rank_islet1_stacks.py primary_readouts and residual-risk specifications; the paper-specific limitation remains attributed to this model.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical endocrine-replacement benchmarks; fasting C-peptide is distinct from stimulated function)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O4, O7, O9, O12 and O13 provide descriptive clinical islet-transplant benchmarks under immunosuppression: fasting-C-peptide-defined graft survival, insulin independence and metabolic changes. The Kaplan–Meier-series cohort remains unresolved (O4); these findings do not demonstrate stimulated C-peptide, dynamic GSIS, edited hPSC-islet performance or a causal high-mass/regimen advantage. Claim-specific quantitative incorporation in the frozen Blueprint is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allosensitisation and rationale for avoiding systemic immunosuppression)

These bound the clinical risk rationale for the Blueprint immunosuppression-free goal, but do not test B2M/CIITA ablation, demonstrate prevention of sensitisation or prove withdrawal caused the increase. Specific quantitative incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (orthogonal hPSC genomic-safety and functional screening)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2/O9 reported similar routine pluripotency, trilineage and monolayer-growth readouts while O10/O11 identified clonogenic/anchorage-independent growth. Genome-wide copy-number profiling plus soft-agar challenge could be evaluated as adjunct assays; their incremental value over the Blueprint Stage-4 longitudinal TP53/PPM1D/BCOR sequencing, Chr20q11.21 ddPCR and functional Nutlin-3a p53 QC is untested. Those existing genomic QC elements are already explicit (Blueprint line 79); adoption of these particular adjuncts is unknown. Data are undifferentiated human cell-line findings, not SC-islet release validation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe rationale and chemotherapy-response transfer boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O11 and O12–O17 support the already-incorporated premise that culture-selected hPSC clones with abnormal TP53 can show malignant-like growth and altered drug sensitivity, motivating orthogonal genomic monitoring and clonogenic fail-safe qualification (Blueprint lines 78–79, 272; ranker lines 5081–5091, 5962–5977). The measured cisplatin/gemcitabine responses do not establish iCasp9/AP1903 escape or predict its kill depth; no suicide switch was tested. O18 nonsignificance for navitoclax does not establish equivalent killing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonal-selection and genome-integrity monitoring boundary)
edges.claim_summary: Gains labeled c20q11 occurred in both LU07 knockout clones but no CNV alteration was detected in H9-KO (O5–O7); the Discussion explicitly leaves clonal-selection pressure versus TP53 loss unresolved. This supports the existing longitudinal TP53/Chr20q11.21 monitoring of edited and expanded clones (Blueprint lines 79, 272; ranker lines 5081–5091) without demonstrating edit-induced CNV causality. It supplies no multiplex/base/prime-edit comparison or effect estimate for GRAVEYARD_006 (graveyard lines 138–160). Source inconsistencies in chromosome-arm descriptions remain annotated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet alpha-cell functional benchmark; paracrine architecture)
edges.claim_summary: Lowering G6PC2 in primary human alpha-cell pseudo-islets made glucagon release more sensitive to glucose suppression (O18, with O6, O15), so a hypothesis is that Gate1 SC-islet panels could add an amino acid-stimulated, glucose-suppressed glucagon assay and G6PC2/GCK balance as an alpha-cell maturation readout. Tested in primary human alpha cells only, not hPSC-derived alpha cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta composition reference)
edges.claim_summary: Islet composition was unchanged (O4) while glucagon secretion shifted ex vivo (O13) and recovery from insulin-induced hypoglycemia was slower in mice (O10, O11), so alpha-cell fraction alone does not capture alpha-cell function. A beta:alpha:delta composition reference would need a functional alpha-cell readout; mouse in vivo findings are not validated for SC-islet grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic beta-cell function benchmarks for SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: Loss of beta-cell GABA left composition unchanged (O3) but deformed Ca2+ oscillations (O5, O6), stopped oscillations in about 30% of male islets versus around 10% in controls at 16.7 mM glucose (O8), and gave insulin oversecretion (O2). A hypothesis is to add islet GABA content, Ca2+ oscillation waveform and fraction of oscillating islets as SC-islet function readouts; this is not tested in SC-beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS stimulation-index benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: GABA-deficient mouse islets oversecreted insulin at 16.7 mM glucose (O2) and in vivo (O11) while having abnormal Ca2+ oscillations (O5, O6, O8), so a high glucose-stimulated insulin output alone does not show regulated beta-cell function. This qualifies reliance on perifusion GSIS magnitude without waveform or feedback readouts; no stimulation index was computed in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (oxygen transport and the acute avascular-window boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O5 is pre-loading NHP bulk UF pO2 (88.8 ± 16.6 mmHg, n = 4), O6 is cell-free rat UF (~60 mmHg), and O16 is qualitative post-loading NHP UF stability (n = 5). These support physiological UF gas transport in this device but do not measure loaded-islet core oxygen or qualify the Blueprint 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/iMVF bridge: device loading followed at least 7 days of healing. The Blueprint specifies a different product and oxygen geometry (§1.2, §4.5); incorporation of these particular device findings is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A, Gate3 / M1, M3 (device immunoprotection as a candidate adjunct)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O2 and O7-O10 describe prolonged porcine xenograft survival, absent inflammatory cells in 58 serial biopsies and no reported post-loading antibody/complement response, despite baseline donor reactivity. They motivate testing an accessible CS-type device adjunct, but do not establish human allograft or recurrent-autoimmune/indirect-APC protection, impermeable exclusion of antibodies or all immune cells, or superiority of pump versus hydrogel. O14 preserves infection/contamination failures. Retrievability is not a clonogenic fail-safe test; adoption of this specific adjunct is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1, Gate5 / M3, M7 (function and structural durability beyond bulk UF oxygen)
edges.claim_summary: O11-O13 show transient metabolic benefit without insulin independence and fragmentation accompanying declining output; O15 separately documents in vitro C-peptide decline despite perfusion. Bulk UF oxygen observations do not prove oxygen sufficiency at every cell or explain this loss. Sampling artifact, porcine-islet fragility, matrix loss and flow injury remain possible contributors. Blueprint §4.5(4) already separates survival from endocrine recovery, but incorporation of this specific porcine convective-device failure mode is unestablished; no exact-product mechanism or requirement is validated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (pre-transplant hypoxic/metabolic conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O5 show that pre-transplant hypoxia-gene expression in primary human islets correlates with worse glycemic control after transplant in diabetic NODscid mice (DDIT4 R = 0.4971; 11-gene model R = 0.6117), supporting a role for pre-transplant hypoxia in graft failure. The islets are donor islets in immunodeficient mice, not SC-islets, and the Discussion notes hypoxia resistance may vary with cell source.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hypoxia-gene qPCR panel as an in-process or release potency assay)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4, O7 and O8 suggest a small hypoxia-gene panel (for example DDIT4, HK, VHL; R = 0.5672) could be tested as a rapid lot-quality predictor for SC-islet products. The model was built on 85 deceased-donor islet batches and the packet describes no independent validation cohort or SC-islet data, and the authors call for validation across cell sources.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (peroxide-based oxygen release plus pre-vascularized subcutaneous site)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 report, qualitatively and without any numbers, that a scaffold combining slow oxygen release from calcium peroxide with VEGF release gives a vascularized subcutaneous site and avoids adverse effects on implanted islets in diabetic rats. This is an abstract-only claim in rats with an unstated islet source, so it cannot show peroxide safety or oxygen adequacy during the avascular window for hPSC islets, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether the Blueprint already includes VEGF pre-vascularization.

edges.claim_summary: This randomized, non-blinded pilot in 43 autologous TPIAT recipients detected no overall drug-group difference in the islet-injury marker trajectory or nominal 2-year metabolic outcomes with these short systemic etanercept/A1AT regimens. It qualifies extrapolation from systemic anti-inflammatory treatment to Gate4 cytoprotection, but does not test cell-intrinsic A20/SERPINB9, allo/autoimmune evasion, or the engineered SC-islet product; limited power means nonsignificance is not equivalence. The frozen Blueprint explicitly covers cytokine resilience (§1.2, §4.3), but incorporation of this specific clinical boundary is not established.

edges.claim_summary: O2, O5-O8 and O17 support evaluating ESRG/LINC00678/LIN28A as candidate residual-iPSC markers in a product-specific SC-islet assay, based on a one-lot cardiomyocyte spike-in model; direct SC-islet performance was not tested. The frozen ranker already describes 14-day mTeSR amplification plus OCT4/NANOG/TDGF1 ddPCR release testing (5955-5960), and Blueprint §7 specifies residual-PSC/clonogenic bounds, so a generic new release-assay claim is inappropriate; adoption of this particular panel is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (analytical detection, full-process reproducibility and clonogenic qualification boundaries)
edges.claim_summary: In cardiac backgrounds, statistical detection at 0.0003% did not imply acceptable reproducibility for each marker (O5, O17), and full-process step-2 reproducibility CVs were 32.5%-56.6% across the tested positive-dose cells (O13, O15, O16). Background-copy LODs also differ by reference matrix (O14). These findings justify product-specific process/marker qualification, but neither validate the Blueprint §7 <=10^-8 residual-PSC bound nor measure AP1903 clonogenic escape or overturn GRAVEYARD_002; incorporation of these precise marker/process limits is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base/nickase/nuclease genomic integrity: translocations between B2M exon 2 and AAVS1, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3/O4/O14 provide a human-HSPC example of residual indels, large target deletions and detectable B2M-AAVS1 translocations with nickase-based editors, supporting the generic residual genotoxic hazard already explicit in frozen Blueprint GRAVEYARD_006 and its genomic QC precautions. This already_accounted_for label applies only to that general hazard: the HSPC editor/site/delivery-specific rates do not establish hPSC/SC-islet rates, the B>=2 plus DSB trigger, or the assigned gamma_B=0.965 engineering discount. The two-gRNA comparison used each editing system separately, not simultaneous BE-plus-Cas9 editing; assay nondetection for ABE8.20-m does not establish zero risk.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (choice of editor chemistry and mRNA design for Locus 1 B2M knockout; genomic-integrity readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O7/O8/O9 suggest testing editor chemistry, mRNA cap/UTR design and exposure timing at the intended target, with junction-PCR, deletion assays and controlled clonal-pool exome analysis as complementary readouts. This remains an unvalidated transfer from HSPCs to hPSC/SC-islet manufacturing: optimized BE4max had no detected translocations in the reported assay, whereas optimized ABE8.20-m showed increased variants and transversion skew (O11), and PE3 combined persistent editing with imprecise alleles and reduced early graft size (O15-O18). Incorporation of this specific optimization-and-assay strategy is unknown; source checking does not establish safety, Blueprint adoption or exact-product qualification.

edges.claim_summary: O1: IFN-α and IFN-γ changed the human beta cell transcriptome more than IL-1β or TNF-α (no magnitudes in the abstract). The cheatsheet lists IL-1β, IFN-γ, TNF-α and CXCL10 for Gate4 without ranking them and without IFN-α, so cytoprotection and stress tests may need to weight IFN-α/IFN-γ and add IFN-α; the beta cell source is not stated and is not SC-islet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune T1D islet milieu; IFN-driven beta cell signatures)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3: IFN-induced signatures in human beta cells correlate with beta cells and islet proteins from people with type 1 diabetes, supporting IFN pressure as a feature of the recurrent-autoimmunity setting that Gate2B protection must withstand. Qualitative abstract statements only, with human beta cells rather than SC-islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 at CXCL10 Locus 3, protection against T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: O8/O9 support a bounded PD-L1-pathway bridge: after systemic HC-5770 in native autoimmune NOD mice, β-cell-region PD-L1 rose and systemic anti-PD-L1 partly antagonized the glycemic effect. The general local PD-L1 checkpoint rationale is explicitly present in frozen Blueprint §4.3 and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9; already_accounted_for refers only to that rationale, not incorporation of this paper or its effect sizes. Blockade is not β-cell-specific and PERK effects on immune/exocrine cells are not excluded (paper Discussion limitations). No edited SC-islet, allograft or indirect-APC protection is demonstrated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (stress resilience of β cells; Locus 3 PD-L1 output under cytokine exposure)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O10/O11 support testing whether transient PERK/ISR modulation or GOLM1 manipulation can alter PD-L1 protein output in SC-islets: human donor islets show recovery of cytokine-inhibited translation, while EndoC-βH1 GOLM1 silencing attenuates PD-L1 protein without matching CD274 mRNA attenuation. These are distinct assays, not one demonstrated causal chain in an edited SC-islet. Frozen Blueprint §4.3 addresses PD-L1 trafficking/stability and the ranker defines checkpoint/ER-stress modules, but incorporation of this specific PERK/ISR/GOLM1 proposal is not established. O13/O16 only bound limited mouse weight/histology observations; they do not qualify PERK inhibition as safe. The paper also reports nonsignificant in-vivo GOLM1 elevation and cannot exclude systemic/off-target contributions. GRAVEYARD_001 promoter-pathway and GRAVEYARD_010 indirect-APC requirements remain untested by this study.

This is endogenous gene expression across all islet cells in non-diabetic donor islets, not promoter-reporter activity in SC-islets.

Qualitative single-cell expression in adult primary islets, without testing BCL2 or XIAP.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet manufacturing release metrics and long-term functional readout)
edges.claim_summary: The pathogenic-INS model had similar reported d27 marker percentages (O1) but poor graft secretion and later loss of the C-peptide-positive fraction (O4/O5/O7/O9/O13), supporting the bounded caution that initial composition alone did not establish durable function in this disease model. Blueprint Gate1 already requires dynamic endocrine function in addition to composition; these data do not contradict that full requirement or establish failure of a WT-INS Islet-1 product. Specific incorporation of this mutation-domain observation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2, M3 (intrinsic ER-stress and identity endpoints during SC-islet maturation and in vivo graft follow-up)
edges.claim_summary: Mutant grafts exhibited high BIP colocalization among C-peptide-positive cells (O8) and ALDH1A3/NKX6.1 or GCG-negative ALDH1A3 marker phenotypes (O10/O11/O14), while terminal TUNEL was nearly undetectable (O12). Blueprint Gate4 explicitly already includes dedifferentiation and unfolded-proinsulin ER stress; a specific long-term BIP/ALDH1A3 panel is an unvalidated measurement hypothesis whose adoption status is unknown. It was not tested in the Islet-1 construct or under an imposed hypoxic/cytokine challenge, and terminal TUNEL does not exclude earlier apoptosis.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-only boundary controls beside the 60:30:10 tri-hormonal reference; IIP-0006 / DEC-084)
edges.claim_summary: Adult-mouse isolated islet phase-AUC null tests (O11), human pseudoislet GSIS/OCR readouts (O14, O15), and the separate human insulin-content null tests (O16) support the rationale for the β-only boundary controls already included under IIP-0006 / DEC-084; human HG + Ex-4 secretion differs (O14, direction unstated), and O12 supplies only within-genotype mouse Ex-4 tests. This is a bridge from adult primary human in vitro tissue and native mouse islets, with no demonstrated equivalence, optimal mixture or qualification of edited hPSC-derived products; total content (O16) does not measure secreted insulin.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (scope of non-β-cell paracrine requirement and retained 60:30:10 reference; IIP-0006 / DEC-084)
edges.claim_summary: Native non-diabetic adult mice after non-β-cell ablation showed no statistically significant fasting-glycaemia or ipGTT-AUC differences (O3-O5), improved glucose-tolerance/insulin-sensitivity/HFD phenotypes attributed by the abstract (O6-O9), and between-group plasma insulin stimulation-index differences of unstated direction (O17), qualifying a universal requirement for non-β-cells in these measured settings. This domain-limited qualification is already considered in the frozen Blueprint IIP-0006 / DEC-084 comparison protocol, but transfer to an edited hPSC product, exercise/nocturnal hypoglycaemia rescue or transplanted T1D remains unvalidated and the 60:30:10 reference is retained.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell memory, recurrent T1D autoimmunity)

This is a mechanistic bridge to Gate2B memory autoreactive pressure, not proof of protection of transplanted SC-islets, indirect APC blockade, or human efficacy. Incidence percentages have an unresolved denominator conflict, and anti-CD69 may also remove CD69+ Tregs; the paper does not establish preservation of unrelated immunity. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 already requires memory autoimmunity protection, but specific FABP4/T RM incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (PDMS-CaO2 oxygen supplementation bounded by peroxide and alkaline byproducts)
edges.claim_summary: The general mechanism is already explicit in frozen Blueprint Stage 2 and §4.5: hydrophobic PDMS-CaO2 oxygen delivery with catalase and peroxide/pH limits. This paper supports that mechanism through cell-free oxygen kinetics and increased MIN6 metabolic activity and total insulin content at 72 h under 1% O2 (O1–O9), while showing formulation-dependent chemical byproducts (O2, O3, O14). Its author-defined transient H2O2 bands (<50, 50–100, >100 μM) do not establish the Blueprint product limits (<5 μM H2O2; pH 7.25–7.45); no human SC-islet, catalase-combination, or assembled-product qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (bench oxygen output versus 24 h murine graft insulin content)

This qualifies using bench oxygen output as a surrogate for this local content endpoint, without asserting equivalence, zero benefit, or a cause of the discrepancy. Frozen Blueprint already requires physical qualification and labels Layer 4 conditional, but incorporation of this specific formulation-level bench/graft finding is not established. Human 72 h graft benefit remains an unvalidated transfer.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (candidate rate-limiting outer PDMS coating alongside catalase)

Testing a rate-limiting outer layer with the Blueprint catalase-containing material is an upgrade hypothesis, unvalidated in human SC-islets, in the catalase combination, and at a 72 h in vivo endpoint; the paper did test MIN6 constructs at 72 h. Claim-specific Blueprint incorporation is unknown.

HSC-humanized CAR T persistence/phenotype observations (O6-O9) support a mechanistic bridge for direct allorecognition, bounded to T cells and operational host reconstitution. They do not quantify the exact HLA-E/CD47-IgV-GPI islet product or establish autoimmune/indirect-APC protection; those residual pathways remain explicit in GRAVEYARD_010.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (completeness of HLA class I/II knockout in the edited population)

Whether this specific heterogeneous-population boundary is incorporated is not established by the frozen references reviewed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 and Gate5 / M5 (CD47 axis as a drug-triggered elimination route alongside iCasp9)

A CD47-targeted islet elimination route remains a hypothesis: Blueprint HLA-E adds another innate shield and the exact CD47-IgV-GPI construct, solid graft, systemic safety and clonogenic escape are untested here. The ranker already includes broad orthogonal eraser concepts, but specific SIRPα-route adoption is unresolved; no quantitative iCasp9 qualification is replaced.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M4 (autoimmunity in T1D; clinical C-peptide benchmark for immune modulation)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine purity and off-target removal in hiPSC-derived islet cells)
edges.claim_summary: O9 reports more than 99% chromogranin A-positive and approximately 60% C-peptide-positive cells after miR-375-CD4 MACS plus puromycin in hiPSC-derived pancreatic cultures, with C-peptide+, glucagon+ and some somatostatin+ cells (O10) and PDX1 co-expression suggesting immature beta cells (O11). This is pan-endocrine and precursor-stage purification, not mature beta-cell purity, and numbers are stated only in Discussion text.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (alloimmune risk and HLA-I/II ablation strategy, Locus 1/2)
edges.claim_summary: O9 and O11 show unedited macaque iHPs with weak MHC class I and mostly no class II (O8) induced no detectable alloantibodies even when mismatched and IFN-γ-stimulated; this qualifies the premise that alloimmune risk simply tracks MHC-I/II level, in a transient (O5) IV hematopoietic progenitor product with a humoral-only readout. It does not test T cell allorecognition or a persistent islet graft, so it does not weaken HLA ablation for islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (tumorigenicity and teratoma safety of an iPSC-derived product in NHP)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 report no teratomas or neoplastic lesions and no residual iPSC-derived cells at 1 year in iHP-infused macaques (3 per iHP group), while O3 and O4 show limited-time tissue persistence in a few animals. This is a transient, differentiated progenitor product with no suicide switch, so it adds NHP safety evidence but cannot speak to persistent islet grafts or iCasp9 escape rates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (surface non-classical HLA ligand principle; Locus 1 HLA-E comparison)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O2 show β2m-HLA-G K562 targets reduced NK92 lysis and degranulation (15.6% vs 29.7% activation). This supports a non-classical HLA ligand strategy at principle level; HLA-G is not a validated stand-in for the Blueprint HLA-E single-chain trimer, and NK92 does not establish protection across primary NKG2A/KIR/NKG2C subsets. The frozen Blueprint §4.1/ranker primary readouts require distinct exact-product density and primary-NK tests; incorporation of these HLA-G-specific results is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M7 (lineage-dependent surface display versus transcript/promoter activity)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O8 and O13-O18 distinguish lineage-dependent HLA/APM surface and transcript phenotypes; O9-O12 show transient TF-associated display recovery and reduced NK92 lysis. These support a hypothesis to pair APM profiling with HLA-E surface/functional testing in SC-islet lineages, without claiming APM is the sole cause or recommending constitutive RelA/NLRC5 adoption. O19 retains an unresolved IFN-γ/HLA-G wording conflict. Blueprint §4.1, GRAVEYARD_009 and ranker Decision Experiment 1 already demand lineage-specific surface measurements; incorporation of this specific APM mechanism is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter/transgene durability and genomic safety scope)
edges.claim_summary: O5 shows maintained EF1α-driven EGFP reporter expression in this β2m-locus neural system and no reported IFN-γ effect; O20 reports a normal karyotype. Neither establishes durability of the Blueprint native 230-bp EEF1A1-core/insulated AAVS1-iCasp9 cassette, clonogenic escape, or comprehensive genomic safety. Blueprint §4.4, ranker shared-promoter-silencing mitigation and GRAVEYARD_002 retain separate pan-lineage switch qualification. Incorporation of this reporter-specific observation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; alternative chemistry to PDMS-CaO2 + catalase)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: a CO2-regulated Li2O2/PFC generator separated from the cells by a gas-permeable silicone membrane could complement or replace the cheatsheet's PDMS-CaO2 + catalase bridge, since solution pH was unchanged over several weeks (O2), iBEDv3 raised bench pO2 to ~180 mmHg (O10) and O2 production persisted at 92 days (O16). Evidence is rat islets and INS-1 in alginate, not hPSC-derived islets, over weeks to months rather than 72 hours.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (beta-cell survival under peri-transplant hypoxia)
edges.claim_summary: Local O2 generation rescued INS-1 viability (2.7-fold improvement, O3) and reduced pimonidazole hypoxia signal in rat islets (O4) after 24 h at 1% O2, and the model keeps islets above the 8 mmHg insulin-secretion threshold in iBEDv2 and iBEDv3 (O9). Rat line and rat islets, not hPSC-derived islets; no intrinsic cytoprotection gene is tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (avascular oxygen bridge: slab physics, Krogh diffusion; passive gas-phase scaffold)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: an internal air-channel scaffold could extend the O2 diffusion distance of hydrogel islet devices beyond the cheatsheet's slab-physics limits: simulated islet pO2 rose 1.8-fold with 5-fold less necrosis (O4, O5), a 6.6 mm device stayed oxygenated in silico (O13), and human-islet simulations favored the SONIC spiral at 4% to 10% loading (O17, O18). Caveats: passive scaffold with no O2 source (all models set a constant 40 mmHg boundary, so it cannot replace a 72-hour oxygen bridge), rat islets in vivo, human islets in silico only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (beta-cell survival under diffusion-limited hypoxia)
edges.claim_summary: In thick bulk alginate, central INS-1 cells died at 5% O2 while SONIC devices kept robust viability (O3), and simulation predicted 5-fold less islet necrosis (O5); fibrosis simulations also kept SONIC islets oxygenated (O12). INS-1 line and rat-islet models, not hPSC-derived islets, and no intrinsic cytoprotection gene is tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5, M3 (physical containment of proliferative cells as a layer beside the Locus 4 iCasp9 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O5 show GFP/luciferase MSC and 4T1 spheroids stayed confined in a nanofiber-skinned alginate device in mice with no signal outside the device (5 months and up to 150 days), while O6 records 2/6 early failures attributed by the authors to possible device defects; this suggests size-exclusion containment could be layered with the genetic kill switch. Evidence is rodent and cell-line, not an hPSC-derived graft; the bridge is the size-exclusion mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A, Gate2B / M3 (immune exposure of a barrier-protected xenograft: CD8 exclusion versus CD4 and humoral responses and function loss in immunocompetent hosts)
edges.claim_summary: A barrier device had <1.5% CD8+ cells around it (O9) and little alloantibody inside (O10, O11), yet 80% of cells on the allo/xeno devices were lymphocytes (O8) and human SC-beta C-peptide response was lost by 4 weeks in immunocompetent mice (O18, after 10/17 initial normoglycemia in O17). This bounds what a physical barrier alone achieves for Gate2A/2B in a xenogeneic mouse host; it does not test a genetically cloaked hPSC islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell memory against PPI in recurrent T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2: PPI15-24-reactive CD8+ T cells are reported at high frequency (one in ten pancreatic CD8+ cells, per the title) in native pancreas of recent-onset T1D patients, supporting the Gate2B premise that PPI-directed autoreactive memory is a graft threat. The data come from native T1D pancreas, not an hPSC-derived islet graft, and no graft-protection test is made.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection under IFNgamma, TNFalpha and IL-1beta exposure; TET2 deletion or inhibition as a candidate perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: Tet2-KO mouse beta cells survived cytokines and islet infiltrates better (O9, O10) with reduced cytokine, chemokine and death-receptor transcripts (O17, O18), and TET inhibition by R-2HG in cytokine-treated human islets gave a similar transcript reduction (O14). This suggests TET2 deletion or inhibition could be tested as a beta-cell-intrinsic cytoprotection layer; evidence is a global KO in NOD mice plus a transcript-level human islet experiment, not a hPSC-derived graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell pressure; beta-cell-intrinsic protection despite a pathogenic repertoire)
edges.claim_summary: Tet2-KO NOD beta cells resisted autoimmune destruction by fully diabetogenic WT immune cells in BMT chimeras, islet grafts and adoptive transfer (O5, O6, O8, O15) even though splenocytes from KO recipients still transferred diabetes to NOD/scid mice (O7), with fewer CXCR3+ T cells in lymph nodes (O11). The domain is syngeneic NOD autoimmunity with a gene-deleted host and graft, not a gene-edited hPSC islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B, Gate4 / Locus 3 (CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 circuit)
edges.claim_summary: In Tet2-KO mouse islets the IFNgamma-induced Cxcl10 and Pdl1 responses were reduced (O13, O18), so combining TET2 deletion or inhibition with an IFNgamma/CXCL10-driven inducible circuit could blunt the circuit's own induction. This is an endogenous-gene result in mouse islets; it does not test an engineered promoter in human cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation and dynamic perifusion GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: Extended culture self-enrichment of hESC-derived sBC (seBC) gave a glucose response in perifusion comparable with human islets while imBC responded only to KCl (O8), with larger Ca2+ responses (O9), twice the insulin content (O6) and a lower proinsulin-to-insulin ratio (O7). This supports achieving dynamic GSIS in vitro for Gate1, with values only in figures and no stimulation index in the text.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification: CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment and maturity-based sorting with ENTPD3)
edges.claim_summary: ENTPD3 sorting isolates a mature INS+ENTPD3+ seBC subpopulation of about 30% (O12) with higher insulin content (O13) and a lower proinsulin-to-insulin ratio (O15) than INS+ENTPD3-, glucose-responsive after reaggregation in hESC (O16, n = 2) and iPSC lines (O18), and enriched single-positive insulin sBC more than ITGA1 (O5). ENTPD3 could be tested as a maturity sort layer beside ITGA1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (maturity benchmark and off-target or proliferative subpopulations in SC-islet products)
edges.claim_summary: Even after self-enrichment, seBC remained heterogeneous with immature, polyhormonal and small proliferative Ki67+ subpopulations (O10, O11), and insulin content of ENTPD3+ seBC stayed lower than cadaveric ENTPD3+ beta cells (O14). This bounds how far in vitro maturation reached the primary-beta-cell benchmark in this study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5 (Locus 4 iCasp9/AP1903 clonogenic suicide switch)
edges.claim_summary: A lentiviral CAGs-driven iC9 switch removed more than 99% of human iPSCs within 24 h at 0.1 nM AP20187 (O10) with unmodified and vector controls insensitive (O11), prevented teratomas when dimerizer was given at injection (O12) and cleared established teratomas to non-palpable size within a week (O13) in NSG mice. This is human iPSC, lentiviral CAGs rather than AAVS1 knock-in, and bulk viability percentages rather than a measured 1e-6 escape fraction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5 (AAVS1 safe-harbor placement of the suicide cassette and promoter silencing)
edges.claim_summary: A biallelic AAVS1 CAGs.TK.007 clone with no detected off-target integration (O1) showed lower marker expression than LV-modified iPSCs (O2) and only 30% versus 80% induced cell death at 0.1 uM GCV (O6), while both settings were almost fully ablated at higher GCV doses and in vitro at 10 uM (O5). The AAVS1 comparison used TK.007, not iC9, and silencing at AAVS1 was not tested, so it qualifies low-dose penetrance of an AAVS1 knock-in switch without showing silencing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5 (promoter choice: ubiquitous versus pluripotency-restricted suicide switch expression)
edges.claim_summary: Pluripotency-restricted Oct4SRE.iC9 spared iPSC-derived macrophages (O15), only delayed or prevented tumors when dimerizer was given at injection (O17) and did not control established teratomas (O18), whereas ubiquitous CAGs-driven iC9 ablated iMAC (O16) and cleared established teratomas (O13). This supports a ubiquitously expressed switch for whole-graft ablation; CAGs is not the EEF1A1 element named for the Blueprint, and no islet-derived cells were tested.

Hypothesis for the Blueprint: add islet-specific T cell cytokine phenotyping as a monitoring readout alongside C-peptide benchmarks; this is a hedged abstract-level association, not a validated predictor.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M7, M3 (Krogh-type diffusion limits and islet size for the avascular oxygen bridge)

The mechanism is passive diffusion-consumption in primary islets, bridged to hPSC-islet clusters only through cluster size and OCR, which the abstract does not give for SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 (macro- versus microencapsulation geometry for oxygen supply)
edges.claim_summary: The model suggests microcapsules deliver more oxygen than macrocapsules (O4) and that high-OCR islets (porcine, ~300) lose 35% of islet volume to the nonfunctional zone in a slab macrocapsule (O2), which qualifies reliance on slab geometry alone for oxygen. The abstract reports passive-supply modeling only and does not mention oxygen-releasing materials such as PDMS-CaO2, so transfer to the Blueprint avascular oxygen bridge is unvalidated.

edges.claim_summary: The fraction of large islets (>250 um) predicted diabetes reversal in the mouse bioassay (O1, O2), which suggests testing the fraction of SC-islet clusters above a size cutoff as a manufacturing release or sorting criterion for Gate1. This is a hypothesis from primary human islets in a kidney-capsule mouse model; no SC-islet data are in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (avascular oxygen bridge; CaO2/PDMS and encapsulation slab physics)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O5, O6: in NHPs, intact non-fibrotic microcapsules still held islets with central necrosis and hypoxia markers, and added oxygen plus MSCs extended function for a longer period (Two NHPs, not separated from MSC effect). edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (survival under peri-transplant hypoxia; hypoxia-tolerant donor cells)
edges.claim_summary: O6 and the abstract conclusion call for identifying donor insulin-secreting cells that tolerate hypoxia, consistent with Gate4's scope of beta-cell survival under peri-transplant hypoxia and hypoxic conditioning. The evidence is qualitative and from NHP-islet microcapsule grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (avascular oxygen bridge; vascularization-dependent device oxygenation)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O6, O1, O2: in a cell-free porous subcutaneous device in nude mice, optical PO2 at the tube surface rose only approximately up to 20 mmHg in a day-3 example, oxygen dynamics differed per implant, and H2S did not change perfusion readouts, supporting the premise that vascular oxygenation of such devices is slow and variable. No islet oxygen consumption is present, only device-surface readings, and the numbers come from one example trace.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularized device: functional perfusion vs vessel density endpoints)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O4, O5: DIGT perfusion readouts showed no change with H2S while CD31 expression and vessel density were lower, so perfusion and density were discordant (the abstract says they are not necessarily correlated). Hypothesis: score device vascularization in Gate5 work with a functional oxygen-transport readout rather than CD31 density alone; this is a nude-mouse device study with a small, underpowered n (O7).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (pan-lineage iCasp9 fail-safe feasibility; not quantitative product qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 support NANOG-iCasp9/AP20187 depletion and teratoma prevention as reported, and O7/O8 support ACTB-OiCasp9/AP21967 killing in tested H9 lineages and NSG teratomas. This is preclinical feasibility evidence; exact study-performance incorporation is unknown. Different loci, dimerizers and cell products do not qualify the Blueprint biallelic AAVS1/EEF1A1/AP1903 product or its <=1e-8 per-clonogenic-cell target (Blueprint §4.4/§7). Reported 19/arm versus four/arm cohort correspondence remains unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (locus- and lineage-specific stability versus AAVS1 anti-silencing qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O11 reports persistent NANOG-linked expression in undifferentiated hPSCs after an unspecified long-term culture; ACTB-linked switches retain function in tested derivatives/teratomas. These observations do not show that an endogenous essential-gene knock-in cannot escape or certify a distinct AAVS1/EEF1A1 cassette across SC-islet and vascular lineages. The need for direct anti-silencing and clonogenic qualification, rather than a safe-harbor guarantee, is already explicit in Blueprint §4.4/§7 and the ranker non-i.i.d. silencing gates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (heterogeneous-product reporter depletion versus clonogenic escape qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O4 reports >10-fold loss of NANOG-YFP+ reporter cells; O15 reports no colonies from sorted survivors within an unspecified detection limit. These are different readouts and cannot be compared directly with the pure-population O1 colony depletion as an efficacy loss, nor used to infer an escape probability. The 10%/1:9 composition conflicts with Methods M32 and is not repaired. Testing spiked heterogeneous products and calibrated clonogenic denominators is already required by GRAVEYARD_002 and Blueprint §7; this study does not newly establish or meet the Blueprint <=1e-8 bound.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (priming-dependent missing-self injury in graft vasculature)
edges.claim_summary: O5 and O8–O10 establish within the tested human-EC and murine-heart models that prior NK priming conditions missing-self activation or vascular lesions; absence of added priming did not establish universal immune tolerance. This bounds the Blueprint Gate3 missing-self rationale (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:63) but does not test its HLA-E/CD47 construct or SC-islet protection. Incorporation of this exact priming-dependent boundary is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (educated KIR subsets and limits of extrapolating HLA-E coverage)
edges.claim_summary: O5–O7 support testing educated KIR-ligand mismatches against allogeneic human endothelial cells; O13/O16 describe repertoire heterogeneity, and O17 qualifies genotype-only prediction. The bounded incorporated claim is the need to evaluate KIR/NKG2A-defined NK subsets, explicitly named in Blueprint:63,270 and ranker:2900,5810. This study does not measure NKG2A status, HLA-E trimer rescue, CD47 rescue or an SC-islet escape rate; its percentages are not the Blueprint NKG2A-negative fraction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (mTOR inhibition as an experimental missing-self control or transfer hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O14 shows patient NK-cell pathway suppression, O15 reduced K562 cytotoxicity, and O11/O12 report less murine graft inflammation with mTOR inhibition than vehicle while cyclosporin was described as having no effect. These motivate an assay-control or separately tested transfer hypothesis, not mTOR therapy adoption, complete lesion blockade or clinical SC-islet protection. The Blueprint immunosuppression-free goal (:59) and its separate rapamycin-dependent biomaterial caveat (:271) do not establish incorporation of this particular mechanism. Drug and effector-preparation conflicts remain annotated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAVS1 differentiation-dependent expression stability)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O6/O7/O11 document variable or declining CAG/pTRE reporter expression at AAVS1 in human cardiac/haematopoietic differentiation. The general lineage-dependent silencing hazard is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §4.4; this paper provides additional non-islet examples, not tested values for the EEF1A1-core/insulated iCasp9 construct. It does not establish methylation causality or switch escape rates, and the proposed anti-silencing element remains function-pending.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (post-differentiation clone/switch qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2/O5/O10 support empirical clone screening: high reporter expression in hiPSCs or biallelic insertion does not by itself ensure stable expression after differentiation. Post-differentiation stressed AP1903 clonogenic testing is already required by frozen ranker lines 5055-5058 and Decision Experiment #4, consistent with the Blueprint/GRAVEYARD_002 pan-lineage fail-safe boundary. No iCasp9 or AP1903 assay was performed here; reporter function in O13-O15 cannot qualify erasure.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate3 / M1 (construct-specific multicistronic P2A processing)
edges.claim_summary: O12 preserves a Discussion report of inefficient P2A cleavage in an incompletely specified AAVS1 hiPSC construct; underlying Extended-data Western blots are outside the packet. This is a construct-testing caution, not a general P2A-versus-T2A ranking or demonstrated failure of OpenIslet GSG-P2A cassettes. Blueprint §4.1 already requires anti-2A Western testing, but incorporation of this exact reported construct-specific failure is undetermined.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic suicide switch; in vitro versus in vivo kill efficacy)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O6/O14 show strong in vitro GCV sensitivity, whereas O8/O9/O12 show growth restraint with incomplete clearance of established teratomas after oral valganciclovir in NOG mice. This bounds the inference from in vitro potency to in vivo eradication; HSV-TK/GCV at Chr1-eGSH is not the Blueprint AAVS1 iCasp9/AP1903 construct. Frozen Blueprint §4.4/Stage 3 and ranker Avascular_Core_Prodrug_Perfusion_Deficit already require in vivo switch/perfusion qualification; incorporation of this exact HSV-TK result is unknown, and vascularization is a suggested explanation here, not a tested causal determinant.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (EEF1A1-promoter transgene stability at a safe harbour)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O7 support expression in hiPSCs/early EBs; O10/O11 report no significant between-teratoma-group expression/methylation difference despite treatment resistance and higher methylation than parental hiPSCs. These bounded observations do not prove long-term stability, nonsignificant equivalence or an absence of silencing-related resistance. Frozen Blueprint §4.4 and ranker Shared_Promoter_Epigenetic_CpG_Methylation address a different AAVS1 230-bp EEF1A1-core/insulator/iCasp9 construct; neither identical promoter sequence nor incorporation of this study-specific result is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAVS1 neighbourhood: genes within the same CTCF loop or TAD)
edges.claim_summary: O1 predicts possible AAVS1-neighbor interactions from public non-hiPSC topology data; O4 reports a small BRINP3 expression increase 2 Mb from Chr1-eGSH but explicitly cannot exclude an artifact. This motivates an unvalidated hypothesis to measure same-loop/TAD neighboring-gene expression after the actual AAVS1 insertion. No AAVS1 knock-in effect, oncogenic consequence or need for a specific replacement locus was demonstrated. Frozen Blueprint genomic QC and GRAVEYARD_006 concern other safety mechanisms; incorporation of this specific topology-neighbor test is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation and dynamic perifusion GSIS; Stage-6/7 maturation)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O4, O6, O8 and O14 show that FACS-purified hESC-derived INS-GFP+ cells reaggregated into eBCs reach 78.1 ± 1.8% C-peptide+/NKX6.1+, respond to glucose in perifusion unlike d20 clusters and unsorted NECs, and secrete C-peptide in NSG grafts from 3 days. The cheatsheet baseline does not state a reaggregation step or its mitochondrial (OXPHOS) maturation read-out (O8, O10).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biphasic GSIS and maturity benchmark, SI >= 2.0-3.0)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O11 and O13 show that eBC second-phase release was not sustained, MAFA was lower than in adult islets, and 3,313 genes still differed from islet beta cells, which qualifies how close reaggregated SC-beta cells come to the biphasic-GSIS maturity benchmark. No stimulation index is stated in the packet text.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (tumorigenic overgrowth risk; purification upstream of the clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O18: eBCs were depleted of PDX1+/NKX6.1+/C-peptide- progenitors, and eBC grafts showed no overgrowth at 8 months (5/5 mice) whereas d20 grafts formed large masses in 7/10 mice at 3 months, supporting purification as a first-line control on overgrowth risk. The study tests no suicide switch or escape frequency, and the eBC result comes from small unedited NSG cohorts.

edges.claim_summary: O17 and O18: omitting Alk5i during stage 6 drastically increased GSIS, and TGFBR1 knockdown reduced it, so permitting TGF-β signalling in the final maturation stage may be required for dynamic function. Hypothesis to test in the Blueprint's Stage-6/7 maturation conditions; the cheatsheet does not state whether ALK5 inhibition is used there.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (mechanistic failure mode: alpha-cell glucose regulation depends on beta-cell contact, not secreted factors)
edges.claim_summary: O12, O8 and O15-O17: beta-cell-conditioned medium (1.18 ± 0.15) and physiological insulin doses did not restore alpha-cell glucose inhibition, only a supraphysiological insulin dose did (0.56 ± 0.05), and glibenclamide inhibited glucagon only when beta-cells were present. This qualifies a Gate1 paracrine-architecture target in that alpha-cell regulation in a graft may need direct beta-alpha contact, a point that rests on primary adult islet cells in vitro.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic integrity release screening for the manufactured product)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4: nonsynonymous mtDNA mutations arose and became enriched during reprogramming, long-term culture and differentiation, and the authors recommend screening iPSC-derived products for them. Hypothesis: add mtDNA variant screening to the Gate5 genomic-integrity release panel, which the cheatsheet describes in nuclear terms (translocations, off-target base edits, chromothripsis, promoter silencing).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK cytotoxicity beyond HLA-E/NKG2A missing-self; TRAIL-DR5 and CXCR3 axes)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4: islet loss in syngeneic (self-MHC) mouse recipients depended on CXCR3 (6/6 vs 0/6 normoglycaemic) and Tbx21-dependent NK cells, and DX5- NK cytotoxicity against islets was partly blocked by anti-TRAIL or anti-IFN-γ. This qualifies Gate3's NK axes (the cheatsheet lists NKG2A/NKG2C/KIR/DNAM-1/CD54/CD58 but not TRAIL-DR5 or CXCR3), but it is a mouse liver-resident NK subset with no human or SC-islet test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M3 (innate NK barrier and secondary graft failure at the intraportal site)
edges.claim_summary: O14, O15 and O17: the same 400-islet mass engrafted in 5/6 mice as primary IT but in 0/6 after a prior syngeneic IT; NK depletion restored 5/6 and anti-TNF-α at both ITs gave 6/7 (vs 0/7), but anti-TNF-α at the secondary IT alone did not (1/5 vs 0/5, O18). It supports innate NK pressure as a graft-loss mechanism independent of alloantigen, within a mouse liver-site syngeneic model that does not test hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (innate blood-contact / complement-coagulation injury to infused islets)
edges.claim_summary: This human intraportal primary-islet trial found no significant difference in Day-75 stimulated C-peptide for the tested LMW-DS regimen versus active heparin control (O1, p=0.66); early TAT/C-peptide rose in both arms (O9), and the trial stopped early at n=24 (O10). This qualifies extrapolation from complement/coagulation mechanism to incremental graft function; it does not establish equivalence, failure to inhibit IBMIR, a no-treatment effect, or efficacy of the Blueprint genetic cloak/SA-THBD adjunct. The frozen Blueprint already discusses Hour-0 IBMIR and a THBD adjunct; incorporation of this exact clinical contrast is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide and glycaemic clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: Provides bounded clinical context under systemic immunosuppression: Day-75 MMTT C-peptide 1.33 (SD 1.10) ng/mL with LMW-DS versus 1.56 (SD 1.36) with heparin (O1, with ITT imputation), functioning graft 80.0% versus 85.7% (O2), and final-transplant Day-365 HbA1c 6.1 (SD 0.7)% versus 6.3 (SD 1.3)% (O4, with late evaluable n unresolved). These primary-donor-islet observations do not qualify hPSC-derived endocrine function without immunosuppression, and incorporation of these exact benchmarks is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell memory against PPI / proinsulin)
edges.claim_summary: Replacing murine Ins1 with human INS lowered diabetes incidence in NOD mice (abstract: 15-20% vs more than 60%; p<0.0001 log-rank for both KI/KI and KI/+ vs WT; O1, O2, O3), consistent with proinsulin being a dominant autoantigen of the Gate2B autoreactivity axis. The bridge to a human SC-islet graft rests on the abstract's statement that insulin/proinsulin T-cell responses are central in both NOD mice and humans; no human cells were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (durability of antigen-sparing protection)
edges.claim_summary: Protection was partial and associated with delayed insulitis: insulitis was reduced at 100 days (p < 0.05) but equal to wildtype by 300 days (p > 0.05; O5, O6), so reduced antigenicity of proinsulin delays rather than abolishes islet infiltration in this model. Whether this scopes autoimmune-evasion strategies for a human graft is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (oxygen bridge: macroencapsulation slab physics, diffusion-consumption limits)
edges.claim_summary: In an islet-alginate slab fed from a gas chamber, the minimum chamber pO2 needed to keep about 50 mmHg at the host-facing face rose with islet density (190 ± 31, 229 ± 57, 305 ± 34 mmHg at 2,400, 3,600, 4,800 IEQ/cm2; O10, O11, O12) and matched a simple analytical diffusion-consumption model (O13). Rat islets and an exogenous gas supply are not hPSC-derived islets or PDMS-CaO2, but the diffusion-consumption physics bridges.
