edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (oxygen supply cannot rescue poor-quality islets)
edges.claim_summary: Duration of normoglycemia tracked pre-implant islet number and OCR (100% vs 0% long-term normoglycemia in upper-right vs lower-left domains; O14, O15) while insulin content did not predict outcome (r = 0.06; O16), and some animals reached 6 months or more even at the 1,000 IEQ/cm2 air design (O5). This qualifies the oxygen-bridge argument: oxygen supply alone does not determine outcome, and graft quality at implant matters. Transfer to hPSC-derived islets is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (anatomical-site oxygen boundary measurements)
edges.claim_summary: Anatomical-site pO2 in anaesthetised NHP was 30.7 ± 1.6 mmHg general IP, 35.1 ± 3.2 bursa, 39.6 ± 3.2 pancreas, 48.7 ± 1.3 kidney capsule and 39.0 ± 2.1 subcutaneous (O7/O8/O14/O16/O17; spread unspecified). Bursa was not significantly different from IP or pancreas. These contextual site measurements may inform Gate5 boundary sensitivity, but are not graft-core oxygenation or an acute 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/iMVF bridge test; direct substitution into the Blueprint boundary requires qualification. Specific quantitative incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (graft/site geometry), with Gate1 functional-readout qualification
edges.claim_summary: Primary allogeneic cynomolgus islets in 1.5-mm Z1-Y15 spheres in the non-diabetic NHP bursa yielded viable and glucose-responsive retrievals without immunosuppression; the 90.0% four-month viability median covers only two non-fibrosed recipients and a third failed with PFO/non-viable islets (O11/O12). Static GSIS and nonsignificant coupling-factor comparisons (O13/O15/O18–O21) do not establish biphasic dynamic insulin secretion, diabetic rescue, hPSC-product protection, or the exact Blueprint oxygen bridge. Specific adoption is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (material-associated macrophage attachment and fibrosis)
edges.claim_summary: Clinical-formulation empty spheres fibrosed by one month; Z1-Y15 islet spheres had less CD68+/CD11b+ macrophage attachment than empty SLG20 controls and less fibrosis than separate islet-loaded SLG20 controls (O2/O9/O10). Material, diameter and implantation-site context matter for this innate failure mode. No HLA-E/CD47 intervention was tested, so the study does not establish whether those edits prevent or fail to prevent material fibrosis. Generic fibrotic-device risk is acknowledged by the frozen ranker, while incorporation of these particular empirical contrasts remains unknown.

The abstract reports no insulin-arm GFR and no formal test, so causality is the authors' interpretation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe rationale: tumorigenic risk of residual undifferentiated hPSCs)
edges.claim_summary: Undifferentiated hiPSCs formed teratomas in NOG mice with a dose-dependent TPD50 (631 with Y-27632, 4642 without; O9, O10, O11) and with strong line-to-line variation in incidence (17% to 100%) and latency (4 to 9 weeks) at 3 × 104 cells (O1, O2), which supports a quantified clonogenic fail-safe for any residual hPSCs in a graft. Domain bridge only: unmodified hiPSCs injected subcutaneously with Matrigel and fibroblasts, not SC-islet grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M6 (genomic-integrity screening as a proxy for tumor risk)
edges.claim_summary: Two of 10 lines carried trisomy 12 and each line carried 61-77 cancer-related gene variants, yet no carcinoma or sarcoma arose and trisomy 12 had no distinct effect on tumorigenicity (O8, O13, O14, O15, O16); pluripotency-marker expression also did not correlate with tumor outcome (O17). This qualifies reliance on karyotype or cancer-gene variant counts as a predictor of malignancy in this assay; transfer to edited, islet-fated grafts is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (classical-HLA ablation and the humoral anti-HLA component of alloimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: O1 reports no accelerated attrition with DSA appearance in the overall 49-patient allogeneic-islet cohort; O3 reports no effect of passive DSAs on mouse islet graft survival. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 explicitly includes DSA evasion, and the ranker combines T-cell/DSA priors, so these observations qualify uniform attribution of islet attrition to DSAs. They do not test B2M editing, establish equivalence, remove T-cell risk, or validate engineered hPSC islets. Donor origin, immunosuppression and subgroup denominators are unspecified in this abstract. Incorporation of this particular boundary is not established by the checked reference passages.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization and host-versus-donor endothelial identity; no oxygen-timing measurement)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O6 report vascular DSA sequestration and lesion-free recipient-capillary revascularization in murine islet grafts, contrasted with DSA-accessible endothelium and microvascular lesions in murine heart grafts. This identifies endothelial origin and antibody access as boundaries for transferring protection to the Blueprint section 4.5 edited isogenic iEC/iPericyte microvessels. It does not establish immune tolerance, protection of donor-derived engineered iECs, a 72-hour revascularization time, or oxygen-bridge performance. Incorporation of this specific endothelial/DSA boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10::SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1; CXCL10 exon 1 knock-in)
edges.claim_summary: Islet-derived IP-10 (CXCL10) harmed early graft function: deletion in donor islets or neutralization improved glucose control in marginal-dose mouse grafts (O5 to O8) and higher early IP-10 exposure tracked with lower C-peptide in autologous patients (O4). This suggests a testable co-benefit of the Blueprint Locus 3 knock-in at CXCL10 exon 1 (reduced native IP-10 release from edited SC-islets), to be measured with an IP-10 release readout under cytokine stress; the data come from primary islets, not hPSC-derived islets, and gene knockout was not tested in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate4 / M4 (hour-0 to 24-h innate inflammatory graft loss window)
edges.claim_summary: In autologous patients, where alloimmunity is absent, early circulating IP-10 exposure was associated with worse graft function (O1, O4), and islets released chemokines at high rates under cytokine stress (O2, O3), supporting the Blueprint premise that innate hour-0 insults require built-in protection. Patient islets were infused intraportally and were not hPSC-derived or edited.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe and genomic oncology safety of the hPSC starting material)
edges.claim_summary: Five hESC lines (including a screen of 140 lines that covered 26 clinical-intent lines) carried six dominant-negative TP53 mutations whose allelic fraction rose with passage (O1, O2, O3), and 12/252 (5%) distinct hPSC lines carried 15 TP53 mutations in combined analysis (O8), supporting the need for a fail-safe against expanding cancer-associated clones. These are undifferentiated hESC/hPSC lines in culture, not islet grafts, and the cheatsheet does not state this TP53 failure mode.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (mechanistic limits: selective advantage is line-dependent and not prevented by culture format)
edges.claim_summary: The selective advantage of TP53 mutations is not uniform: ESI035 mutant cells declined while CHB11 and WA26 approached fixation (O5), and mutations arose across feeder-based and feeder-free cultures and were not prevented by rock inhibitor (O16, O17). This qualifies any assumption that a defined feeder-free culture or standard supplements keeps hPSC stocks free of TP53 mutants; counts per condition are only in figures.

edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link M0255:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O12,O7,O8 | text_sha256=4f1c1a75ed2faba848357d6fa9ed1621784e1a453ac37eff274459c0b3d30191]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (donor SIRPalpha polymorphism sensed by recipient CD47)
edges.claim_summary: Donor SIRPα allele mismatch (NOD-derived Sirpa sufficient, O6; stronger CD47 binding by NOD and CAST SIRPα, O11) drove host mono-DC infiltration via recipient CD47 (O7, O8), which qualifies the cheatsheet's CD47-SIRPalpha engagement as a purely inhibitory axis; the donor cells here are bone marrow myeloid cells in mice, and transfer to SIRPα-low hPSC-derived islet cells is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO and CIITA KO scope versus innate monocyte-DC pathway)
edges.claim_summary: Donor B2m-deficient and Mhc2-deficient grafts did not reduce the innate alloresponse (O4, O5) and MHC mismatch was not required, so B2M and CIITA ablation addresses T-cell allorecognition but would not by itself remove this monocyte-DC pathway; the model is mouse and lacks lymphocytes.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (suicide switch; HSV-TK/ganciclovir at HPRT versus iCasp9 at AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: A knock-in HSVTK checkpoint at the HPRT locus allowed ganciclovir elimination of CPTK hESC-derived cells in vitro and in vivo (O2, O3), supporting the general logic of a clonogenic fail-safe; the abstract gives no escape frequency, so it cannot test the Blueprint's <1e-6 threshold, and the switch differs from iCasp9/AP1903 at AAVS1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 immune evasion of allo-T cells)
edges.claim_summary: CPTK hESC-derived cells coexpressing CTLA4-Ig and PD-L1 were reported protected from immune rejection in humanized mice (O1), supporting PD-L1-based allo-T evasion; the effect cannot be attributed to PD-L1 alone since CTLA4-Ig is also expressed, and the abstract names no control arm or islet cell type.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK missing-self; KIR2DL1/2/3 and NKG2A-negative KIR+ NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: Licensed KIR2DL1+ NK subsets killed iPSC-derived T and VE cells lacking the cognate group 2 HLA-C ligand, while KIR-ligand-matched donors did not (O2, O4, O6, O12), which supports the cheatsheet's Gate3 KIR2DL1/2/3 missing-self axis and its evaluation of KIR+ NK subsets; targets here are HLA-homozygous iPSC-derived T and VE cells with intact HLA class I, not B2M-null islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (B2M KO background: HLA-C ligand add-back for KIR2DL1/2/3 on top of HLA-E, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: Lentiviral overexpression of the missing HLA-C group blocked KIR-ligand-mismatched NK cytotoxicity and returned responses to the autologous-control level (O7, O9, O10, O13), whereas a group 1 control did not (O8), suggesting an HLA-C ligand could be tested alongside HLA-E to cover KIR+ NKG2A-negative subsets; B2M-null graft cells and surface HLA-C without B2M were not tested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (competence of humanized-host graft-rejection assays)
edges.claim_summary: In the tested hSRC/hBLT hosts and time windows, unmodified PSC/endothelial graft persistence co-occurred with incomplete rejection, sparse local immune populations and age-associated anergy (O1-O9, O13-O16, O18), qualifying inference of allo-evasion from graft persistence unless relevant model rejection competence is demonstrated. This is a justified methodological bridge to Blueprint Stage-3 humanized-mouse qualification, not exact SC-islet product validation or a claim that every humanized model fails; claim-specific incorporation is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate3 / M1 / M3 (immune-pressure adequacy and minor-antigen graft-rejection limits)
edges.claim_summary: Allogenized mouse-immune hosts rejected major allogeneic miPSC and xenogeneic hESC grafts with site-dependent delay, yet failed to reject mHA-mismatched mESCs and had lower splenocyte IFN-γ (O10-O12, O17); Fig 7E stimulus descriptions conflict and no selective innate-cell causal intervention is reported. This provides an unvalidated-transfer caution for Gate2B/Gate3 assay competence, without directly measuring human autoimmunity, host-APC indirect presentation or an Islet-1 immune-cloaking construct; the frozen Blueprint/ranker/graveyard establish those gate hazards but do not establish incorporation of this specific model limitation.

edges.claim_summary: In forty-two allogeneic islet recipients, DSA titers were low, none bound C3d, and DSA did not seem to harm graft survival (O4, O5, O6), which qualifies how heavily antibody-mediated rejection should weigh against T-cell allorecognition in Gate2A; these are allogeneic islets from an immunosuppressed cohort, not SC-islets, and the abstract hedges the conclusion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant hypoxic stress, BCL2-family survival, inflammatory stress)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4: higher seeding density coincided with a higher Bax/Bcl-2 mRNA ratio and MCP-1 release, a hypoxia-linked pro-apoptotic and proinflammatory signature that bears on Gate4 stress-resilience targets. Primary human islets, 24 h in vitro only; whether the Blueprint already uses these readouts cannot be settled from the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; pO2 maintenance)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4: 7-day culture of human islets at 270 or 350 mmHg pO2 preserved volume, viability, oxygen consumption and GSIS better than 160 or 90 mmHg, supporting the premise that the oxygen bridge matters. The cheatsheet states no pO2 setpoint; primary human islets in vitro with qualitative abstract-only results, not SC-islets or an avascular graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (pre-transplant conditioning; hyperoxic maintenance as a candidate setpoint)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O1-O4 (the abstract itself predicts it): test hyperoxic pre- and peri-transplant maintenance as a pO2 setpoint for SC-islets instead of normoxia. The abstract does not test SC-islets, oxidative or peroxide toxicity, or in vivo transplant outcomes; the cheatsheet lists hypoxic or metabolic conditioning, not hyperoxic maintenance.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; diffusion-reaction and Krogh-type slab physics)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O5, O6, O9, O10: a steady-state diffusion-reaction model of an avascular islet predicts a size- and P ext-dependent anoxic core (AVF 30.8% at 300 um versus 0 at 150 um; AVF 13.6% and FLISC 72% at 5 mm Hg), supporting oxygen diffusion as a limiting failure mode before revascularization. It models primary human islets at an intraportal site, not SC-islets in a device, and no experiments were run; the shared reason is diffusion-limited supply against Michaelis-Menten consumption.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (cluster-diameter ceiling for SC-islet oxygenation; size-sorting)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O1, O2, O14: because predicted anoxia rises steeply with diameter and ~20% of islets by number (>200 um) carry ~72% of volume, an SC-islet cluster-size cap or size-sort could be tested as an oxygenation lever. The cheatsheet states no cluster-diameter limit; the source is a model of human alloislets with no SC-islet or device data, so this is speculative.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic suicide switch escape; <1e-6 escape threshold at Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: HSVtk iPSCs with GCV still formed teratomas at 8 of 10 and 9 of 10 sites by week 8 after none at week 5 (O4, O5), and 6 of 11 clones had resistant colonies, with nonsense mutations and preexisting inactivating mutations (O8-O10), qualifying any assumption that a single suicide switch reaches a very low escape frequency; the switch is HSVtk delivered by lentivirus, not iCasp9 at a safe harbor, so transfer to the Blueprint design is by mechanistic analogy only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (suicide switch redundancy and pre-transplant detection of resistance mutations)
edges.claim_summary: Because resistance mutations preexisted in rare cells and were selected by GCV (O10, O9), the authors argue in the Discussion for deep-sequencing detection and for redundant kill or purge approaches; this suggests testing a second independent elimination layer beside iCasp9, a proposal drawn from the Discussion rather than tested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of multiplex-edited hPSC-derived product; genomic-integrity release assays)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O5, O6, O8, O12, O16: karyotyping, qPCR, ddPCR and FISH on hPSC mixing models missed variants below roughly 5% to 10% (1% undetected at 100 metaphases; >500 metaphases needed for <1%), so a normal genomic-integrity result qualifies only down to that assay limit. The cheatsheet states multiplex genomic integrity but not culture-aneuploidy detection limits; the data are from hPSC lines, not edited SC-islet lots, and carry-over to derivatives is the bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (rapid recurrent-gain screen for 1q, 12, 17q, 20q11.21 in hPSC seed lines)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O9, O13, O14, O15, O17: add a qPCR copy-number panel on recurrent gains as a rapid screen, with 1,000-cell FISH as confirmation, for edited hPSC clones and seed banks. The panel matched karyotyping and FISH and caught 20q gains in four G-band-normal lines, but would cover about 45% of reported changes (O18) and was not tested on edited or islet-fate cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive memory and recurrent autoimmunity after islet transplant)
edges.claim_summary: In islet allograft recipients, HLA-A*24 carriage or an early autoantibody surge was associated with worse graft function (O1-O4), consistent with Gate2B treating autoreactive memory as a failure mode. The cohort is primary-islet allograft recipients, not hPSC-derived grafts, and the abstract does not separate autoimmune from alloimmune mechanisms; the HLA-A*24 association itself is not stated in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical C-peptide and insulin-independence benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: Insulin independence of 16% versus 68% and C-peptide positivity of 47% versus 100% by risk group (O1, O2) give clinical islet-allograft outcome benchmarks of the kind M4 tracks. The patients received primary islets under their own immunosuppression, so transfer to an hPSC-derived graft is a bridge only; whether the Blueprint uses these figures cannot be settled from the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet cluster size selection and architecture-preserving manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O1, O5, O9, O18: in syngeneic mouse islets smaller islets engrafted better at equal IEq (marginal mass 75% vs 10% for large) while fragmentation lowered reversal (14% vs 24% naive medium and large) and mild over-digestion raised it (57% vs 36%), so SC-islet cluster size could be controlled as a manufacturing variable without disrupting architecture. The cheatsheet states no size cutoff; mouse primary islets are not hPSC-derived clusters, so this is untested for SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (early engraftment before revascularization; size-dependent graft loss)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O5, O7: engraftment fell as islet size rose in all three masses, consistent with a size-dependent early-graft loss that the Gate5 oxygen-bridge and vascularization logic would predict. Oxygen, diffusion and vascularization were not measured here; the mechanism appears only in the Discussion, and the model is syngeneic mouse islets under the kidney capsule.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: O15: CXCL10 and other type I IFN pathway genes were significantly induced in human islet grafts after CVB4 infection, supporting CXCL10 as an activated stress-responsive locus in human islet cells in vivo. Fold changes are plotted only; primary human islets in immunodeficient mice, with no CXCL10-promoter reporter or SC-islet data, and the cheatsheet states the CXCL10-inducible design but not viral induction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (TXNIP and ER stress axis; PDX1 maintenance)
edges.claim_summary: O16, O17, O8: CVB4 infection of human islet grafts raised TXNIP (moderate) and DDIT3/CHOP and lowered PDX1 expression, consistent with TXNIP and ER stress as a stress-resilience target. The cheatsheet lists TXNIP for Gate4 but not this viral-stress evidence; magnitudes are plotted only and the cells are mature primary islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (direct viral beta-cell dysfunction independent of immune evasion edits)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O6, O8, O10, O13: in mice lacking T, B and NK cells, CVB4-infected human islet grafts lost INS and PDX1 expression and some mice became diabetic with no inflammatory infiltrate, indicating direct viral beta-cell dysfunction that HLA or NK-evasion edits do not address. The cheatsheet states no viral-resilience element; only mature primary islets were tested, so SC-islet susceptibility is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (β-cell-intrinsic cytokine and stress response; type I IFN / Tyk2 signalling)
edges.claim_summary: Mouse EMC-D experiments show that Tyk2 loss or natural downregulation can impair β-cell IFN-dependent antiviral protection (O1, O2, O9, O10, O12, O16), qualifying transfer of TYK2 attenuation as intrinsic cytoprotection. Frozen ranker DEC-053 already preserves TYK2-WT in lead candidates and requires Gate 0V for optional P1104A satellites; exact incorporation of this mouse-specific boundary into the Blueprint is not established. Complete KO/natural mouse mutations do not establish the response of human SC-islets or human P1104A variants.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (β-cell-restricted gene expression as cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: β-cell-restricted MIP-Tyk2 expression maintained normal glycaemia in KO mice (O4) and restored resistance in Tyk2-mutant mice (O13), providing a rodent principle-level precedent for β-cell-intrinsic antiviral protection. It does not test the OpenIslet constructs, hypoxia protection, clinical benefit or qualification of a human SC-islet TYK2 edit; adoption of the specific MIP-Tyk2 rescue precedent is unknown.

edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O5, O6, O1, O2: test CHOP or JNK suppression as an additional intrinsic cytoprotection module in SC-islets, and screen stress-resilience edits in human rather than rat beta cells because NO-dependent ER stress occurred in rat islets but not mouse or human islets. Neither CHOP nor JNK appears in the cheatsheet Gate4 list; SC-islets and any edit were untested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (BCL2 and XIAP intrinsic anti-apoptotic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: BCL-2 overexpression, BAX/BAK deficiency, BH3-only loss and RIPK3 loss, alone or combined, did not protect mouse islet grafts from CD4+ T cell-mediated destruction (O1, O2, O5, O6), so the cheatsheet's BCL2/XIAP element should not be assumed to protect against autoreactive T cell attack. The result is for T cell killing in mouse islets, not for hypoxia or cytokine stress where Gate4 uses these genes, and the bridge to hPSC-derived islets rests on conserved cell-death machinery.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune effector pressure including FAS)
edges.claim_summary: Fas or FADD loss in islets was not protective and dying beta cells showed necrosis features (O3, O4), qualifying FAS as a necessary effector in CD4+ T cell-mediated beta cell killing in this mouse model. The cheatsheet lists granzyme/FAS effector pressure under Gate2B; this abstract does not test granzyme pathways or CD8+ T cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (long-term β-cell stress failure mode: islet amyloid polypeptide aggregation)
edges.claim_summary: Two failed whole pancreas grafts kept α and β cells but accumulated prominent islet amyloid (O2), and the authors propose amyloid as a candidate late failure mechanism (O3). The proposal for Islet-1 is to add IAPP amyloid accumulation as a long-term durability readout and failure mode, since β cells make IAPP; the cheatsheet states no amyloid element, and two human whole-organ cases are far from hPSC-derived islet grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: In both patients, graft failure occurred with preserved C-peptide levels (O1), so in these two cases C-peptide positivity did not guarantee a functioning graft; C-peptide benchmarks should be read together with glycaemic outcomes. This is a two-patient whole pancreas report and the cheatsheet does not state how the Blueprint treats C-peptide-positive graft failure.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M4 (clinical benchmarks for macro-encapsulated islet devices)
edges.claim_summary: The registry record (O1-O4) documents a Phase 1/2 pilot of macro-encapsulated human islets in a bioartificial pancreas device with a 365-day device-safety primary outcome and an enrollment of 4.0. It adds a trial-landscape entry only: no efficacy, oxygenation or graft-survival results are posted, and the islets are human islets rather than hPSC-derived cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (small-cluster geometry and prevascular oxygen bridge)
edges.claim_summary: The observational association of smaller ISI/more IPs per kg with better 6-month autotransplant outcomes (O2–O5, O12–O14) is directionally consistent with the small-cluster diffusion rationale already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate5 (≤120 μm) and §4.5 single-sphere Krogh physics; the ranker also encodes that geometry. This incorporation label covers the existing directional rationale, not adoption of this study’s coefficients/cutpoints. Oxygen causality was speculative, not measured; intraportal autologous primary islets do not qualify the engineered SC-islet product or establish its 72-hour window.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical dose metrics and insulin-use benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: Within this marginal-dose TP-IAT cohort, daily insulin-use correlations were ρ=−0.50 for IPs/kg, ρ=0.51 for ISI and ρ=−0.08 for IEs/kg (O4); 8/58 were independent (O1), and O6–O8 give in-cohort prediction performance. Frozen Blueprint §4.5 uses IEQ volume/cell conversion and explicitly bounded dose/area, while the frozen ranker specifies viable beta-cell covariates and size-controlled spheroids. Those positive provisions do not establish incorporation of this exact clinical IP/ISI finding. Retrospective outcome-defined cohorts and incompletely specified insulin-data n limit transfer; the native HbA1C row’s assay timing is not explicit (O11).

edges.claim_summary: In HLA-intact hESC derivatives challenged by a human allogeneic immune system, PD-L1 alone did not prevent rejection while CTLA4-Ig plus PD-L1 did (O8, O2, O4), so PD-L1's contribution to Gate2A should be judged in a B2M/CIITA-ablated context rather than as a stand-alone shield. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (local co-stimulation blockade added to the PD-L1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: Co-expressing secreted CTLA4-Ig with PD-L1 gave rejection protection lasting up to three months in Hu-mice for several cell types (O2, O5, O6, O7), and CP cells protected co-grafted parental cells locally (O9). edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual undifferentiated cell tumorigenicity versus differentiated product)
edges.claim_summary: Undifferentiated autologous RhiPSCs formed teratomas in macaques only at the higher doses (4/10 at 1×107 per site versus 0 of the 5, 5 and 1 sites at 5×105, 2×106 and 5×106) and these persisted to at least 30 weeks, whereas RhiPSC-SC implants showed no teratoma at 27-39 weeks (O2, O4, O8, O9). This supports keeping a clonogenic fail-safe and purification step for Gate5; the data are subcutaneous rhesus iPSC grafts, and the cheatsheet states no dose-response for residual pluripotent cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 with M1 (teratoma safety testing under immune cloaking)
edges.claim_summary: Teratoma formation was less efficient in immunocompetent autologous macaques than in NSG mice (7/25 versus 9/9, p=0.0002; authors estimate at least 20 fold per cell) and masses carried a lymphoid infiltrate absent in NSG (O1, O3, O6). The hypothesis is that an immune-cloaked allogeneic graft loses this restraint, so residual-cell escape and suicide-switch thresholds should be tested in cloaked grafts in a human-immune-system or immune-deficient host; the link between infiltrate and reduced teratoma growth is correlational and the grafts were not cloaked.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M3 (durability and transfer limits of graft cytoprotection and transgene expression)

The cheatsheet Gate3 receptor list (NKG2A, NKG2C, KIR2DL1/2/3, DNAM-1/PVR, CD54/CD58) does not include KIR2DL4, so adding it to the NK panel is a hypothesis only, from a rat-cell-line, abstract-only source.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (oxygen diffusion gradients in large constructs)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O6: in 3D constructs PDMS-CaO2 prevented detrimental oxygen gradients, and mathematical simulations were reported to predict the oxygen gradients accurately. These are qualitative abstract statements with no error metric or construct geometry given.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 / M7 (functional graft perfusion and scope of the 72-hour oxygen bridge)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O4/O7/O11 show severe hypoperfusion (5% of native, approximately 0.2 mL per min per g islet tissue), low vascular density (24% of native) and low donor vascular contribution at 1 month in primary murine intraportal grafts. O3 versus O8, measured in separate assay cohorts, also separates a source-reported six-fold perfusion difference from a nonsignificant 70% vascular-density difference. These observations qualify reliance on structural vessel density as evidence of functional perfusion; they do not measure graft pO2 or establish the sufficiency/failure of the Blueprint 72-hour PDMS-CaO2 bridge, its prevascularized site, or edited iMVFs. The actual Blueprint §1.2/§4 and iMVF paragraph already require a 72-hour bridge plus patency/inosculation qualification, but incorporation of this specific month-long intraportal boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (controlled matrix remodeling hypothesis for graft vascularization)
edges.claim_summary: O9/O10 support an integrity/revascularization association and a pretransplant-fragment comparison; O13/O14 show approximately doubled MMP-9/VEGF-A release in separate acute in vitro assays. O18/O21 show increased insulin release interpreted by the authors as leakage and lower preparation purity; O19 insulin-positive composition does not establish preserved secretion. Controlled matrix remodeling that preserves regulated secretion is therefore a hypothesis for SC-islet testing, not a demonstrated causal mechanism or a recommendation to fragment the Blueprint product. The Blueprint specifies small reaggregated clusters, Laminin-511 E8 and pre-lumenized iMVFs (§2/§4), but adoption of this specific integrity/MMP-9 strategy is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition within Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: In NOD mice, effector-side granzyme B deficiency did not prevent spontaneous diabetes or transferred diabetes, and granzyme B-deficient IGRP-specific CTL retained islet killing in vitro (O3, O5, O6); these reported null comparisons do not establish equivalence. This bounds any claim that inhibiting granzyme B alone must protect beta cells. The frozen blueprint places the Locus 3 SERPINB9/PD-L1 candidate at Gate2B/Gate4, but incorporation of this particular limitation is unverified. Mouse effector-side knockout is an unvalidated transfer to target-side SERPINB9 in human engineered islets and does not qualify the product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (timing of autoreactive CD8+ T cell effector pressure)
edges.claim_summary: Granzyme B deficiency showed model- and age-dependent findings: reduced insulitis at 70 days in NOD that was not maintained at 100/150 days (O1, O2), impaired early islet homing (O10), and delayed diabetes onset in CD8-dependent NOD8.3 mice (O4). In the separate 50-day NOD8.3 insulitis cohort no significant difference was reported (O13), which neither proves equivalence nor explains the onset delay. These findings bound granzyme-targeted protection claims; transfer to target-side inhibition in human islets is unvalidated and outcome-specific blueprint incorporation is unknown.

edges.claim_summary: O1, O8, O9 and O10: IGRP-specific CD8 cells are found in T1D but not healthy PBMC, and the clone infiltrated islets (10/49 vs 0/20, p = 0.013) and was linked to islet disruption and cCaspase-3 positivity within 4 weeks, despite low avidity (O5) and no blood-glucose change (O11). Murine HHD islets and a single clone from one donor; no cytoprotective or cloaking edit was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablation of classical HLA class I)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O7 and O9: class I HLA sensitization is frequent in multi-donor allogeneic islet recipients (cumulative incidence of PRA >=20% 33% at 6 years under immunosuppression) and PRA >=20% after transplant carries HR=3.6 for graft failure, supporting the rationale for removing HLA class I. Recipients got HLA-mismatched primary islets from several donors, not a single HLA-null hPSC line, and PRA was class I only (class II data incomplete in the registry).

edges.target_gate_or_module: M4 (clinical benchmarks; HLA antibody surveillance alongside C-peptide and CGM TIR)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: O7 (HR=3.6), O10 (higher PRA >=20% after graft loss off immunosuppression) and O8 (baseline PRA not predictive of failure) suggest tracking post-transplant HLA class I antibodies as a clinical benchmark next to the stimulated C-peptide and CGM TIR benchmarks in the cheatsheet. The data are registry associations in primary-islet recipients, not hPSC-islet trials, and donor-specific antibody data were not available.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide and hypoglycemia clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O5: all four patients had positive basal and stimulated C-peptide after undetectable baseline (patient 4 postmeal 1.10 at 3 months, 0.76 at 36 months) and severe hypoglycemia events/week fell to 0, while insulin independence was only transient (O3). A small encapsulated-islet clinical benchmark, not an SC-islet trial.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 (macro- or micro-encapsulation exchange and site limits)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O7 and O9: benefit was partial and transient (BG drifted up after 24 months; all patients back on original insulin regimens at 7 years; ectopic capsules held no viable islets), and the authors attribute the limits to capsule size relative to transplant site and functional exchange, not to oxygen measurements. This qualifies reliance on an encapsulation-type bridge for years rather than the 72-hour Gate5 target; oxygen was not measured.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 suicide switch)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3, O5 and O6: iCasp9-modified human T cells expanded despite constitutive expression, and a single AP1903 dose removed more than 90% of circulating modified cells within 30 minutes (2 log by PCR) and ended GVHD without recurrence in four patients. This is clinical proof of the iCasp9/AP1903 mechanism, but in retrovirally transduced polyclonal T cells, not a safe-harbor iCasp9 hPSC-islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M5 (iCasp9 escape threshold <1e-6 at AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O8, O7 and O11: after one dose a small transduced population remained and re-expanded, re-exposure killed approximately 85% in vitro, and only 90 to 93% of the infused product carried the switch, so this clinical dataset sits at roughly 1 to 2 log of depletion and neither tests nor supports a <1e-6 escape threshold. The cheatsheet states that threshold for AAVS1-insulated iCasp9; the T-cell system differs (multi-copy retroviral vector, variable expression).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (b) / M4 (switch and dimerizer safety benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10 and O12: AP1903 at 0.4 mg/kg over 2 hours had no noted adverse effects or effect on non-transduced T cells, and no destructive immune reactivity to the transgenic cells was found over more than 1 year, giving a human safety benchmark for the dimerizer and the human-derived switch. Five pediatric haploidentical transplant patients; supplementary tables are not in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual clonogenic/oncology hazard after purification)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O4 show that SSEA-5 depletion alone can leave teratoma-forming populations in generic hESC assays. This supports the existing broad premise that purification does not replace independent residual-clonogenic safety control: frozen Blueprint section 7.1-3 retains post-purge residual burden and a separately qualified pan-lineage iCasp9 fail-safe; ranker 5948-5960 already combines anti-SSEA-5/TRA-1-60 and YM155 purges; Graveyard_002 rejects lineage-restricted switches. Incorporation applies to that safety premise, not these exact fractions. The study tests no iCasp9 construct or quantitative escape bound, and O5/O7 starred small growths do not establish confirmed residual teratomas.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hypothesized transfer to SC-islet residual-PSC purification, not a measured M2 endpoint)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O7/O10 motivate testing whether the exact SSEA-5/CD9/CD90 or SSEA-5/CD30/CD200 selection strategy improves residual-PSC removal during SC-islet manufacture while preserving endocrine recovery and function. These generic RA-differentiated hESC tumor assays do not validate that transfer or complete clonogenic clearance. Frozen Blueprint section 6.4 already specifies CD49a/NTPDase3/CD9-based endocrine sorting and section 7 a residual-PSC purge; ranker 5951-5955 already includes anti-SSEA-5/TRA-1-60 plus YM155. Generic marker depletion is therefore not a new missing element; incorporation of these exact triple-marker proposals is not established by the bounded source review.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O5: in human MSCs, PI-9 (SERPINB9) is a major defense against granzyme B-mediated destruction, siRNA knockdown increased cell death and transgenic expression protected cells, in line with the SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition element already in the Blueprint. Human MSCs in vitro, not SC-islets; the abstract gives no quantitative data.

Whether hPSC-derived beta cells form such amyloid is not addressed in this abstract, so IAPP amyloid readouts in SC-islet grafts would be a proposal, not an established gap.

edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2: human islets failed in streptozotocin-diabetic immune-deficient mice with amyloid at 4 and 8 weeks while porcine islets stayed normoglycemic for up to 195 days, so graft loss in immunodeficient hosts can have a non-immune, amyloid component. This qualifies attributing graft loss differences to immune cloaking alone; primary human islets, not SC-islets, and animal numbers are not stated.

edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: the cotransplant assay (unrelated-donor human islets plus sorted GAD-autoreactive CD4 T-cells under the kidney capsule of athymic mice; beta/alpha ratio 0.6 and 0.7 vs control ratios of 1.0 to 2.0, O11 to O13) could test whether CIITA-null or SERPINB9/PD-L1-protected islets resist autoreactive CD4 attack. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks; humanized-mouse validation platform)
edges.claim_summary: In this Balb/c Rag2gc CD34+ HIS model, human T cells were alloreactive to allogeneic human dendritic cells (O1) yet did not reject a human islet allograft, with few T cells reaching the graft (O2, O3). This qualifies the use of such HIS mice as a rejection-competent platform for testing Gate2A evasion; it is primary human islets rather than hPSC-derived islets, and the abstract gives no quantitative data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (microencapsulated graft necrosis and fibrotic encapsulation; oxygen-bridge scoping)
edges.claim_summary: The 16-month biopsy from one four-infusion recipient showed necrotic islets inside intact capsules surrounded by fibrous tissue with few blood vessels (O5), alongside early loss of urinary C-peptide (O2) and undetectable day-7 plasma C-peptide (O9). This is a clinical warning about the viability of primary cadaveric human islets in this intraperitoneal barium-alginate system, not evidence that necrosis was central, that ischemia rather than inflammation caused it, or that a 72-hour oxygen intervention or the Blueprint product was tested. Blueprint §1.2/§4.5 and ranker macrodevice penalties already address broad avascular-device hazards; incorporation of this exact microcapsule finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B (post-infusion cytotoxic-antibody and GAD-autoantibody readouts)

The cytotoxic-antibody assay is relevant to Gate2A humoral risk, but antigen/HLA and donor specificity are not specified; GAD antibodies supply a Gate2B humoral readout, without measured autoreactive T-cell or indirect-APC activity. These uncontrolled observations do not demonstrate that antigen shedding, capsule pore transit or any specific immune mechanism caused sensitization or graft loss. Blueprint §1.2 and GRAVEYARD_010 recognize humoral/indirect-pathway risks in different edited-product contexts; this exact unedited-microcapsule finding has unknown incorporation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe; tolerance for residual undifferentiated cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5, O10-O14: in SCID beige mice a minimum of 1 x 10^5 hESCs in the myocardium (2 of 7 at 1 x 10^5; 0 of 7 at 1 x 10^4) and 1 x 10^4 in skeletal muscle with Matrigel (5 of 7) formed teratomas, giving empirical dose thresholds for residual pluripotent cells that support a residual-cell fail-safe. Mouse xenograft model; whether the Blueprint already conditions its threshold this way cannot be settled from the cheatsheet.

The data are mouse islets in rodent hosts, not hPSC-derived islets, and STAT-1 is not named in the cheatsheet's Gate4 element list.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CIITA KO contribution within the B2M + CIITA stack)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O6: class II-null islets were rejected at rates comparable with wild-type, so in this NOD recurrence model protection tracked with class I loss and CIITA KO alone did not delay failure; this qualifies how much of the Gate2A/2B benefit can be attributed to CIITA. No B2m-only arm result is reported in the abstract, so class I alone is untested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (avascular oxygen bridge window; revascularization timeline)
edges.claim_summary: In one primate, intraportal allogeneic islets showed no capillary formation 5 d after transplant (O1) but an abundant capillary supply at 30 and 90 d (O2), while the primates stayed insulin independent (O5). This qualifies the oxygen-bridge window: the avascular period was at least 5 d in this animal (longer than 72 h), but intraportal liver blood contact differs from a device graft, so the data do not test a PDMS-CaO2 bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant islet loss; intraportal blood-contact injury)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 show that primary human islets (endocrine cells) produce active TF and that coagulation activation with insulin release follows clinical intraportal transplantation, supporting the premise of substantial acute peri-transplant graft damage. Primary islets in an intraportal site are not an hPSC-derived islet graft, so transfer to SC-islets is bridged only by shared endocrine-cell identity.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TF-driven thrombotic injury as a cytoprotection target; TF check on SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 show in vitro abrogation of islet-triggered clotting by TF blockade and propose it as a therapy; the cheatsheet lists no coagulation/TF element in Gate3 or Gate4. Hypothesis: test TF expression and TF-dependent clotting on SC-islets and consider TF blockade or knockdown in the peri-transplant protection package (SC-islet TF status is untested here).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; PDMS-CaO2 bridge scope)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 show graft PO2 of approximately 5 mmHg vs approximately 40 mmHg in native islets at 9-12 weeks, at all three sites, i.e. after revascularization. This qualifies the Gate5 framing of an acute-phase primary avascular oxygen bridge (a short-duration target in the cheatsheet): the data indicate hypoxia persists in revascularized rat islet grafts, so a bridge alone may not secure long-term oxygenation. Rat primary islets are bridged to hPSC-islets only through shared diffusion/perfusion physics.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (intrinsic hypoxia resilience; hypoxic conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O4 indicate that revascularized grafts with similar perfusion across sites remain markedly hypoxic (lower still in diabetic recipients), supporting the need for intrinsic beta-cell hypoxia resilience in Gate4. The cheatsheet states hypoxic conditioning generally but not these PO2 values, hence the specific numbers are tagged not yet accounted for.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (B2M KO, Locus 1/2; recurrent T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O4 show that MHC class I-deficient NOD islets survived indefinitely in diabetic NOD recipients with a nondestructive infiltrate, supporting B2M loss as protection against autoreactive CD8-mediated destruction. Mouse NOD islets are bridged to human SC-islets only through conserved MHC class I recognition; the cheatsheet does not state this autoimmune-specific benefit of B2M KO.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (ligand-expression strategies for allo-T-cell evasion, e.g. inducible PD-L1 and allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3: transgenic beta-cell CD95L failed to protect murine fetal pancreas allografts from rejection, qualifying the assumption that expressing an immune-inhibitory or apoptosis-inducing ligand is by itself protective; it is a different molecule from PD-L1, in mouse fetal tissue, with no n or rates in the abstract, so transfer to the Blueprint stack is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate infiltrate beyond NK and macrophage scope)
edges.claim_summary: O2: a beta-cell transgene (CD95L) drove granulocytic infiltration in transgenic mouse pancreata, an innate cell type outside the NK and macrophage scope the cheatsheet lists for Gate3, suggesting granulocyte infiltration be monitored when adding immunomodulatory ligands. Single abstract sentence in mice, no counts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (recurrent T1D autoimmunity; GAD65-directed autoreactivity)
edges.claim_summary: O1 to O3 show in 23 islet-grafted IDDM patients that graft survival differed significantly by islet cell and/or GAD65 autoantibody status (P < 0.05), supporting recurrent autoimmunity as a graft-loss route despite immunosuppression. Gate2B already lists recurrent T1D autoimmunity and GAD65 autoreactivity as its scope; the grafts here are primary allogeneic islets, not hPSC-derived.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M4 / Gate2B (autoantibody status as a clinical stratifier or monitor)
edges.claim_summary: O1 associates ICA/GAD65 positivity with earlier failure and O4 gives C-peptide failure definitions. A trial-specific hypothesis is to stratify/monitor hPSC-islet recipients using baseline and post-transplant autoantibodies. The full frozen Blueprint already mentions baseline autoantibody stratification in its Stage 5 long-horizon recipient axes; this does not establish implementation in a lead trial or adoption of ICA-specific/post-transplant monitoring. The source is a small retrospective cohort and does not test monitoring utility.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (host vascular ingrowth and islet-type endothelium during revascularization)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: in free hamster and rat islet grafts, new microvessels grow from the host muscle vascular bed, rat islets are revascularized by host-origin (hamster) endothelium, and the lining shows islet-typical diaphragmatic fenestration, supporting host-vessel ingrowth as the route by which an oxygen-bridged graft becomes vascularized. Rodent free islets, no timing or perfusion data in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (where direct allorecognition must be blocked in a revascularized graft)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O4: host-origin endothelium lining revascularized rat islet xenografts suggests donor graft endothelium need not be the recognition target in free islet grafts, narrowing where direct allorecognition evasion (the B2M and CIITA edits) must act to donor endocrine and passenger cells. This is the authors' suggestion from rodent histology with no rejection data, and prevascularized or device-grown vessels may differ.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 / M7 (species-specific stress resilience and antioxidant association)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O7, O4/O5/O10 and O9 show species differences in hsp70, catalase/SOD activity and peroxide-associated reduced-glutathione depletion; O2/O3 report human-versus-rat differences in streptozotocin apoptosis and peroxide glucose oxidation. These primary-human-islet observations qualify rodent-to-human transfer for the intrinsic stress scope of Blueprint section 1.2 Gate4. They do not test SC-islets, causal antioxidant engineering, an hsp70 protective mechanism, or SOD2 specifically; the reported SOD activity is not isoform resolved.

The cheatsheet names macro- or micro-encapsulation slab physics but not this clinical viability figure; the cells were primary islets and the observation window was only 2 weeks.

It therefore bounds, rather than validates, any transfer to a genetically cloaked non-encapsulated hPSC-islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M3 (macrophage-associated foreign body response and encapsulated graft niche)
edges.claim_summary: In healthy T5 mice, locally secreting RPE-IL10 helper capsules limited fibrotic overgrowth at 1 month and showed partial deposition in 1/6 and 2/6 mice at 3 and 6 months (O1/O2). This suggests testing compartmental helper-cell delivery for an encapsulated SC-islet niche, but it does not establish Hour-0 human macrophage/NK protection, protection of the materialized Blueprint graft, or absence of systemic immune effects; IL-12 had inflammatory transcriptional effects and diabetic-mouse ascites (O7/O10/O19/O21). Claim-specific adoption of this helper-cell architecture is not established by the frozen sources.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (in vivo graft-function evidence and transfer domain)
edges.claim_summary: Encapsulated primary human islets with RPE-IL10 helper capsules maintained reported glycemic correction up to 100 days in immunocompetent STZ mice (T5; O8/O16), with higher serum human C-peptide (O9). The NHP pilot had one animal per arm, no islets, transient systemic IL-10 and local IL-10 detection at 1 month (O11/O12); its peripheral immune-cell change (O24) and unlabelled safety tables cannot qualify NHP islet efficacy, graft fibrosis prevention or long-term immune safety. Transfer to edited hPSC-derived islets remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 / GRAVEYARD_008 / CYTO_CONSTITUTIVE_IL10_VIRAL_OE (scope of the constitutive-IL10 exclusion)
edges.claim_summary: Frozen Blueprint §5, Graveyard_008 and ranker module/block explicitly exclude unbuffered constitutive viral IL10 in allogeneic islets as a conservative policy under mechanistic uncertainty; the ranker description also asserts failure of durable alloprotection. Here PiggyBac-engineered encapsulated RPE helper cells with separate primary human islet capsules showed mouse graft benefit and local monocyte cross-presentation signature suppression (O5/O8), qualifying any universal claim that constitutive secreted IL10 cannot help. The helper-cell/dose/compartment architecture differs from the blocked module; no functional human indirect-APC/T1D challenge, intrinsic SC-islet stress assay, or infection/tumor-immunity challenge supports overturning the policy or changing its scores.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (pre-transplant potency and maturation readout for beta-cell products)
edges.claim_summary: NKX6.1 copy number correlated with mouse-bioassay graft function (O1, P < 0.01) and its in vitro silencing or induction was reported to indicate a causal link to graft function (O6). Hypothesis for Islet-1: digital-PCR NKX6.1 copy number could serve as a lot-release potency readout for SC-islet batches; this was measured in donor islet preparations, not SC-islets, and the cheatsheet lists no NKX6.1 criterion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 suicide switch, Locus 4)
edges.claim_summary: An iCasp9 safety switch carried in a piggyBac-integrated transgene was activated in 24% (n = 8) of 33 treated patients, with symptom resolution in seven (O3), giving human in vivo precedent that the iCasp9 module can be triggered clinically. The cells are autologous CAR T cells treated for toxicity, not hPSC-derived islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 as clonogenic fail-safe, escape threshold < 1e-6)
edges.claim_summary: In O3 the switch was used to rescue acute toxicity of activated CAR T cells, and one activation case was ultimately fatal, so this clinical precedent shows usability but not rescue in every case. It does not test clonogenic-escape elimination or the < 1e-6 threshold the cheatsheet lists, and the abstract gives no ablation kinetics.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (context-dependent iCasp9 fail-safe potency; Locus 4 AAVS1; conditional per-clonogenic-cell escape target <=1e-8)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 support the bounded requirement to test iCasp9 potency in relevant pro-survival and proliferative states rather than assume uniform elimination. That generic boundary is already explicit in frozen Blueprint sections 4.4/7 and ranker hazard-state stress/clonogenic gates; this value does not assert incorporation of the specific hTERT NK-cell findings. The study measures 24 h AP20187/DMSO-normalized live-cell reduction in retrovirally engineered primary human NK cells, not AP1903 clonogenic escape for the biallelic AAVS1 islet product. It neither quantifies nor directly contradicts the conditional <=1e-8 target.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (hTERT/DN-hTERT-associated resistance, BIRC3 and splicing/cell-cycle transcript signatures)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O13 identify associated transcript/splicing changes; O7 reports no detectable rescue by shBIRC3, without equivalence bounds or reported knockdown efficiency. A bounded candidate extension is to stratify existing hazard-state kill tests by hTERT state and profile iCASP9/BIRC3 transcripts and splice patterns in survivors, without selecting a causal target or adopting a construct change. Generic stress and Ki67+/SOX2+/OCT4+/SLC18A1+ testing is already present in the ranker, but incorporation of this specific hTERT/BIRC3/splicing extension is not established by the frozen references. Transfer to hPSC-derived islets and AP1903 at AAVS1 remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (orthogonal clone-level genomic QC after nuclease editing)
edges.claim_summary: O1 supports the need for clone-level genomic characterization beyond conventional PCR after nuclease editing. That broad safety principle is already addressed by the frozen Blueprint Stage-4 long-read/flanking-LOH and CAST-Seq QC requirements; the specific STAG2-clone inversions, plasmid integrations and rearrangements are abstract-only findings, and this packet does not establish whether those existing assays would detect every reported event or quantify risk in the Islet-1 workflow.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (candidate capture-based sequencing complement to existing edited-clone QC)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3 motivate evaluating hybridization capture-based targeted sequencing as a possible complement to the Blueprint's existing long-read, LOH-phasing and CAST-Seq workflow. The abstract reports revised interpretations in selected STAG2-duplication iPSC clones, not superiority over the existing Blueprint QC panel, performance at Islet-1 multiplex loci, or evidence for mandatory sequencing of every cut site; incorporation of this specific capture workflow is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (base-editor-specific genomic off-target assessment; distinct from GRAVEYARD_006 structural-variant and nickase-complexity precaution)
edges.claim_summary: The T-cell comparison found 83 ABE8e off-target sites versus one Cas9 site (O2; O1 reports 98.8% unique to ABE8e), with high on-target activity (O6); CBE CIITA OT-1 reached 17% (O5) and CHANGE-seq-BE found cellular 1.7-7.5% CBE sites missed by Digenome-seq (O12). This supports a method-level requirement to evaluate the actual base editor rather than substitute nuclease nomination. Frozen Blueprint section 5/GY006 and ranker gamma_B address precautionary structural risk, not a validated mapping of these base-substitution rates to hPSC risk or gamma_B. CHANGE-seq-BE is Cas-dependent and does not detect Cas-independent off-targets (packet Discussion); these data do not qualify Islet-1 guides or quantify simultaneous multiplex hPSC risk. Specific incorporation is not established by the frozen sources.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (synthetic gRNA lot identity and cross-contamination as a genomic manufacturing failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: Supplier-A batch-1 CBLB/CIITA gRNAs contained 0.09-2.71% contaminating gRNA reads (O8), associated with 0.83-5.24% unintended on-target ABE8e edits in T cells (O9). The source calls shared-column sequential HPLC the most likely cause and reports mitigation in a later batch, without assigning a quantitative mitigation effect. A bounded Islet-1 hypothesis is to evaluate guide-lot identity/cross-contamination sequencing before hPSC editing; efficacy, limits and relevance to the actual AsCas12a/HiFi-SpCas9 or base-editor process require product-specific testing. Existing GY006 structural QC and the ranker complexity discount do not establish whether this specific guide-lot assay is incorporated; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex-editing genomic safety assessment)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 show a draft regulatory guidance on NGS-based safety assessment of genome-edited human gene therapy products exists, consistent with the Blueprint's requirement for genomic integrity of multiplex-edited cells in Gate5. The packet has no methods, thresholds or islet-specific content, and the cheatsheet does not state whether the Blueprint cites this guidance.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (multigene PD-L1-containing cassette design, e.g. Locus 3 SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: O1 is a title-only statement that multigene IDO1/PD-L1 cassette architecture matters in human skin cells; no measured result, cassette feature or direction is in the packet, so it cannot support, qualify or contradict the Blueprint cassette design. Flag for full-text retrieval.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 safe harbor; promoter silencing of the inserted cassette)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3 and the qPCR-only decitabine response in O4 support the general AAVS1 exogenous-promoter silencing risk already explicitly incorporated in frozen Blueprint §4.4/§7 and ranker Shared_Promoter_Epigenetic_CpG_Methylation. The specific TRE3G BI percentages are additional context, not a measured iCasp9 escape rate; promoter, payload, insulation and lineage differ from the proposed biallelic 230-bp EEF1A1/HNRNPA2B1-proximal-candidate iCasp9 cassette. O4 does not establish protein restoration.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (EEF1A1-type promoter choice for iCasp9 at AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O7 and O12 show clone-variable methylation of the assayed EF1α region and CoGFP expression despite high methylation in HEK293T. The tested reporter uses an EF1α-core/truncated HTLV-1 5′LTR composite at PiggyBac integration sites; neither the Blueprint 230-bp native EEF1A1 core nor its proposed insulation at AAVS1 is tested. These findings scope transfer of promoter-class claims without proving failure or protection of the exact cassette; incorporation of these specific composite-promoter results is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (clone release criteria for an iCasp9 cassette: functional readout, not methylation alone)
edges.claim_summary: O8 with O5/O7 shows that methylation of the assayed CMV CpGs alone did not predict target protein detection; O10/O11 show persistent high methylation and protein non-detection in two neural derivatives. This provides an unvalidated-transfer rationale for the functional post-differentiation AP1903/clonogenic testing plus bisulfite QC already specified in frozen Blueprint §7 and ranker lines 4974-4977/5056-5058, rather than a newly missing release assay. No endocrine-lineage iCasp9/dimerizer experiment was performed.

edges.claim_summary: HLA-E single-chain trimer (SP-1C peptide) protected MHC-I-deficient K562 and CAR T cells from NKG2A+ NK cells but not from NKG2A-C+ cells (O1, O4, O6, O7, O5), consistent with the Blueprint's stated NKG2A-engagement boundary; tested in K562 and T cells, not islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M4 (clinical benchmark for HLA-I-deficient allogeneic cell product with NK-evasion armor)
edges.claim_summary: In 5 patients an HLA-I-deficient allogeneic CAR T product with NKG2A CAR armor showed no dose-limiting toxicities or GVHD (O1), 3 confirmed responses including 2 sCR (O2), and responses lasting 20 months to >23 months (O3); a hematologic CAR T setting, not an islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: Human CD47 on pig cells improved survival against human macrophages in HIS mice, with more benefit against human than murine macrophages (O1, O4, O13), supporting the CD47-SIRPalpha element of Locus 1; target cells are xenogeneic pig splenocytes and marrow, not islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 as sole macrophage-evasion element)
edges.claim_summary: Even with hCD47, macrophage depletion still markedly increased pig cell numbers in HIS mice (O5, O6) and opsonization sharply cut cell numbers with only a modest hCD47 benefit (O9, O8), so CD47 alone is not sufficient against human macrophages in this xenogeneic setting; the cheatsheet states CD47 as an element but not this residual-destruction limit, and pig cells carry xenoantibody and Gal-related macrophage triggers that islet cells may lack.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO; cytokine-inducible MHC-I and MHC-II in human islet beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: IFN-gamma, IL-1beta and TNF-alpha raised HLA-DR protein (O5), NLRC5, HLA-A/B/C, B2M (O7), CIITA and MHC-II transcripts (O8) in primary human beta cells, the pathways the B2M and CIITA knockouts target; tested in adult cadaveric islets, not hPSC-derived islets, and NLRC5 is not in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M6 (autoreactive T-cell targets: PPI epitopes and modified insulin peptides presented by cytokine-stressed islets)
edges.claim_summary: The known preproinsulin CD8 epitope HLVEALYLV and post-translationally modified insulin peptides were naturally presented on islet MHC-I and MHC-II after cytokine stress (O12, O13), consistent with PPI as a Gate2B autoreactivity target; primary islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B (autoantigen repertoire beyond PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8, IA-2)
edges.claim_summary: T cells from T1D donors validated 28 new epitopes (O2) and islet-derived T cells recognized a modified CHGA peptide (O18), so the cheatsheet's named autoantigen set is not the full target set; control donors also responded weakly (O17), and SC-islet presentation of these peptides was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 safe-harbor knockin at Locus 4 AAVS1; genomic-integrity QC of multiplex editing)
edges.claim_summary: Cas9/AAV6 editing produced concatemeric insertions in 36% of AAVS1 clones and 39% of CD14 clones (O3/O4), with common PCR blind spots (O1/O2) and two different reporters sometimes linked to one allele (O7). This qualifies genotype verification for the frozen Blueprint's AAV6-compatible AAVS1 iCasp9 delivery option, not iCasp9 performance: the exact safety cassette, islet differentiation, spontaneous apoptosis and drug-induced escape were not tested. The frozen ranker already requires ddPCR plus long-read biallelic AAVS1 verification; adequacy for this specific ITR-linked artifact is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAV6 donor-integration fidelity and post-transduction ITR removal; distinct from GRAVEYARD_006 base/prime-edit structural-risk rule)
edges.claim_summary: Post-transduction ITR removal reduced PSC concatemer frequencies from 59% NC to 13.2% IC and 4.8% DC (O8/O9), with reported overall fluorescent-yield decreases of 19%/9% and double-positive-yield decreases of 42%/23% (O10/O11/O19/O20). HSPC reductions and four-month persistence data (O15–O17) support testing a concatemer-aware donor/QC pipeline for the Blueprint's AAV6 options, with residual errors remaining. The mismatched-homology-arm NHEJ data test IC only and provide descriptive rates, not equivalence or DC safety (O13/O14). Exact iCasp9/islet performance and incorporation of this IC/DC method remain unestablished; GRAVEYARD_006 translocation penalties are not measured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 knock-in at Locus 4 AAVS1; nuclease-plus-AAV6 safe-harbor editing and genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: Human CB/mPB HSPC Cas9/AAV6 HDR caused persistent senescence-associated responses (O1-O3, O6, O23), and the AAVS1 downstream deletion readout was increased in edited mPB colonies (O14). This qualifies transfer of nuclease/AAV6 safe-harbor editing to Locus 4 iCasp9 in hPSCs; the study does not test SC-islets, iCasp9 function or switch escape. The frozen Blueprint already specifies two-step editing, TP53/clonal QC and long-read/CAST-Seq checks (lines 79, 272), and the ranker penalizes clonal attrition/p53 selection (lines 124-134). Adoption of this specific HSPC senescence/AAV6 boundary is not established; the broad risk is not new.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (editing-time IL-1 versus p53 modulation; genomic safety and clonal output)
edges.claim_summary: Testing ANAK as an editing-time adjunct in hPSCs is an unvalidated hypothesis from HSPC assays: ANAK reduced the reported downstream deletion, micronuclear and cancer-panel endpoints and enhanced HDR clonal output (O9, O13, O16, O18), but CH mutations were comparable (O19) and only GSE56 improved lower-dose CB total engraftment (O20). GSE56 had higher deletion and WES variant readouts, with engraftment/clonality confounding noted by the authors (O15, O17). SC514 had mixed tradeoffs (O17, O21). Blueprint i53/RAD51 enhancement is not GSE56 p53 inhibition. GRAVEYARD_006 concerns multiplex base/prime/nuclease precautions, not this single-target Cas9/AAV6 experiment; no empirical change to its penalty follows. Specific adjunct adoption is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease-editing genomic safety, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: A Cas9 DSB produced megabase-scale LOH in ~4-5% of mESCs (O1) and 4% of human RPE1 cells (O14), mostly terminal deletions or chromosome loss (O3, O4, O8), with centromere-proximal LOH up to 50-88 Mb in some clones (O7). This supports the Gate5 genomic-integrity concern for nuclease edits, but the cheatsheet does not name LOH or chromosome truncation, and the data are cell lines, not hPSC or islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (base-editor and nickase versus nuclease modality)
edges.claim_summary: Cas9 nickases and dCas9 (O17) and ABE8e with ~70% editing (O18) showed no discernible LOH increase at the two loci tested in mESCs, unlike a Cas9 DSB (O1). This bears on comparing base, nickase and nuclease modalities, but the evidence is two loci, plasmid delivery and mouse ES cells, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether the Blueprint already adopts this distinction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (end-joining inhibitors and HDR-enhancing steps in DSB-based editing)
edges.claim_summary: Pol theta inhibition raised DSB-induced LOH to ~20% (O10) and combined Pol theta plus DNA-PK inhibition to ~50% (O11) in mESCs, and combined inhibition reached 22% in RPE1 cells (O16); a homologous ssODN did not change LOH alone (O12) but partially offset the Pol theta-inhibitor effect (O13). Hypothesis: avoid end-joining inhibitors in DSB-based editing and add allele-aware LOH or copy-number screening of edited clones; the cheatsheet does not state that the Blueprint uses such inhibitors.

Hypothesis: Gate5 genomic-safety QC should add long-read, copy-number and allele-aware assays beyond short-read on-target sequencing; the cheatsheet cannot show whether the Blueprint already specifies such assays.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (longitudinal hPSC bank and final-product genomic safety QC)
edges.claim_summary: Earlier negative genomic screening (O12) coexisted with an EP300 deletion in the transplanted lot (36.1% ddPCR VAF, O13), retrospective mutant-cell estimates of 6.3% at MCB and 79.2% in final product (O15), and final-product test results available only after administration (O20). This reinforces the existing longitudinal low-fraction QC principle: frozen Blueprint Stage 4 already specifies Seed -> MCB -> Stage 7 EOPC TP53/PPM1D/BCOR duplex sequencing plus 20q11.21 ddPCR (Blueprint:79,272; ranker:5087-5090). The specific EP300 panel coverage or prospective release-timing implementation is unknown; this corneal product does not quantify risk in edited SC-islets or establish the cause of the mutation, and does not test the multiplex-edit trigger in GRAVEYARD_006.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M4 and M5 (bounded first-in-human iPSC-product and preclinical tumorigenicity observations)
edges.claim_summary: The single ocular recipient had no prespecified proliferation/rejection events during 1 year under topical betamethasone (O1), with the separate urinary finding retained (O19); no mutation-attributed events were reported (O2). Nude-rat tests reported no tumors at 52 weeks or during the second assay's limited graft persistence (O6-O7), and residual-iPSC screening was <0.01% with no back-culture colonies (O8-O9). These bounded non-islet observations do not validate immune independence, long-term EP300 safety, a suicide switch, or Blueprint's quantitative clonogenic-escape limits (Blueprint:251-261). Incorporation of this exact ocular benchmark is not established from the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 targeted safe-harbor knock-in versus random integration)
edges.claim_summary: Cas9 AAVS1 knock-in gave a single insertion at the intended locus in one iPSC line (O5, O17), whereas piggyBac and lentiviral lines carried 8 to 105 insertions (O7-O9, O11, O13). This supports targeted safe-harbor insertion over random integration for Gate5, with the cheatsheet not stating these insertion counts; the payloads are CARs rather than iCasp9, the lines are non-islet iPSCs, and only 2 Cas9 lines were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genome-wide structural-variant QC of edited iPSC clones; optical genome mapping plus sequencing)
edges.claim_summary: Karyotype-normal parental lines carried multiple OGM-detected SVs and CNV gains (O3, O4), one Cas9 AAVS1 line had an unintended 234.5 kbp chromosome 11 duplication (O6), and a Cas9 knockout line had two heterozygous deletions (O15), while OGM missed a 60 bp deletion (O16). Hypothesis: Islet-1 clone release QC should pair OGM-type genome-wide SV mapping (about 5% VAF, about 500 bp resolution) with sequencing; the cheatsheet cannot show whether the Blueprint already specifies this.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic integrity of the hPSC-derived product: culture-acquired aneuploidy, 1q gain)

The cheatsheet's Gate5 genomic-safety scope lists editing-driven lesions and does not state culture-acquired aneuploidy; evidence is hESC-derived RPE, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmarks: stimulated C-peptide and CGM TIR)
edges.claim_summary: O5: a registered phase I type 1 diabetes transplantation trial lists HbA1c ≤ 6.5% with freedom from severe hypoglycemic events as its primary efficacy outcome, a composite the cheatsheet's Gate1 benchmark list (stimulated C-peptide, CGM TIR) does not state. The record has no results and does not describe the product, so it shows only what is being measured.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; Blueprint sections 1.2 and 4.5)
edges.claim_summary: At modeled boundary pO2 of 10-50 mmHg the reconstructed native human islets had predominantly non-viable cells (O1-O3); at 70 mmHg the reported functional fraction was only 3.8-16.3% across glucose conditions (O4), which does not identify the remaining hypoxic/non-viable split. Encapsulation was predicted to worsen oxygenation (O11). These results directionally support the existing Gate5 oxygen-bridge rationale, but do not establish the Blueprint's 72-hour survival, PDMS-CaO2 performance or oxygen-permeable-shell sufficiency; they are steady-state model predictions for reconstructed native islets, not a product-validation experiment.
