edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate validation of absolute static-GSIS Delta alongside ratio-based Stimulation Index)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O7 report predictive advantages of static-GSIS Delta over SI in primary human islets paired with a nude-mouse full-mass bioassay; O2 reports that four of five non-significant sGSIS preparations still reversed hyperglycemia. The frozen Blueprint already requires dynamic GSIS and low-glucose shut-off and includes incremental insulin/C-peptide output measurements. A static-Delta-based release threshold is not established by the reviewed frozen references, and its broader incorporation status is unknown. Testing incremental predictive value and prospective cut-point performance in engineered SC-islets is an unvalidated transfer hypothesis; declared n=32 versus 33 listed rows remains unresolved and no product qualification or IIP acceptance follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 (functional potency validation; primary-human-islet full-mass transplant reference)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O7 and O11 connect primary-human-islet secretion assay measurements with diabetes reversal defined as non-fasting glucose <200 mg/dL on three consecutive days after 2000 IEQ subrenal-capsular grafts in athymic nude mice. This supports the general functional-potency concept already present in frozen Blueprint Gate1; it does not establish incorporation of an exact days_to_normoglycemia specification, engineered-SC-islet performance, or immune-protection qualification. The declared 32-preparation cohort versus 33 listed HP records remains unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 safe-harbor expression durability; mechanistic qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O6/O7/O8 qualify safe-harbor expression durability in a T5 WTC11 reporter/cardiac-lineage model; original EGFP clone inactivity is not directly assigned to transactivator silencing. The general need to qualify AAVS1 silencing and anti-silencing elements is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §4.4 and ranker non_iid_common_mode_failure_gates. That incorporation applies to the general hazard, not these reporter rates: the Blueprint uses biallelic EEF1A1-core-iCasp9 with engineered cHS4 plus a function-pending HNRNPA2B1-proximal 455-bp candidate, whereas this paper tests synthetic TRE promoters, a different 0.7-kb UCOE and CAG-Tet-On 3G. No SC-islet/AP1903 escape probability or protection by the exact Blueprint cassette is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (alternative safe harbor, CLYBL, for the Locus 4 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O9/O11 support an unvalidated candidate comparison of CLYBL-containing insulated constructs versus AAVS1 for a future expression-durability experiment, not adoption of CLYBL-iCasp9. O9 reports ~1.9-fold higher MFI (p < 0.05 for both AAVS1 comparisons), but locus, insulators, zygosity and clone integration profiles differ. O11 preserves 45.6%/43.2% maintained expression without an established denominator or reconciled UCOE comparison. O10 shows extra integration in all five CLYBL clones; O15 documents it in AAVS1 screens too, with unresolved UCOE row totals. The frozen Blueprint §4.4 declares AAVS1 and a GAPDH contingency; incorporation of this specific CLYBL/reporter proposal is not established. Graveyard 002 addresses lineage-restricted switches and 006 multiplex base/prime-editing hazards; neither converts these ZFN/TALEN plasmid observations into an islet switch qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease-editing genomic integrity, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: Cas9 nuclease editing caused arm-scale copy-number loss in 4–25% of targets in two scRNA-seq datasets, preferentially toward the telomere, in a minority of cells (mean 4.3%, maximum 15.1%) (O4, O5, O6), with telomeric deletions also seen in HUVEC bulk RNA-seq (O7). The data are from HUVEC and cancer or non-islet lines, not hPSC-derived islet cells; the bridge is the shared Cas9 double-strand-break mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (editor-modality and TP53-status scope of genomic-integrity risk)
edges.claim_summary: Arm-scale loss was far less frequent with non-cutting CRISPRi (up to 2.6%, no telomeric enrichment, P = 0.68) and absent from shRNA data (O8, O9, O10), while TP53 LOF increased proximity bias (O13) and MDM2 AMP raised it only with functional TP53 (O14, O15). This qualifies the generic multiplex-editing integrity concern as nuclease- and TP53-status-dependent; base editors and nickases were not tested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 / M6 (copy-number-loss readout in the genomic-integrity panel)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: add an arm-scale copy-number-loss readout (scRNA-seq or sequencing-based, as used here in O4 and O7) to release testing of nuclease-edited lines, since events occur in a minority of cells (O6) and the authors note they are hard to detect in bulk RNA assays (O7). The detection method was applied to non-islet cell types and is untested in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (nuclease and HDR editing-process toxicity and clonal restriction in stem cells)
edges.claim_summary: In autologous macaque HSPC transplants, HDR-edited cells fell about two logs by 2 months and long-term HDR stayed below 1%, with oligoclonal output and lower infusion-product viability than LV (O1, O7, O10, O14), indicating the editing procedure itself can damage long-term repopulating stem cells. Hematopoietic cells in autologous macaques are far from hPSC-derived islet grafts, so transfer to Gate5 multiplex editing is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (off-target readout for Cas9 nuclease editing)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (FAS effector pressure; FAS ablation as an added protective edit)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO, Locus 1/2 class I ablation for T-cell evasion)

edges.target_gate_or_module: M4 (clinical trials and regulatory benchmarks)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ODC/polyamine inhibition as an intrinsic stress-resilience hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: Odc1 deletion improved glucose tolerance, delayed diabetes and increased beta-cell mass in STZ-treated non-autoimmune mice (O1-O3), with residual ODC-positive cells (O26_added) and no detected PI:insulin improvement (O27_added). This packet therefore cannot establish alloimmune evasion, autoreactive-memory control or indirect-APC protection required in frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.2 and Graveyard010.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical endocrine-function benchmark transfer limits)

This is not a monotonic efficacy proof or a graft benchmark: native recent-onset beta-cell preservation, masking exception at 1,000 mg/m2, small cohorts and printed AUC unit inconsistency limit transfer to frozen Blueprint Gate1/§3.2 clinical graft references.

O7 supports transient ITR-driven reporter expression and O11 reports PGK1-associated insertions with a suggested homology mechanism. A test of ectopic transcription and endogenous-promoter capture in the actual iCasp9 donor is an unvalidated extension; neither EEF1A1 recombination nor engrafted-cell ITR transcription was tested here. Incorporation of this exact mechanism is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter- and cell-context-dependent AAVS1 reporter expression; candidate insulated EEF1A1-core-iCasp9)

This qualifies extrapolation from an AAVS1 locus label to uniform output, but does not measure long-term silencing, iCasp9 killing or escape. The frozen Blueprint already recognizes differentiation-associated AAVS1 methylation and marks the HNRNPA2B1-proximal 455-bp candidate anti-silencing function as pending; incorporation of these exact reporter findings is unknown. Transfer to its candidate insulated EEF1A1-core-iCasp9 in hPSC-derived product lineages remains unvalidated.

This study samples sorted Cerulean+/mCherry+ cells and compares only DNA/cDNA-co-occurring barcodes, so it does not validate enumeration of completely silent or escape-capable cells; barcode sharing and assay/expansion bottlenecks also limit per-cell inference (O6/O7/O11). Any adaptation requires those blind spots to be tested and cannot replace the Blueprint's functional ≤10^-8 per-clonogenic-cell escape qualification with calibrated effective denominators. Incorporation of this precise complementary method is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic safety: chromosome-arm loss and truncation at cleaved loci)

These support the Gate5/M5 genomic-safety concern by a shared nuclease-DSB mechanism. The frozen Blueprint Stage-4 roadmap and §8 row 4 already require sequential editing and longitudinal genomic QC; its ranker/GRAVEYARD_006 address different hPSC/nickase-editing precautions. Incorporation of these specific T-cell rates is not established, and they do not calibrate SC-islet risk, editing utility discounts, or prove the Blueprint workflow protective.

edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: qualify scRNAseq inferCNV with complementary FISH and ddPCR for monitoring chromosome-arm abnormalities during multiplex-edited hPSC manufacture, alongside the Blueprint’s existing long-read/LOH/CAST-Seq and genomic QC. O3-O5 support complementary T-cell assays; ddPCR cannot distinguish breaks, translocations and deletions, and day-11 FISH sensitivity was insufficient. O12/O13 show reduced population prevalence but persistence after single-locus T-cell editing; multiplex follow-up beyond day 4 was not performed. Transfer to hPSC/SC-islets, assay sensitivity and release thresholds, and specific incorporation are unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic integrity: translocations, GRAVEYARD_006)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (pre-transplant genomic safety screening of hPSC-derived products; CNV at 14q32.33 and 17q12)
edges.claim_summary: Research QC hypothesis: evaluate final-product CNV monitoring at 14q32.33/17q12 alongside genomic and functional safety assays. The non-islet RPE/CM/NSC NOG transplant analyses reported 86% versus 29% within-cohort predictivity for maximum CN >3 versus cancer-gene SNV/del detection (O1/O4/O17); these are the same cases, not independent validation. This does not validate an SC-islet CN>3 release threshold, show that CN<=3 guarantees safety, or test locus-specific causality. Frozen Blueprint Stage-4 QC and ranker 20q11.21/structural-variant gates establish existing CNV surveillance, but adoption of this exact two-locus criterion is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe as a backstop independent of sequence-based screening)

In this paper all 5 abnormal analytical transplants lacked detectable listed cancer-gene SNV/del (O2), under study-specific VAF thresholds (O18), and the authors state CN<=3 is not a sufficient safety guarantee. This scopes screening performance in non-islet NOG grafts; no iCasp9/AP1903 or other switch was tested, so switch efficacy and product qualification cannot be inferred.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (on-target structural defects and hidden failed correction in edited iPSC founder clones)

Blueprint Stage 4 already addresses genomic integrity, but adoption of this specific study rate/mechanism is not established; the rate cannot calibrate Islet-1 multiplex yield. GRAVEYARD_006 concerns combined base/prime-edit and DSB burden, which this study did not compare; O14 does not prove delivery-method equivalence and O17 is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (existing biallelic-integrity and structural/LOH QC requirement for edited founder clones)

The requirement for biallelic integrity and structural/LOH QC is already explicit in frozen Blueprint Stage 4 (15–25 kb long-read and ±50 kb SNP phasing) and the ranker (AAVS1 ddPCR plus long-read verification); this is supporting evidence for that existing requirement, not proof that the product assays detect all defects. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (avascular oxygen supply for encapsulated grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O4 supports the bounded Gate5 oxygen-limitation premise: encapsulated adult porcine islets lowered mouse peritoneal DO approximately dose-dependently, with severely hypoxic levels described in the Conclusions. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and Stage 2 explicitly require oxygen support, and the frozen ranker penalizes avascular/unedited encapsulation niches, but this abstract supplies no quantitative DO threshold or controlled dose-response estimate and does not test the 72-hour PDMS-CaO2 bridge, human SC-islet geometry or fail-safe. Incorporation of this specific study-level empirical boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant hypoxia as a cause of viability loss)
edges.claim_summary: O6 and O7 report declining viable-islet number and insulin content over time; O5 is the authors' suggestion that hypoxia contributes to deterioration despite maintainable normoglycemia. This is a bounded bridge to the frozen Blueprint section 1.2 Gate4 hypoxic-stress scope, not evidence for a cytoprotective edit, causation, measured secretion decline or human-product qualification. O8 is a separate normoglycemic retrieval observation with unresolved cohort assignment, not proof that hypoxia alone caused failure. Incorporation of this specific empirical observation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (MANF loss-of-function and intrinsic ER-stress cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: Clinical MANF loss-of-function and human SC-islet KO support a role for endogenous MANF in ER homeostasis and beta-cell function: brefeldin-A apoptosis was 29% versus 18%, while TM/TG responses were described as similar (O7,O25–O27); graft PROINS/BiP/GRP170 and functional effects remain correctly distinguished (O12–O17,O30–O31). This is loss-of-function evidence, not recombinant rescue or MANF-overexpression protection; the cheatsheet names MANF, but actual Blueprint §1.2 only establishes the general proinsulin-ER-stress scope and checked candidate/specification/ranker/Graveyard content does not establish incorporation of this specific MANF claim.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (in vivo graft functional-load qualification)
edges.claim_summary: The relatively mild in vitro phenotype and preserved fold responses coexist with lower graft function, especially after mouse beta-cell ablation (O8,O14,O20,O30–O31), supporting evaluation under sustained secretory demand rather than relying on basal assays alone. Human SC-islets in non-humanized NSG kidney grafts provide a bridge to stress-test design, not proof for the exact edited Blueprint product, immune protection, or zero cumulative graft loss; incorporation of this specific functional-load boundary is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (fractional GSIS, absolute insulin output and proinsulin processing)
edges.claim_summary: Twofold glucose and fourfold KCl responses on a content-normalized static assay coexist with lower insulin content/absolute secretion, higher proinsulin-to-insulin ratio but similar proinsulin content, and increased graft PROINS-high cells (O8–O10,O15,O20,O28–O29). This qualifies use of fold response alone; actual Blueprint Gate1 requires dynamic biphasic GSIS and rapid low-glucose shut-off, so this study neither measures that full gate nor establishes incorporation of the specific processing defect.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (hIAPP amyloid toxicity under metabolic stress)
edges.claim_summary: The broad amyloid-stress concern and an amyloid challenge/readout route are already represented: frozen Blueprint section 1.2 Gate4 explicitly includes IAPP amyloid toxicity, and ranker DEC-053 specifies high-glucose/fibril-seeded ThT/A11/apoptosis testing. O6-O8 and O15-O17 give rodent ZnT8-genotype context for that concern; they do not validate the human SC-islet product, the existing assay thresholds, or a need for an otherwise absent amyloid screen.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (diet- and age-dependent beta-cell perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 scope the ZnT8/hIAPP phenotype by diet and age: chow glucose intolerance without a reported secretion/sensitivity effect, stronger early HFD secretion impairment, and author-described convergence after longer HFD. Specific incorporation of this genotype-by-diet-by-age boundary is not established; the comparisons are mouse evidence, not equivalence tests or validated human transfer.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M1, M7 (ZnT8 perturbation, insulin packaging and glucose responsiveness)
edges.claim_summary: O10 and O19-O25 distinguish zinc/granule changes, attenuated glucose-stimulated secretion, and author-reported unchanged KCl secretion/content in hIAPP mice; O27 preserves elevated basal secretion. Frozen ranker AUTO_NONE already avoids SLC30A8-null dense-core defects and the pan-autoantigen branch penalizes Gate1, but incorporation of these precise heterozygous/homozygous hIAPP findings is not established. The cheatsheet does not list ZnT8/IAPP as Gate1 maturation markers, and mouse results do not justify a validated human SC-islet bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (on-target DSB genomic-safety failure mechanism)
edges.claim_summary: Single-site Cas9 DSB editing caused micronucleation in RPE-1 cells (O1) and HSPCs (O13), while selected p53-depleted RPE-1 micronucleated lineages showed clustered rearrangements in 13/18 pairs (O5). This supports a genomic-safety hazard to consider for nuclease-edited hPSC manufacturing, without measuring risk in hPSCs or the Blueprint product. Frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and GRAVEYARD_006 already address related structural-variant/QC hazards, but incorporation of this precise single-cut micronucleus-to-chromothripsis mechanism and its conditional rates is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (conditional lineage rates, p53 status and transfer to manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O7/O8/O20/O21 share selected RPE-1 Look-Seq lineages and cannot estimate incidence among all edited cells. Micronucleated p53-proficient cells divided in 46 % of cases; p53-knockdown cells failed to divide in 8 % (O9), and the Fig 4a test detected no micronucleation-frequency effect rather than proving equivalence (O19). Frozen ranker lambda_K/gamma_B are engineering priors, not physical event probabilities; this study calibrates neither them nor clinical cancer risk, and directly detected no HSPC chromothripsis (O18).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M6 (candidate micronucleus/bridge imaging and single-cell genomic QC)
edges.claim_summary: Consider testing micronucleus/bridge imaging with appropriately sensitive single-cell genomic analysis as complementary QC during hPSC nuclease-editing protocol development. O18 is a sensitivity-limited negative LOH screen and O7 shows copy-neutral chromothripsis that such a screen can miss; neither establishes HSPC chromothripsis prevalence or assay performance in the exact product. Frozen Blueprint Stage 4, ranker failure-mode mitigations and GRAVEYARD_006 specify existing duplex/LOH/CAST-seq and related structural QC; incorporation of this exact proposed assay combination is unresolved, and no validated release threshold is supplied here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (on-target LOH and edited-clone genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: Globin Cas9 editing produced RRM1 LOH in HEK293T clones (18.5-25.8% versus 1.9%, O1-O3), acquired megabase LOH in 7/648 primary CD34+ clones (O9), and 5.2 Mb copy-neutral LOH in two intensively analyzed HSPC clones (O13). This supports the relevance of LOH-sensitive Gate5 genomic QC. Frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and its GMP safety row already specify long-read sequencing plus +/-50 kb flanking SNP LOH phasing; claim-specific incorporation of this paper's copy-neutral arm-scale event and rates is not established. These are HEK293T/HSPC data, with no hPSC or Blueprint-locus qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (distal SNP/allelic screening for copy-neutral LOH)
edges.claim_summary: In two HSPC clones, array-CGH showed no genomic loss while SNP-aware analysis mapped 5.2 Mb CN-LOH (O13); small bulk-FISH changes were limited by background (O20). The existing Blueprint +/-50 kb SNP LOH phasing requirement should be distinguished from the hypothesis of validating informative allelic markers across each relevant distal chromosome segment. Frozen ranker 5083-5090 and Graveyard 006 also mandate structural/translocation QC; those controls do not alone demonstrate sensitivity to this copy-neutral event. Adoption and product-specific detection performance of an expanded distal allelic assay are unknown. This is genomic safety M5, not an M6 screen/omics result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (locus-dependent imprinting consequences of LOH)
edges.claim_summary: The globin-distal 11p imprinted region showed opposite paternal/maternal clone profiles (O15-O16); the two paternal-UPD clones had reduced H19 and slight IGF2 induction (O17-O18). This qualifies transfer of any generic LOH risk into a locus-specific consequence claim. Frozen Blueprint already recognizes pre-banking LOH as a safety-switch common-mode hazard, but this does not establish that its edit sites share the 11p imprinting consequence. No Blueprint edit site, malignancy endpoint, graft behavior, or in vivo immune protection was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (mechanical clonal selection during hPSC expansion; genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O6, O10-O15 and O19-O22 characterize density/mechanical/YAP-dependent competition among undifferentiated hPSC sublines, including loss of wild-type cells and context-dependent winner status. Frozen Blueprint Stage-4 QC and section 7, and ranker 20q11.21 surveillance/outgrowth gates, already address genomic selection and mosaic BCL2L1 risk; incorporation of this specific mechanical/YAP mechanism is not established. These assays do not measure edited SC-islet genomic integrity, iCasp9 escape, or product tumor risk.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (culture-condition hypothesis upstream of SC-islet manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: O17-O18 and O23 support testing low-density expansion or 1 uM (R)-PFI-2 as conditions that suppress hPSC competition; the PFI-2 competition assays include H7, H14 and HUES-17. O16 limits simple caspase/ROCK inhibitor rescue, while O14 and O22 show that YAP gain can itself confer winner behavior as well as resist variants. Specific adoption of these conditions is not established; differentiation, clonal safety and function in edited SC-islet manufacturing remain untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(b) / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic safety: chromosomal translocations)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O6 document a t(2;11) translocation hazard after dual Cas9 nuclease targeting in primary adult human CD34+ cells. The general multiplex-DSB genomic-integrity concern is already accounted for by frozen Blueprint Stage 4 (line 79) sequential editing plus CAST-Seq/long-read QC and frozen ranker engineering-prior rationale (lines 124–129). This is a justified mechanistic bridge to Gate5/M5, not a measured SC-islet rate, oncogenesis endpoint, base/prime-editing test, or calibration of the ranker penalty. GRAVEYARD_006 instead concerns a related but distinct base/prime-nickase precaution.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(b) / M5 (sequential versus simultaneous multiplex nuclease edits; translocation persistence in vivo)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O8: spacing the same Cas9 targets 22–24 h apart reduced measured in vitro translocation frequencies (0.11%/0.04% versus 0.97%/0.58%) but did not eliminate translocation-bearing progeny, which persisted in human cells in NSG BM at 23 weeks. Event #1 and #2 were each detected in 4/6 sequential mice; these overlapping event counts are not eight independent positive mice. The frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and ranker lines 5087–5090 already prescribe two-pass orthogonal editing plus longitudinal QC; this same-Cas9 HSC experiment does not directly test that product workflow. Incorporation of these exact interval/rate/persistence observations is not established, so unknown is retained instead of an absence inference from the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual pluripotent-cell tumor hazard and pan-lineage fail-safe rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O6 show teratoma formation by undifferentiated macaque iPSCs in one immunocompetent autologous recipient and in immunodeficient NOG mice. This supports the residual-pluripotent-cell hazard already explicitly addressed by the frozen Blueprint section 7 and section 4.4 pan-lineage fail-safe; it does not show absent immune clearance, switch efficacy, an escape frequency, or safety of engineered human SC-islets. The no-detected-tumor allogeneic observations (O1/O3/O4) do not establish a general clinical safety exemption.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (MHC-matched acquired immune recognition; boundary on indirect-APC transfer)
edges.claim_summary: O12/O13 document weak acquired responses despite MHC matching; O16 documents no detectable binding to the tested PBMC/embryonic-carcinoma targets in #303/#307 and very weak embryonic-carcinoma binding in #1497. Antigen targets, direct versus indirect presentation, and causation of graft disappearance were not established. These findings qualify any assumption that MHC matching removes all antigen recognition, but do not demonstrate Gate2B autoimmunity or the host-APC pathway in B2M/CIITA-edited human SC-islets. Frozen Blueprint section 4.2, GRAVEYARD_010 and ranker Gate2B already address indirect-APC hazard generally; incorporation of this specific empirical boundary remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate-ligand expression versus functional protection)
edges.claim_summary: O8-O10 report native HLA-G/HLA-E, CD47 and sialic-acid expression in macaque iPSCs; O7 reports grouped NOD-SCID/NOG teratoma observations with a Discussion clone exception and unresolved CMT1/1-4 versus CMF1/1-4 label. No specific ligand perturbation, NK-killing, macrophage-phagocytosis or complement-function experiment establishes protection by those molecules here. This bounds transfer to the engineered human HLA-E/CD47 product: frozen Blueprint section 4.1 and GRAVEYARD_009 require functional and density qualification, and the ranker Gate3 prior is not validated by these descriptive results.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (KIR-mediated NK missing-self risk)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4 provide human kidney-transplant clinical association evidence for KIR-ligand missing-self risk, including HLA-DSA-negative MVI. The already-accounted-for claim is the need to address KIR-mediated missing-self as a Gate3 axis (frozen Blueprint section 1.2, line 63; risk-table item 2, line 270; frozen ranker counter_evidence_and_residual_risks and sorted NK panel, lines 2900 and 5810). The abstract does not phenotype NKG2A-negative NK subsets or test HLA-E, CD47 or B2M-null islet protection; transfer to engineered SC-islets is a bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (anti-donor-HLA humoral allosensitization; domain boundary for B2M/CIITA immune-cloak rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O4/O12/O19/O20 provide clinical rationale to consider donor-HLA sensitization in allogeneic islet protocols; O1/O2/O8/O11 retain source-specific persistence claims and unresolved denominator/status conflicts. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 already includes DSA and §§4.1–4.2 describe B2M/CIITA deletion; ranker Gate2A includes DSA and existing serum-crossmatch gates. Incorporation of this study's exact long-term postfailure findings is unknown. These unedited clinical graft cohorts under heterogeneous immunosuppression do not test HLA-null SC-islet protection or prove antibodies caused failure. HLA-DP was excluded from the assays; no claim covers all class-II specificities.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M4 (clinical benchmarks: longitudinal cPRA/DSA surveillance after allogeneic-cell graft failure and immunosuppression withdrawal)
edges.claim_summary: The paper recommends allosensitization monitoring for allogeneic cell-product protocols and prevention strategies before postfailure immunosuppression withdrawal. O3/O4/O11/O13 motivate a hypothesis for longitudinal cPRA/DSA surveillance, including after failure; waiting-list consequences are discussed, not measured here. Frozen ranker already specifies high-cPRA serum panels, Luminex SAB and exact-product crossmatch assays, which are distinct preclinical checks. Adoption of the specific longitudinal clinical endpoint is unknown after reviewing Blueprint trial/gate sections and ranker/graveyard context. Small retrospective, heterogeneous cohorts and unresolved O1/O2/O11/O18 source conflicts preclude adopting a numerical postfailure risk or inferring MMF efficacy.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (adaptive alloimmunity, T-cell infiltration under conventional immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: Under ATG with or without RTX, FK506/MMF and peri-transplant anti-inflammatory drugs, transplanted livers had reported higher CD3 area than normal controls (O12); lower-dose islet CD3 differences were nonsignificant (O10), and the group-3 liver significance claim conflicts across sections (O13). The source could not identify T-cell origin, so this scopes residual T-cell infiltration rather than proving allo-specific rejection, recurrent autoimmunity, or cloak efficacy. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.2 addresses allo/indirect pathways; exact incorporation of these measurements is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (mechanistic IAPP stress/infiltration hypothesis in an in vivo graft)
edges.claim_summary: IAPP-CD3 correlations use only 2-12 islets per fit (O16/O17); dose-group IAPP differences were nonsignificant (O15), and transplanted-versus-normal significance is internally inconsistent (O14). These motivate a bounded dose/stress/IAPP/infiltration experiment in SC-islets, not causal proof. Amyloid resilience is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2; ranker DEC-053 already defines an amyloid challenge/promotion rule, so this is not a new generic amyloid safeguard. Incorporation of this specific dose-linked association is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (acellular peritoneal oxygen measurement and transfer boundary)
edges.claim_summary: The same three healthy NHPs had acellular capsule MRR pO2 of 147 ± 9 mmHg immediately after room-air-equilibrated infusion and 61 ± 11 mmHg at Day 7 (O1/O2); the paired test was not significant (O3), and fiber-probe reports conflict (O4/O5). This informs site oxygen measurement under anesthesia and supplemental oxygen, not oxygen demand, toxicity or functional protection in the Blueprint SC-islet product. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.5 already requires a 72-hour oxygen bridge in a prevascularized scaffold and models a 40-mmHg boundary; these two acellular time points neither calibrate that product nor establish its oxygen-generator requirement. Incorporation of the exact NHP measurement remains unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (free-floating capsule aggregation and site/geometry transfer limits)
edges.claim_summary: Day 7 acellular capsules showed local pooling, caudal accumulation and omental trapping (O6-O8). This is a boundary for transferring free-floating microcapsule distribution to the Blueprint §4.5 scaffold/lamina and prevascularized pouch, which has distinct geometry and packing assumptions. No aggregate-specific pO2 decrement, islet injury or test of that scaffold was measured; detrimental effects were predicted by the authors. Exact incorporation of this distribution finding is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M3 (short-term acellular capsule foreign-body response; no innate shield efficacy test)
edges.claim_summary: Free-floating recovered capsule samples lacked attachment/fibrosis, while rare omentum-adherent capsules had a benign host-cell foreign-body response at Day 7 (O9-O14); immune-cell phenotype findings are descriptive and include an unresolved CD11a/CD11b source conflict (O16/O17). This supports Gate3 metadata relevance, but Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 requires NK/macrophage protection of the living graft from Hour 0. This acellular study tests neither NK killing, phagocytosis nor protection by the engineered islet stack. Exact material-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (peri-transplant inflammatory damage; pharmacologic chemokine-receptor blockade as cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: In a double-blind phase 3 trial, CXCR1/2 inhibition added to immunosuppression did not change C-peptide AUC at day 75 (27 vs 18, P = 0.99) or day 365 (24 vs 15, P = 0.71) (O1, O2, O5), qualifying the premise that blocking this chemokine axis rescues islets from inflammation-mediated loss. The study is in primary-islet recipients on systemic immunosuppression with a pharmacologic agent, so it does not test genetic cytoprotection of SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmarks: stimulated C-peptide AUC and insulin independence)
edges.claim_summary: The trial supplies placebo-arm clinical islet-allograft benchmarks: C-peptide AUC of 18 at day 75 and 15 at day 365 (O1, O2), and 0% insulin independence at 1 year in the placebo ATG single-infusion subset (O4); units, group sizes and the mean/median type are not stated in the abstract. Primary human islets differ from SC-islets, so these are bridge benchmarks only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic safety: translocations and off-target edits)
edges.claim_summary: The already explicit multiplex-editing genomic-safety/QC boundary is corroborated by translocations in all manufactured clinical T-cell products, an abundant 9.3 kB TRBC1:TRBC2 deletion, and off-target events (O8-O15). Incorporation refers to the broad hazard and QC requirement in frozen Blueprint Stage 4/§5/§9.4 and GRAVEYARD_006, not adoption of these clinical numbers as SC-islet parameters. Declining rearrangements in proliferating autologous T cells do not validate the proposed SC-islet editing schedule, engineering discount, or long-term safety.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (editing-reagent immunogenicity: residual Cas9 and pre-existing anti-Cas9 immunity)
edges.claim_summary: Residual Cas9 <0.75 fg/cell, no newly detected humoral response in three heavily pretreated lymphodepleted patients, and pre-existing Cas9 reactivity (with serum/cellular source limitations in O18) motivate a hypothesis to test residual-reagent content and recipient reactivity for edited allogeneic SC-islets (O16-O18). The study does not establish that low Cas9 caused the absence of immunization or validate a screening threshold in T1D recipients; claim-specific adoption is unknown after bounded frozen-reference inspection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of edited hPSC lines: on-target large deletions and loss of heterozygosity)
edges.claim_summary: Up to 40% of CRISPR-edited human stem cell clones carried large mono-allelic deletions or loss-of-heterozygosity that passed standard quality controls (O1), adding clone-level on-target damage to the genomic-integrity hazards for edited hPSC lines. The abstract names no loci or clone numbers and covers disease-mutation HDR and NHEJ edits, not the Blueprint's specific edits.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (clone-release quality control for multiplex-edited hPSC lines)
edges.claim_summary: Because standard quality controls missed these events (O1), adding qgPCR and SNP genotyping as clone-release checks for each edited locus in a multiplex-edited line is a candidate Blueprint upgrade (O2). Their performance is not quantified in the abstract, so this remains a hypothesis to test at the Blueprint's loci.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic-integrity QC of edited hPSC loci, e.g. AAVS1 iCasp9, B2M, CIITA)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: add UMI-based long-read on-target sequencing (IDMseq-like) of each edited hPSC locus to Gate5 genomic-safety checks, because the authors report that a 2375-bp deletion at VAF of about 0.1% (O9) and Cas9-induced SVs up to 5506 bp (O10) would be missed by short-read or ensemble sequencing. The assay was not tested at any Islet-1 locus or in multiplex-edited cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement, Locus 1 CD47-IgV-GPI)
edges.claim_summary: The observed hCD47/hCD55 BM macrochimerism and descriptive 13/14-day survival of the two EC-hCD47-positive lungs (O2, O3, O12, O14) are consistent with the already incorporated Gate3 CD47-SIRPalpha protective rationale (frozen Blueprint section 4.1). This incorporation label applies to that rationale, not adoption of the pig-to-baboon effect sizes or qualification of CD47-IgV-GPI. Coexpressed hCD55, historic controls, systemic conditioning, donor/SLA differences and no isolated macrophage readout prevent attribution to hCD47 alone or validated transfer to SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (cell-type-appropriate expression of CD47 and HLA-E effectors)
edges.claim_summary: The transgene-versus-surface-expression distinction in lung ECs (O13/O14) and weak HLA-E on donor BM (O6) reinforce the already incorporated requirement to verify HLA-E/CD47 surface expression in each relevant graft lineage. Frozen Blueprint section 4.1 and GRAVEYARD_009, with ranker Decision Experiment 1, already require Hour-0 lineage-specific flow/functional checks. This labels the verification boundary only; this study does not quantify a human islet surface threshold, demonstrate HLA-E failure, or validate CD47-IgV-GPI. The hCD46/HLA-E arm is one confounded recipient (O5/O18).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (donor-reactive cellular response and preserved unrelated response under systemic conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: Pre-lung IFN-gamma ELISPOT showed donor-pig unresponsiveness with anti-human responses preserved in all seven recipients (O9); MLR separately showed general unresponsiveness in 15P17 (O11). Lungs were nevertheless lost (O12/O14), and the animals received extensive systemic conditioning/immunosuppression. These xenogeneic functional assays cannot establish drug-free allogeneic SC-islet tolerance, protection from T1D autoimmunity, or blockade of indirect host APC presentation. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 places those distinct autoimmunity/indirect pathways under Gate2B; incorporation of this exact regimen-specific boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (peri-transplant IL-1beta and TNF-alpha cytokine stress)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: a short course of systemic IL-1beta plus TNF-alpha blockade at graft infusion could be added as a clinical co-therapy to protect Gate4-vulnerable cells during engraftment; in 9 islet recipients it was tolerated (no infections or portal thrombus, O3, O4; mild enzyme rises, O5 to O8). With no control group and primary islets placed intraportally, benefit for SC-islet engraftment is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO, Locus 1/2 ablation of HLA class I and II)
edges.claim_summary: In human iPSCs placed in immunocompetent rhesus macaques, B2M plus CIITA knockout lowered CD3 and CD20 in cell plugs (O9, O10), gave 11.17x the WT survival in wound lesions (O12) and reduced PBMC and T-cell stimulation in vitro (O16, O17), supporting the Gate2A B2M/CIITA design. Host is xenogeneic, cells are non-islet iPSCs, CD3 in wound lesions differed only from CIITA-/- (O13), and most readouts are figure-only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (completeness of B2M-KO ablation of classical HLA-A/B/C)
edges.claim_summary: After B2M knockout in human iPSCs, HLA-A stayed PCR-detectable and HLA-A/B/C alpha-subunit mRNA fell by only 43.3/72.7/46.3% (O3), qualifying the assumption that B2M KO fully ablates classical class I. Surface protein was not measured in this paper, so residual class I at the cell surface is not shown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate NK and macrophage arm beyond B2M/CIITA KO; HLA-E and CD47 at Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: B2M/CIITA knockouts did not change NK or macrophage infiltration (O11) and all iPSC tumor masses, including dual knockout, were gone within 28 days (O7), which the abstract attributes possibly to innate immunity; this is consistent with the Gate3 premise that adaptive-arm knockouts do not address innate rejection. The innate cause was not tested and the host is a xenogeneic macaque, so it is not evidence for HLA-E or CD47 efficacy.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (host-liver load-associated hypoxia after portal microcapsule infusion)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O4 and O17-O19 show lower host-liver delta R2* at greater portal microcapsule dose; O9-O11 and O14 describe greater pimonidazole hypoxia grade and O13/O20 describe hepatocyte injury. These are rabbit host-liver findings after portal infusion of capsules of unstated islet content, supporting a local load-associated oxygenation failure mode. They do not measure SC-islet viability, graft pO2, diffusion limits or successful 72-hour oxygen bridging in the Blueprint device (frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and oxygen/vascular niche section); exact incorporation of the rabbit dose-response is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (pre-vascularized extrahepatic subcutaneous device site; oxygen supply)
edges.claim_summary: The two-operation protocol included 10-day bFGF-collagen-sheet pretreatment before rat-islet device implantation and was followed by a reported 10-day glucose decrease versus untreated diabetic mice (O1); relatively higher serum insulin was also reported, with comparator unspecified (O5). The simultaneous one-operation protocol remained hyperglycemic and showed no body-weight or IPGTT-AUC improvement (O2-O4). These abstract-only functional findings support a contextual bridge to prevascularized-site design, but formulation, pretreatment and operation timing differ; vascular supply, oxygenation and a causal prevascularization benefit were not isolated or quantified, and the Blueprint 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/iMVF product was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (exogenous cytoprotection at the time of transplantation)
edges.claim_summary: The tested simultaneous bFGF/rat-islet device protocol remained hyperglycemic and showed no reported improvement in body weight or IPGTT AUC (O2-O4). The abstract cites prior in-vitro bFGF cytoprotection as background but reports no direct intrinsic stress-protection endpoint here; these whole-graft functional findings neither establish failure of intrinsic cytoprotection nor test the Blueprint CXCL10::SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette or other genetic cytoprotection components.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune Th1/Th17 effector pressure; systemic immunomodulation as a possible adjunct)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 report that signaling in human TH17, TH1, B and myeloid cells was blocked by BMS-986165 in vitro and in a phase 1 trial, and O4 and O5 report efficacy in murine lupus nephritis and IBD models. Whether systemic TYK2 inhibition could protect islet grafts from T1D autoimmunity is a hypothesis only; no islet, beta-cell or transplant data are in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (genomic-integrity release assays for edited cells)
edges.claim_summary: The paper notes that amplicon-based HDR/indel NGS cannot reveal large chromosomal abnormalities, whereas FISH and array-CGH detected the truncations (O6, O8). This suggests adding arm-level integrity assays to edited-line release criteria, a hypothesis not tested in hPSC-derived islet material.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base-editing genomic safety: off-target base edits)
edges.claim_summary: In GOTI mouse embryos, BE3 yielded 283 ± 32 SEM off-target SNVs versus 14 ± 12 SEM for Cre and 12 ± 4 SEM for Cas9 (O1/O2), with transcribed-region enrichment and higher expression of SNV-bearing genes relative to simulated genes (O9/O10); the abstract gives a more-than-20-fold headline with an unnamed exact reference frequency (O5). This supports genomic-safety caution under Gate5/M5 with unvalidated transfer to edited hPSC-derived islets: frozen Blueprint §5/GRAVEYARD_006 and the ranker address nickase/deaminase structural-variant precautions, but incorporation of this particular BE3 SNV burden is not established and this study does not calibrate the manufacturing discount.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (editor-class choice: cytosine versus adenine base editors)
edges.claim_summary: In this mouse-embryo assay, Cas9 and ABE7.10 SNV counts were descriptively near the Cre baseline (O3/O4), whereas BE3 counts were higher (O1/O2); the abstract supports a near-spontaneous-rate interpretation, not mutation protection, equivalence, or a class-wide guarantee of safety. Editor-specific transfer remains unvalidated, especially with Cre n = 2, ABE7.10 SNV n = 4 and on-target n = 2 (O8); the frozen generic base-edit penalty and GRAVEYARD_006 structural-variant rule do not establish incorporation of these specific SNV findings.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base-editing genomic safety: off-target base edits in hPSC)
edges.claim_summary: AncBE4max in the CL1 human iPSC line produced increased total sequence variants after sustained induction (O1) and heterogeneous transient-clone loads (O5), with TCW-context cytidine substitutions (O2, O10, O17). This supports a genomic-safety concern at the hPSC engineering stage; it does not measure an SC-islet product mutation rate, tumorigenicity, endocrine function or immune protection. The separate NSG teratoma assay characterized the parental line. Frozen Blueprint Stage-4 QC and GRAVEYARD_006 address genomic risk, but incorporation of this specific AncBE4max random-SNV mechanism is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (limits of predicted off-target site panels as a safety assay)
edges.claim_summary: The particular 557-site predicted Cas9 off-target panel found no variants despite genome-wide variants (O11); induction without exogenous gRNA (O12), descriptively similar PAM frequencies in named clones (O13), and limited recurrence with a stated long-term-clone exception (O14) qualify reliance on that panel for AncBE4max. These results support, rather than definitively prove, a gRNA/PAM-independent APOBEC mechanism. The frozen Blueprint Stage-4 targeted-driver/structural QC and GRAVEYARD_006 structural precaution are not evidence that this exact SNV boundary has been incorporated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (WGS clone screening and editor exposure control for edited hPSC lines)
edges.claim_summary: A bounded hypothesis is editor-specific unbiased clonal SNV assessment plus controlled exposure before promoting a CBE-edited hPSC product, motivated by O5/O7 and the authors' Discussion recommendation for unbiased sequencing. WGS itself is already a QC assay in frozen GRAVEYARD_006; novelty/adoption of the specific AncBE4max SNV/exposure acceptance rule is unknown. Cross-experiment higher loads after sustained expression do not establish a controlled causal duration effect, and transient RNA delivery also yielded high-load clones. No safe exposure level or product-release threshold was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (BCL2/XIAP anti-apoptotic cytoprotection: genomic-safety cost of constitutive anti-apoptotic expression)
edges.claim_summary: Anti-apoptotic perturbation of undifferentiated hPSCs (BCL-XL overexpression, NOXA knockout) cut mitotic-stress death (O6, O7, O8) but let cells survive repeated mitotic insults (O11), raised aneuploidy to 37% after AZD (O12; 6% to 12% without drug was not significant, O13) and gave larger teratomas (O15, O16). This qualifies any BCL2-family cytoprotection design for hPSC-stage use; the data are for BCL-XL and NOXA in hPSCs, not BCL2/XIAP in beta cells, and RA-differentiated cells were far less sensitive to mitotic stress (O3).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (hPSC starting-material genomic integrity: aneuploid cell retention with anti-apoptotic lesions)
edges.claim_summary: In hPSCs, a 20q11.21 BCL2L1-amplified line and BCL-XL overexpression cells showed reduced death after AZD-induced abnormal mitosis (O9) and BCL-XL overexpression permitted aneuploid cells to persist (O11, O12), supporting genomic-safety concern for hPSC stocks that carry anti-apoptotic lesions. Teratomas from the modified lines lacked OCT4 expression (O17) and endoderm differentiation was similar to wild-type (O18), so the data show larger but not undifferentiated growth. Bridge is the hPSC stage preceding islet differentiation; no islet cells were studied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (release screening of hPSC banks for 20q11.21 / BCL2L1 gain and aneuploidy)
edges.claim_summary: Because the ESI-CNV line resisted AZD-induced death (O9) and BCL-XL overexpression enabled aneuploid survival (O12), the authors argue that low-cost single-cell detection of 20q11.21 CNV in hPSC cultures is needed; adding such a screen to hPSC bank release criteria is an untested hypothesis here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 clonogenic fail-safe rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O5 show human iCasp9-transduced T cells persisting at 3.6 years in one patient and one dominant clone expanding 6-log in vivo, illustrating the proliferative capacity a transgene-bearing clone can reach. The abstract reports no AP1903 dosing, so switch efficacy is not tested, and the cell type (T cells) differs from a hPSC-derived islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonal dominance versus autonomy in genomic/oncology safety)
edges.claim_summary: O5 and O6 report a monoclonal/oligoclonal expansion that was not autonomous and contracted with resolution of EBV-PTLD, so clonal dominance of a transgene-bearing population was antigen-driven rather than transformed. This qualifies how clonal expansion readouts should be read for the Gate5 genomic-safety criteria, though the vector (viral integrant), cell type and indication differ from a safe-harbor edited SC-islet product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-IgV-GPI / SIRPalpha engagement, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O5 and O8 show that donor CD47 loss prolonged vascularized mouse heart allograft survival in MHC-II, MHC-I/II and anti-Gal humoral settings, while O1 and O2 show no harm from CD47 loss in syngeneic or class I-mismatched hosts and O13 reports no benefit in full mismatch. This qualifies the assumption that donor CD47 is uniformly protective, but it tests knockout (not overexpression) in a vascularized organ, not an hPSC-derived islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (anti-donor T-cell response; CD47-TSP1 signaling)
edges.claim_summary: O7, O10, O11 and O12 link donor CD47 and TSP1 to anti-donor T-cell responses and faster allograft rejection in mice; this suggests testing, in SC-islet CD47 designs, whether TSP1-CD47 signaling or TSP1 blockade changes allo-rejection. This is a hypothesis only: the data are from mouse heart and skin, not islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1 single-chain HLA-E trimer; peptide dependence)
edges.claim_summary: O6 and O8 show that sNKG2A/CD94 binding to p:HLA-E depends on the bound peptide (highly reduced for non-canonical LNL15, highest for canonical VIL9), qualifying the assumption that any HLA-E presentation engages NKG2A equally. Evidence is soluble receptor binding on T2E cells, with no NK cytotoxicity assay and no islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: [Structured target_gate_or_module (M0436) | text_sha256=b4e92f6e544b2c3b18e021cd066d586e9dcc1f431a772e0d56625046f7cf4093]
edges.claim_summary: O9-O11, O14 and O17 show that primary human CD8+ T cells from two donors proliferate and shift toward CD45RO+ after stimulation with HLA-E loaded with three non-canonical peptides, whereas VIL9 gave no specific proliferation (O13). This indicates HLA-E can be a CD8+ T cell target depending on the peptide, which the Gate2A description does not address, but the setting is artificial APCs with cell-line-derived peptides, not an SC-islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NKG2C+ NK subset evaluation)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK missing-self; HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O6/O7 document low classical MHC class I on mouse iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, O4 documents NK infiltration, and O1/O2 show NK depletion improves day-7 BLI (relative to day 1) and lowers graft apoptosis. These findings support the general missing-self/NK-protection rationale explicitly present in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 and Locus1 and the ranker Gate3 rationale; that general rationale is already accounted for. No HLA-E/CD47 construct, NKG2A-selective mechanism, edited human islet, or exact-product protection was tested, and IFN-gamma pleiotropy prevents assigning rescue exclusively to classical MHC re-expression.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (DNAM-1/PVR and NKG2D activating axes beyond HLA-E and CD47)
edges.claim_summary: O8/O9 show CD112/CD155 expression; O14, O24 and O26 report reduced LDH, greater CAM viability, and lower supernatant Granzyme B after CD226 or NKG2D blockade in mouse NK/cardiomyocyte co-cultures, without numerical magnitudes or mapped contrast p values. O16 and O22 show lower NK infiltration with the in vivo anti-CD226/anti-NKG2D cocktail, including the IFN-gamma combination. This motivates testing activating-axis mitigation as an incremental graft-protection hypothesis, with transfer to edited human islets unvalidated. O18 is IFN-gamma versus no IFN-gamma within antibody-treated grafts and does not establish an antibody-versus-control apoptosis benefit. The examined Blueprint Locus1/Stage1 designs and ranker entries specify inhibitory HLA-E/CD47 approaches; adoption of this specific activating-axis intervention is not established, so incorporation remains unknown. Systemic receptor blockade does not demonstrate graft-restricted protection or preserved unrelated immunity.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M and CIITA ablation versus IFN-gamma-driven MHC re-expression)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O13/O15/O17 and O21 show that IFN-gamma pretreatment induces classical MHC class I and improves mouse NK/cardiomyocyte readouts, while O11/O12 show increased CIITA/NLRC5 transcripts and MHC class II. Frozen Blueprint Locus1 disrupts B2M and Locus2 knocks out CIITA to remove classical HLA-I and inducible HLA-II; the unedited mouse IFN-gamma rescue is therefore a scoping qualification, not a drop-in rescue for that null chassis. No B2M/CIITA-null background or human-islet allo-T-cell assay was tested. O23 is qualitative non-classical MHC non-upregulation, not HLA-E failure or equivalence; alternative inhibitory or activating-axis strategies still require product-specific testing. Incorporation of this exact cross-domain qualification is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (limits of MHC matching as an alloimmune-protection strategy)

This qualifies reliance on matching alone in that neural context; it does not establish that B2M/CIITA ablation or any checkpoint would prevent this process in SC-islets. Frozen Blueprint §§1.2 and 4.1–4.2 define the adaptive-cloaking rationale, but incorporation of this specific neural finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (systemic endocrine efficacy versus residual local secretion and recovered explant function)

These observations distinguish residual viability/secretion from durable in-situ systemic efficacy; they neither establish a transport mechanism nor certify the human SC-islet dynamic-function requirements in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 (line 61). Specific incorporation of this compartment/bioassay boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification and enrichment of the endocrine fraction; Stage-6/7 maturation and CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment)

This qualifies the assumption that higher purity is always better, but the preparations are primary donor islets contaminated with exocrine/ductal cells, not SC-islets with off-target enterochromaffin cells, and the abstract gives p-values only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease/base/nickase editing genomic safety; GRAVEYARD_006)

edges.claim_summary: O2-O6: in human adaptive NKG2C+ NK cells, prolonged exposure to HLA-E presenting VMAPRTLFL (HLA-G leader peptide) increased FcεRγ-low enrichment, CD25, proliferation, ADCC and IFN-γ versus other HLA-E peptide complexes. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (graft-produced CD80/CD86 costimulation blockade; human SC-islet adjunct hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O5 and O7–O12 show improved graft-dependent metabolic control and less human T-cell infiltration with INS-promoter-driven LEA29Y in neonatal porcine xenografts in CD34+ HSC-humanized NSG mice; O19 measures systemic exposure but not local concentration or preserved unrelated immunity. Testing this approach alongside the human B2M/CIITA/PD-L1 architecture is a transfer hypothesis, not validation of that combined product, autoimmune-memory protection, or an isolated indirect-APC mechanism. The reported 70.4% remains inconsistent with Fig2 counts. Frozen Blueprint §§1.2/4.1–4.3 define the baseline and indirect-APC boundary; frozen ranker lines 4582–4593 already name sCTLA4-Ig in a radical wildcard. Specific INS-LEA29Y adoption is not established, so incorporation is unknown rather than inferred absent from the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (limits of NK and macrophage evidence in HU-SRC-SCID mice)
edges.claim_summary: O13/O15: NK cells were not detected in either group and Fig4 calls the macrophage-density difference a non-significant trend; the compound Results p-value is not assigned to macrophages. Discussion documents impaired innate development, including reduced monocyte/NK activation, and impaired B-cell maturation. Thus graft preservation does not establish protection against functional human NK killing, macrophage-mediated rejection, or clinical humoral xenorejection; Gate3 efficacy remains unresolved despite measured infiltration. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 requires functional innate protection; incorporation of this exact model limitation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (preclinical graft endocrine function; not human SC-islet manufacture)
edges.claim_summary: O2–O5/O16/O26 provide neonatal porcine graft functional context: prolonged maturation, glucose tolerance and first-phase porcine serum insulin in selected normoglycemic recipients, diabetes recurrence after graft removal, and below-detection mouse C-peptide in an incompletely assigned subset. Unassigned numerical group order and a selected two-mouse long-term extension limit comparison. These data do not establish human SC-islet lineage purity, physiological 60:30:10 architecture, full biphasic perifusion or low-glucose shutoff required by frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1. No clinical trial or regulatory endpoint supports module M4.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (transplant site selection: omentum versus intraportal for Islet-1 grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O6 with O1-O5: omental grafts were functionally superior to intraportal grafts at 1 month, with restored vascularity and oxygenation, so evaluating the omentum as an Islet-1 graft site is a candidate upgrade. The cheatsheet is silent on site choice, so incorporation cannot be settled here; the authors note larger grafts in humans remain untested, and hPSC-derived clusters were not studied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M7 (Locus 3 SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cytoprotection; ROS-inactivation failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports ROS-mediated inactivation of Sb9 through a vicinal disulfide in its reactive center loop, a candidate limitation on Locus 3 SERPINB9 activity under oxidative stress. The abstract does not assign this molecular finding to a specific cellular assay or validate the exact beta-cell cassette or peri-transplant conditions; transfer remains untested in the available packet. Frozen Blueprint section 4.3 and section 8 row 1 and ranker Decision Experiment #3 establish general cytosolic activity/half-life/kinetic checks, but do not establish incorporation of this specific redox mechanism; incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: O4, together with O2, reports functional GzmB inhibition and ROS resistance after converting the reactive-center-loop cysteine pair to serines in human or mouse Sb9. This supports a candidate ROS-resistant SERPINB9 variant for testing against the Locus 3 granzyme shield, not demonstrated islet or graft protection; the abstract gives no assay-specific provenance or quantitative potency. The reviewed frozen Locus 3 architecture and ranker activity/kinetic decision gates do not establish whether this specific variant is incorporated; incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (graft-function readouts by host thyroid status)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O5 motivate testing recipient thyroid status as an experimental covariate when interpreting C-peptide, GSIS and glucagon in comparable progenitor-graft studies. Transfer to OpenIslet's mature SC-islets or human recipient management remains unvalidated: the supplied evidence is an abstract from induced thyroid dysfunction in SCID-beige mice, with no human recipient data, numeric effect sizes, sample sizes or p-values in the packet. This is a testable hypothesis rather than evidence that screening or correcting thyroid status improves the target product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 biallelic AAVS1-iCasp9 fail-safe; conditional per-clonogenic-cell escape target <=1e-8 in frozen Blueprint section 7)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O5 establish an abstract-level clinical warning that CID need not eliminate every vector-integrated iC9-T cell. This is a qualitative safety-switch boundary in donor T cells, not a measured clonogenic escape rate or a test of hPSC-derived islets, AAVS1 targeting, insulation or the <=1e-8 product target. The frozen Blueprint already addresses expression/silencing and common-mode escape, but incorporation of this specific four-patient VIS pattern is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (expression stability and post-differentiation potency/escape testing of the insulated biallelic AAVS1-iCasp9 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: O6 supplies a proposed mechanistic rationale for verifying adequate, stable iC9 expression rather than assuming complete killing. Frozen Blueprint sections 4.4 and 7 already specify a biallelic insulated cassette and distinct potency/rare-clonogenic-escape testing; this rationale is therefore not a newly adopted upgrade. The abstract does not prove the expression mechanism, safe-harbor superiority, insulation efficacy or any monoallelic-versus-biallelic benefit.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (biallelic AAVS1 iCasp9/AP1903 fail-safe; Blueprint conditional <=1e-8 per-clonogenic-cell escape qualification target)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O6 report 95% initial circulating iC9-T-cell elimination in one HSCT recipient, more than eightfold residual-cell expansion three months later, lower iC9 expression and diminishing elimination with repeat AP1903. O7 reports unquantified activation-associated enhancement without specifying its setting. These observations bound expectations for durable clearance in this T-cell case; they do not test the Blueprint AAVS1 construct or measure clonogenic escape in SC-islets. The frozen Blueprint already addresses expression loss, common-mode escape and separate bulk-kill versus <=1e-8 rare-escape qualification; incorporation of this specific clinical serial-dose evidence is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M4, M5 (serial AP1903 clinical tolerability context for fail-safe activation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O2 describe mild transient grade 2 pancytopenia after each of three AP1903 administrations and no non-hematological toxicity in one HSCT recipient. This is limited clinical tolerability evidence for repeat dimerizer dosing in that setting; it does not establish population safety, causation of pancytopenia, SC-islet kill or vascularized-product tolerability. Whether this specific clinical observation is incorporated in the frozen references is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 promoter methylation and silencing failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O7 report higher 5'-LTR promoter methylation in low AP1903 responders, reduced methylation/increased transgene expression after 5-azacytidine, and restored sensitivity. The broad methylation/silencing failure mode is already addressed in frozen Blueprint §4.4 and §7; this incorporation label does not cover the study's numeric pairs or specific rescue intervention. These cell-line findings do not validate the Blueprint's EEF1A1/insulator/AAVS1 design or islet escape threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 demethylation-rescue assay hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O5-O8 motivate testing whether 5-azacytidine-mediated demethylation can restore AP1903 sensitivity in low-responding SC-islet iCasp9 subclones. Frozen Blueprint/ranker already address promoter methylation and bisulfite QC; incorporation of this specific rescue test is not established. Transfer from the studied 5'-LTR cell-line system to the EEF1A1/insulator/AAVS1 islet cassette, including rescue efficacy and safety, is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1, M4 (separate recurrent-autoimmunity protection requirement)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 and O9-O12/O19 associate recurrent T1D with posttransplant autoantibody positivity/conversion in immunosuppressed whole-pancreas SPK recipients. The design boundary supported here—separate autoimmune protection from alloimmunity—is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2; incorporation refers to that boundary, not adoption of these cohort estimates. This is neither a stem-cell-islet product test nor proof that autoantibodies cause recurrence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate2A / M1 (CIITA donor HLA-II ablation and residual host-APC presentation)
edges.claim_summary: O16-O18/O21-O22 associate recipient HLA genotype or donor-recipient HLA-DR sharing with recurrence, without testing CIITA/B2M editing or identifying direct versus indirect recognition. Frozen Blueprint §4.2, Gate-0D indirect-APC CD4 check and GRAVEYARD_010 already distinguish donor HLA-II ablation from residual host-APC presentation. These observations motivate checking that boundary; they do not validate CIITA-mediated autoimmune protection or constitute a newly adopted edit.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M4 / Gate2B (candidate serial autoantibody monitoring in beta-cell replacement trials)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O13/O19-O20 support evaluating serial GADA, IA-2A and ZnT8A monitoring as a candidate recurrence-risk readout: source Results gives ZnT8A-to-diagnosis 0.66 versus IA-2A 3.36 years, with Discussion instead giving IA-2A 3.63. Frozen Blueprint §2 Stage 5 specifies baseline HLA/autoantibody stratification; reviewed references do not establish incorporation of this study-specific longitudinal lag or serial panel. Performance and clinical utility for SC-islet grafts remain unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (potency and release-assay benchmarks for islet product quality)
edges.claim_summary: O6-O11 provide a clinical autologous-islet association between pre-IAT OCR dose and insulin independence at 6-12 months (AUC 0.96 versus IE-dose AUC 0.94; no significant difference, O8), while FDA/PI and OCR/DNA alone were not predictive. The frozen ranker already specifies Seahorse basal/maximal OCR with dynamic GSIS (line 5812), and Blueprint section 6 (lines 245-247) measures state-qualified oxygen consumption and function-burden trade-offs. Testing whether this particular viable-dose metric adds predictive value for edited SC-islet release is a justified research bridge; adoption of the IAT-derived metric or threshold is not established, and SC-islet/allogeneic/device transfer remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour oxygen bridge: islet oxygen demand inputs)
edges.claim_summary: O4 reports freshly isolated human autoislet OCR/DNA (115 ± 5 and 110 ± 6 nmol O2/min•mg DNA; mean ± SE), measured about 1-4 hours after isolation. These DNA-normalized observations may motivate an assay-matched benchmark against SC-islet oxygen demand. Blueprint section 4.5 already budgets volumetric Vmax = 0.034 mol/m3/s with 72-hour demand and geometry; these clinical data do not directly estimate that parameter without justified normalization, state and composition mapping. O1 is a group OCR-dose mean comparison; O14 is a recipient-mass-normalized clinical predictive cut-off, not an oxygen-sufficiency threshold. Incorporation of these specific cohort values is unknown; no 72-hour bridge or device protection was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M3 (innate macrophage barrier at a device or capsule graft; material-driven foreign body response)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2/O4 and O5-O8 describe sphere-size/geometry-associated foreign-body response and fibrosis in mouse and cell-free cynomolgus macaque implants, a bounded material-driven innate context for Gate3/M3. They do not test HLA-E or CD47 or establish protection of an edited human SC-islet. The frozen ranker already represents general fibrotic foreign-body risk under its macrodevice niche, but adoption of this particular size/geometry finding is not established; incorporation remains unknown. O1 overlaps the figure-level records.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization and prevascularized device)
edges.claim_summary: In this abstract-only murine adipose-MVF/nano-hydroxyapatite/poly(ester-urethane) scaffold study, 28-day pre-cultivation was followed by loss of native vessel morphology (O1). After implantation, pre-cultivated scaffolds showed reduced functional microvessel density (O3), a lower central GFP-positive microvessel fraction (O4), and worse host incorporation (O5) compared with freshly seeded controls. This is an unvalidated-transfer qualification for prolonged in vitro pre-cultivation of vessel units; the frozen Blueprint instead proposes edited isogenic iEC:iPericyte iMVFs and explicitly requires native-MVF-controlled lumen-patency/inosculation qualification. The packet reports no islet, measured oxygen/hypoxia, or 72-hour oxygen-bridge efficacy endpoint, and O5 is an association rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization and prevascularized device in a diabetic host)
edges.claim_summary: O1 reports lower capillary density in scaffolds in diabetic versus non-diabetic mice from day 6 onward; O3 reports denser microvascular networks with cell seeding within both host groups. These findings qualify transfer of host vascularization expectations to diabetic settings, but the abstract provides neither effect sizes nor exact inosculation times and studies non-islet PLGA constructs in a mouse diabetes model. This is an unvalidated transfer to the Blueprint oxygen bridge and edited iMVF-islet product; it neither tests nor disproves the 72-hour target. The frozen Blueprint already requires exact-product inosculation qualification and includes a delayed-inosculation sensitivity, but incorporation of this specific diabetic-host finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical glycemic-function benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O7, O18–O19 provide clinical islet-graft benchmarks under systemic immunosuppression: HbA1c was 7.1 ± 0.2 before vs 5.6 ± 0.1% after transplant (Table 1, time unspecified), and 72-h CGMS time <70 mg/dL was 12 ± 2 vs 2 ± 1% at 75 days (both P < 0.01). The Blueprint §1.2 requires regulated endocrine function, but these data neither measure stimulated C-peptide/CGM TIR directly nor qualify edited hPSC-derived grafts without immunosuppression. The specific study/quantitative benchmark incorporation is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (hypoglycemia counterregulation; clinical-to-product scope)
edges.claim_summary: O8–O17 and O20–O22 show improved counterregulatory responses at 6–7 months in the clinical islet-transplant cohort: EGP 0.59 ± 0.12 before vs 1.18 ± 0.13 mg/kg/min after (P < 0.05); posttransplant EGP was not detectably different from controls, while glucagon, epinephrine and PP remained lower. Autonomic improvement was a P = 0.06 trend. This does not establish equivalence, a causal hormone mechanism, optimal alpha-cell fraction or edited-product performance. Frozen Blueprint lines 78 and 246–247 and ranker lines 5801/6116 already specify counterregulation/low-glucose glucagon testing; claiming the general endpoint is novel or absent is unsupported. Incorporation of this specific clinical EGP profile remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe; residual pluripotent and off-target cells in hPSC-derived grafts)
edges.claim_summary: Grafts of iPSC-derived pancreatic cells in immunodeficient mice still contained pluripotent and some neuronal cells (O5), a residual-pluripotency and off-target failure mode that supports the need for a clonogenic fail-safe. The abstract gives no proportions, tumor data or kill-switch test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation, maturation and purification)
edges.claim_summary: An unpurified early iPSC protocol gave 5 ± 2.9 % insulin-positive cells (O1) and grafts lost insulin secretion capacity over time (O4), consistent with the need for maturation and purification. The abstract reports no stimulation index or perifusion data, so no quantitative comparison with the Gate1 benchmarks is possible.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 landing pad for insulated iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O11, O15-O17: CAG reporter expression was ~5-10-fold higher at CLYBL than AAVS1, while downstream host-gene and neighboring-gene transcripts changed in dual-targeted clone 1. This provides a locus/promoter-scoping caution for the frozen Blueprint's AAVS1-EEF1A1-core-iCasp9 design. It neither tests that exact donor nor establishes toxicity or functional superiority of CLYBL; no islet-lineage/iCasp9 experiment was performed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex safe-harbor knock-in; alternative or second landing site)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O7, O9 and O20: one-step AAVS1-plus-CLYBL targeting and stronger CAG reporter output at CLYBL justify a research comparison of CLYBL as an alternative/additional landing site. The iPSC dual-targeting rate was 14/16, joint TI-only result was reported as 50% without an explicit joint denominator, and NSC dual-targeted clones retained RI (4/8). This is an untested iCasp9/islet transfer hypothesis, not a qualified replacement for the Blueprint's AAVS1 plus GAPDH contingency.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety: promoter silencing and karyotype)
edges.claim_summary: O12-O14, O18-O21: reporter persistence through expansion and selected non-islet differentiation, reported normal CLYBL-iPSC karyotype, and high global-expression correlations support bounded safe-harbor engineering feasibility. O19 shows expression variability with RI; O20 confirms residual RI in dual-targeted NSCs; O21 retains a source discrepancy. These observations do not measure clonogenic escape, rare variants, methylation, or the exact Blueprint's lineage-wide safety; its anti-silencing candidate remains pending qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 landing pad for insulated iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O5: in a human fibroblast line, transgene knock-in at AAVS1 reduced MBS85 expression and raised contractile force, reversible by MBS85 re-expression. This qualifies treating AAVS1 as a neutral Locus 4 landing site; the cheatsheet lists no host-gene (MBS85) effect, and fibroblast contractility has no shown counterpart in beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 promoter reliability and insulator limitations)
edges.claim_summary: O2–O7 establish promoter-dependent AAVS1 inhibition and OCT4p rescue by cHS4; O12/O13 separate approximately 60% (day-8 start) from 35% (day-12 start) tdT+ on day 16, while O15 shows late-start TRE inhibition was not rescued by insulators. The broad AAVS1 silencing risk is already incorporated in frozen Blueprint §4.4 (line 157); this does not mean these exact reporters, quantitative values or insulator performance qualify the different EEF1A1-core/iCasp9 SC-islet product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (late-stage safety-switch qualification; frozen Blueprint conditional escape target ≤1e-8)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O12–O15 motivate checking expression after differentiation and induction timing; the specific proposal to combine late-stage/stress AP1903 testing with promoter bisulfite QC is already present in frozen ranker lines 5058 and 4977 and Blueprint §7. This paper tests neither iCasp9 killing nor any clonogenic escape threshold; the ≤1e-8 target belongs to the frozen Blueprint, replacing the oversimplified <1e-6 link label.
