edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (<1e-6 escape threshold for iCasp9/AP1903)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O6: the abstract reports a fractional clearance (85% to 95%) of circulating T cells after a single dose and recovery of virus-specific T cells, not a clonogenic escape frequency, so it cannot test a <1e-6 escape threshold and shows residual cells after one dose. Different cell type, delivery and endpoint from an iCasp9 islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 clonogenic suicide switch as the tumor fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O6/O9-O14/O18-O20: xenogeneic tumorigenic neural grafts in intact BALB/cA spinal cords regressed after FK506 plus anti-CD4 withdrawal, but BLI negativity at 64 days coexisted with HNA-positive cells and histological disappearance was reported only by 97 days after withdrawal. This qualifies immune-rejection safety-lock claims and motivates independent clearance verification; it does not test iCasp9/AP1903, establish clonogenic eradication, or show whether an engineered hypoimmune SC-islet graft can be immune rejected. Blueprint section 4.4 already specifies a pan-lineage switch; paper-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M3 (in vivo xenograft rejection; host-APC/CD4 pathway hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O15-O17 show survival under combined FK506 plus anti-CD4 and rejection with immune-cell infiltration after withdrawal; authors hypothesize indirect host-APC/CD4 recognition. This is mechanistic context for the general residual-host-APC/CD4 hazard already explicit in Blueprint section 4.2 and Graveyard 010, not direct demonstration of that pathway: no APC-specific or anti-CD4-only contrast isolates it. Xenogeneic neural cells in ordinary BALB/cA mice provide unvalidated transfer to SC-islet autoimmunity; no specific kinetic/ranker effect is inferred.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO ablation of HLA class I and class II targets)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O4, O5: in human islet allograft recipients on tacrolimus/mycophenolate, 5 of 26 grafts (19%) drew de novo anti-HLA DSA, and DSA positivity went with lower 3-month stimulated C-peptide (106 vs 613 pmol/L, p = 0.004) and loss of graft function. This motivates removing the HLA targets by B2M/CIITA KO; the abstract does not name HLA classes or test any edited graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Locus 1 single-chain HLA-E trimer; HLA-E-NKG2A axis)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O7, O10: HLA-E-peptide complexes are recognized by clonotypic TCRs of CD8+ T cells (UL40-specific cells in 7 of 15 recipients), and their presence was associated with BOS (5 of 5 BOS patients; p = 0.007) but not with ACR (p = 0.11). This scopes the HLA-E trimer from an NK-inhibitory cloak to a molecule that can also be a T-cell target; small cohort, native HLA-E, no engineered grafts tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate3 / M1 (choice of peptide carried by the HLA-E trimer)
edges.claim_summary: O10, O11: with CD94 blocked, the VMAPRTLIL (UL40/HLA-C leader) HLA-E tetramer stained effector-memory-like CD8+ T cells in healthy donors while the VMAPRTLFL (HLA-G leader) tetramer did not. Hypothesis: test the HLA-E trimer peptide against CMV-seropositive donor T cells; the cheatsheet does not state which peptide the trimer carries.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3, M4 (in vivo graft-site dependence and clinical alpha-cell counter-regulation)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O4, O5 and O18: at 50 mg/dl, combined-site autograft recipients had greater glucagon increments (54 +/− 14 versus 1 +/− 6 pg/ml) and symptom scores than hepatic-only recipients. Site allocation followed portal-pressure limits and graft doses/preparations differed; these are between-group associations, not demonstrated causal restoration by extrahepatic placement. O12 shows present but lower arginine-stimulated glucagon in a TP/IAT subset whose site composition and spread are not fully resolved. This justifies checking site-dependent counter-regulation in alpha-cell-containing SC-islet products, not transferring the numerical effect or qualifying OpenIslet; the specific empirical site boundary's incorporation remains unknown after the bounded frozen-reference review.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmarks: CGM and stimulated C-peptide)
edges.claim_summary: O14 and O16: five insulin-independent hepatic-only autograft recipients had mean CGM glucose 107 +/− 6 mg/dl yet spent 15.2 +/− 3.5% of monitored time below 70 mg/dl. This supports the already explicit requirement to test regulated insulin/glucagon function and hypoglycemic counter-regulation (frozen Blueprint §2 Stage 3 and §6 Step 2; ranker's clinical-success definition also names freedom from severe hypoglycaemia). Incorporation here refers to that requirement, not adoption of this study's numerical result or a new threshold. Mean glucose alone cannot establish hypoglycemia protection; the small autologous cohort does not qualify a T1D SC-islet product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS benchmark for SC-islet maturation)
edges.claim_summary: The early hESC protocol showed 70-75% NKX6.1 positivity at d17 (O1) but no glucose response in perifusion (O2; assay day unstated), supporting functional testing alongside lineage markers. The general Gate1 dynamic GSIS requirement is already explicit in frozen ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61 and rank_islet1_stacks.py:5583; this abstract does not validate modern Stage-7 exact-product function or any numeric release threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M7 (mechanistic failure modes of absent GSIS: GLUT1 localization and KATP SUR1:KIR6.2 stoichiometry)
edges.claim_summary: In this early hESC protocol, GLUT1 protein localization (O4), channel-response defects (O5), SUR1 transcript imbalance (O6) and a missing higher molecular weight SUR1 band (O9) motivate exploratory GLUT1-localization and KATP-function maturation readouts; a separate COSM6 ratio assay (O11) is mechanistic support, not an hESC rescue. Adoption of these exact readouts is unknown: frozen Blueprint Gate1/Stage-7 QC, ranker Gate1 logic and GRAVEYARD_003/004 establish broader function/metabolic boundaries, not verified incorporation of this specific proposal. Transfer to current edited Stage-7 SC-islets and causal correction remain unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of hPSC starting material and edited clones)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O6: a recurrent culture-acquired 20q11.21 gain raised Bcl-xL (on average 3-fold), cut apoptosis 2- to 3-fold after loss of cell contact and raised single-cell colony formation ∼2-fold, with BCL2L1 shown causal. Supports the Gate5 genomic-safety emphasis, adding a selectable culture-acquired gain-of-function copy-number change not among the listed failure modes; undifferentiated hESC, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clone QC and iCasp9 clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis (untested here): because 20q11.21-gain cells form colonies from single cells ∼2-fold more efficiently (O4) and resist apoptosis (O3), single-cell-cloned edited lines could be enriched for the gain, so add 20q11.21/BCL2L1 copy-number screening to clone QC and test whether such clones resist iCasp9 killing. The abstract tests neither drug-induced apoptosis nor cloning after editing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic and oncology safety of hPSC starting material)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4: culture-acquired trisomy 12 in hPSCs gave a germ-cell-tumour-like expression programme, higher proliferation and higher in vivo tumorigenicity with recoverable pluripotent cells. Supports the Gate5 genomic-safety concern, adding culture-acquired aneuploidy of the source line as a failure mode not listed in the cheatsheet; undifferentiated hPSCs, not SC-islets, and abstract-level evidence only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (source-line karyotype QC and clonogenic fail-safe backstop)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis (untested here): O4 and O5 suggest checking chromosome 12 gain in master and edited cell banks and testing whether the replication-inhibitor sensitivity of trisomy 12 hPSCs can serve as a second kill route beside iCasp9. The abstract tests neither differentiated SC-islets nor the suicide switch.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK missing-self; evaluation of inhibitory-receptor-defined NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: Depletion of all NK cells gave the greatest mouse ESC engraftment (O1) and depleting Ly49C/I versus Ly49G2 subsets gave differential engraftment (O2), consistent with rejection depending on which inhibitory-receptor-defined NK subsets are present. The bridge is that Ly49 (mouse) and the Blueprint's KIR/NKG2A are both inhibitory NK receptors, but this is undifferentiated mouse ESC in allogeneic mice and the abstract gives no values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NKG2D activating axis not listed among the Gate3 NK receptors)
edges.claim_summary: NKG2D blockade reduced NK killing of mouse ESC (O3), suggesting Gate3 NK assays could include NKG2D engagement alongside the listed NKG2A, NKG2C, KIR, DNAM-1/PVR and CD54/CD58 axes. This is untested in human SC-islet cells, since the abstract reports no human ESC result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (revascularization of the graft)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O6 (human single-case morphology/T1): intraportal grafts in one deceased recipient showed extensive revascularization and no visible differences from native-islet vessel number, distribution or shape; fewer <39 µm islets were observed in liver, and most transplanted islets remained intraluminal against the vessel wall. This provides a limited bridge for the possibility of vascularized human free-islet grafts. It supplies no post-transplant interval, functional perfusion measurement, equivalence test, or evidence that the Blueprint's 72-hour bridge target is sufficient for its edited SC-islet/pre-vascularized patch. Claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3, M7 (hypoxic-stress endocrine dysfunction; contextual relevance to Gate5 oxygen protection)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 report impaired mouse graft/endocrine function after unspecified hypoxic preexposure, with concomitant HIF-1α/LDHA changes; this provides a qualitative caution for transferring hypoxic-preexposure protocols but does not identify a harmful oxygen dose/duration or test the exact SC-islet product. The frozen Blueprint already addresses hypoxic stress and post-bridge endocrine recovery (Gate4 and §4.5, IIP-0004/DEC-082); it does not establish adoption of this study-specific HIF/LDHA boundary. The abstract reports no 72-hour oxygen-device or fail-safe test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (unvalidated SC-islet release-screen hypothesis: GSIS plus hypoxia-response markers)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: O3-O5 motivate testing whether adding an LDHA/HIF-target readout to functional GSIS testing improves prediction of SC-islet lot performance. Gate1 already requires biphasic GSIS without basal insulin leak; the abstract supplies no SC-islet validation, marker cutoff, human functional association, or incremental predictive-performance test, and adoption of this specific marker-screen hypothesis is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (stacked cytoprotective effectors incl. HMOX1; Gate2B autoimmune setting)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: in syngeneic NOD islet grafts, coexpressing HO-1 and DcR3 gave no survival gain over nontransgenic islets and shorter survival than either single transgene. This qualifies any assumption that stacking cytoprotective effectors (the Gate4 HMOX1 element) is additive; mouse constitutive islet-specific transgenes in an autoimmune host, abstract-level evidence with no survival times or p values, and the cause of the adverse effect is not stated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (cell-line QC and iCasp9 clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis (untested here): O8, O9 and O16 show BCL-XL-driven apoptosis resistance in 20q11.21 CNV cells that ABT-263 or shRNAi reverses, so add a BCL2L1 copy-number qPCR or FISH screen to cell-bank and clone QC and test whether such clones tolerate iCasp9 dimerizer exposure. The study did not test iCasp9, differentiated cells or edited clones.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (pan-lineage clonogenic fail-safe rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O6 support, by a non-islet bridge, the already explicit Gate5 rationale for a pan-lineage fail-safe addressing residual or reverting pluripotent cells and teratoma risk. This incorporation judgment is confined to that general safety rationale; the abstract supplies no risk frequency, SC-islet differentiation, suicide-switch test or proof that the viral-versus-episomal contrast is incorporated as a product rule.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1, Gate5 / M2, M5 (candidate line-selection and post-differentiation release QC)
edges.claim_summary: Untested transfer hypothesis from O1-O5: evaluate TG30 (CD9)/GCTM-2 FACS fractionation followed by culture and reversion assessment for SC-islet line selection and lot QC, including comparisons across derivation histories. Gate1 concerns the proposed manufacturing/purity application and Gate5 the clonogenic hazard; the abstract does not validate this assay in SC-islets or establish clinical safety of hESC/episomal lines, and claim-specific incorporation of this assay and selection rule is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 / SIRPalpha macrophage axis; humanized-mouse host choice)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3: efficient human hematopoietic engraftment in NOD-based models was attributed solely to polymorphic NOD Sirpa, with the abstract stating it recognizes human CD47. This qualifies Gate3 readouts: in NOD-Sirpa hosts a human CD47-SIRPalpha signal is already present, so graft survival there may under-report the added benefit of engineered CD47; hematopoietic cells, not islets, and no CD47 manipulation was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M3 (complement and macrophage testing in a defined humanized host)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis (untested here): O2 reports BRGS mice with normalized C5 function that allow complement-dependent cytotoxicity evaluation, so a BRGS-type host could test complement and SIRPalpha-dependent loss of a hypoimmune SC-islet graft with fewer NOD-specific confounders. The abstract tested only human hematopoietic engraftment.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1, Gate2A, Gate2B / M4 (clinical functional benchmarks with serial immune-marker monitoring)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis for evaluation, not tested clinical benefit: pair serial DSA/islet-autoantibody monitoring with C-peptide and insulin-independence endpoints. O4/O5/O6/O19/O22 show median 16 days from first infusion to antibody increase, subsequent failure associations, median 304 days from increase to graft loss, and R = 0.87 between antibody-modification-free and insulin-free times. Applicability to engineered SC-islets and improvement from monitoring-triggered treatment were not tested; exact adoption of this monitoring proposal cannot be established from the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1, Gate4 / M1, M7 (INS processing, ER stress and dominant-negative proinsulin failure)
edges.claim_summary: A(SP24)D lowered human insulin production and induced a BiP-reporter stress response in MIN6 cells (O1, O3), blocked bystander WT export (O9), and showed ≤10% steady-state oxidized monomer recovery with a majority in disulfide-linked complexes (O19). These cell-line findings bridge to the Blueprint Gate4 unfolded-proinsulin stress scope; they do not show that ER stress itself causes export blockade or establish protection in SC-islets or transplantation. Incorporation of this specific mutant/monomer finding remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M7 (ERO1-mediated WT proinsulin oxidative-folding rescue)
edges.claim_summary: ERO1alpha/beta, unlike PDI, showed rescue of WT proinsulin export in 293T cells (O14, O15); human insulin content doubled in INS1 cells (O17). ERO1beta improved native WT folding and final total WT recovery (O18, O20), while pulse-chase rescue was partial and did not change mutant behavior (O21). This is an unvalidated Gate4 transfer hypothesis from mutant-overexpressing cell lines, with no SC-islet or transplant protection demonstrated; incorporation of the exact ERO1 maneuver is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic and oncology safety: residual undifferentiated pluripotent cells in a differentiated graft)
edges.claim_summary: Residual undifferentiated ESC-marker-positive cells in a hESC-derived neural preparation induced tumors in monkey brain (O1), whereas a 42-day BDNF/GDNF-matured preparation did not (O2), consistent with the rationale for a clonogenic fail-safe and purification. Neural lineage in the primate brain, not islet cells; abstract gives no incidence numbers, and the title implies maturation may trade off dopaminergic function (O5).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M4 (clinical NK-proliferation monitoring boundary)
edges.claim_summary: NK cells were among the proliferating cells in the mixed lymphocyte cultures (O6), while the abstract reports no low-function group difference in CD56+Ki67+ cells (O4; group sizes, values and p-value unreported). This bounds what this clinical monitoring assay shows; it is neither equivalence nor evidence that NK cells do not contribute to graft injury. No missing-self cytotoxicity, HLA-E/NKG2A, macrophage or edited-product protection test is described, so it does not contradict the specific frozen Gate3 mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1, M4 (alloreactive CTL frequency, donor-mismatch avidity and in vitro pharmacologic inhibition during tapering)
edges.claim_summary: In a five-recipient clinical pilot, overall alloreactive CTL precursor frequency was reported unchanged (O3), whereas donor-mismatch avidity increased after tapering (P = 0·035; O4); in vitro tacrolimus, but not MPA, was reported to strongly inhibit alloreactivity (O5). These findings support the relevance of adaptive alloimmune monitoring, but do not prove tapering caused the changes or validate any edited SC-islet cloak; assay-specific n and a direct between-drug test are unavailable. The frozen references recognize alloimmune risk, but incorporation of this specific frequency/avidity boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 and Gate1 / M3, M7 (amyloid-associated graft beta-cell mass and functional decline)
edges.claim_summary: The general amyloid-resilience hazard is explicitly incorporated in frozen Blueprint section 1.2 Gate4, and the frozen ranker includes IAPP/amyloid qualification. This NHP primary-islet study reports amyloid in four longer-followed cases (O2), associations with time and beta-cell area (O3/O4), and coincident functional decline in two recipients (O5); autologous subcutaneous amyloid is a separate qualitative observation (O6). Incorporation applies to the general hazard, not adoption of these numerical coefficients, proof that amyloid causes graft loss, or qualification of the edited human SC-islet product or any IAPP edit.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (allograft rejection and systemic immunosuppression context)
edges.claim_summary: O7 distinguishes the reported histological rejection contexts of primary NHP allografts under systemic immunosuppressive regimens. The abstract does not establish a causal comparative drug effect, and these observations do not qualify the Blueprint's genetically cloaked human SC-islets for drug-free alloimmune protection. Incorporation of this specific regimen/cohort observation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (early post-transplant inflammatory chemokine damage; CXCL1/CXCL8-CXCR1/2 axis not listed among Gate4 cytokine stressors)
edges.claim_summary: Islets released CXCL1/CXCL8 (O1), levels rose after infusion (O2), and CXCL1-CXCR1/2 blockade improved engraftment in mice (O3) and improved outcome with reparixin in a phase 2 pilot of allogeneic islets (O6), suggesting early chemokine-driven damage as a candidate target beyond the Gate4 cytokines named in the cheatsheet. Data are for primary islets infused intrahepatically; no hPSC-derived islet or non-hepatic-site data, and the human result lacks stated outcome and n in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization as part of the oxygen bridge; adipose MSC co-encapsulation)
edges.claim_summary: AMSCs secreted significantly more VEGF than BM-MSCs in vitro (O3) and improved implant oxygenation and vascularization in vivo (O4, O5), suggesting AMSC co-encapsulation as a vascularization adjunct once the acute avascular oxygen bridge ends. Evidence is from rats with porcine islets, and the abstract gives no values, comparator or durability data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (site-dependent preimplant cavity contrast enhancement and prevascularized-device assessment)
edges.claim_summary: Rat cavity DCE-MRI findings (O1-O3) and the authors' site/timing assessments (O4-O5) justify source-limited evaluation of site-dependent device vascularization before islet loading. No detectable contrast is not proof of absent oxygen supply, and normalized MRI signal does not establish tissue pO2, the adequacy or duration of the Blueprint's 72-hour oxygen bridge, iMVF inosculation, islet survival/function, or human site suitability. The frozen Blueprint already specifies a prevascularized site, but incorporation of this particular cavity-imaging method and its reported signal series is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (in vivo graft-site vascularisation; acute oxygen-bridge qualification)
edges.claim_summary: One anti-CD154-treated baboon had iris graft vascularisation reported at POD 24 (O3) and <15% islet-mass loss over 357 days (O2). These late site observations do not measure perfusion onset or establish the Blueprint’s 72-hour oxygen bridge, PDMS-CaO2 kinetics, forearm/omental-site transfer, or fail-safe performance. Limited visible second-infusion engraftment (O11), synechia (O21), cataract (O17) and unmeasured direct visual function (O22) qualify an anterior-chamber site hypothesis; they do not establish site adoption or product safety.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide, HbA1c and insulin-requirement benchmarks for a functioning graft)
edges.claim_summary: In one STZ-diabetic baboon, insulin requirements fell to ~60% of pretransplant requirements (O5), circulating C-peptide exceeded 2 nmol/l at 3 months (O6), and IVGTT responses increased over time (O8). Pancreatectomy occurred later at POD 256; subsequent glucose-stimulable C-peptide (O10) and loss of the glucagon C-peptide response with eye removal at POD 357 (O13,O14) support graft-dependent endocrine function, despite terminal dysfunction (O18). Primary islets with systemic anti-CD154 and exogenous insulin are a bounded benchmark bridge, not qualification of drug-free hPSC-derived product function or the Blueprint’s dynamic GSIS criteria.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (insulated iCasp9/transgene expression stability against position effects and silencing)
edges.claim_summary: In lentiviral GFP vectors in human CD34+ cells, chicken HS4 insulators lowered titers (O1), reduced %GFP without raising MFI (O2), cut transduction efficiency fivefold with the full-length form (O4), lowered CV only with the full-length vector (O3), and the single core decreased %GFP and MFI in xenografted mice with no CV difference (O5, O6): minimal barrier benefit. The cheatsheet lists insulated iCasp9 without naming an element, so an insulator benefit should not be assumed; random-integration lentivirus in hematopoietic cells does not test safe-harbor knock-in in hPSC-derived islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NKp46-dependent beta-cell killing; boundary for HLA-E/CD47 cloak testing)
edges.claim_summary: O1 reports NKp46-ligand expression and NKp46-dependent killing of human beta cells; O2 establishes a human-versus-mouse developmental expression difference. These findings justify testing NKp46-dependent recognition within Gate3 assays of engineered SC-islets, alongside the frozen Blueprint HLA-E/CD94-NKG2A and CD47 design. The abstract does not report testing HLA-E/CD47-engineered cells or show that NKp46-mediated activation defeats their inhibitory protection. The exact NKp46-specific claim incorporation is not established by the reviewed frozen design and assay passages.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M7 (SC-islet NKp46-ligand profiling and receptor-recognition mechanism)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis from O1, O4 and O5: profile NKp46-ligand binding and NKp46-dependent killing in engineered SC-islets, and test whether the mapped membrane-proximal domain, stalk, Thr(125) and Asn(216) recognition requirements can inform a blocking strategy. Transfer to SC-islets, blockade efficacy, preservation of unrelated immunity and the ligand identity are not established by this abstract; the reviewed frozen design and assay passages do not establish adoption of this specific profiling/blockade hypothesis.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; B2M + CIITA ablation rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O1 shows allogeneic mouse ESCs are rapidly rejected by immunocompetent recipients while syngeneic ESCs are not, the baseline premise behind Gate2A evasion by B2M/CIITA ablation. Mouse ESC teratomas are a bridge, not an islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (T-cell immunogenicity of syngeneic iPSC derivatives; neoantigen-like aberrant expression)
edges.claim_summary: O2 to O6 report that syngeneic B6 iPSC teratomas can be immune-rejected or T-cell infiltrated, with overexpressed gene products contributing, so autologous origin does not by itself guarantee immune tolerance of iPSC derivatives. Mouse teratoma data; transfer to human iPSC-derived islets is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate cell infiltration of PSC-derived grafts; macrophage axis)
edges.claim_summary: Allogeneic mouse ESC-derived IPCC grafts drew Gr1+ neutrophils at day 1 (O3) and Mac-1+ macrophages above sham by day 3 (O6), but with less Gr-1+ and CD11b+ infiltration than islet allografts (O5, O8), supporting a real but smaller innate-cell burden on PSC-derived tissue. Mouse ESC clusters in non-diabetic mice, counts only in figures, and neutrophils are not named in the Gate3 scope.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (complement within the macrophage/innate axis)
edges.claim_summary: C3 staining at the kidney-capsule site was strong and similar in IPCC, islet and sham sites (O9), so C3 deposition there is not a graft-specific readout of complement attack and cannot explain the attenuated IPCC infiltration. This qualifies how complement is read out for Gate3 in a kidney-capsule mouse model.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (inflammatory cytokine/chemokine exposure incl. CXCL10, Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible cassette)
edges.claim_summary: Intra-graft IP-10/CXCL10 mRNA was similar to sham at day 1 and very low in IPCC grafts at day 3 versus islets (O15), with IL-6 not up-regulated (O11). This suggests early (days 1-3) CXCL10 drive in an ESC-derived graft may be limited, scoping when a CXCL10-driven cassette could be induced; whole-graft mouse mRNA, no cassette tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (recurrent autoimmune hazard and infiltrating-cell granzyme B / Fas ligand expression)
edges.claim_summary: The broad need to address recurrent T1D autoimmunity separately from alloimmunity is already explicit in frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and the Gate2B ranker. O1, O3-O5, O7 and O10/O12 supply one descriptive human whole-pancreas case under systemic immunosuppression. Fas ligand/granzyme B expression does not prove the killing route or efficacy of SERPINB9/PD-L1, and this case does not demonstrate host-APC presentation or performance in edited SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B boundary (minimal acute rejection alongside recurrent insulitis)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports beta-cell loss and alpha-cell predominance with minimal acute allograft rejection in the second biopsy of an HLA-mismatched pancreas graft. This supports keeping reported recurrent autoimmunity distinct from acute allograft rejection, but minimal acute rejection is not proof that all alloimmunity was controlled or absent. Blueprint section 1.2 separates Gate2A from Gate2B; incorporation of this specific case-level observation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate4 / M1 / M3 (macrophage infiltration and stress-pathology context in a human in vivo graft)
edges.claim_summary: O3 documents CD68-positive macrophage infiltration; O9 documents 8-OHdG staining, and O11 records no TUNEL-positive islet cells seen in the second biopsy. These justify bounded innate/stress-context routing, but do not measure phagocytosis, NK activity, oxidative injury magnitude, causal macrophage killing, or an intrinsic protective intervention. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and ranker distinguish Gate3 innate protection from Gate4 cytoprotection; incorporation of these specific histological observations is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical trials and regulatory benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: The packet holds only the guidance title (O1-O3), so no requirement, threshold or benchmark can be extracted and the Blueprint cannot be supported, qualified or challenged. Whether its allogeneic islet cell scope covers hPSC-derived islet products cannot be determined from the title.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(a) / M3 (in vivo graft vascularization; post-bridge internal vascularization boundary)
edges.claim_summary: At one month, the abstract describes similarly low vascular density in human islet grafts at the liver and kidney capsule sites (O1), with numerous vessels around but few within the intrahepatic islets (O2); O3 repeats the liver conclusion. This qualifies transfer of peripheral vascularity to adequate internal graft vascularization and motivates site/product-specific validation after an oxygen bridge. The frozen Blueprint already requires prevascularization, conditional capillary inosculation and edited iMVF qualification, but incorporation of this specific one-month cross-site finding is not established. These nude-mouse histological findings do not measure oxygen, perfusion or function, determine the day-3 state or establish failure of the SC-islet/iMVF/PDMS-CaO2 product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(b) / M5 (clinical HSV-TK suicide-gene control of donor-lymphocyte-associated GVHD; bounded bridge to an SC-islet iCasp9 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports that acute and chronic GVHD were controlled by HSV-TK suicide-gene induction in a non-randomised human donor-lymphocyte trial; O5 reports no adverse events attributed to gene transfer. This supports a limited clinical feasibility bridge for inducible suicide-gene management, not measured cell clearance or an SC-islet safety qualification. The frozen Blueprint already specifies a pan-lineage iCasp9/AP1903 fail-safe, but incorporation of the specific TK007 clinical findings is not established. No kill depth, clonogenic escape frequency, induction drug, clearance kinetics, endocrine-cell performance or exact-product safety is reported in the abstract.

edges.claim_summary: A metabolic-labeling assay detecting under 5 pg/microl de novo insulin (O1) and C-peptide quantification distinguished synthesized from medium-derived insulin (O2, O3), suggesting adding a de novo synthesis or C-peptide specificity control to Gate1 QC of SC-islet lots. Not tested on human SC-islets or current protocols; the cheatsheet does not state such a control.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 iCasp9 transgene-integrity boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O5 report internal HSV-tk transgene deletions in long-term persisting donor GMCs, present in most circulating NeoR-expressing GMCs and arising at production. This provides a bounded transgene-integrity caution for Gate5, not a measured functional killing/escape rate or validation of biallelic AAVS1 iCasp9 in SC-islets. The frozen Blueprint already includes cassette-loss and pre-banking integrity QC, and the ranker includes focal deletions during MCB expansion; incorporation of this specific HSV-tk clinical observation is unknown. Anti-HSV-tk immunity and/or ganciclovir selection remain suggested mechanisms.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (optional transgene-walking assay for cassette integrity)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O5 motivate considering transgene-walking PCR as an assay-specific manufacturing-integrity hypothesis for SC-islet safety cassettes. General clone-level biallelic integrity QC is already present in the frozen Blueprint/ranker (long-read sequencing and ddPCR); whether a walking-style assay adds useful coverage is unestablished. This HSV-tk donor-T-cell abstract does not validate the assay or a full-cassette integrity/functional escape threshold in SC-islets, and adoption of this assay-specific proposal is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter-silencing risk of insulated transgene cassettes)
edges.claim_summary: Insulation is sequence- and distance-dependent: the 250-bp core alone failed (O1), spacer length changed barrier activity (O2), and four 90-bp enhancer-blocking copies repressed GFP (O3), so 'insulated' does not by itself guarantee non-silencing. This qualifies Gate5 insulation assumptions only for these vectors, since no suicide gene or human cell is tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (minor-antigen indirect CD4+ presentation, Locus 3 SERPINB9 + PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: O1 shows that minor histocompatibility antigen disparity alone provokes acute rejection of ES cell-derived tissue in mice, consistent with Gate2B treating minor-antigen responses as a residual rejection route. The model is mouse ES-derived non-islet tissue, so it is a bridge to hPSC-derived islets, not a direct match.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (adjunct tolerance induction: nondepleting anti-CD4/CD8, TGF-beta2, regulatory T-cell polarization)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O5 report that minimal nondepleting anti-CD4/CD8 conditioning established tolerance to mH-mismatched ES cell-derived tissue, with low professional APC content, TGF-beta(2) and regulatory T-cell polarization named as contributors. This suggests testing short-course coreceptor blockade or local TGF-beta2 as an adjunct for residual mH rejection, but the cheatsheet states no tolerance-induction element and the data are mouse, non-islet and qualitative.

The cohort is primary-islet allotransplants, not hPSC-derived grafts, and the abstract does not define the comparator group.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (BCL2/XIAP anti-apoptotic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O4 show that bcl-2 overexpression (8 of 18 cell lines, 12 of 14 primary lymphomas) did not change sensitivity to T and NK cell cytolysis, so anti-apoptotic BCL2-family expression should not be counted on to protect against perforin-dependent immune killing. This limits only the immune-killing role of BCL2; the abstract does not test hypoxic, nutrient or cytokine stress, and the targets are lymphoma cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK cytotoxicity assay conditions: resting versus cytokine-activated NK cells)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O6 show that all lymphoma cells were killed by cytokine-activated NK cells whereas the majority resisted resting allogeneic NK cells, so NK killing of allogeneic targets depends on NK activation state. Gate3 NK assays may therefore need to state the activation state of the NK cells used, though no hPSC-derived or islet target was tested.

edges.claim_summary: O2-O5 support the shared safety rationale for depleting residual pluripotent cells from differentiated products: the initial cyESC derivatives contained 38.2% +/- 10.3% SSEA-4-positive cells and teratomas were reported in all newborns; after SSEA-4-negative transplantation (group n = 6), teratoma was no longer observed and engraftment was described as unperturbed. This is a bridge from fetal NHP hematopoietic transplantation; it does not validate SSEA-4-only selection, the numeric rates, or preservation of human SC-islet function.

This is consistent with removing donor HLA targets as a Gate2A strategy, but it is an association in a small retrospective cohort of primary-islet recipients and no HLA-null cells were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate4 / M3 (adequate islet mass and non-immune graft loss)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O5 report slow progressive loss of NHP islet allograft function without a destructive lymphocytic infiltrate, reproduced in islet autograft and partial pancreatectomy experiments and attributed to a marginal islet mass. This qualifies any expectation that immune protection alone preserves long-term function: islet mass and non-immune loss remain separate limits, although the grafts were adult NHP islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity control, allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 show in NHP that conventional and several anti-CD154 regimens failed through rejection, whereas an optimized short-term DST + rapamycin + anti-CD154 regimen allowed drug-free allograft function for months, supporting adaptive alloimmunity as a real barrier whose control is measurable in NHP. The regimen is a drug-based tolerizing approach, not a gene-edited graft, and no numbers are in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide and clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O5 show intrahepatic human islet grafts suppress C-peptide appropriately during hypoglycemia (similar to controls) and suppress glucagon under euglycemic hyperinsulinemia. Primary islets at an intrahepatic site are a bridge to a hPSC-derived islet graft, not a matched domain.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (paracrine architecture and clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 show glucagon and pancreatic polypeptide counterregulatory activation stays impaired in islet transplant recipients despite appropriate C-peptide suppression (O1), so a C-peptide or CGM benchmark alone does not capture alpha-cell counterregulation; the cheatsheet does not state this boundary.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M7 (Locus 1 HLA-E cloak: antiviral CTL-recognition boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports HLA-E-restricted recognition of naturally processed CMV-derived peptide on UL40+ RMA-S transfectants, and O3 reports killing of HCMV-infected targets by NK-CTL. This scopes an HLA-E-based NK cloak by identifying a CTL recognition route; it does not test SC-islets, the Blueprint VMAPRTLVL tethered trimer or a CD8-null variant. The frozen Blueprint portfolio and ranker already specify CMV+ UL40 CTL-lysis testing, so this hazard is accounted for as a required assay boundary, without establishing protection of the exact product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (CXCL10-inducible Locus 3 SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: O1 shows IP-10 (CXCL10) transcripts significantly increasing in livers bearing islet xenografts between 12-24 h and 48-72 h in non-immunosuppressed macaques, consistent with CXCL10 being an early graft-site inflammatory signal that a CXCL10-inducible cassette could sense. Porcine islets in a primate liver without immunosuppression are a bridge, not a matched hPSC-islet context.

edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O4 show that primary human islets produce tissue factor, clotting-cascade markers rise within 15-60 min of infusion, and a strong initial IBMIR goes with no significant 7-day C-peptide rise. The cheatsheet lists hypoxia, nutrient, ER/oxidative and cytokine stress under Gate4 but not blood-mediated loss; relevance to hPSC-derived islets (tissue factor expression, delivery route) is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (macrophage-associated functional impairment in encapsulated rat islets)
edges.claim_summary: Macrophages were quantified on overgrown retrieved capsules (O3), and NR8383 coculture reduced GIIR (O4) without a reported increase in necrosis (O5), supporting evaluation of endocrine function alongside macrophage-associated cell-death endpoints. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and GRAVEYARD_010 already recognize innate/macrophage and cytokine-bystander hazards; whether this precise rat coculture functional finding is incorporated is not established. No phagocytosis, CD47 intervention, human SC-islet transfer or complete macrophage causation of graft dysfunction was tested in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 / M7 (encapsulated-graft cell-death failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: At four weeks, retrieved rat grafts had 37 +/- 4% necrotic islet surface (O2) with rarely observed apoptosis (O10). The abstract reports 13 +/- 1.3% necrotic islet cells in the in vitro context without an increase attributed to macrophage presence (O5); these denominators and environments do not support a quantitative between-model contrast. The authors recommend improving nutrition, but oxygen/nutrient levels and causal nutrient deprivation were not measured in this packet, so neither Gate4 stress resilience nor the Gate5 72-hour oxygen bridge is validated. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 already scopes hypoxic stress and central ischemic necrosis; incorporation of this precise endpoint is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (endocrine function after encapsulated-islet transplantation)
edges.claim_summary: GIIR of retrieved nonovergrown rat islets was reduced versus freshly encapsulated islets at four weeks (O1), even though only 9.2 +/- 0.3% of retrieved capsules were overgrown (O9). This supports measuring post-transplant endocrine function rather than treating low capsule overgrowth as a functional surrogate; the abstract supplies no GIIR values, dynamic GSIS criterion, human SC-islet test or matched product qualification. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 requires biphasic endocrine function, but incorporation of this specific rat microcapsule boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (inducible suicide switch; AP1903 dimerizer, clonogenic escape threshold <1e-6)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show an AP1903-dimerizable Fas switch rapidly clears most engineered autologous T cells in macaques, yet a small fraction of cells escaped, partly through low transgene expression in resting cells. This qualifies how a dimerizer-triggered switch is judged against an escape threshold; T cells with a retroviral transgene are a bridge, not matched to iCasp9 at AAVS1 in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 switch immunogenicity and expression-level dependence)
edges.claim_summary: O4 shows a macaque immune response to non-self portions of a human Fas switch, and O2 ties escape to low expression in resting cells; the hypothesis to test is whether the proposed iCasp9 switch needs checks for transgene immunogenicity and for silent or low expression in quiescent beta cells. Neither is shown for iCasp9 or islet cells here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 / M7 (donor MHC class I-loss boundary; relevance to B2M-null designs)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1, M7 (Locus 2 CIITA knockout and direct class II presentation)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports CIITA-independent class II expression and cytosolic-OVA presentation in corneal endothelial cells, similar wild-type/CIITA KO corneal rejection fates with fewer class II-KO rejections, and class II-bearing macrophages in CIITA KO brain lesions (O1-O5). These model-specific observations qualify a universal reading of the Locus 2 CIITA-ablation premise (frozen Blueprint section 4.2); they do not establish escape in human SC-islets or the separately modeled host-APC indirect pathway.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1, M3 (CIITA KO versus direct class II-deficient donor grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O4 motivate a human-product validation hypothesis: test CIITA-null SC-islet and endothelial lineages under simultaneous IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha for residual HLA-II and functional endogenous-antigen presentation, with an appropriate class II-deficient comparison if residual presentation occurs. The abstract alone does not establish the molecular bypass mechanism, a need for direct HLA-II editing, or superiority/equivalence in humans.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (avascular oxygen bridge; pO2 maintenance)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O5 report approximately 35 mmHg endogenous-islet Po(2) and markedly lower graft Po(2) at 1 day and 1 month in syngeneic rat renal-subcapsular grafts, supporting the physiological rationale for oxygen provision. Blueprint sections 1.2 and 4.5 and ranker NICHE_VASCULAR_MODULES explicitly address oxygen limitation, but adoption of this specific rat finding is not established; these data do not validate the human SC-islet/device product or its oxygen thresholds.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour primary oxygen bridge window)
edges.claim_summary: O5 documents reduced graft Po(2) at 1 month at the rat renal-subcapsular site, a sampled late endpoint beyond the 72-hour primary target, without specifying its magnitude or continuous persistence. This qualifies transfer of a short bridge to other sites; it does not establish a failure of the intended human product, and Blueprint section 4.5 already includes a 336-hour dynamic trajectory and post-bridge recovery qualification, so the specific 1-month rat boundary has unknown incorporation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (hypoxic-stress context; graft acidification)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports graft pH 0.11-0.15 units lower; O6 reports a negative Po(2)-H+ correlation restricted to 1-month grafts in diabetic recipients. These findings give bounded rat stress context for Gate4, without demonstrating causal hypoxia-induced acidification, directly measured anaerobic flux or cytoprotection; Blueprint sections 1.2 and 4.5 address hypoxic stress and device pH/alkalinity, but incorporation of this specific association is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization handoff after the avascular oxygen bridge)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O3 report reduced histologic vascular density in transplanted mouse islets relative to native islets and no improvement during study-level 1-to-6-month sampling; O2 reports no recipient-diabetes-group difference without establishing equivalence or causal glucose independence. This is an unvalidated-transfer scoping caution for Gate5 vascular handoff after the 72-hour oxygen bridge, not a measurement of perfusion, oxygen tension, endocrine function or the prevascularized hPSC-islet product. The frozen Blueprint already requires vascular and oxygen qualification, but incorporation of this specific chronic-density boundary is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (FAS effector pressure on beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: in a mouse HIPFasL model, FasL-expressing beta cells are described as highly sensitive to Fas-mediated apoptosis under an inflammatory infiltrate, and blockade of FasL-Fas interaction prevents it. This is qualitative mouse evidence for the FAS effector pressure named in the Gate2B scope; the cheatsheet does not state whether Fas-specific protection is in the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; adequacy of post-bridge revascularization)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link M0533:L1 | relation=scoping_qualification | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O1,O2,O3 | text_sha256=8c66d99cc07bd76597742970d904a908befa95e92f6d1a0ab5d86adeca1be218]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (graft vascular supply; primary-islet mechanistic evidence)
edges.claim_summary: The general need to qualify islet-graft vascular supply is already explicit in Blueprint Gate5 and its microenvironment/iMVF qualification provisions. Reduced graft vascular density (O3) and low relative pO(2) (O1, O2) provide supporting primary-islet evidence in nude mice; the approximately 50%-of-renal-cortex perfusion observation (O4) is descriptive and species-unresolved. This is a mechanistic bridge to SC-islet grafts, not evidence that the proposed prevascularized device works; the specific numeric findings are not asserted to be adopted.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (post-transplant intra-islet vascular density versus surrounding vascularization)
edges.claim_summary: At 1 month, syngeneic mouse islet grafts had decreased intra-islet vascular density versus endogenous islets despite richly vascularized surrounding tissue (O1, O3). This qualifies using surrounding vascularization as a surrogate for intra-islet revascularization in Gate5 assessment; the abstract measures neither perfusion nor oxygenation and cannot validate or refute the Blueprint 72-hour oxygen bridge, its inter-capillary distance target, or edited human SC-islet/iMVF performance. Specific incorporation of this compartmental histology observation is not established by the reviewed frozen Blueprint sections.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (implantation-site dependence and peri-islet vessel formation)
edges.claim_summary: Spleen-implanted mouse islets were described as preferentially affected by reduced vascular density (O2), and islet-sized microspheres had much lower surrounding vascular density than the contextual islet comparison (O4; exact microsphere site and matching unresolved). These observations motivate site- and compartment-specific assessment of revascularization but test no prevascularization intervention and do not rank the Blueprint human forearm/omental products or establish their oxygen adequacy; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (inflammatory cytokine exposure; IFN-inducible CXCL10 Locus 3 circuit)
edges.claim_summary: An intact beta cell interferon response was critical for preventing CVB4-induced diabetes (O1) and for beta cell survival (O4), so dampening IFN responsiveness as cytoprotection could remove an antiviral defense. The abstract does not state the model system, and the transfer to an engineered SC-islet graft is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK-mediated killing of beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: NK cell-dependent death of virus-infected beta cells was reduced when beta cells mounted an IFN-driven defense (O2, O3), supporting NK cells as an effector against beta cells under viral stress. No NK receptor, HLA-E or CD47 axis is examined in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture and alpha-cell glucagon function; counterregulation benchmark)

The abstract does not say why counterregulation fails in intrahepatic recipients, so whether SC-islet alpha-cell content or the implant site would change this is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Locus 1 single-chain HLA-E trimer; HLA-E-peptide recognition by CD8+ T cells)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-E-specific CD8+ iNKR+ T cells proliferated in response to allogeneic cells and lysed a broad panel of HLA-unmatched PHA blasts (O1, O2), so HLA-E can be an alloreactive T-cell target and not only an NKG2A ligand. The abstract uses PHA blasts and RMA-S transfectants, not HLA-E-overexpressing islet cells, so the effect on an HLA-E trimer graft is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (residual CD8 allorecognition after B2M and CIITA knockout; HLA-E trimer peptide choice)
edges.claim_summary: Because recognition varied with the HLA-E-binding peptide (many but not all peptides, O4) and may involve peptides absent in the host (O5), the peptide carried by an engineered HLA-E trimer could be tested against HLA-E-specific alloreactive CTL. This is a proposed test, not a result of the study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 clonogenic suicide switch, Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 provide a justified human-drug bridge to the AP1903 inducer of the Gate5/M5 iCasp9 fail-safe: descriptive tolerability through 1.0 mg/kg IV in healthy adult men (possible flushing in one volunteer), dose-proportional plasma levels, and a reported rapid distribution phase. This is no evidence of engineered-cell killing, graft penetration, repeat-dose or pediatric safety, or clonogenic escape control. edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (in vivo graft site; intraportal vs renal subcapsule)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O5: intraportal grafts failed sooner than renal subcapsule grafts in autoimmune-NODs (p = 0.032 to 0.008 across donor types), so graft site could be treated as an explicit variable when benchmarking immune-evasion edits against recurrent autoimmunity. Rodent data with a hypothesis-level transfer to a hPSC-derived islet graft; the cheatsheet states no site-specific immune-pressure assumption.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 (vascularization around a macroencapsulation device)
edges.claim_summary: O2: in rats, flow around an empty subcutaneous TheraCyte macroencapsulation device returned from a 4-week dip to values not significantly different from day 1 from 2 months onwards, in line with device-surface vascularization named in the Gate5 scope. The device was empty and the rat host not hPSC-islet related, and the cheatsheet does not say whether the Blueprint cites this.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 + M7 (time-dependent perfusion after implant)
edges.claim_summary: O1: perfusion around the device fell to 72+/-17 PU at 4 weeks (p < 0.01) after being 133+/-28 to 158+/-42 PU from day 1 to 2 weeks, so a transient perfusion trough may follow the early window covered by the 72-hour bridge. This is a hypothesis only: perfusion units are not oxygen delivery and the device was empty.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 / M7 (oxygen bridge and chronic graft oxygenation boundary)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (in vivo graft hypoxic exposure; intrinsic-resilience relevance)
edges.claim_summary: The approximately 6-7 mm Hg rat graft pO2 and further reduction with persistent diabetic hyperglycemia define a possible chronic hypoxic exposure relevant to Gate4 stress qualification (O2-O4). Graft blood flow was approximately half the cortex reference yet described as similar across groups (O6, O8); flow alone does not establish tissue oxygen adequacy. No intrinsic-cytoprotective perturbation or endocrine-function/survival benefit is quantified in this abstract, and contribution to graft failure is unresolved. Hypoxic stress is within the frozen Blueprint Gate4 scope, while incorporation of this exact renal-graft exposure is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (72-hour oxygen-bridge target; recipient-state dependence of angiogenic marker timing)
edges.claim_summary: HGF, uPA and uPAR gene expression was clearly expressed at post-transplant day 5 in diabetic Lewis-rat recipients rather than day 3 in normoglycaemic recipients (O4). This is contextual evidence that recipient state can affect angiogenic-marker timing; it does not measure perfused revascularization or oxygen supply, establish a day-5 avascular interval, or validate or refute the 72-hour oxygen bridge of the engineered human SC-islet/iMVF product. The frozen Blueprint already requires direct iMVF inosculation qualification and includes a delayed-inosculation sensitivity; incorporation of this specific diabetes-associated transcript finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (hypoxic-stress response in rat islets; no measured cytoprotection endpoint)
edges.claim_summary: Hypoxia induced HGF gene expression but not c-MET induction in cultured rat islets (O1). This describes stress-associated transcript regulation, without evidence here of receptor dysfunction, HGF protein activity, graft protection or improved survival/function; transfer to intrinsic cytoprotection of engineered human SC-islets remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune protection: SERPINB9 + PD-L1 at CXCL10 Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: Because an intrinsic anti-apoptotic factor alone did not prevent autoimmune beta cell destruction (O3), protection against T1D autoimmunity appears to need immune-facing layers rather than anti-apoptosis alone. SERPINB9 and PD-L1 were not tested here, so this is consistent with, not proof of, the layered design.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (recurrent T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: In nine unsuppressed recipients of fetal pancreatic tissue, ICA seroconversion, conversion of the two baseline GADAb-negative subjects, and post-transplant PBMC reactivity support the recurrent-autoimmunity rationale of Gate2B explicitly recognized in Blueprint section 1.2; already_accounted_for refers only to that broad boundary, not this cohort's counts or peak times. This is a justified bridge from fetal pancreas to SC-islet engineering: the abstract attributes findings as most consistent with reactivation, reports maxima rather than reactivity onset, and establishes neither edited-product protection, graft loss, GAD65 isoform specificity nor a host-APC mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (direct CD8+/CD4+ allorecognition evasion, B2M + CIITA KO)
edges.claim_summary: In human islet allograft recipients, rapid graft failure (<3 weeks) coincided with increased graft-specific alloreactive T-cell precursor frequencies while long-surviving grafts showed none (O1, O3), consistent with adaptive alloimmunity as a failure route that Gate2A targets. Primary human islets in immunosuppressed patients are not hPSC-derived hypoimmune grafts, so this is a qualitative clinical correlate from seven patients.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1, M4 (autoreactive T-cell memory against islet autoantigens)
edges.claim_summary: Increased autoreactivity to islet autoantigens preceded alloreactivity in one rapid-failure case and appeared as a delayed rise in the 33-week-loss recipient (O4, O6), while surviving grafts showed only marginal increases (O2). This is a small-n clinical correlation bearing on Gate2B recurrent autoimmunity; the abstract does not name the autoantigens.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 + M7 (macroencapsulation slab loading and packing density)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3: in syngeneic mouse islets in a planar diffusion device, 750 or 1000 islets gave no improvement over 500 in one device, 250 rarely succeeded and two devices of 500 islets did best at week 4. This fits a diffusion-limited loading ceiling for macroencapsulation, but it is a qualitative mouse result without rates and the cheatsheet states no per-device loading figure.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (early functional safety readout of an encapsulated graft)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (acute graft oxygen deficit and 72-hour oxygen-bridge context)
edges.claim_summary: Day-1 rat renal-capsule graft PO2 was reported as 14-19 mmHg versus native-islet 31-37 mmHg (O1/O2); surrounding cortex was described as stable at 13-21 mmHg (O7, group/time allocation unspecified). This supports the acute oxygen-deficit rationale explicitly addressed in frozen Blueprint section 1.2, but does not validate its 72-hour device bridge, establish a device boundary condition, or establish incorporation of these precise empirical ranges; the section 9.3 model boundary of 40 mmHg and minimum target of 15 mmHg are distinct quantities.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (measured graft oxygenation after revascularization)
edges.claim_summary: At 1 month after reported revascularization, graft PO2 remained below native-islet values: normoglycemic 9-15 with source unit printed mmHgf (unresolved) versus diabetic 6-8 mmHg, despite author-reported similar graft perfusion (O4/O5/O6); acute IV D-glucose reportedly did not alter tissue PO2 (O8). These rat renal-capsule observations support measuring oxygenation beyond vascularization alone, without proving causation, equivalence of perfusion, or transfer to the prevascularized human device; frozen Blueprint section 9.3 already models oxygen over 336 hours, and incorporation of this particular chronic glycemic-context finding remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical functional benchmarks beyond C-peptide and CGM TIR)
edges.claim_summary: One month after intraportal primary islet transplantation in three patients, counterregulatory hormone responses (epinephrine, norepinephrine, cortisol) improved and autonomic hypoglycemia warning symptoms appeared (O5, O6), showing clinically meaningful graft function readouts from hypoglycemic clamps. Primary islets in three patients with no p or values do not transfer directly to a hPSC-derived islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (alpha-cell glucagon counterregulation within the beta:alpha:delta paracrine reference)
edges.claim_summary: Hypoglycemia-induced glucagon secretion was absent before and showed no improvement one month after intraportal islet transplantation (O1, O4), qualifying the expectation that a transplanted islet graft restores glucagon counterregulation. The abstract gives no mechanism, graft composition or values, and the graft is primary islets at the portal site.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-E-peptide complexes on 721.221 cells were recognized by CD94/NKG2A+ NK clones, which appeared more sensitive to most complexes than CD94/NKG2C+ effectors (O2), consistent with the HLA-E-NKG2A engagement axis. Evidence is an NK clone assay on a lymphoblastoid line with peptide loading, not an HLA-E trimer on SC-islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M7 (HLA-E-bound peptide choice and NKG2C-mediated triggering)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate rejection beyond NK and macrophage axes)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2: Fas ligand expression on islets and cell lines is reported to give accelerated neutrophilic rejection. The cheatsheet defines Gate3 around NK and macrophage effectors and lists no FasL element, so this qualifies Gate3 scope only in that neutrophil-mediated rejection can be triggered by an immune-modulatory transgene. The packet is a title-length abstract with no host, numbers or controls.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo hepatic islet graft site and glucagon counter-regulation)
edges.claim_summary: In intrahepatic primary-islet auto- and allograft recipients, glucagon did not rise during sustained hypoglycemia although arginine responses were present (O1-O3; O6 is overlapping author synthesis). This is a clinical scoping caution for Gate1 regulated glucagon function: insulin independence, normoglycemia and arginine responsiveness do not demonstrate hypoglycemic counter-regulation. The frozen Blueprint already specifies exact-product counter-regulation testing; the study does not test its SC-islet 60:30:10 mixture, prove a hepatic-site cause, or compare alternative implant sites. Incorporation of this specific clinical boundary remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(a) / M3 / M7 (oxygenation and external diffusion resistance)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 and O6 support the general relevance of external oxygen-transport resistance: barium-alginate-encapsulated fish islet organs had lower surface/center PO2, a wider outer oxygen-depleted zone (188 +/- 16 vs 94 +/- 14 microns, P < 0.001), and a narrower oxygen-consuming rim. The frozen Blueprint section 4.5 explicitly models Krogh/slab diffusion and external pericellular hydrogel permeability, so the general oxygen constraint is already recognized; incorporation of these specific fish-organ findings is unknown. The bridge is mechanistic only: no human SC-islet calibration, absolute mmHg threshold, 72-hour graft result, or product qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(a) / M7 (convection and unstirred-water-layer boundary sensitivity)
edges.claim_summary: O5 and O7-O9 show source-reported effects of convection on radial oxygen profiles, including a thinner outer oxygen-depleted zone with convection (81 +/- 16 vs 196 +/- 57 microns, P < 0.001); the rim contrast was NS. Alongside the author interpretation O6, this motivates testing whether a separately measured external boundary-layer/convection resistance is needed in the existing oxygen model, with care not to double-count its hydrogel resistance. This is an abstract-only fish-organ hypothesis with no human SC-islet validation or adopted coefficient; exact incorporation cannot be established from the supplied Blueprint section 4.5, ranker Gate5 scoring branch, and graveyard context.

This scopes what a CIITA knockout can deliver; the abstract tests a class II-deficient donor (not CIITA specifically) in skin, not islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 (implant-site dependence of fibrosis and lumen oxygen)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4: fibrosis was highest subcutaneously and lowest at the kidney, fibrosed fibers kept or improved insulin permeability, and lumen oxygen differed by site (42 vs 30 mm Hg), so implant site could be proposed as an explicit variable for the oxygen-bridge design. Hypothesis only: rat hollow fibers, no values for fibrosis, no tests.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablating classical class I, Locus 1/2)
edges.claim_summary: In mice, beta 2m-deficient cells carrying class I heavy chains were killed by allospecific, class I-restricted CD8+ CTLs and were rejected in allogeneic recipients (O1, O2, O6), qualifying the assumption that B2M loss alone removes class I-restricted CD8+ recognition. Murine H-2 molecules, a mutant lymphoma line and in vivo priming do not establish the same residual surface class I or CTL recognition after B2M knockout in human SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1, Gate4 / M1 (endocrine cost and intrinsic beta-cell disruption associated with transgene expression)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports lineage-dependent mouse beta-cell insulin depletion and homozygote diabetes, attributes dysfunction to transgene expression level, and reports protein-level disruption involving defective secretion (O1-O5); B2M coexpression also improved the heavy-chain model morphology/insulin content, while females remained normoglycemic (O6-O7). This qualifies the assumption that added protein expression preserves endocrine function, but supplies neither a quantitative safe expression window nor direct ER-stress measurements. Frozen Blueprint section 4.1 disrupts endogenous soluble B2M while including a B2M domain in its HLA-E single-chain trimer and already requires construct/GSIS testing; transfer from these mouse transgenes to that human SC-islet architecture remains unvalidated. Adoption of this specific lineage/dosage finding is not established, so incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (requirement to address recurrent T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: This HLA-identical segmental-pancreas case series provides clinical rationale for addressing pre-existing T1D autoreactivity as a separate Gate2B hazard: islet-centred infiltrates, selective beta-cell loss and the beta-cell-associated infiltration pattern (O2-O4, O6-O7) were consistent with the authors' cell-mediated-recurrence interpretation. Already accounted for refers only to the explicit autoreactive-T-cell requirement in frozen Blueprint section 1.2, not incorporation of this paper's case-level histology or validation of any engineered cloak; humoral absence and autoimmune causation were not experimentally established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M4 (clinical recurrence timing and histologic follow-up)
edges.claim_summary: All four patients developed impaired graft function 6 to 12 weeks after initially normal glucose metabolism; the immunosuppressed fourth patient had resolved insulitis with beta-cell destruction in 70% of islets and continued low-dose insulin use at 15 months (O1, O2, O5). This bounds the clinical recurrence and monitoring context in whole segmental-pancreas grafts, without estimating SC-islet failure rates, causal immunosuppression benefit or reversibility; abstract-only evidence and unspecified regimen/timing limit transfer. Incorporation of these specific timing and histology observations is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease editing genomic integrity and longitudinal LOH quality control)
edges.claim_summary: The broad LOH hazard and longitudinal genomic-QC requirement are already explicit in the frozen Blueprint Stage4/section8 row4 (three timepoints and long-read plus flanking-SNP LOH phasing). HBG1/2p dual-promoter Cas9 targeting yielded 4.6% LOH by global UMAP versus 7.4% by refined SNP analysis (O1/O3; different retained denominators), with interstitial events (O4); these human HSPC findings reinforce that existing hazard, without calibrating exact-product islet rates or validating base/prime-edit safety.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (HDR-booster genotoxicity, delayed detection and bounded post-graft non-detection)
edges.claim_summary: AZD7648 increased UROS HDR (77% versus 12%, O20) alongside HSPC micronuclei up to 3-4% (O9; control not numerically reported) and approximately threefold telomeric LOH (O10). hFF LOH was undetected at D2 but present at D7/D20 (O7/O8/O19). D90 targeted LOH non-detection in n=2 NSG mice per condition (O17) neither proves zero risk nor transfers to islet grafts. The Blueprint has general longitudinal QC, but incorporation of these drug/time-dependent assay boundaries is not established by inspected sources.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M6 (palbociclib mitigation and single-cell SNP/CNV omics quality control)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease choice for multiplex editing genomic safety)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (dynamic perifusion functional-assay metrology and proxy limits)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O6 show correlated but noninterchangeable SI values and wider perifusion SI range in 10 paired primary-islet donors; O7 shows higher assay SI in the full, partially overlapping cohorts, and O8 reports descriptive chamber-profile alignment after insulin-content normalization. This supports the dynamic biphasic GSIS readout already required by Blueprint §1.2 (line 61) and frozen ranker lines 5810–5812. Incorporation here refers only to that general readout, not to adoption of the paper’s normalization procedure or donor-specific numeric ranges. Primary-islet data are a bridge to SC-islet testing, not product qualification. M7 denotes the bounded quantitative assay/proxy-failure context: method-dependent SI ranges and chamber-normalization sensitivity, not a universal biophysical constant or an SC-islet maturation experiment.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (assay-specific SI and low-glucose shut-off proxy boundaries)
edges.claim_summary: Accept Seat2 addition of insulin-content O19 and SI associations O20–O25 as context for assay/donor dependence. O1/O7 contain inconsistent perifusion means, and O4’s claimed 22-fold SI variation remains internally unresolved, so neither is promoted as a calibrated cutoff. The actual frozen ranker uses dynamic GSIS SI ≥3.0 (line 5583), while Blueprint §1.2 requires <3-min shut-off at 16.7→2.8 mM (line 61), beyond the cheatsheet’s 2.0–3.0 shorthand. This study uses 3→15→3 mM and describes a 20-min return window without t50/t90 (O27); it does not validate, refute, or reset those SC-islet thresholds. Detailed incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (donor-stratum and normalization limits on primary-islet reference assays)
edges.claim_summary: A proposed Gate1 reference protocol could report donor HbA1c/BMI, insulin-content normalization and absolute output alongside SI. HbA1c strata differ in basal secretion (O9), while BMI and metabolically impaired cluster comparisons also show higher stimulated secretion (O13/O16); the original basal-rather-than-stimulated claim is rejected. O26 retains a normal-BMI sex subgroup result despite whole-analysis nonsignificance (O17/O18). Require transparent subgroup denominators and protocol matching; no causal donor-variable effect, clinical potency prediction, SC-islet threshold, or implementation adoption is established. Blueprint §1.2 and ranker Decision Experiment 5 support regulated-function testing generally; this specific reference refinement has unknown incorporation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (EEF1A1/insulated transgene cassette at a safe harbor, promoter silencing)
edges.claim_summary: In human iPSCs, a 0.9 UCOE anti-silencing element kept more EF1a-driven reporter-positive cells at Day 30 (32.0% vs 14.0%, O1), retained rtTA and mScarlet transcript (O2, O3) and preserved doxycycline responsiveness (O4), supporting an insulator-protected constitutive cassette design. No iCasp9, AAVS1 or SC-islet cells were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter silencing as a failure mode of safe-harbor cassettes)
edges.claim_summary: Protection was design-dependent and incomplete: the CBX-only fragment decayed to w/o-UCOE levels (O12), Day 30 RFP+ was only 32.5-38.2% across effective fragments (O11), and the system without SV40 poly-A showed 40 to 85.8% clone-dependent silencing at CYBB and TRBC1 (O18). This qualifies, not contradicts, the assumption that an insulated safe-harbor cassette stays on; per-clone expression checks may be needed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette design)
edges.claim_summary: A chromatin-opening UCOE next to an inducible promoter caused ligand-independent leakage (O5, O8, O9, O10), and an SV40 poly-A spacer between units reduced leakage (O13) while keeping induction (O15) and silencing resistance (O16); AT-rich spacers alone did not (O14). Hypothesis only: could be tested for any constitutive-plus-inducible Blueprint locus; Tet-On/FOXN1 data do not validate the CXCL10 promoter.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 + M3 (HTR1F perturbation and transplant survival); Gate1 (primary-human GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports reduced beta-cell death with 5-HT1F knockdown during transplantation (O3), increased primary-human-islet GSIS and beta-cell cAMP with an antagonist in vitro (O4, O5), and improved glycemia with the antagonist in marginal-mass human-islet xenografts (O6). These are distinct interventions/endpoints supporting cytoprotection and secretory-function priorities, not proof that the antagonist reduced graft death, that survival mediated glycemia, or that the SC-islet product passes Gate1/Gate4. Incorporation refers narrowly to HTR1F targeting as a configured intervention: the frozen Blueprint locus-3 specification and ranker cytokine/ER module catalogs configure other mechanisms, not this target.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 + M6 (HTR1F knockdown or antagonism as a cytoprotection hypothesis; pooled shRNA discovery); Gate1 (secretory-function scope)
edges.claim_summary: The HTR1F screen nomination (O1), knockdown-associated transplant-death reduction (O3), and separate antagonist-associated functional findings (O4-O6) motivate testing HTR1F targeting in SC-islets as an added intervention beyond the frozen configured cytokine/ER modules. The abstract does not test SC-islets or the OpenIslet construct, give effect sizes or safety data, or establish that pharmacological antagonism reproduces knockdown survival effects. In-vitro knockdown-induced proliferation required harmine plus exendin-4 (O2); it cannot be generalized to knockdown or antagonist treatment alone. M6 is retained for pooled-screen discovery, without calling this shRNA experiment CRISPR or omics.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7; Gate4 stress-survival context (hydrophobic CaO2 oxygen generation and catalase-mediated peroxide control)
edges.claim_summary: C2C12/GelMA experiments support the hydrophobic-CaO2/catalase mechanism as a bridge, not exact-product qualification: catalase in GelMA had a reported 19-h versus 33-min half-life (O5), CITG/COTP released H2O2 below the authors' 10 x 10-6 m reference for seven days (O6/O7), and CITG improved myoblast survival (O9/O11/O18). Additional acellular stability and thermal-gelation observations (O19-O21) compare PCL-encapsulated versus unencapsulated CPO, with unresolved printed/rheology CPO doses. Frozen Blueprint section 4.5 already specifies PDMS-CaO2 plus co-immobilized catalase and a stricter <=5.0 uM peroxide screen; adoption of these particular PCL/GelMA placement, half-life and printing findings is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (catalase dosing and early-phase oxygen exposure in the CaO2 bridge)
edges.claim_summary: In C2C12/GelMA, higher catalase than the tested 1:5 optimum correlated with reduced viability (O13), catalase inside PCL particles did not prevent cytotoxic H2O2 at >0.25% w/v particles (O8), and early viability/MTS dips occurred without a demonstrated hyperoxia mechanism (O16). Frozen Blueprint section 4.5 explicitly distinguishes input/retained catalase activity and location, but these myoblast dose-response and transient-toxicity observations cannot be transferred quantitatively to co-localized PDMS-CaO2 or beta-cell safety; their specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (oxygen supply versus cellular demand, hydrogel diffusion physics)
edges.claim_summary: Acellular HOGMPs in DPBS released 0.47-0.65 umol oxygen over 14 days at 0.5-1% w/v against an author-calculated literature-demand estimate of about 0.31 umol per construct (O1); this is not measured construct oxygen consumption. Matrix comparisons report lower oxygen release in GelMA and similar alginate/PEGDA profiles (O2-O4), but their Results 14-day versus Fig 2B up-to-seven-day duration conflict remains unresolved. Frozen Blueprint section 4.5 already models 72-hour oxygen supply/demand for a different PDMS/islet geometry; incorporation of these empirical release figures is not established, and cumulative output does not prove adequate local pO2 throughout the 72-hour target.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 + M7 (iCasp9/AP1903 fail-safe; conditional clonogenic-escape target <=1e-8)
edges.claim_summary: HeLa lentiviral full-length iCasp9/AP20187 shows incomplete 24 h killing and declining per-round killing after survivor reculture (O2, O10, O13-O16); this is mechanistic context for expression and schedule dependence, not a quantitative estimate of SC-islet clonogenic escape. Frozen Blueprint §7 distinguishes the >=99.9% 24 h bulk-kill screen from the <=1e-8 conditional rare-clonogenic-escape target requiring about 3e8 effective detectable opportunities. Neither endpoint equivalence nor product qualification follows from these HeLa measurements; incorporation of the specific repeated-dose result is unestablished.
