edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (maintained iCasp9 expression; candidate insulation and EEF1A1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: The dependence of cell fate on initial iCasp9 and enrichment of low-iCasp9 survivors (O1, O8, O12, O14, O16) support the expression-maintenance rationale already embodied by Blueprint §4.4 and the ranker shared-promoter-silencing mitigation. This study does not test AAVS1, EEF1A1, insulation, DNA methylation, biallelic independence, or a clonogenic escape frequency. The Blueprint explicitly marks anti-silencing function of the 455-bp candidate as pending; HeLa expression selection does not validate it.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual undifferentiated hPSC detection as an oncology-safety release benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: The HEC assay detected undifferentiated hiPSCs down to 0.001%, and MACS enrichment reached 0.00002% (O1, O2), giving quantitative detection limits for residual pluripotent cells in hPSC-derived products. The abstract concerns hPSC-derived products generally, not SC-islets, and the cheatsheet does not state these assay limits.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (verification of the iCasp9 clonogenic-escape threshold in SC-islet batches)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: an HEC-plus-MACS style residual-undifferentiated-cell assay (O2) could serve as an orthogonal release test alongside the suicide-switch fail-safe, but the abstract tests neither SC-islets nor a suicide switch, and its detection limits are given as percentages, so any comparison with the Blueprint's escape threshold needs a unit conversion and direct testing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of edited hPSC lines: hotspot CNV release screen)
edges.claim_summary: The study defines hPSC recurrence hotspots (20 regions cover 90.7%, Table 1; six-probe panel stated as 61%; O5, O6, O7, O14) and shows a supernatant-DNA ddPCR screen concordant with karyotyping in 3 lines (O15). This suggests, as a hypothesis, adding a hotspot CNV screen of the hPSC master line and edited clones to Gate5 genomic-integrity release testing; the work is in undifferentiated hPSC lines, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing and culture-acquired genomic integrity)
edges.claim_summary: Single-cell passaging led to a chromosome 1 gain in HY03 by passage 15 (O16) and the one correctly edited CRISPR clone carried a chromosome 5q CNV (O17), whereas four CCDC40_KO clones showed no abnormality (O18); this supports routine genomic QC of edited hPSC clones, but the clone numbers are very small and the host is a non-islet hiPSC line.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (scope limit of CNV-targeted ddPCR for genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: The recurrent abnormalities identified were only CNVs (O3), none under 10 bp were recurrent (O4), and ddPCR detected trisomy 12 cells from a 10% mixture (O10), so a CNV hotspot panel cannot replace assays for balanced translocations, small variants or off-target base edits that Gate5 lists; the text itself excludes balanced translocations from probe-based detection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nearest element: EEF1A1 promoter in transgene cassettes; no silencing or safety readout)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 compare UCOE fragment and EF1a promoter performance for CD18 surface expression in LAD1 patient CD34+ HSCs; the abstract reports no immune, stress-resilience, silencing, genomic-safety or islet measurement, so it provides no evidence on any Islet-1 gate parameter (EF1a is only a tested promoter, not a silencing or safety measurement).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (hypothesis of pharmacologic enrichment against culture-adapted hPSC survival variants)
edges.claim_summary: ABT-263/ABT-737 and WEHI-539 support a bounded hPSC-bank enrichment hypothesis against BCL-xL-high, YM155-resistant culture-adapted populations (O12-O17, O20-O22); O22 retains the P3/P4 monoculture conflict. ABT-263 reduction was incomplete, resistant cells regrew, and prolonged exposure also killed sensitive cells (O17). This is not validated SC-islet purification, an iCasp9 rescue regimen, or fail-safe replacement. The frozen safety architecture includes surveillance and AP1903 qualification, but adoption of this exact BH3-mimetic enrichment step is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (BCL2L1-associated clonal-selection risk and longitudinal genomic surveillance)
edges.claim_summary: The association of BCL2L1/BCL-xL-high late-passage hESCs with stress resistance and population dominance (O1-O10, O17) supports the broad BCL2L1 clonal-selection surveillance concern already explicit in frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and GMP safety row, and ranker clonal-selection/surveillance blocks. This incorporation label concerns that broad risk and monitoring rationale only; the exact T12/YM155 phenotype, quantitative surveillance thresholds, and hESC-to-SC-islet transfer are not validated by this paper.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (scope of anti-apoptotic stress resistance; boundary with Gate5 iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: Endogenous BCL2L1/BCL-xL upregulation accompanies broad stress resistance and clonal outgrowth in undifferentiated culture-adapted hESCs (O4-O10), providing mechanistic caution when considering anti-apoptotic protection. The paper did not test engineered BCL2/XIAP, cytokine-stressed differentiated beta cells, iCasp9/AP1903, or intrinsic protection of the exact product. Blueprint §4.4 treats XIAP/caspase-9 resistance separately; no contradiction or specific incorporation of these hESC data is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (structural revascularization time course and oxygen-bridge rationale)
edges.claim_summary: In syngeneic rat intraportal native-islet grafts, histological vascular density and vascular area fall by day 1 (O1, O3), then exceed native-islet values at day 14 (O2, O4). This supplies indirect structural support for the already-explicit Gate5 oxygen-bridge rationale (Blueprint sections 1.2 and 4.5), but does not measure oxygen tension, functional perfusion, or oxygen-bridge efficacy; incorporation of this particular rat quantitative series is not established. Species, graft product and liver site differ from the engineered SC-islet/prevascularized device.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (structural revascularization timing versus oxygen-bridge assumptions)
edges.claim_summary: Branching is depressed at the sampled day-3 point (0.465 +/- 0.02 versus native 0.771 +/- 0.017, p = 0.001; O5), and the authors describe return to native values at day 7 (0.726 +/- 0.03; O6); the exact recovery time between sampled points is unresolved. This is an unvalidated transfer qualification for the 72-hour primary bridge target, not proof of a 7-day oxygen requirement or failure of the Blueprint, whose section 4.5 also describes a 336-hour trajectory and exact-product lumen-patency/inosculation benchmarking. This rat histological series neither measures functional perfusion nor calibrates those product-specific kinetics; its specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 dimerizer-induced apoptosis, Locus 4 suicide switch)
edges.claim_summary: iCaspase-9 cells underwent apoptosis on dimerizer exposure while control cells did not (O4), which supports the general inducible-caspase-9 mechanism the Blueprint uses. The cells are human dermal endothelial cells with a retroviral vector and the dimerizer AP20187, not hPSC-derived islet cells at a safe harbor, and the abstract reports no values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (mixed-population design and modeling for tolerable iCasp9-nonresponsive fractions)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: the mixed responder to non-responder cell-ratio design combined with differential-equation modeling (O1, O3, O5) could be adapted to estimate what fraction of iCasp9-silenced or non-responding cells a graft can tolerate. The study measures vessel disruption in endothelial cells, not clonogenic escape, so its 17% and 22% thresholds do not transfer to the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex genomic safety; GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 report combined CAR KI/quadplex KO feasibility and assay-bounded translocation non-detection / no significant off-target edits in human T cells. This is a source-checked non-islet bridge to genomic QC, not an estimated low-translocation rate or a contradiction of GRAVEYARD_006: assay power, hPSC transfer and a combined base-edit-plus-DSB-nuclease regimen are not established. The frozen Blueprint section 5, graveyard rule 006 and ranker engineering prior already warn against zero-risk/zero-DSB assumptions; this abstract does not calibrate or remove gamma_B, prove absence of DSBs, or establish clinical safety. Specific incorporation of INSERT is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nickase-stimulated targeted knock-in hypothesis for Blueprint payload loci)
edges.claim_summary: O4 reports enhanced ABE8e-stimulated HDR efficiency using a new sgRNA design and rAAV template in human T cells, while O1 reports CAR KI combined with quadplex KO. Testing this nickase-stimulated KI approach for hPSC payload installation is a bounded hypothesis; no hPSC, AAVS1/GAPDH, exact Blueprint donor-size, stable expression, fail-safe function or DSB-absence result is supplied. Blueprint sections 4.1 and 4.4 specify different payload loci/cargo and require separate qualification; adoption of INSERT is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M-target engineering versus allorecognition protection)
edges.claim_summary: O1 includes B2M in a reported >95% quadplex KO platform, supporting Gate2A/M1 target relevance but not a separately resolved B2M editing percentage. Blueprint section 4.1 uses B2M disruption within a distinct hPSC immune-cloak construct. This abstract supplies no HLA-surface, allogeneic host immune-evasion or islet-protection endpoint; anti-cancer efficacy in O5 cannot substitute for those outcomes. Incorporation of this specific engineering result is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (donor design for Locus 4 AAVS1 knock-in: donor-derived integration)
edges.claim_summary: Linear dsDNA gave 69.78% donor-derived LgIns, with near full-length and concatemeric insertions (O11-O13); phosphorylated-donor samples had lower LgIns and large-deletion frequencies (O14-O15, O19-O20), while HDR similarity is descriptive (O16-O17). This supports testing end chemistry and donor-integration QC for Blueprint section 4.1 nonviral donors and section 4.4 AAVS1 payloads. Transfer from EPOR short point-mutation donors to multi-kb SC-islet payloads/AAV6 is unvalidated, and the phos donor has additional orientation segments. Ranker Y-02 already specifies zero concatemer/backbone insertions for a different integrase wildcard; exact adoption of this end-chemistry hypothesis remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base-editing genomic integrity: DSB intermediates and translocations)
edges.claim_summary: C-to-G base editors generated substantial intermediate DSBs with deletions and translocations between the target and off-targets (O1, O2, O3, O4), so base-editing safety checks under Gate5 should be editor-class-specific rather than assuming DSB-free editing. The abstract does not state the cell type or frequencies and does not test other base editor classes.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (mitigation of base-editing DSB byproducts)
edges.claim_summary: HMCES shielding of abasic sites reduced CGBE-initiated DSBs without affecting substitutions (O5, O6), which suggests, as a hypothesis, testing HMCES-aided CGBEs if C-to-G editing is used in multiplex hPSC engineering; the abstract gives no magnitude and no hPSC data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing genomic safety; GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: O11/O19 report four-locus SpCas9 translocations (individual event frequencies 0.2%-1.6%; aggregate estimate up to one in 17-25 diploid cells), while Pin-point abnormalities were described as unlikely; O6 reports better proliferation qualitatively. This is a mechanistic bridge from primary T cells to genomic-safety design, not a measured hPSC risk or calibration of gamma_B. Blueprint sections 2/5/7 and ranker engineering priors already recognize DSB and nickase/deaminase risk, but incorporation of these particular rates is not established. The study does not test or lift GRAVEYARD_006's base/prime-plus-multiple-nuclease precaution.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (off-target base edits and transient RNA deamination)
edges.claim_summary: O8 finds base edits at four of 456 selected CHANGE-seq-nominated candidate sites (0.7%-2.2%); O13 describes approximately 60 additional RNA C-to-U events at day 1, and O14/O15 count transcriptome perturbations. These are guide-, cell-, assay- and time-specific observations, not a genome-wide zero-risk finding or product release limit. Ranker and GRAVEYARD_006 already acknowledge deaminase/bystander hazards, but adoption of these DNA/RNA findings at their reported specificity is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (paired-nick TRAC knock-in plus multiplex base-edit knockout; AAVS1 iCasp9 transfer hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O16/O17 show a joint 60%-90% depletion range and author-described comparable TRAC CAR knock-in to SpCas9 (~20%; separate Pin-point estimate unreported); O12 reports undetectable translocations without an assay limit. Hypothesis: evaluate this aptamer-directed format for the Blueprint section 4.4 AAVS1 iCasp9 cassette plus B2M/CIITA editing in hPSCs. No such hPSC/cargo/locus result or switch function is demonstrated, paired nicks do not establish zero DSB risk, and O18 does not establish an arm-specific AAV insertion advantage. Incorporation of the specific platform is unresolved from the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO at Locus 1: complete versus partial HLA-I ablation)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O4: in MSCs, epigenetic B2M-SE repression lowered HLA-I below an allogeneic T cell activation threshold and the cells survived better in a humanized mouse. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (oxygen-delivery device and peroxide-toxicity design principle)
edges.claim_summary: The general principle of combining a peroxide oxygen source with catalase is explicitly included in the frozen Blueprint section 4.5 and Stage-2 roadmap. Here, elevated medium oxygen over 28 days (O1) and higher metabolic activity/lower LDH with catalase-containing vs matched catalase-free hydrogels (O6, O8) provide bounded cell-line bridge support for that principle. This incorporation label applies to the general mechanism, not adoption of the PVA multilayer architecture, DMSO fabrication or its exact results; no SC-islet oxygen or 72-hour product-qualification threshold is demonstrated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate5 with secondary Gate1 functional readouts / M3, M7 (formulation-dependent hypoxic cell-line response)
edges.claim_summary: The 0.1% (w/v) CPO formulation reached 170.0 ± 9.1% relative metabolic activity at day 7 and supported GSIS (O2, O3); the 0.5% formulation had reduced metabolic activity at unspecified later times, increased LDH and lower INS expression (O4, O5, O7). The abstract supports formulation-dependent benefit and harm in 1.1B4 cells, but unspecified references, different or unreported assay times and absent quantitative contrasts do not establish a tight non-monotonic loading window, optimal dose or peroxide/alkaline mechanism. Whether these exact PVA-specific findings are incorporated is not established by the frozen references; they do not set PDMS-CaO2 or SC-islet parameters.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (intraportal coagulation/complement-associated IBMIR and graft engraftment)
edges.claim_summary: Separately TF- or PAI-1-targeted rat islets reduced plasma TAT/C3a and retained 100% glucose-defined graft survival through day 30 versus complete control failure by day 10 in athymic mice (O12, O14-O16, O19). This suggests a conditional intraportal IBMIR intervention hypothesis, not autoimmune/NK/macrophage protection or intrinsic stress resilience. The frozen Blueprint already evaluates SA-THBD-containing adjuncts (§4.2); no superiority/additivity to that comparator, exact hPSC-islet stack compatibility, dual TF+PAI-1 knockout, or immunocompetent/humanized-host protection was tested. Exact-result incorporation is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease editing genomic safety, off-target)
edges.claim_summary: At selected doses, rat-islet TF and PAI-1 indel frequencies were 18.09% ± 0.52% and 22.46% ± 2.25% (O2/O3; mean ± SD). O5 found no significant increase at two TF/nine PAI-1 predicted off-target sites, not zero off-target risk or equivalence. This does not test multiplex structural variants, translocations, selected hPSC clones, clonogenic safety, or an iCasp9 fail-safe. Frozen GRAVEYARD_006 requires broader structural QC, and the ranker multiplicative edit-burden term is an engineering prior; neither is empirically waived or calibrated by this panel. Exact-result incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M1 (endocrine-function scope of gene-edit cytocompatibility)
edges.claim_summary: At selected rat-islet doses, CCK-8, static GSIS secretion profiles and stimulation indices showed no reported significant deterioration relative to controls (O6-O9); higher eVLP doses were cytotoxic (O4). Null tests do not establish equivalence, human SC-islet compatibility, dynamic biphasic GSIS, rapid low-glucose shutoff, or full-product manufacturing yield. The Blueprint Gate1 dynamic-function target is broader than these assays; exact empirical incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta:alpha:delta 60:30:10 paracrine-architecture reference; SC-islet composition)
edges.claim_summary: In this human SC-islet differentiation model, artemether shifted progenitor/hormone composition (O10-O14) without demonstrated improvement in static GSIS (O15); the distinct pooled sorted-cell assay gave mixed hormone outcomes without demonstrated alpha-to-beta conversion (O16). This qualifies interpreting more insulin-positive cells as improved function. The frozen Blueprint section 6 specifies live-lineage purification followed by controlled 60:30:10 input reseeding and a bounded mixture/function comparison; unsorted artemether cultures do not directly test or contradict achieved final Blueprint composition, dynamic GSIS, or glucagon counter-regulation. Incorporation of this exact drug-specific observation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M6 (SC-islet progenitor fate allocation and enrichment informed by single-cell multiomics)
edges.claim_summary: PAX4 reporter-enriched S5d4 fractions mostly produced insulin-positive cells, whereas ARX reporter-positive fractions mostly produced glucagon-positive cells (O3-O6); REST inhibition modestly increased PAX4-reporter and insulin-positive cells (O8-O9). These nominate process hypotheses, not demonstrated replacement of the Blueprint section 6 Stage-7 CD49a/NTPDase3/CD9 live-surface purification workflow. Findings use one engineered reporter line, n = 3 differentiations for the potency/REST assays, and absent numerical effect sizes. M6 denotes the actual single-cell-omics work, not a restriction to Gate5; product transfer and exact incorporation remain unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (granzyme/FAS effector pressure from autoreactive CD8+ T cells)
edges.claim_summary: Perforin carries much of CD8+ CTL beta-cell killing in NOD mice: inhibitor cut islet cell death by approximately 50% in vitro and ~50% in vivo (O1, O2), diabetes incidence fell from approximately 60% to 10% with perforin deficiency (O3) and from 91.2% to 58.4% with 7-day inhibitor (O4). Mouse islets and NOD CTLs, not hPSC-derived grafts; the cheatsheet names granzyme B inhibition, not perforin.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B element; perforin-pathway protection)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: because perforin sits upstream of granzyme delivery and its loss or inhibition protects NOD beta cells (O3, O4) without altering T cell activation, expansion or infiltration (O5-O10), perforin-pathway protection (transient pharmacological inhibition, or a cell-intrinsic equivalent) could be tested beside the SERPINB9 element. Untested in human or edited grafts; protection was partial and systemic.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 PD-L1; staged cell-free product-conditioned effluent functional screen, IIP-0005/DEC-083)
edges.claim_summary: EndoC-βH1 EV binding (O9), HEK293 expression controls (O10), and PD-L1-overexpressing NIT-1 EV effects/reversal in activated NOD splenocyte assays (O11-O14) provide mechanistic rationale for the bounded PD-1-responsive conditioned-medium screen already explicitly adopted in frozen Blueprint §4.3 and ranker lines 5743–5760 with PMID39508879. This incorporation claim covers the planned assay rationale and safeguards, not adoption of each EV fold-change as a product parameter or proven intrinsic/graft protection. Human-islet EV induction (O5,O8) and soluble-PD-L1 nonsignificance (O19) remain different readouts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1, M4 (hypothesized EV-mediated graft checkpoint extension and circulating graft-protection biomarker)
edges.claim_summary: EV-mediated checkpoint extension from engineered SC-islet grafts and use of plasma EV PD-L1 as a graft-protection biomarker remain hypotheses. O17/O18 report positive C-peptide correlations in human observational cohorts; plasma EVs were not isolated specifically from beta cells, and the study has no engineered graft, human responder efficacy, pharmacokinetics, or causal protection endpoint. Frozen references explicitly adopt a bounded functional screen, which does not establish adoption or validity of these broader product/biomarker claims.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 / M1 (PD-L1 pathway dependence versus source attribution, intrinsic survival and indirect-APC protection)
edges.claim_summary: Anti-PD-L1 reversal in NIT-1-EV/NOD cultures supports pathway dependence in that assay; it does not show that exact-product effluent activity is due to graft-derived PD-L1 rather than receiver/accessory-cell induction. This boundary is expressly retained in Blueprint §4.3 and ranker 5756–5760. No defined autoreactive-antigen or host-APC experiment, target-cell survival, or preservation of unrelated immunity was measured here; GY-010 indirect-pathway precautions remain applicable and are not contradicted by this paper.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (proliferative off-target depletion before the clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: Bleo reduced SOX9+/KI67+ fractions 10-/4-fold (O3-O4) and improved 4-week graft morphology/proliferation endpoints in immunodeficient mice (O15-O18). This supports a bounded alternative-process hypothesis, not measured clonogenic eradication or genomic safety. The frozen Blueprint already specifies S7w0 ZM447439 plus lineage sorting and a separate pan-lineage iCasp9/rare-escape release contract (Blueprint §§6-7; ranker whole_product_safety_model and two_stage_orthogonal_psc_purge_requirement); exact incorporation of this Bleo-specific regimen is not established. Transfer to the edited whole product needs direct comparison, DNA-damage assessment (O6), and timing-toxicity qualification (O20); the study does not test iCasp9, rare clonogenic escape or long-term tumor safety.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet enrichment and glucose-responsive function)
edges.claim_summary: In human hESC-/iPSC-derived clusters, Bleo enriched insulin-producing cells about 1.7-fold (O7), with Results-reported beta-cell/maturation transcripts (O9-O10) and stronger high-glucose Ca2+/perifusion responses (O13-O14); sorted insulin-positive-cell content showed no detected difference (O11). The frozen Blueprint already uses live lineage purification and controlled 60:30:10 reaggregation (§6), but exact incorporation of this Bleo-specific finding is not established. These findings support the human SC-islet manufacturing domain; they do not establish a stimulation index, biphasic/shut-off acceptance threshold, absolute viable beta-cell yield, preserved alpha/delta function or qualification of the exact edited product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (innate blood-contact reaction, IBMIR; non-genetic islet surface protection for intraportal delivery)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports protection from IBMIR after biotin/avidin heparin surface coating in a blood loop and an allogeneic porcine model (O1/O2), using barely 40 IU per full-size clinical transplant (O5). A localized non-genetic coating is an unvalidated adjunct hypothesis for intraportal delivery: primary-islet glucose-challenge function and qualitative mouse cure similarity (O3/O4) provide limited compatibility context, not cure-rate equivalence or SC-islet qualification. Blueprint sections 1.2, 4.2 and 8 already recognize thrombo-inflammatory protection and discuss distinct SA-THBD/SA-CD47/SA-FasL adjuncts; adoption of this heparin-specific mechanism/dose is not established. O6/O7 safety claims are unquantified abstract conclusions.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1+/NKX6.1+ progenitor specification and SC-islet glucose responsiveness)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link M1466:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=matched_domain | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O1,O2 | text_sha256=e8fcf9503cde38155311d5a8c3d368d2385cfa951df301606cff954bdb1f999c]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (progenitor-stage ECM-integrin-TRPV-CaMKII lever as a manufacturing upgrade)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4 and O6 propose an ECM (collagen I/IV)-integrin-TRPV-Ca2+-CaMKII-HDAC4/MEF2 route to NKX6.1-enriched progenitors that the cheatsheet's Gate1 elements do not mention. It is an untested hypothesis for Islet-1 manufacturing, with no quantities in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M3 (adenosine cytoprotection perturbation in primary human islets; hypoxia-conditioning bridge)
edges.claim_summary: In primary cadaveric human islets, 24 h 1 mM AD preconditioning increased viability and SI versus hypoxia alone after 48 h at 1% O2 followed by R2/R24/R48 (O11/O15); these measured endpoints showed no significant difference from normoxic controls (O12/O14), without proving equivalence. This supports a primary-islet bridge to intrinsic stress resilience, not edited SC-islet or exact-product qualification. Blueprint §§1.2/4.5 bound hypoxia protection and history/recovery testing, but adoption of this specific AD regimen and values is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; demand-side complement to supply-side oxygen)
edges.claim_summary: Testing transient AD preconditioning as a complement to the Blueprint §4.5 PDMS-CaO2/catalase oxygen bridge is an unvalidated transfer hypothesis. O5 measures reduced resazurin reductive activity, not OCR; O11/O15 show improved viability/SI after 48 h hypoxia, not a 72-hour assembled-product oxygen budget. No demand-reduction factor or improved pO2 is established. O19 has unresolved D0/D4 timing and cannot substantiate 48-hour secretion recovery; specific incorporation of this proposal is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M1 (absolute insulin output versus static GSIS ratios during a cytoprotection perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: Absolute insulin content and HG secretion decrease after 24 h AD despite nonsignificant SI/RI differences (O2/O3 versus O4/O21), with separate non-hypoxic withdrawal recovery (O7/O8). Preserved static ratios therefore do not prove preserved absolute endocrine output or Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS/rapid shutoff. The frozen ranker Y-03 already flags adenosine-associated GSIS liability for a CD39/CD73 comparator, but that continuous paracrine mechanism is not this transient regimen and its specific quantitative incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (HLA class I and PD-L1 mechanistic relevance)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 provide abstract-level human-islet evidence of reduced HLA class I induction and increased PD-L1, a bounded mechanistic bridge to the adaptive-immune gates. Frozen Blueprint sections 1.2, 3.2 and 4.3 already include HLA editing and the CXCL10::SERPINB9-PD-L1 element, but these expression findings do not test human alloreactive/autoreactive killing or indirect APC presentation, functional checkpoint activity, or the engineered SC-islet product. Claim-specific incorporation of the ZnT8-antibody findings is unknown; generic PD-L1 inclusion does not establish adoption of this antibody route.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M3 (ZnT8-associated inflammatory stress and in vivo graft function)
edges.claim_summary: O8 reports human-islet binding immunoglobulin protein attenuation; O7 reports mouse beta-cell protection/ER-stress suppression, while O4 and O5 report mouse-host graft glycemic function and autoimmune-NOD reversal/remission. O6 limits the reported efficacy to ZnT8-associated inflammatory stress, and O1 has unresolved wording and is not counted as favorable evidence. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and the ranker Gate4 terms include intrinsic ER/cytokine resilience, but the antibody-specific results do not qualify the edited SC-islet product or imply protection from direct cytotoxicity; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation period and beta cell content)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 report a 19-day induction period and up to approximately 70% beta cell content for a GCN-reconstructing protocol. This supports the general Gate1 manufacturing domain, but the abstract lacks absolute yield, off-target lineage composition and dynamic GSIS/low-glucose shut-off data needed to assess the frozen Blueprint Gate1 contract (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61,76). Specific adoption of this protocol or its parameters is unknown; beta-cell content is not the Blueprint 60:30:10 re-aggregation recipe.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M6 (human developmental single-cell GCN benchmarking of SC-islet differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O7 motivate testing whether Islet-1 differentiation can reproduce human developmental pancreatic GCNs, with attention to human-mouse differences in robustness and dorsal-ventral progenitor propensity. M6 follows the explicit single-cell/omics taxonomy, independently of Gate1. The frozen Blueprint specifies lineage, composition and dynamic-function requirements (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61,76), but this packet cannot establish claim-specific incorporation of GCN benchmarking or its performance in the exact edited product. No network threshold or validated improvement magnitude is available.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (SC-islet function after mouse transplantation)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment and off-target SC-EC depletion)
edges.claim_summary: O9 and O11 report that CD49a/CD133 dual sorting of hPSC-derived SC-islets gave >75% INS+NKX6.1+ cells and fewer enterochromaffin-like cells than unsorted. The cheatsheet states CD49a enrichment and SC-EC elimination as Gate1 elements but not these figures or the added CD133, and the EC effect was not tested for CD49a alone.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (adding CD133/PROM1 to the CD49a purification step)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10 and O12 show dual CD49a/CD133 sorting gave the highest purity and most efficient GCG+ removal vs CD49a alone, with CD133 alone enriching CFTR+ ductal-like cells (O8). It is a hypothesis that adding CD133 to the CD49a step could remove alpha/polyhormonal cells; the cheatsheet does not mention CD133, and CD133 marks immature beta cells (O3).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS stimulation index as a separate criterion from purity)
edges.claim_summary: O15, O14 and O17 show that sorting raised beta cell number and total insulin (O13) but not the static-GSIS stimulation index or insulin per beta cell, so purification should not be assumed to improve function. This qualifies, and does not contradict, the Gate1 SI benchmark (dynamic perifusion in the cheatsheet; static GSIS here).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M6 (SC-islet differentiation, composition and functional assays)
edges.claim_summary: The shortened-S4 LN-521 protocol supplies human SC-islet manufacturing and GSIS evidence, including biphasic 16.1-/6.1-fold insulin release (O10), but its day-43 H1 profile retains 12% EC-like cells and reports 17% alpha/1% delta cells (O5/O19/O23), with approximately 40%–50% aggregation loss (O21). Frozen Blueprint Gate1 and sorting/re-aggregation rules (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61,245-247) require <1% EC QC and a 60:30:10 input recipe; these unedited, unsorted S6 data neither qualify that product nor establish rapid shut-off, alpha-cell counter-regulation, or equivalence to primary human islets. Specific incorporation of this paper's values is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual proliferation, purity and bounded graft safety observations)
edges.claim_summary: S6w4 residual Ki-67+ cells were 0.88 ± 0.37% and NEUROD1− cells 2.2 ± 1.32% (O2/O3); post-transplant scRNA-seq detected 1% proliferating beta cells and a minor non-proliferating stellate population (O24/O25). The Discussion reports no graft growth/cysts at 6 months (O18), without a specific safety denominator. Frozen Blueprint:65,253-260 and GRAVEYARD_002 require pan-lineage switch/clonogenic qualification: marker fractions and limited NSG-eye observations do not estimate clonogenic escape, test iCasp9, or establish the Blueprint's <=10^-4 residual clonogenic target. Specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3 (in vivo graft endocrine function and maturation)
edges.claim_summary: Intraocular HS980 SC-islet grafts in STZ-diabetic NSG mice showed hyperglycemia reversal by 3 months, increasing human C-peptide and improving within-cohort IPGTT (O13-O15); the 20-week scRNA profile shifted from 22% to 54% mature and 28% to 20% early beta cells, with 74% total post-transplant beta fraction (O16/O17/O22, one shared composition comparison). These T5 host outcomes support an endocrine-maturation bridge to frozen Blueprint Gate1 (:61); immune-deficient hosts, eye site, early exogenous insulin and unedited unsorted product prevent qualification of the Blueprint graft or its immune/oxygen/safety gates. M3 denotes in vivo graft evidence under STAGE1-SCREENING-RUBRIC.md:45-52; M4 clinical/regulatory evidence is not present. Specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (cluster-resolved functional readout for SC-islet GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 suggest label-free impedance on MEA chips could report glucose-responsive secretion from single SC-islets, which the cheatsheet's Gate1 does not mention (it names perifusion GSIS and a stimulation-index benchmark). The abstract gives no correlation values or SI-equivalent, so this is a hypothesis for a functional QC readout only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (pooled GSIS stimulation index as a population average)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 report cluster-to-cluster and intra-cluster heterogeneity of secretion that pooled secretion assays obscured, so an SI benchmark from pooled islets describes an average rather than every cluster. It qualifies, and does not contradict, the Gate1 SI benchmark; no heterogeneity magnitude is given and the cheatsheet cannot show whether the Blueprint already tracks it.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3, M4 (candidate adjunct for non-invasive graft imaging)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O3/O21 support graft detection and association with graft status at 7–8 weeks in intramuscular non-humanized nude-mouse xenografts; O4/O19 support in-vitro purity-related binding and blocking specificity, retaining unresolved reported coefficient pairs. This motivates an adjunct imaging hypothesis for human-islet/SC-islet graft monitoring. O22 and Discussion identify an endocrine-islet marker rather than beta-cell-only mass. Actual Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and the frozen ranker Gate1 branch concern lineage purity, regulated GSIS and low-glucose shut-off; PET does not establish those functions or immune/oxygen protection. Clinical/edited-product transfer and claim-specific adoption are not established; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (translational imaging/dosimetry scope)
edges.claim_summary: O7/O8 bound specificity to tested tissue assays; O16 shows rat renal clearance rather than an absence of all extra-pancreatic in-vivo uptake. O17/O18 are preliminary rat-derived predicted human dosimetry (0.025 mSv/MBq; about 400 MBq/year under the authors' assumed 10 mSv/year limit), with unavailable Table S2 cells and an unresolved bladder-dose unit issue. O9 shows no Alexa binding in tested mouse/pig pancreas, limiting target-mediated transfer from these host biodistribution models. These observations qualify a clinical-monitoring hypothesis, not human radiation safety, a verified regulatory limit, or Gate5 oxygen/fail-safe qualification. Specific Blueprint incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (primary-human-islet endocrine function in a vascular-niche model; no SC-islet differentiation or clinical benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link M1496:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O2 | text_sha256=7247a8e7c48e6ef14bc0509de847fb21d9c073fd81054a62cd52bf8bd22d0d95]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascular-niche and oxygen-bridge scope only; no fail-safe or genomic-safety evidence)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 supply an ex vivo human islet-BVO assembloid/testbed observation, not a demonstration of the Blueprint 72-hour vascular/oxygen bridge. Frozen Blueprint section 1.2, Stage 2 and section 4.5 already specify pre-lumenized isogenic iEC:iPericyte microvessels, direct lumen-patency/inosculation qualification and an oxygen carrier; this abstract gives no oxygen tension, oxygen consumption, perfusion, host anastomosis, hypoxic survival or graft outcome. Transfer to that product remains unvalidated, and incorporation of this specific study or testbed is unknown; no suicide-switch or genomic-safety endpoint is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (measurability of rare tumorigenic or clonogenic contaminants in a cell product)
edges.claim_summary: O4 reports that all laboratories reached a 0.0001% HeLa-in-hMSC detection limit, with no colonies in hMSC-alone wells (O5) and an inter-laboratory CV of 18% (O2). The matrix is hMSCs with a HeLa spike, not hPSC-derived islets or iCasp9 escape clones, and the cheatsheet cannot show whether the Blueprint names a release assay for residual clonogenic cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (soft-agar release assay for residual transformed cells in the Islet-1 product)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 suggest a D-SAC-type assay, sized at 314-570 wells per laboratory for a stated false-negative rate, could be tested as an orthogonal release readout for residual proliferative or escaped cells in a hPSC-derived islet product. The cheatsheet does not name such an assay; the spike-in model and positive-control concentration change (0.002% HeLa) limit transfer, and no SC-islet data exist in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet composition and paracrine architecture, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference)
edges.claim_summary: Representative H1 stage-7 flow gives 26.7% SST+/PDX1+ and 31.6% SST+/CHGA+ (O2/O3), supporting a possible hPSC-derived delta-cell input for Gate1/M2, not a measured 60:30:10 product or endocrine-function pass. Frozen Blueprint lines 61 and 244–246 already specify tri-hormonal composition and lineage sorting/re-aggregation; incorporation of this exact FGF2/FGF7 differentiation protocol or its reported yields is not established. The packet reports no combined-islet GSIS or somatostatin-secretion experiment.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (delta-cell component of a 60:30:10 SC-islet)
edges.claim_summary: Protocol-specific candidate hypothesis: evaluate separately differentiated FGF2/FGF7-directed SC-delta cells as input to the existing Blueprint lineage-sorting and 60:30:10 re-aggregation workflow (frozen Blueprint 244–246; ranker 5595–5611). General tri-hormonal reconstitution is already planned; adoption of this exact source protocol is unknown. O18 requires line-specific yield checks, and discussion paragraph 153 describes lower maturity than human-islet delta cells (attributed to Chen et al. 2024) and uncertain additional cell identities. No combined-islet functional benefit or validated edited-product transfer is shown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 manufacturing geometry; Gate5 oxygen-bridge cluster-size boundary
edges.claim_summary: O20 is an approximately 200–250 µm stage-6 culture benchmark. Frozen Blueprint lines 65 and 77 already require ≤120 µm final clusters (<5% >150 µm at assembly); lines 245–246 and ranker 5595–5611 specify dissociation, sorting and re-aggregation. Source-culture size therefore cannot certify the downstream geometry or oxygen gate and does not directly contradict an already planned resizing process. O9 warns of up to 50% loss in the source aggregation step; this is not the Blueprint's separate re-aggregation handling-loss estimate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-beta maturation and GSIS function)
edges.claim_summary: O3 supports qualitative improvement of glucose-stimulated insulin release in human hPSC-derived sBC cultures versus unspecified controls, matching Gate1/M2's endocrine-function domain (frozen Blueprint section 1.2 and Stage 1). The abstract supplies no SI, dynamic biphasic response, shut-off time, effect size or exact-product qualification; O4 is separate in vivo feasibility context with an unspecified host and no quantitative endpoint. Incorporation of this cryopreservation-specific finding is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet purification and enrichment; Blueprint uses CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 motivate testing cryopreservation as a manufacturing adjunct alongside the Blueprint's existing live-lineage sorting and re-aggregation workflow (frozen Blueprint Stage 1; ranker constant_isogenic_backbone.dosing_unit). Enrichment and progenitor depletion are qualitative abstract claims; the abstract does not establish a sorting-free protocol, head-to-head superiority, absolute viable endocrine yield or preservation of the edited 60:30:10 product. Whether this specific step is already incorporated is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (proliferative-progenitor depletion as a candidate adjunct to clonogenic safety controls)
edges.claim_summary: O2 suggests testing whether cryopreservation can reduce the proliferative-cell burden relevant to Gate5 safety, whose frozen Blueprint Stage 3 and ranker whole_product_safety_model require quantified residual proliferating fractions and clonogenic escape qualification. The abstract does not identify the depleted progenitor lineage, quantify residual clonogens or demonstrate tumor-risk reduction, prodrug killing, genomic integrity or oxygen bridging. This is an unvalidated safety-transfer hypothesis and does not replace pan-lineage iCasp9 qualification or rebut GRAVEYARD_002.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and survival; supportive niche cells)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: embryonic-type macrophages are reported to support endocrine differentiation and viability in vitro and to enhance engraftment (O2, O3, O4), so a macrophage niche could be tested as a differentiation or engraftment aid; the cheatsheet states no such element. Evidence is abstract-level and unquantified, the engraftment host is unstated, and the abstract does not test macrophage phagocytosis of grafts (Gate3).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hPSC to beta-like cell differentiation capacity)
edges.claim_summary: O13, O14 and O16 support in-vitro differentiation capacity: higher day-27 NKX6.1/INS expression and approximately 60% insulin-producing (C-peptide+) cells, while O6 reports no adverse impact on PP markers without establishing equivalence. This is matched to the differentiation part of Gate1/M2 only. O17 measures end-of-culture supernatant insulin, with no glucose-stimulated/perifusion response, low-glucose shut-off or 60:30:10 tri-hormonal architecture measurement; these data do not qualify the actual Blueprint Gate1 contract (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md §1.2). Specific incorporation of this protocol is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization within the oxygen-bridge scope; prevascularized graft)
edges.claim_summary: The specific co-differentiation method is an unvalidated manufacturing/vascularization hypothesis for Gate5/M3, supported only by in-vitro EC fractions (13.9% in O7; approximately 7% in the earlier iteration O20) and pericyte markers (O8). The frozen Blueprint already specifies pre-lumenized isogenic 3:1 iEC:iPericyte microvessels from a parallel mesodermal stream (§1.2, Stage2 and §4.5); this is not a newly identified absence of vascularization. Incorporation of this particular co-differentiation route is unknown. There is no perfusion, host inosculation, oxygenation, hypoxic survival or 72-hour bridge test. Day-27 CD34 nonsignificance (O15) does not establish equivalence, vessel persistence or loss.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic suicide switch; HSV-TK, Cdk1-linked, versus Locus 4 iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: a proliferation-coupled HSV-TK switch (O6 two-phase killing, O7, O8 no regrowth over 8 days) removes dividing cells while sparing non-dividing cells that secrete more insulin (O15, O16), so it could also serve as a pre-transplant enrichment step; the cheatsheet states only iCasp9/AP1903 at AAVS1. Evidence is a single mouse βiPLC clone with no escape frequency, so it does not address the <1e-6 threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (drug-inducible kill-switch ablating dividing cells)
edges.claim_summary: A GCV-inducible switch killed knock-in cells in 2D (O5, O6) and in a perfused 3D chip (O10, O11) without toxicity to TK-negative parental cells (O12). Different effector, species and cell type from the hPSC-derived iCasp9 design, so this supports only the general switch concept.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perfusion GSIS readout and function after gene editing)
edges.claim_summary: On-chip perfusion GSIS showed glucose responsiveness in line 2 (O1) and no significant difference between parental and non-GCV Cdk1-TK knock-in cells (O17), but content stayed below MIN6 (O18). Mouse reprogrammed line, no stimulation index, so it cannot be compared with the Gate1 SI benchmark.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (HLA class I reduction plus PD-L1 induction on human beta cells; Locus 3 PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: TRP raises PD-L1 while avoiding or attenuating IFN-γ-induced HLA-I in ECN90 cells and primary human islets (O2–O7, O13–O16, O25), supporting the molecular direction of the frozen Blueprint HLA-I cloak plus Locus-3 PD-L1 rationale (§3.2, §4.1–4.3). This is a justified molecular bridge, not an allogeneic rejection assay or proof of CIITA/B2M editing, PD-L1 causality, SC-islet protection, or the exact construct; the TRP-specific finding’s incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive PPI-specific CD8+ T-cell recognition of beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: TRP-pretreated ECN90 reduced PPI15–24-TCR Jurkat reporter activation (O17) with accompanying PD-1 reduction (O18), supporting a bounded Gate2B autoantigen-recognition bridge to Blueprint §1.2/§4.3. Peptide-pulsed antiviral-TCR responses were inhibited similarly (O24), so autoantigen-selective protection is not established. No primary memory-T-cell killing, host-APC pathway, or PD-L1-dependence test was performed; lower PD-1 is not proof of stronger checkpoint signaling. TRP-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1; IFN-γ response of human beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: TRP suppresses endogenous IFN-γ-induced CXCL10 while increasing endogenous PD-L1 (O4, O8, O12–O15); AKT inhibition and activator results provide bounded mechanistic context (O9, O20, O22–O23). This raises an unvalidated compatibility question for the CXCL10-driven Locus-3 shield in Blueprint §4.3 and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9, not demonstrated cassette failure: endogenous mRNA does not distinguish promoter regulation from post-transcriptional effects, and no edited SC-islet cassette was tested. It neither overturns GRAVEYARD_001 nor establishes that the TRP-specific concern is incorporated; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual pluripotent-cell release testing alongside the iCasp9 clonogenic fail-safe and genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: Candidate non-destructive adjunct to Gate5/M5 release testing: supernatant miR-302b detected 0.001% iPSCs (10 cells) in the RPE spike model versus cellular LIN28 0.01% and H-type3 0.1% (O13–O15); mixed-supernatant backgrounds required 0.01% (O16), and the HCT116 scale-up tested 1%/10% spikes rather than a rare-escape threshold (O17). The frozen Blueprint §7 already specifies post-purge residual-PSC and conditional clonogenic escape targets of <=1e-8 with effective clonogenic denominators; the analytical marker result here (0.001% = 1e-5 fraction) measures neither AP1903 survival nor whole-product clonogenic escape, tumorigenicity, or common-mode batch failure. No SC-islet or vascular-product assay was performed, and specific incorporation of this miRNA adjunct is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and control of nonendocrine expansion)
edges.claim_summary: APH raises day-27 C-peptide-positive fraction (O1/O2), reduces nonendocrine representation (O6), and improves the poorly differentiating 1018E line (O20). This motivates testing a differentiation-process option, but does not establish the exact edited 60:30:10 product, achieved monohormonal composition, or biphasic function. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and §6 specify lineage sorting, yield accounting and re-aggregation; ranker lines 5595–5611 specifies S7w0 ZM447439 plus live sorting. These source-checked scopes do not establish incorporation of the particular APH process, so incorporation is unknown rather than inferred from a keyword absence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (graft outgrowth/cyst suppression alongside quantitative clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: APH-pretreated MEL1 grafts show fewer large growths (O12, calendar anchor unresolved), 2.6-fold versus 53-fold bioluminescence growth relative to week 2 at week 22 (O13), fewer cysts (O14), and supporting iPSC cyst counts 0/3 versus 2/2 (O19). These small non-humanized NSG cohorts suggest an upstream proliferation-limiting process; they do not establish whole-product genomic safety, iCasp9/AP1903 killing, clonogenic escape bounds or safety of APH replication stress. Blueprint §4.4 and §7 specify biallelic AAVS1 iCasp9 and quantitative whole-product clonogenic qualification; no APH adoption is established by the reviewed provisions, so incorporation remains unknown. GRAVEYARD_006 concerns multiplex editing risk and is neither tested nor falsified here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic biphasic GSIS and rapid low-glucose shutoff boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O9 is a static glucose fold response averaging 3 (range 2–6), with Results/caption disagreement over C-peptide versus insulin; it cannot qualify the dynamic Gate1 requirement. O25 reports dynamic responses only as comparable to controls (n = 3), without a numerical SI, phase metrics, shutoff kinetics or equivalence test. The boundary itself is explicitly incorporated at frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 (line 61): biphasic GSIS, rapid shutoff <3 min for 16.7 to 2.8 mM glucose, and no basal insulin leak. The already_accounted_for label applies to that existing dynamic-function requirement, not APH adoption or unsupported SI values 1.44/2.66.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization of the subcutaneous graft site; recipient-side oxygen conditioning)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual pluripotent-cell depletion as a manufacturing release step beside the iCasp9 clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: rBC2LCN-magnetic bead negative selection cut residual hESCs to 0.092% (O1), brought hiPSC TRA-1-60 to about the HDF-alone level (O3), and gave 0% teratoma formation in sorted-cell testes versus 14/16 large teratomas with unsorted cells (O9, O10, O11); a non-genetic hPSC depletion step that the cheatsheet's Gate5 elements do not state. Tested only on acute hPSC/fibroblast mixtures in immunodeficient-mouse testis, not on SC-islet products, and the authors say trace hPSCs remain (O14).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic suicide switch iCasp9 at AAVS1 as a backstop to purification)
edges.claim_summary: After lectin-bead depletion the authors still report trace residual hPSCs (O12, O14) and call the removal efficiency insufficient for products with high transplanted cell numbers, consistent with keeping a genetic clonogenic fail-safe as a backstop to cell purification; the study itself tests no suicide switch, and the cheatsheet does not state whether the Blueprint already cites this rationale.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual-iPSC analytical release testing); M6 (scRNA-seq marker discovery)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O11 report qPCR detection thresholds only in HE: ESRG 0.005%, CNMD 0.025%, SFRP2 0.025%, versus SOX2 1%, NANOG 5% and OCT4 2.5%; these are separate from the re-seeding report at 0.0025% (O3). Mesoderm/neural background expression and cultivation nondetection do not establish those numerical LODs there. Pancreatic marker downregulation and cultivation nondetection were reported only as data not shown (O19/O20); mature SC-islet identity, recovery and LODs are unspecified. ESRG/CNMD are candidate orthogonal analytical markers for product-specific validation, with SFRP2 limited by neuronal expression. Specific adoption of these markers is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic risk from starting iPSC line quality)
edges.claim_summary: O4 describes an association between passage over 35, doubling time faster than 20.5 hr and more residual undifferentiated iPSC after differentiation; FigS4 is absent. This is a starting-line surveillance hypothesis for SC-islet manufacturing, not a validated pass/fail cutoff, a causal passage effect, or measured safety-switch escape. Specific incorporation of these passage/doubling-time values is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (analytical residual-iPSC detection versus whole-product clonogenic fail-safe qualification)
edges.claim_summary: The paper reports marker detection and short re-seeding culture, without AP1903/iCasp9 challenge, whole-product hazard-state testing or an effective detectable clonogenic denominator. Discussion identifies background dilution and cDNA input/sampling limitations. These analytical findings cannot establish the distinct product targets already specified in frozen Blueprint §7 (residual-PSC effective fraction <=1e-8 and conditional clonogenic escape <=1e-8 with calibrated effective opportunities). Frozen ranker lines 5948-5977 separates the 14-day amplification/ddPCR residual gate from a 28-day stress/AP1903 survivor assay; this study neither validates nor contradicts those numerical targets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation, dynamic perifusion GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: After two weeks, 50% and 25% amino-acid cultures of HUES8 ESC-derived SC-β cells showed stated 1.6-fold and 2-fold GSIS improvements (O15, O16); the perifusion traces are basal-normalized. Torin1 enhanced GSIS qualitatively (O17), and reduced amino acids enabled glucose-dependent mTORC1 suppression (O14). This supports testing a nutrient/mTOR-directed maturation lever in the Blueprint’s Stage-6/7 function program; transfer to its edited, tri-hormonal product and release gates remains unvalidated, and neither exact 48-hour Torin1 dose nor the specific O14 contrast p is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS quality control)
edges.claim_summary: Standard HUES8 SC-β cells showed amino-acid-induced, glucose-independent insulin secretion and mTORC1 activation (O10, O11), paralleling the fetal phenotype (O1, O2). A physiological amino-acid perifusion challenge is a candidate additional functional readout beside the Blueprint’s dynamic GSIS and low-glucose shut-off gates; this study does not validate it as a release criterion for the edited tri-hormonal product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (post-implant maturation of SC-β cells in vivo)
edges.claim_summary: SC-β cells in nonhumanized SCID-Beige mouse kidney-capsule grafts shifted toward glucose-sensitive mTORC1 regulation at 12-18 days (O12), with inhibitory-regulator induction in the separate 4-week transcriptome comparison (O13). This supports a bounded graft-environment/maturation bridge (M3) relevant to Gate1 function, but supplies no immune protection, encapsulated-device, oxygen-bridge, or exact Blueprint-product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment of SC-islet β cells)
edges.claim_summary: O6/O7 qualify the efficiency of ITGA1/CD49a labeling in H9-derived S6 cells: no differential expression for INShi cells and incomplete labeling in C7/C10/C15. This is transcriptomic/marker evidence, without an ITGA1 sorting test or exact edited Stage-7 product validation. Frozen Blueprint lines 76/245 already combine CD49a/NTPDase3/CD9-negative selection and require lineage QC, but incorporation of this particular H9-specific limitation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (CD9-negative β-like-cell enrichment)
edges.claim_summary: O10-O14 support CD9-negative enrichment of H9-derived S6 β-like cells: more NKX6.1/C-PEPTIDE and MAFA/C-PEPTIDE cells, better glucose response than CD9-positive cells, and greater KCl-evoked insulin. The specific CD9-negative sorting mechanism is explicitly incorporated with this study PMID:33096048 in frozen Blueprint lines 76/245 and ranker lines 5603-5606. These in-vitro comparisons do not validate a combined-marker Stage-7 product, removal of all off-target cells, a 60:30:10 mixture, or dynamic biphasic/shut-off performance.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and maturation; bounded in-vitro evidence)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 support efficient differentiation and glucose-responsive insulin secretion in H9-derived S6 cells; O2 nonsignificance versus cadaveric islets is not equivalence and O4 does not establish a comparative advantage. O19/O21 are historical polyhormonal benchmarks, not matched head-to-head tests. The frozen Blueprint Gate1 contract (line 61) requires a defined tri-hormonal mixture, <1% SC-EC contamination, biphasic dynamic GSIS, and <3 min low-glucose shut-off; this study does not establish those exact-product requirements or incorporation of its specific modified protocol.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (primary human-islet graft assay for regulated alpha-cell glucagon output)
edges.claim_summary: In GKO-NSG mice, primary human-islet grafts supplied the measured circulating glucagon and increased secretion during insulin-induced hypoglycemia (O1, O5, O6). Testing SC-islet alpha-like output with this host is an assay-transfer hypothesis; the study did not test SC-islets, an engineered 60:30:10 recipe, or human immune protection. The actual Blueprint already specifies counter-regulation assays, but incorporation of this particular GKO-NSG method is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (primary human-islet graft endocrine-function and persistence benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Primary human islets under the kidney capsule supplied detectable glucagon from two weeks to at least fourteen weeks (O2), a qualitatively regulated human insulin excursion (O13), and correction of several glucagon-deficient host phenotypes (O7-O12). This supports a bounded endocrine-function benchmark and a bridge to the Blueprint aim; it does not qualify exact edited SC-islets, their mixture, a device, or immune evasion. T2D donor preparations retained abnormal glucagon output while insulin was described as comparable (O14-O16, O19-O21), so hormone-specific readouts remain necessary.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation, GSIS benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: ERRγ expression in HUVEC-iPSC beta-like cells increases extracellular c-peptide and enables glucose-responsive c-peptide secretion (O6-O7), with metabolic-profile/mitochondrial changes (O9,O12-O13); intracellular c-peptide content is not significantly altered (O19), and increased KCl maximum capacity or lineage-gene expression is not demonstrated (O8,O10-O11). This motivates testing an ERRγ metabolic-maturation step, but static 3/20 mM secretion after transient adenoviral expression in this differentiation protocol does not establish the Blueprint Gate1 dynamic biphasic GSIS, low-glucose shut-off or tri-hormonal product performance. Actual Blueprint Gate1 (§1.2), §6 and ranker maturation/readout clauses were checked; specific ERRγ incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo functional graft of hPSC-derived beta-like cells)
edges.claim_summary: iβeta grafts (10 million cells, kidney capsule) began normalizing glucose within days in STZ-diabetic immunodeficient NOD-SCID mice, controlled glucose for 56 days, and approximately 50% of chronic recipients reached <250 mg/dL (O14-O16; denominator not supplied). This supports in vivo endocrine-graft function as a justified bridge to Gate1 / M3, not exact-product qualification: no human immune reconstitution or immune protection is tested, and the adenoviral ERRγ product, renal site and endpoint differ from the Blueprint tri-hormonal SC-islet product. Results/Methods transplant timing/eligibility and Results/F6 figure numbering remain inconsistent. Claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic suicide switch fail-safe, iCasp9/AP1903 at Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O4: a ganciclovir-activated episomal suicide construct killed pluripotent but not differentiated cells and reduced or inhibited tumor formation, supporting the concept of a clonogenic fail-safe against residual pluripotent cells. Vector architecture (episomal S/MAR with ganciclovir, not iCasp9/AP1903 at AAVS1), species and escape frequency are not given in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (suicide-switch delivery and promoter-silencing risk)
edges.claim_summary: O1: the abstract reports an episomally maintained suicide construct as a non-integrating alternative to integrating vectors. Hypothesis: test an episomal arm as a comparator to the integrated Locus 4 iCasp9 cassette; the abstract has no silencing, escape-rate or durability data to support the idea.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (survival of beta cells under hypoxia without a vascular supply)
edges.claim_summary: O4: with CPO membranes pancreatic beta cell spheroids showed > 90% viability at Day 5 in hypoxia, while non-CPO controls had no surviving cells. Cell species and type, n and the assay are not stated in the abstract, and hPSC-derived islet cells were not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (CaO2 plus catalase oxygen bridge, peroxide toxicity)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O7, O11, O12 and O24 support the general CaO2/catalase peroxide-detoxification mechanism: coating suppressed detectable peroxide and improved the reported fibroblast viability contrasts. Already_accounted_for applies only to that mechanism, explicitly present in frozen Blueprint section 4.5 (especially line 172) and ranker NICHE_VASCULAR_MODULES (lines 488-495); it does not assert adoption of this paper, its 1-uM measurement, percentages, or hydrogel formulation. The study uses gamma-PGA-Aln-Phe/fibrin and non-islet human cells, so no PDMS/islet dose, peroxide threshold or product protection is qualified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (catalase placement and bubble-formation failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 qualify catalase placement: direct mixing caused aqueous structural failure, while surface coating retained structure and yielded smaller ambient-air bubbles/pores. Frozen Blueprint section 4.5 line 172 already requires catalase co-localization on/within the PDMS-CaO2 lamina for peroxide clearance, but that is not the same claim as surface coating versus bulk mixing to prevent bubble-driven hydrogel collapse; adoption of this specific result is not established. Treat this as a mechanism-level qualification requiring transfer testing in PDMS, not a validated material upgrade or an inferred blanket absence from the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (duration and cell survival of an oxygen bridge for thick avascular constructs)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O11, O13-O15 and O19-O23 describe cell-supportive oxygen delivery in non-islet cultures, including up to 3 days in a full-hydrogel DMEM assay and 30 h versus 15 h in a separate quarter-hydrogel fibrin/TBS assay. The later approximately-two-day statement is unresolved; the reported centimeter-scale scaffold dimensions also conflict and the 86% viability samples are areas within one representative experiment. The Blueprint section 4.5/ranker retain an independently calibrated PDMS-CaO2/catalase 72-hour bridge, with maintained tissue oxygen and islet function requirements; none is established by these fibroblast/hNSC measurements. M3 remains the explicit oxygenation/device taxonomy, with M7 for mechanistic physics; incorporation of this particular assay evidence is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M6 (SC-islet differentiation, maturation and islet function; single-cell/multi-omic regulatory networks)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 report a systems-level transcriptomic and chromatin characterization of a human stem cell-derived ePP-islet system and regulatory networks for endocrine fate and islet function, expanding the evidence base for Gate1 differentiation and function. Abstract-only, qualitative, and the ePP route differs from the Stage-6/7 protocol named in the cheatsheet, so it is a bridge not a matched domain.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate regulatory node for SC-islet differentiation and function: NKX2.2-CLEC16A endosomal axis)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O5 identify the NKX2.2-CLEC16A/endosomal axis as essential and show pharmacological rescue of CLEC16A deficiency; the cheatsheet does not state this axis. Hypothesis only: it could serve as a Gate1 regulatory or quality readout, with no quantitative support in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (surface-marker enrichment and depletion of off-target populations in SC-islet manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4 and O6 show that marker-based magnetic enrichment of a precursor stage depletes side populations (somatostatin-positive, SOX9-positive) and improves glucagon secretion, in line with the cheatsheet's surface-marker purification logic (CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment). The cell type is alpha, not beta, and the abstract is qualitative, so this is a bridge; CD98hc as a sort handle is not stated in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (alpha compartment of the 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta paracrine reference)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O5 and O6 suggest that enriching a CD98hc-high pre-alpha precursor improves alpha-cell function without raising total alpha yield, so CD98hc sorting could be tested as a way to improve the alpha-cell fraction quality in SC-islets. Hypothesis only; no co-culture with beta cells or in vivo data in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference, dynamic perifusion benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4 and O5 indicate that delta-cell somatostatin acts through temporal dynamics (post-inhibitory rebound) rather than static inhibition in mouse and human islets, so a static beta:alpha:delta ratio alone may not define functional paracrine coordination. Native islet physiology is the benchmark that SC-islets aim to reproduce, but the abstract is qualitative and not an SC-islet test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet delta-cell function readout)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4 and O6 suggest adding triple-hormone perifusion with delta-cell rebound testing as a Gate1 readout for SC-islet delta-cell function. The study was done in native mouse and human islets, so transfer to SC-islets is unvalidated.

edges.claim_summary: O4 and O5 show that knockin route changes random AAV donor integration (higher with HITI) and that ITR-mediated integration is junction-asymmetric, suggesting that a Gate5 knock-in of iCasp9 at AAVS1 should audit random donor and ITR-junction integration by WGS or long-read sequencing if an AAV donor is used. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (dual VLP-RNP plus IDLV HDR-donor delivery as an investigational hPSC engineering option)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 support testing dual VLP-Cas9 RNP plus integrase-deficient lentiviral HDR-donor delivery in hPSCs against the existing delivery options in Blueprint §4.1. O7/O8 provide a separate primary CD34+ HSPC integration/differentiation bridge, while O5 reports lower early cytotoxicity without identifying its cell context. These abstract findings do not demonstrate an advantage for the exact islet constructs or a safe multiplex workflow; direct genomic-integrity, biallelic-yield and post-differentiation tests remain necessary. Incorporation of this specific delivery proposal is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (biallelic AAVS1 iCasp9 qualification and multiplex-editing safety boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O6 reports predominantly mono-allelic integration, without a cell-specific allelic distribution. The Blueprint §1.2/§4.4 requires biallelic AAVS1 iCasp9, and the frozen ranker explicitly requires biallelic clone verification; the TIVID claim therefore cannot qualify that requirement. Lower early cytotoxicity in O5 likewise does not measure the translocations, LOH or clonal-selection risks retained in GRAVEYARD_006 and the ranker safety QC. The biallelic/QC boundary is already explicit, but incorporation of the TIVID-specific result is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 delivery to AAVS1 without relying on HDR)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O5 suggest MINT-retargeted Bxb1 as a candidate route for placing an iCasp9 cassette at AAVS1; this needs testing in hPSCs for efficiency, genomic integrity and promoter silencing, none of which the abstract measures. The abstract does not state whether the approach avoids double-strand breaks.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 suicide switch at Locus 4 AAVS1; <1e-6 escape threshold)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 report an auxin-activated caspase 9 with activity comparable to iCasp9 and shown orthogonal to it, suggesting a second independent kill switch that could be layered with iCasp9 to lower clonogenic escape. The cheatsheet states a single iCasp9 switch; the abstract gives no killing efficiency, escape frequency, cell type or hPSC/SC-islet data, so transfer is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing genomic safety: inter-locus translocation and on-target aberrations)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 support the existing mechanistic distinction that CBE can reduce structural aberrations relative to DSB editing, while genomic-safety QC remains required. Frozen GY-006 explicitly describes lower CBE structural variation than Cas9, and Blueprint Stage 4 already requires CAST-Seq plus longitudinal genomic QC. The new observations are in HSPCs at BCL11A/HBG, not a test of hPSC/SC-islet engineering, manufacturing yield or the ranker gamma_B penalty.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (base-editing genomic integrity: indels, translocations, paralog deletion)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O5/O7-O9/O20 show source-specific residual BE-associated indels, a described HMT locus, measurable HBG paralog deletion estimates, and low off-target C>T conversion. These scope any aberration-free interpretation; 7.9%/9.86% deletion differences versus mock were nonsignificant, not equivalent. Blueprint GY-006 already recognizes nonzero BE structural risk, but adoption of these exact HSPC loci/rates is not established. They do not calibrate hPSC risk, gamma_B, or the combined BE-plus-nuclease graveyard trigger.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (scope of existing CAST-Seq and complementary genomic release assays)
edges.claim_summary: Blueprint Stage 4 and GY-006 already require CAST-Seq with complementary genomic QC, so adding CAST-Seq is not a novel upgrade. Source Methods adapt the pipeline to two gRNAs, but transferring that specific HSPC workflow to hPSC/SC-islet lines remains unvalidated and its adoption is unknown. O24 documents SNV/guide-independent blind spots and deletion-versus-insertion ambiguity; CAST-Seq plus target amplicons is not established here as a sufficient release panel or as passing the Blueprint threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (local large-deletion evidence and GRAVEYARD_006 multiplex-editing scope)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O3 show markedly fewer captured >200-bp-deletion reads with CBE6 than archived SaCas9-treated mouse-liver samples, with nonzero guide 2 deletions and single-site guide 1 near background. Four sites in one repetitive hepatic transgene do not test mixed base/nuclease editing across multiple hPSC loci, translocation risk, or gamma_B=0.965. Amplicon dropout and unresolved Methods filter statements limit interpretation. The frozen graveyard already acknowledges lower CBE structural variation than Cas9, but adoption of these exact CBE6 rates is not established by this bounded reference check.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (guide-specific off-target editing and functional specificity)
edges.claim_summary: O11–O16 bound any genomic-safety inference: HEK293T guide 2 edited 10/16 selected predicted OT sites including human PLG 45.8 ± 0.01%, while guide 1 still edited MRPS22 OT3 at 2.67 ± 0.17%. Mouse PLG editing/protein findings have a different PAM context and do not establish human specificity. The authors disqualify guide 2 despite apo(a) lowering. These targeted panels support empirical guide-specific QC but do not qualify an hPSC islet product or establish exhaustive genome-wide safety; incorporation of this exact boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (large-CBE transient-delivery limits in the tested hepatic models)
edges.claim_summary: O21–O24 separate formulation and model: SORT-LNP reached approximately 9–10% maximum observed LPA editing in tested mice, 306-O12B gave high Huh7 editing but no significant mouse-liver LPA editing at 7 days, and the MC3 negative pilot targeted Dnmt1 in one LPA-null mouse. Payload uptake/endosomal escape is an author hypothesis, not a measured cause or universal ceiling. Frozen Blueprint delivery ledgers concern DNA donor/AAV6 packaging and ex vivo hPSC delivery, so transfer of these liver mRNA results is unvalidated; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nickase-compatible off-target profiling alongside existing genomic QC)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3 support AviTag sensitivity in HEK293T/iPSCs; O6/O8/O9 support ABE8.20/PEmax capture and independent OFF2 validation in the VEGFA editor experiment (Fig 4C is K562; iPSC nickase profiling was not demonstrated). This is a candidate complementary assay for the optional PEmax workflow and genomic QC in the frozen Blueprint §9.4 and Graveyard 006, not a replacement for CAST-seq, long-read or duplex-seq release gates. The stated ~0.45% assay limit (O18), model-limited coverage (O20), omitted bulge sites and absence of Blueprint-guide/product validation prevent comprehensive genomic-clearance claims; adoption of AviTag at this specificity is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (guide-level off-target clearance in the editing cell type)
edges.claim_summary: O4 shows cell-type-dependent SpCas9 VEGFA off-target spectra across K562, HEK293T and iPSCs; it supports profiling the actual editing cell context rather than assuming surrogate-line clearance. Frozen Blueprint §9.4 already labels its specificity priors as NOT_ENUMERATED and pending empirical genome-wide assessment, but incorporation of this specific cell-context boundary is not established. No Blueprint guide, edited SC-islet product, or quantitative transfer factor was validated in this study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAV donor integration profiling in genomic safety assessment)
edges.claim_summary: O13/O15 describe 1,857 detected AAV integrations from one Pcsk9-edited mouse, including 34.6% promoter share; O14 gives 17% promoters in a separate Alb-targeted mouse (n=1), and O19 gives 10.6–12.3% across cultured human lines. Frozen Blueprint §4.1 delivery vectors and Locus 4 explicitly contemplate AAV6 donors, but AAVS1 is a genomic locus, not proof of AAV use. The AAV8 mouse-liver versus AAV6 in vitro contrast confounds host/cell/route/serotype and cannot predict a promoter rate, per-cell integration incidence, or cancer risk for ex vivo hPSC manufacture. Incorporation of this precise boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease genomic-integrity risk of Cas9 double-strand-break editing: large SVs, off-target edits, heterogeneous outcomes)
