edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (readout for editing outcomes and structural variants at edited loci)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4, O5, O8, O17: amplification-free Cas9-enrichment long-read sequencing (1168x average coverage, QV39, near 50-50% allele balance where LR-PCR was biased, 1% VAF threshold) is a candidate unbiased readout of mosaic editing outcomes at predefined loci of an edited hPSC line, tested only in zebrafish; it cannot see events that disrupt an excision gRNA site and covers regions of about 5 kb, so it does not replace translocation or chromothripsis assays.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of ex vivo nuclease editing: translocations, large deletions, micronuclei as a chromothripsis precursor)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O4: in human HSPCs, transient p38 MAPK inhibition during CRISPR-Cas9 editing left structural alterations (large deletions, AAV mis-integration, CAST-seq translocations) unchanged, reduced micronuclei and lowered exome mutational burden after xenotransplantation. This suggests testing a transient p38 inhibitor during ex vivo multiplex editing of the hPSC line, but the evidence is abstract-only, without values, in another stem-cell type, and p38i is not in the cheatsheet's Blueprint elements.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (existing base/nickase genomic-integrity precaution)
edges.claim_summary: O13, O15-O18 provide human-HSPC evidence that base-editing conditions can retain off-target base edits/indels and estimated translocations; this reinforces the existing generic nickase/base-edit structural-variation hazard in Blueprint section 5 GRAVEYARD_006 and graveyard v0.5 entry 006. Already accounted for applies only to that generic precaution: the HSPC-specific counts and 1.4%/2.2% PDCD1 burdens are not adopted product rates or a calibration of ranker gamma_B = 0.965. The source tested individual guides, not the Blueprint multiplex SC-islet stack; PE2 was inactive and not further evaluated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M6 (candidate empirical off-target nomination and confirmation workflow)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4, O7-O8 and O10 support investigating replicated UNCOVERseq nomination in a promiscuous cell system plus modality- and target-cell-matched amplicon confirmation. The proposed transfer must preserve assay limits, event-frequency versus unique-site denominators, SSB-only events, and independent structural-variant QC. Frozen Blueprint section 9.4 explicitly leaves genome-wide enumeration NOT_ENUMERATED and empirical guide specificity pending; section 2 Stage4 already requires sequential editing and genomic QC. The supplied sources do not establish adoption of this exact UNCOVERseq upgrade. No SC-islet, AsCas12a or verified Islet-1 guide assay is supplied; O19-O21 are not evidence that PE2 or the product is safe.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (surface HLA class I suppression and allogeneic PBMC effector response)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O8 provide a mechanistic bridge from lower, incompletely eliminated surface HLA class I to reduced allogeneic PBMC-associated VIC loss/clustering in susceptible donor combinations, with residual HLA, unchanged/slightly increased clustering in other pairings, and HLA-matching dependence retained. Frozen Blueprint sections 4.1-4.2 already target donor HLA suppression, but incorporation of these particular valve-cell findings is not established; combined lentiviral US2/Spi9 neither isolates US2 nor tests the B2M/CIITA-edited SC-islet product, newly quantifies class II suppression, or resolves direct versus indirect T-cell contributions.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 effector protection and indirect host-APC boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O9/O20 are predicted epitope associations and O11-O15 are combined-construct PBMC supernatant Granzyme B/IFN-gamma responses, with donor-dependent effects; they do not isolate intracellular SERPINB9 activity, demonstrate indirect recipient-APC blockade, or test T1D autoimmunity. Generic cytosolic SERPINB9 protection and persistent host-APC presentation despite donor CIITA KO are already explicit in frozen Blueprint sections 4.2-4.3 and Graveyard 010, but incorporation of these specific observations is unknown: all PIRCHE-T2 combinations exceeded 276 (no failure threshold), and O19 describes localization without establishing loss of protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E/NKG2A and CD47/SIRPalpha innate protection)
edges.claim_summary: O16/O18 list immune-regulatory transcripts including CD47/HLA-F in cell profiling and HLA-E in tissue, while O19 identifies CD68-positive cells in tissue; these are not quantitative surface-protein, NK subset-killing, or macrophage-phagocytosis protection assays. Mixed PBMC Granzyme B cannot identify its T-cell versus NK source, and the seven-day assay primarily represents lymphocyte effector responses with limited myeloid-survival interpretation (Results conclusion); none of these observations qualifies the exact HLA-E/CD47 SC-islet construct or establishes preservation of unrelated immunity. Frozen Blueprint section 4.1 and Graveyard 009 separately require exact-construct, lineage-specific innate testing; incorporation of this study-specific transcript/localization detail is unknown.

edges.claim_summary: O16-O18/O20/O22 associate mixed chimerism with donor-specific MLR hyporesponsiveness, Vbeta11-cell depletion, increased host-thymic-DC PD-L1, donor-enriched ICOS+ splenic Tregs and reported host-cell anergy. These observational mouse immune-compartment phenotypes do not establish causal PD-L1 or Treg suppression, efficacy of graft-intrinsic Locus-3 PD-L1, recurrent autoimmune protection, or the Blueprint section 4.2 recipient-APC indirect-presentation endpoint. Diabetes was ablation-induced; NOD/autoimmune testing is future work. O17 donor/host CD45 mapping remains source-inconsistent.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (host-conditioning and donor-matched hematopoietic support as a future tolerance hypothesis)

Discussion proposes future renewable stem-cell-islet and autoimmune adaptation, not a tested hPSC-derived hematopoietic/islet pair. Any human host-tolerance adjunct requires separate validation of engraftment, specificity and toxicity; Blueprint section 9.4 explicitly describes removed systemic-conditioning inputs under DEC-047, so this is not an adopted compiler option.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (β-cell PD-L1 checkpoint mechanism; Locus 3 CXCL10 shield)
edges.claim_summary: O8, O9 and O12 support a β-cell PD-L1 checkpoint strategy through transient LNP-CD274 delivery in prediabetic NOD mice: prose diabetes-free ranges were approximately 80%–90% versus 30%–40%, and severe insulitis decreased with eGLP-LNP+CD274. The broad checkpoint mechanism is explicitly accounted for in Blueprint §4.3 and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9 as inflammation-inducible CXCL10::SERPINB9-PD-L1, not constitutive GAPDH expression. This does not establish adoption of this study’s percentages, long-term protection, SERPINB9 synergy, or performance of the engineered human product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (GLP-1R-targeted delivery boundaries across NOD age, STZ injury and human islets)

These are distinct cohorts/endpoints, not equivalence, proof of receptor-independent delivery, or a human GLP-1R/insulitis causal chain. O11 reports an increasing mass trend without statistical significance. The genomic CXCL10 shield does not establish whether these specific delivery boundaries are incorporated; no PD-L1-versus-SERPINB9 comparison was performed.

edges.claim_summary: O1–O4, O7–O8, O10 and O18 describe short-term viability/ATP in standard in vitro culture; O16–O17 and O20/O22/O23 characterize the porous microwell geometry. No oxygen tension, oxygen flux, imposed hypoxia, perfusion, or 72-hour avascular graft challenge was measured, so these results do not qualify the Blueprint Gate5 oxygen bridge (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md §1.2 and §4.5). Reported nonsignificance is not equivalence. The frozen ranker separately models a cell-impermeable avascular macrodevice; its penalties cannot be empirically replaced by this porous in vitro device study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (in vitro endothelial adhesion and prevascularized-device hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O11–O13 support HUVEC adhesion, high viability and pore-bridging/sprouting-like morphology on device films at 14 days. They do not demonstrate lumenized functional vessels, host anastomosis, perfusion, or graft protection. Blueprint §4.5 instead specifies same-line iEC:iPericyte lumenized microvessels and direct inosculation qualification; incorporation of these specific PVDF/HUVEC findings is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (device-associated static GSIS readout in primary human islets and rodent pseudoislets)
edges.claim_summary: O5–O6 and O9 support retained glucose responsiveness in the tested encapsulated INS1E and primary cadaveric human islets: human SI was 5.51 ± 0.72 in hybrid versus 5.54 ± 0.38 free-floating, and INS1E day-1 SI was significantly higher in hybrid. Methods use sequential one-hour 1.67/16.7 mM incubations. This is a bounded static functional observation; it does not establish SC-islet differentiation/maturation, biphasic dynamic secretion, absolute secretory dose, or the Blueprint §1.2 <3-minute 16.7→2.8 mM shut-off target. M2 is not assigned to generic primary-islet metrology.

edges.claim_summary: O1 reports normoglycemia in 5/10 PSS recipients vs 2/9 USS recipients (contrast p-value not reported); O3 reports significantly better IPGTT glucose tolerance in PSS recipients than diabetic comparator mice, without numerical values, exact p-value, or cohort size. These primary mouse-islet outcomes bound functional expectations for a prevascularized site; transfer to SC-islet maturation, dynamic insulin/glucagon regulation, and human clinical performance remains unvalidated, and incorporation of these specific results is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO missing-self trade-off; HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 support the B2M loss/direct-allorecognition versus NK missing-self trade-off; O10 and O16-O17 contextualize the NKG2A-negative/NKG2C+ protection gap in human T-cell cultures. Incorporation applies to this mechanistic boundary: frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.1 and the ranker portfolio require innate-subset testing. It does not assert incorporation or islet validation of this study’s 45-donor result or O20’s 12/24 prevalence and >5% association.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK-ligand edits other than HLA-E: CD47, CD54/CD58, PVR/CD155)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O5 describe a single-NK-donor screen in B2M KO T cells, while O9/O11 compare NK protection by CD47 with HLA-E/CD300a TASR under the stated expression/culture conditions. These qualify transfer of NK-cloaking claims; they do not test macrophage phagocytosis or the Blueprint’s exact CD47-IgV-GPI construct. Frozen Blueprint §4.1 and ranker portfolio already require exact-construct NK/macrophage testing, but incorporation of these specific T-cell results is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD300a agonist TASR as NK-inhibitory ligand reaching NKG2A-negative NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: O14 reports protection across the tested 45/45 PBMC donors, supported by receptor phenotype (O15), 2Cdom protection (O10/O17), and cytokine-release suppression (O19); O18/O21-O23 extend only to an allogeneic CAR T-cell model. This supports a CD300a-agonist TASR upgrade hypothesis, with transfer to islets unvalidated. The frozen Locus 1 architecture and ranker/graveyard constraints were source-checked, but they do not establish adoption of this specific mechanism; incorporation remains unknown. Broader therapeutic-cell, long-term product, genomic-safety and in-vivo efficacy are explicitly untested (Discussion limitations).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP, intrinsic cytoprotection under ER stress)
edges.claim_summary: O5 and O6 report functional/metabolic recovery, preservation of functional beta cells and prevention of diabetes progression after Txnip deletion in Wfs1-deficient mice. This supports a bounded mechanistic bridge to Gate4 intrinsic cytoprotection, not efficacy in a human SC-islet graft; deletion route, effect size and follow-up are unstated. The frozen Blueprint explicitly evaluates TXNIP knockout as X5 (line 209), but that broader inclusion does not establish incorporation of this specific WFS1-deficiency rescue finding; claim-specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate4 / M7 (beta-cell identity-loss failure mode and proposed stress-readout extension)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 describe Wfs1-deficient mouse beta-cell dysfunction/dedifferentiation and a mixed insulin/glucagon phenotype after weaning; O7 separately captures hormone-negative cells retaining general endocrine features. These findings motivate an unvalidated SC-islet hypothesis of measuring lineage/identity retention alongside hormone staining during ER stress. The frozen Blueprint already names dedifferentiation prevention under Gate4 (line 64), and Gate1 lineage maturity plus marker-based readouts (lines 61 and 245) are established design goals; whether this particular lineage-tracking extension is incorporated remains unknown. No SC-islet differentiation, human intervention, lineage-promoter shutdown or suicide-switch escape was tested in the supplied abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 / M6 (ER-stress-associated endocrine identity and metabolic transcriptional response)
edges.claim_summary: O9 and O11-O14 support an intrinsic-stress/identity failure-mode bridge: 5 μM TM in mixed HUES8 SC-α protocol cultures produced transcriptional changes including reduced PDX1/MAFB and negative metabolic-pathway enrichment without reported loss of viability at that dose. These are chemical-stress and transcriptomic endpoints in alpha-directed cultures, not beta-cell, whole-product, or peri-transplant protection. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and ranker Gate4 already scope ER stress generally; their incorporation of this precise alpha-culture finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (alpha-cell fraction of the 60:30:10 paracrine architecture; stem-cell-derived alpha cell authenticity)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 establish bounded alpha-directed differentiation/transcriptomic context: approximately 30% monohormonal GCG+ by flow, 68% glucagon-expressing cells by scRNA-seq, and 77 shared top-100 genes with primary human alpha cells, with remaining identity differences. O6 reports undetected insulin secretion. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and §6 steps 1-2 use sorted tri-hormonal 60:30:10 input seeding; this study neither tests that mixture nor establishes counter-regulation in the edited product, and these two percentages are not the Blueprint alpha fraction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER-stress relief vs identity preservation; small-molecule cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: O15/O18/O20 support partial functional/identity rescue by sunitinib during TM treatment, while O18 reports unchanged UPR/processing markers; O16-O17 separately compare vehicle, sunitinib, or TUDCA and report TUDCA-associated ARX/MAFB reduction. O21 null cell counts and O22 lower glucagon content limit claims of normalized processing or preserved reserve; IRX1/IRX2 source inconsistency remains. This qualifies transfer of ER-stress relief to endocrine identity, not a demonstrated contradiction of the Blueprint, a proven IRE1α/PERK rescue mechanism, or evidence to adopt sunitinib in beta cells or the product. Some support is Results-only for unavailable supplemental figures; main Fig 6 supports secretion/transcript context.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (islet diameter and IEQ-volume measurement failure boundary; clinical-dose comparison is a transfer hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O15 identify single-section diameter underestimation and diameter-binned IEQ excess in fixed native pancreatic-tail islets, with reported overall IEQ 57.72 versus 30.79 and 87.51% excess. Frozen Blueprint §4.5 already defines IEQ by a 150-μm sphere and couples volume to packing, while the ranker HIP-Core dosing unit additionally records viable cell counts; these findings motivate checking measurement comparability before transferring clinical IEQ benchmarks, without establishing a universal multiplier or contradicting the definition of IEQ. Incorporation of these particular empirical morphology biases remains unknown; isolated/SC-islet geometry, function, transplantation outcomes, and oxygen protection were not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet ECM-associated maturation, composition and endocrine function)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O6: the abstract reports Col VI-associated islet-cell viability/function improvements and describes optimized iPSC organoids as comparable with human islets in composition/endocrine function. This is qualitative support within the SC-islet manufacturing domain, with unresolved Col-VI assay cell provenance and no numerical composition, secretion kinetics, equivalence test or exact edited-product qualification. Frozen Blueprint sections 1.2, 2 and 4.5 specify dynamic GSIS, a 60:30:10 mixture and a Laminin-511 E8 vascular niche; they do not establish whether this specific dAM/Col-VI evidence is incorporated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (dAM sheet-assisted graft engraftment and endocrine-function bioassay)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: dAM sheet-assisted organoids reportedly facilitate engraftment and restore normoglycemia in diabetic mice, with increased body weight and augmented glucose-responsive insulin release. This is a qualitative rodent-host functional bridge; the insulin-release assay setting, comparator, immune status, magnitude and duration are unresolved. It does not demonstrate the Blueprint section 1.2/4.5 72-hour avascular oxygen target, perfusion timing, fail-safe efficacy or immune protection. The frozen Blueprint/ranker niche definitions do not establish claim-specific incorporation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation; pancreatic ECM and basement-membrane niche)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O9 support PINE-associated improvements in INS/CHGA markers, high-glucose insulin output and secretagogue-assisted Ca2+ response in stage-6 H1 SC-islets in vitro; O6 shows no detected GCG+ difference, not equivalence. This is maturation evidence, not exact-product qualification. Blueprint §1.2 and §4.5/Stage2 already use Stage7 maturation and Laminin-511 E8/iMVFs; those are different from this porcine pdECM+laminin/collagen-IV recipe. Incorporation of this specific PINE finding is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic biphasic GSIS and low-glucose shut-off boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O14-O16 report 3.63-fold basal and 3.82-fold stimulated insulin output versus random dispersion but no detected stimulation-index difference in static GSIS. This does not establish equivalence or dynamic first/second-phase response, step-down shut-off or basal-leak control required by Blueprint §1.2 (line 61). The ranker niche prior (lines 148-153,170-177) bundles Stage7/size/microvessels, so these stage6 static results do not recalibrate its +0.45 prior. Incorporation of the HICA-specific empirical boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate5 / M2 / M3 (prevascularized-niche assembly hypothesis; no measured oxygen bridge)
edges.claim_summary: O10-O13 and O18 support a bounded hypothesis that geometry-guided EC proximity may help preimplantation SC-islet niche assembly and maturation. Viability >94% is imaging based; CD31 networks and higher CX36/VE-CAD mRNA are not demonstrated perfusion. Blueprint line177 specifies isogenic iEC:iPericyte iMVFs with Laminin-511 E8 and direct patency/inosculation qualification. HUVEC/PINE results do not establish oxygen delivery, host integration, 72-hour bridge survival or fail-safe function; Discussion[26] places perfusion and transplantation in future work. Incorporation of the particular HICA-V strategy is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (primary-islet somatostatin metrology boundary; bridge to SC-islet paracrine composition/function)
edges.claim_summary: O13 and O15-O18: primary T2D human islets had fewer somatostatin-positive cells (11 healthy/5 T2D islets, 3/2 donors) and larger reporter responses at 11 mM glucose or 30 mM K+ in a separately described secretion cohort (22/17 islets, 5/4 donors); stimulation-index differences were significant without contrast-resolved p symbols or numerical indices. These cohort-level observations motivate functional somatostatin assessment beside composition, but do not measure secretion per delta cell, prove a causal number/output relationship, or contradict the 60:30:10 SC-islet recipe. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §6.4 and ranker mixture/readout clauses already require measured composition and endocrine function; incorporation of this particular T2D metrology boundary remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (single-islet somatostatin reporter calibration and failure boundaries; proposed transfer to M2 SC-islet function QC)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O19 calibrate a HeLa SSTR2/Gα15 reporter (half-maximal 1.6 ± 0.4 nM, maximal ~30 nM) against R-cells without Gα15 (9.8 ± 0.9 nM, ~500 nM). O2-O3 show mouse-islet antagonist-sensitive signals; O4-O7 show human-islet glucose/hormone responses. An SC-islet delta-function assay is a testable transfer hypothesis: no SC-islets were tested, readout is semi-quantitative, and Discussion explicitly leaves detection-limit/endogenous-activation explanations for absent modulator effects. The frozen Blueprint/ranker composition and dynamic insulin/glucagon requirements do not establish adoption of this assay; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAVS1 safe-harbor insertion with nickase; editing efficiency and off-target/karyotype safety)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O3, O5 give a bounded non-islet human-iPSC AAVS1 engineering bridge: junction-positive rates were 4.54% (WT donor) and 5.43% (FE donor), four predicted off-target sites had no significant mutations reported, and G-banding showed normal 46, XY karyotypes. These assay-limited findings do not establish genome-wide absence of lesions, translocation safety, multiplex-edit performance or iCasp9 escape control. Blueprint §4.4, GRAVEYARD_006 and ranker non-IID safety gates explicitly retain broader lineage/genomic qualification requirements; incorporation of these exact study-specific findings is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAVS1 EF1α-driven expression after EC differentiation; bounded durability evidence)
edges.claim_summary: O6/O10 show AAVS1 EF1α-driven FVIII expression in iPSCs and ECs; separate luciferase-KI ECs retain detectable signal at 13 weeks (O17), and corrected-EC recipients have FVIII recovery at weeks 4 and 13 (O18) in immunodeficient mice. O15 documents short-lived activity after intravenous delivery under cyclosporine, confounded with host immunity, route and cell persistence; it does not prove promoter silencing. The study does not test the exact Blueprint §4.4 230-bp EEF1A1/insulator/iCasp9 architecture, endocrine lineage durability, rare silencing frequency, or clonogenic kill escape. Incorporation of this specific bounded durability evidence is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 expression-stability benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: AAVS1-targeted MND-eGFP in primary human CD34+ HSPCs showed qualitative persistence at 45 days (O9) and a reported edited/total allele ratio of 0.65 (O5); the authors' roughly 40% biallelic interpretation is internally inconsistent and unresolved. This is a same-locus bridge only: no SC-islet lineage, insulated EEF1A1-iCasp9 cassette, AP1903 killing or clonogenic escape was tested. Blueprint section 4.4 and the frozen ranker already require a qualified biallelic, pan-lineage insulated AAVS1 switch; incorporation of these specific HSPC findings is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (locus-, promoter- and lineage-dependent safe-harbor expression)
edges.claim_summary: Reduced CFU GFP at some EPV loci (O15), lineage-biased expression (O16/O18), and Prot.218 silencing after hEPO maturation (O17) provide HSPC-context examples of expression instability; Dep.55 source wording conflicts are retained. The general need to prevent silencing and preserve pan-lineage fail-safe expression is already explicit in Blueprint section 4.4, frozen ranker SAFETY_SWITCH_MODULES and GRAVEYARD_002. These non-AAVS1 EPV results neither establish failure of the exact Locus 4 cassette nor demonstrate its qualification, and their specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (research hypothesis: Dep.3 and Ap.102 as alternative insertion loci)
edges.claim_summary: Dep.3 and Ap.102 produced descriptively fewer DEGs against same-donor mock (509/496) than AAVS1 (1,595) in primary HSPCs (O12); GO interpretation is a short-term snapshot (O14), and Dep.3 showed qualitative 45-day eGFP persistence (O9). These observations motivate cell-context-specific comparison only, with Ap.102 lineage bias (O16) and no SC-islet, functional genotoxicity or fail-safe evidence. Blueprint section 4.4 and the frozen ranker specify AAVS1 with a GAPDH contingency; adoption of these EPV candidates is not established, so incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic integrity: cell-cycle-dependent long deletions and chromosome-fragment loss)
edges.claim_summary: Human HSPCs show a cell-cycle/cytokine-culture boundary for nonprogrammed long deletions and chr2p-containing micronuclei (O4-O12): reported median input residual long deletions/rearrangements were 8.3%, and no-culture conditions reduced these endpoints. This qualifies transfer of editing protocols to hPSCs, not an existing off-target-only Blueprint: the frozen Blueprint already requires sequential editing, long-read/LOH and CAST-Seq QC. The quiescent HSPC mechanism and numeric rates are not validated for hPSC HDR manufacturing; specific incorporation is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (off-target integrity of high-fidelity Cas9 RNP editing)
edges.claim_summary: The tested HSPC off-target panel had a donor-variant-specific exception and 19 insufficiently covered nominated sites (O14); prior-cited HiFi mitigation (M1852_O20) and the current editing-efficiency tradeoff (M1852_O22) are distinct evidence. This supports cautious use of high-fidelity R691A already named in Blueprint Pass 2, while adding context on donor-aware nomination; it does not validate the Blueprint guides or its assigned specificity scores, which the Blueprint labels non-exhaustive. Specific incorporation of this donor-variant finding is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M7 (genomic safety release assays for multiplex-edited hPSC lines)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: test whether cell-cycle-stratified drop-off/offset ddPCR and micronucleus/chr-fragment measurements add information to the Blueprint existing long-read/LOH, CAST-Seq and genomic QC workflow. HSPC data (O4-O12) motivate the comparison, not a claim that structural-variant assays are absent or that limiting cycling is compatible with hPSC HDR. Optimize only after matched hPSC editing, yield, integrity and differentiation assessment; specific adoption of these adjunct assays is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 safe harbor as a receptive landing site for large-cargo knock-in)

edges.claim_summary: Specific transfer hypothesis: test the attP-installed/attB-donor eeBxb1 configuration at AAVS1 for the actual fail-safe cassette (O4/O16), with full-length/single-copy/genomic and functional qualification. Prime-editing nickases are not nuclease-free or demonstrated zero-risk (GRAVEYARD_006).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 / M7 (configuration-specific off-target insertion and measurement-artifact boundaries)
edges.claim_summary: O12/O15 show off-target insertion with an attP donor/attB genomic configuration; O16 and M1857_O22 bound the attB-donor/attP configuration only in the tested assays. O18 and M1857_O23 show why UDiTaS nominations require orthogonal validation. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 / M7 (prime-editing indel burden versus multiplex genomic-risk precautions)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (lead time for a prevascularized site before transplantation)
edges.claim_summary: Four-week device placement yielded higher day-30 cure rates than Ipo-Tx/d10 groups at 300 IEQ (O1–O3 and Figure 3 caption); O13/O14 show selected day-7 interstitial vessel-density differences and O17/O18 selected collagen-III differences. This qualifies device/site-specific lead time rather than establishing a universal duration: the ranker labels a different 14d prevascularized pouch, and 10 days versus four weeks in this mouse RCP model does not directly validate or refute that pouch. Added ADSCs gave no significant high-dose glycemia/cure advantage (O4), reduced-dose cure difference was nonsignificant (O6), and reduced-dose AUC was nonsignificant with the printed ADSC value numerically higher (O10). O19 supplies only a numerical d10 vessel increase; vessel functionality remains uncertain in Discussion. Specific duration/ECM incorporation is unknown; no human-product or 72-hour oxygen qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (islet cell-composition and beta-cell-normalized function readout; paracrine architecture reference)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract proposes cell-type-specific DNA methylation as a protein-content-independent way to infer islet cell fractions and to normalize insulin secretion to beta-cell DNA (O2, O6). That could be tested as a composition and function readout for SC-islet batches, but the markers are described only for human pancreas and islet samples; nothing in the abstract tests immature SC-islets, and the cheatsheet does not name this method.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (upstream pancreatic-progenitor expansion and banking for SC-islet manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: C6 PP expansion and cryobanking are a bounded upstream manufacturing hypothesis (O1,O6,O7,O9,O19,O20): the paper reports 2000-fold expansion and enriched PP-marker immunophenotypes, with an unresolved H1 p10 numerical conflict and NKX6-1/2 antibody specificity limitation. O16/O17 report similar endocrine content and static function after expansion, not equivalence or improved maturation. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§2/§6 states Stage7 lineage sorting, functional release, and MCB requirements; the reviewed references do not establish claim-specific adoption of this exact C6 expansion/banking process, so incorporation remains unknown. Compatibility of components with GMP is not full GMP manufacture or edited-product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation and GSIS benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O17/O18 scope the Gate1 / M2 transfer: expanded and direct PP-derived SC-islets had reportedly similar static C-peptide responses, while INS/GCG/MAFA expression was lower than primary human islets. This does not prove that expansion leaves maturation unchanged, nor that either preparation meets the frozen Blueprint §1.2 dynamic first/second phase GSIS, rapid shut-off and lineage-purity requirements. No dynamic perifusion, formal equivalence or exact edited-product result is provided; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic stability of banked progenitor cells)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O22/O23 report no gross G-banding abnormalities after H1 p16, H9 p12 and CRTD1 p13 C6 expansion, with at least 20 metaphases per reported assay. This supports only limited cytogenetic stability of the unedited cells; it cannot qualify multiplex-edited MCB safety. Frozen Blueprint §2 Stage4, ranker OQ-006 and GRAVEYARD_006 require sequence/structural QC beyond G-banding; no safety-switch escape or oxygen endpoint was tested. Incorporation of this specific unedited PP result is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet functional maturation; dynamic phases and <3 min low-glucose shut-off)
edges.claim_summary: H1 SC-islets show protocol-dependent sequential static GSIS (O3/O4/O7), not dynamic perifusion or low-glucose shut-off qualification. Fig. 3A pairwise tests O5/O6/O20 are nonsignificant and have an unresolved response variable. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 explicitly requires biphasic GSIS and <3 min shut-off at 16.7→2.8 mM; these 2→20→2 mM hour-scale incubations cannot establish that requirement or edited-product performance. Incorporation of this exact protocol-specific boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (stage 4 NKX6.1/PDX1 co-expression as a candidate process QC readout)
edges.claim_summary: Descriptive stage 4 co-expression is 14.5% for A, 48.2% B and 42.8% C (O12/O13), with the printed A-versus-B/C p values 0.076/0.220. This motivates evaluating early process QC, not adopting a predictive threshold from three adapted protocols in one H1 line. Blueprint §6 already specifies terminal NKX6-1/C-peptide lineage QC and yield tracking; adoption of this distinct stage 4 predictor is not established by the reviewed references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (manufacturing logistics: cryobanking of dissociated SC-islet intermediates)
edges.claim_summary: Whole-aggregate freezing failed under tested conditions (O14), while stage 5/6 single cells reconstituted glucose-responsive islets (O15/O17/O18), with Recovery Cell stage 6 survival failure in 2/3 preparations (O16). Eight-/ten-month storage pertains to stage 5 protocol C progenitors; O19 p=0.133 does not establish medium equivalence. This supports a bounded process-development comparison; edited-product post-thaw function and claim-specific Blueprint incorporation remain unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (functional maturation; static GSIS versus Blueprint dynamic-function requirements)
edges.claim_summary: These H1 SC-islets had a static 20 mM/2 mM glucose SI of 1.43 versus 3.13 for primary human islets (O16), with SI 1.4 at stage-6 week 8 (O11). They provide protocol-specific evidence of limited static responsiveness relevant to Gate1, but do not measure the Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS or <3-minute shutoff and cannot qualify or fail an edited OpenIslet product against those requirements. The specific protocol finding's incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (off-target SLC18A1 characterization and purification rationale)
edges.claim_summary: SLC18A1+ SC-ECs were detectable in this unpurified stage-6 H1 product (O4), supporting the general off-target characterization/purification rationale already explicit in Blueprint §1.2 and §6 step 1 (lines 61, 245). No SC-EC fraction or CD49a/ITGA1 purification experiment is supplied here, so the paper cannot establish a threshold breach or validate the selected sorting method.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (culture-dependent composition; bounded relevance to measured 60:30:10 manufacture)
edges.claim_summary: During prolonged stage-6 ESFM culture, total Cp+ cells declined and GCG+ cells rose (O7,O8), while bi-/tri-hormonal fractions changed (O5,O6,O9). Holding time is therefore a relevant measurement variable in this H1 protocol. Blueprint §6 steps 1–2 and its mixture sub-study (lines 245–247) already require measured composition; these unsorted cultures do not test the controlled 60:30:10 product, prove lineage conversion, or select an optimal mixture. Incorporation of this specific temporal boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (live in-process quality readouts: MAFA maturation, Ca2+ function)
edges.claim_summary: H1-derived MAFA-mCHERRY and INS-GCaMP6 reporter lines enabled live detection of rare MAFA-positive cells and glucose-plus-KCl-evoked Ca2+ responses (O9, O10), supporting a research-tool hypothesis for microwell screening of SC-islet differentiation conditions. Transfer to the Blueprint's edited manufacturing line remains to be tested: one clone per reporter line was studied and some reporter derivatives showed lower GK or PCSK1 expression (O6, O7), without proving the edits caused those differences. The reporters do not replace the independent dynamic GSIS requirements in frozen Blueprint §1.2, and exact tool adoption/incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (scope of single-site hESC landing-pad genomic-safety characterization)
edges.claim_summary: Single-site knock-in in H1/H9 hESC showed no detected changes at five predicted off-target sites per clone by PCR/Sanger (O4), no abnormalities in sampled G-banded metaphases (O12), and small reported nearest-gene qPCR ranges (O5-O7). H1 DE counts were below an independent-wild-type comparison (O8-O10), while H9 counts were 60/51/91 versus 15 (O19); these are descriptive transcriptomic observations, not equivalence or causal safety proof. Nearest-DE-gene distances (O20) do not exclude cis regulation. These assays cannot qualify the Blueprint multiplex product or discharge GRAVEYARD_006/§8 genomic release checks, including structural-variant/translocation and deep clonal surveillance. Whether these exact study findings are incorporated is unknown; general genomic-safety requirements are already explicit.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (AAVS1 safe-harbor expression; transfer to Locus 4 EEF1A1-core-iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: An EF1α-driven ChR2 cassette at AAVS1 retained expression across hPSC passages 5, 10 and 15 (O8) and in day-150 forebrain organoids (O15); O19-O21 record protein dosage in hPSCs and neural derivatives. The frozen Blueprint §4.4 instead specifies an insulated 230-bp EEF1A1-core-iCasp9 cassette: shared AAVS1 targeting and promoter-family ancestry justify a bounded engineering bridge, without establishing exact promoter identity, SC-islet expression stability, iCasp9 killing, anti-silencing function or escape frequency. Study-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base/nickase editing genomic integrity, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: The general precaution that nickase-based editing can create deletions/indels is already explicit in Blueprint §5 GRAVEYARD_006 and the ranker engineering prior. The homologous-globin HSPC findings (O7, O14) support that bounded mechanism by a justified non-islet bridge. Their 10-fold qPCR deletion-amplicon result is not a deletion prevalence, does not measure cross-locus translocations or chromothripsis, and does not calibrate the ranker gamma_B = 0.965 manufacturing penalty.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing strategy for hypoimmune and safety loci)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: nickase-deficient dABE8e could be compared with nickase editors for homologous/complementary-strand editing to reduce deletions/indels (O8, O11, O14, O15), while preserving the lower-efficiency and slower-kinetics tradeoffs (O3, O9, O10, O20, O21). hPSCs, SC-islets, the actual Blueprint loci, long-term engraftment and genome-wide safety were not tested. The inspected Blueprint/ranker/graveyard establish the general warning but do not establish adoption of this particular editor substitution; this finding cannot waive genomic QC or remove gamma_B.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing genomic integrity; GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: Bounded hypothesis: PE-Plus improved small-edit generation in H1 hESCs and yielded five dual-EGFR mutant clones (O18). Sorted transiently edited populations had descriptively lower SNV/indel counts than PEmax (O4/O5), with no WGS replicate count or statistical equivalence evidence, while 6/42 dual-edit clones had unwanted sequences (O17). Frozen Blueprint §5/GRAVEYARD_006 and ranker lines 1282-1297,2047 address multiplex base/prime edits with nuclease burden; this same-locus dual-EGFR experiment did not test the combined multi-locus DSB workflow, translocations, edited SC-islets or long-term oncogenic selection under MLH1dn/P53DD. It neither clears that warning nor establishes product safety; adoption of this exact PE-Plus hypothesis is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 integrated inducible-cassette scope)
edges.claim_summary: AAVS1-targeted TRE/CAG-rtTA editing cassettes supported doxycycline-controlled editing in H1 hESCs and neural progenitors, with undetectable no-doxycycline ddPCR mutation rates (O6/O9/O10). This supports only short-term locus/inducible-expression feasibility. Frozen Blueprint §4.4 instead specifies biallelic insulated EEF1A1-iCasp9 and long-term pan-lineage clonogenic ablation; its quantitative qualification is at the 10^-8 level (Blueprint OQ-012 and ranker S7/S9), which this study did not test. Doxycycline suppression of editing is distinct from AP1903 activation of apoptosis, and there is no evidence here for exact-cassette silencing resistance, SC-islet persistence, kill efficiency or escape. Incorporation of this bounded feasibility evidence is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 knock-in; transgene silencing in differentiated progeny)
edges.claim_summary: A heterozygous UCOE-CAG-GCaMP6 insertion at AAVS1 (O1) still gave visible GFP and calcium transients in 3-week induced neurons (O10, O11), consistent with continued expression after differentiation. Evidence is qualitative: no silencing quantification, no non-UCOE comparator, one monoclonal neural line, and no off-target assessment (O3), so it is a weak bridge to an hPSC-derived islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (insulated iCasp9 cassette at AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: adding a UCOE-type anti-silencing element (as paired with CAG here, O10, O11) to the AAVS1 iCasp9 cassette might protect against promoter silencing in differentiated cells. This was shown only for a neural GCaMP6 reporter without a quantitative silencing assay, and the UCOE element is not stated in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (direct HLA-dependent allorecognition; B2M and CIITA loci 1/2)
edges.claim_summary: O4/O5/O8/O9 measure residual donor-cell HLA-I/II after combined US2-Spi9 delivery; O18 reports 38% lower MIP1β activation by one HLA-A2-specific CD8+ clone. This bounded bridge supports the Blueprint §4.1/§4.2 rationale for reducing direct HLA recognition, which is already represented there and in ranker Gate2A branches. It does not test B2M/CIITA knockout efficacy, HLA-II-dependent CD4 function, target-cell survival, or the exact SC-islet product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 function and indirect host-APC evidence boundary)
edges.claim_summary: The proposed Gate2B inference is unsupported: O8/O9 are donor-VIC HLA-II expression, O6 is Serpin 9 protein expression, and O18 is CD8-clone MIP1β activation under a combined perturbation. No isolated Serpin 9 granzyme-inhibition, immune-mediated target-cell protection, autoreactive-memory or host-APC functional assay is reported here. Blueprint §4.2 and GRAVEYARD_010 keep indirect host-APC presentation distinct from donor HLA loss; §4.3/ranker Decision Experiment #3 require functional granzyme testing. These data neither establish CIITA knockout superiority nor resolve those hazards.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (B2M loss and NK missing-self activation)
edges.claim_summary: B2M KO primary human T cells increased NK CD107a activation relative to WT (O6; P < .001, 3 technical replicates), supporting the shared missing-self hazard already addressed by Blueprint §1.2/§4.1 and the ranker B2M-without-shield branch. This is a T-cell-to-islet mechanistic bridge, not a test of the exact HLA-E/CD47 SC-islet product or direct target killing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (recipient matching and donor-dependent residual class-I allorecognition)
edges.claim_summary: O1 supports reduced direct CD8 recognition after B2M KO; O10/O11 show that single-allele HLA reduction remains recipient/donor dependent, including recognition of retained mismatched HLA-A2. Blueprint §3.2 already requires one matched HLA-C allele for Scenario B; incorporation of this specific primary-T-cell A2/A3 donor pattern is not established. CD8 activation is not demonstrated killing, and no islet or indirect-APC/autoimmune test is supplied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate2A / M1 (B2M-sparing canonical-HLA allele editing as an experimental comparator)
edges.claim_summary: A narrow candidate comparator is allele-level HLA editing that preserves beta2m and endogenous HLA-E while reducing canonical HLA, including the A2/A3/BC-negative T-cell phenotype (O9/O12-O14); endogenous HLA-E causality is hypothesized and its reduced expression matters. General matched-allele retention is already present in Blueprint Scenario B, with GRAVEYARD_005 requiring HLA-E verification; the exact alternative is not shown incorporated. O16-O18 measure CAR-mediated B-cell depletion rather than direct rejection escape; O19/O20 are matching calculations, not evidence for a universal SC-islet cloak.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (intrinsic cytoprotection and in vivo graft survival)
edges.claim_summary: In a marginal-mass primary human islet xenograft in immunocompetent mice, 8 weeks of BL001 was associated with preserved insulin-expressing cells and detectable human C-peptide versus vehicle (O7, O13), but hyperglycemia persisted and glucose tolerance did not improve at 4 weeks (O1, O5). No group sizes are stated and the host is a murine immune system, so transfer to a hPSC-derived allograft is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; small-molecule host-side adjunct to a genetic cloak)
edges.claim_summary: Pharmacological LRH-1/NR5A2 activation improved survival and human graft readouts (O3, O4, O13) while CD4+ infiltration was not significantly reduced (O12, O15), suggesting a host-side tolerizing small-molecule adjunct to gene-edited SC-islets; the cheatsheet lists no such element. Evidence is xenogeneic, unquantified in the packet and mechanism (tolerization) is not measured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization component of the avascular oxygen bridge; prevascularized site)
edges.claim_summary: In syngeneic mouse subcutaneous grafts, cure rate (O3, O4) and glucose tolerance (O5, O6) improved without a significant gain in vWF-positive vessels (O7) or CT vessel volume (54.5 vs 51.8 mm3, O12), so improved engraftment at a subcutaneous site was not explained by neovascularization in this model. This qualifies treating vascularization as the sole determinant of subcutaneous graft success; rodent, syngeneic mouse islets, so transfer to hPSC-derived islets is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (site pretreatment with bioabsorbable ECM scaffold as a prevascularized-device alternative)
edges.claim_summary: GHNF pretreatment, which raised capsule laminin (O9) and IGF-2 mRNA and protein (O14, O16), produced 100% (15/15) cure vs 22.7% (5/22) control and 35.7% (5/14) intraportal at 42 days (O3, O4); this suggests testing ECM/growth-factor site conditioning as an adjunct to oxygenation and prevascularization strategies for SC-islet grafts. Mechanism is inferred by the authors, graft-side effects were not measured, and the data are mouse-syngeneic.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation, maturation and off-target EC purity)
edges.claim_summary: Static versus shaker culture improved NKX6.1+/INS+ yield, maturation-marker expression and reduced SLC18A1 marker/cell abundance (O5/O7-O9), with supported static-GSIS and perifusion gains (O10/O21). Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §6 specify mature beta-cell function and <1% EC QC; this study does not establish the <1% release threshold, edited-product function, scale-up or causal protection. The specific static-format effect is not established as adopted by the bounded reference review.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (primary-islet functional benchmark and 60:30:10 input reference)
edges.claim_summary: Despite static-format gains, reported GSIS was roughly 22% of the human-islet reference, with half the insulin content and increased glucagon content (O11-O13); assay inputs and normalization remain local. Stage 7 versus stage 6 GCG+/INS+ ratio (O16) is not a full lineage mixture or an optimum. Blueprint §1.2 and §6.4 require dynamic function, rapid low-glucose shutoff and controlled re-aggregation; this paper does not test the final 60:30:10 edited product or resolve those gates. Incorporation of these exact empirical bounds remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (96-well process and maturation-screen replication hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: The 60-well consistency result and pilot fluorescence/GSIS contrasts support replication of this small-scale platform (O14/O17-O18/O24-O29), not manufacturing qualification. Frozen ranker dosing_unit explicitly already uses a stage 7 ZM447439 pulse for EC suppression (Balboa PMID35241836); this paper measures a different endpoint, static GSIS, and does not show ZM-induced EC depletion. The proposed process-screen replication, NAC fluorescence and exact ZM GSIS effects have no adoption established by the bounded reference review.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet purification handle; CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment baseline)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O4, O7: antibody-free DA-ZP1 FACS gave ~95% GCG+ (intermediate) and ~83% CPEP+ (bright) fractions from primary human islet cells, and ZIGIR/NPG did not resolve an intermediate alpha-cell cluster. This supports the Gate1 premise that sorted endocrine purification is feasible, but it is a different handle from CD49a/ITGA1 and was not tested on SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference)
edges.claim_summary: O13, O17, O10: alpha-only pseudoislets kept ~81% of alpha-enriched genes (O13) and glucose-responsive glucagon release (O10) over 10 days, yet 413 genes drifted in alpha-pseudoislets and 341 in unsorted pseudoislets versus 11 in intact native islets (O17), consistent with intact multi-cell architecture stabilizing the islet transcriptome. Adult primary human islets in vitro, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic integrity, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O4: excess gRNA drastically increased on-target large deletions and lowered point-mutation knock-in efficiency in rat embryos. The cheatsheet lists translocations, off-target base edits, chromothripsis and promoter silencing but not gRNA-dose-driven on-target large deletions, so this proposes adding RNP stoichiometry control and an on-target large-deletion readout to the multiplex-editing safety panel; shown only in rat embryos, not hPSC or islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 iCasp9 knock-in editing protocol)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3: an equimolar Cas9:gRNA RNP was optimal by nanoDSF, gave almost 50% GFP-to-BFP conversion in a GFP hiPSC line, and raising the ratio did not further improve knock-in. This suggests fixing equimolar RNP stoichiometry for hPSC knock-in steps; the bridge rests on RNP-formation biochemistry and a ssODN point-conversion readout, not a transgene-scale AAVS1 insertion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease-DSB genomic integrity at B2M and AAVS1, GRAVEYARD_006)
edges.claim_summary: The general DSB deletion/LOH hazard and orthogonal genomic QC are already accounted for: frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and section 6 specify 15-25 kb long-read sequencing with +/-50 kb flanking SNP LOH phasing and CAST-Seq, while GRAVEYARD_006 explicitly discusses deletion risk and OGM. O1/O3 and O9-O11 supply a hematopoietic-cell qualification: early amplicon-loss burden and viable CFU deletions can differ from end-process detection. They do not establish that the Blueprint regards AAVS1/B2M editing as benign, validate its sequential multi-locus process, or supply SC-islet deletion rates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 and M7 (calibration of orthogonal genomic QC: drop-off ddPCR, OGM filters and structural donor-integration checks)
edges.claim_summary: A bounded incremental hypothesis is to compare per-locus drop-off ddPCR tiling and reviewed OGM filters with existing long-read/CAST-Seq QC on the actual hPSC/SC-islet manufacturing process. O12/O20/O23 show event-specific OGM recovery at intended 10%/2.5% VAF; O13/O22 expose filter misses; O14/O15/O21/O24 show imprecise donor integration despite marker enrichment and retained population function. OGM itself is already prescribed by frozen GRAVEYARD_006, so adding OGM is not a demonstrated new gap; adoption of this exact assay-calibration bundle is not established. Portability requires validation, sufficient high-molecular-weight DNA and local performance controls; these experiments do not validate an SC-islet release threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (human SC-islet differentiation: Stage-4 progenitor purity boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2/O4/O6–O10/O19/O26 support improved Stage-4 pancreatic progenitor specification with AT7867 versus its control protocol in three healthy iPSC lines; O3/O5/O20 show no detected increase in cell yield or proliferation. O11/O18/O21/O27/O28 constrain interpretation: endocrine commitment differs, marker similarity is descriptive, and some source details conflict. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and §6 require mature tri-hormonal dynamic function and late-stage lineage purification; these progenitor assays do not establish that release gate. Specific incorporation of this chemistry or numerical findings is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (non-humanized renal-subcapsular PP graft maturation)
edges.claim_summary: O12/O13/O22/O24 support earlier glycemic reversal and 8-week functional maturation of AT7867 PP grafts; O14 is a null within-control test, not an interaction test. O15/O23/O25/O29–O31 retain distinct comparators and source uncertainty; nonsignificance does not prove convergence/equivalence. O17 reports greater MAFA positivity at day-90 recovery. One differentiation run per group and five mice for Fig4B/C in SCID beige hosts without human immune reconstitution provide T5 bioassay evidence, not immune protection or validation of Blueprint §1.2 mature edited tri-hormonal dynamic GSIS. Incorporation of these exact findings remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (non-endocrine graft overgrowth as an oncology-safety rationale for a clonogenic fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O16 shows smaller graft area with AT7867 but residual CK19+ cysts/SOX9+ tissue. This supports an off-target overgrowth concern consistent with frozen Blueprint §7 and ranker whole_product_safety_model effective-denominator definition, and scopes interpretation of the abstract highlight claiming teratoma elimination: Results supply cystic graft pathology, not a teratoma-incidence denominator. GRAVEYARD_002 concerns lineage-restricted switch escape; no switch/promoter or clonogenic escape was tested here. This is a justified safety bridge, not evidence for a specific iCasp9 design or hazard probability; incorporation of the specific cystic-area findings is unknown.

Proposal: add a donor copy-number QC step plus insert-confirmation PCR to clone release of an iCasp9/AAVS1 hPSC line; not tested in islet-lineage cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (prevascularized macroencapsulation device)
edges.claim_summary: In an acellular silicone macroencapsulation device in rats, VEGF microspheres increased peri-device vascular network volume (O1), the percentage of αSMA+ vessels (O5) and vessel diameter (O6) at 4 weeks, with no increase in fibrous capsule thickness (O8). No islets were loaded, so graft survival or function is untested.

edges.claim_summary: CD68+ macrophage volume and M1/M2-like phenotype were unchanged by VEGF (O11, O12), while the M1-like (CCR7+) fraction exceeded the M2-like (CD163+) fraction in both groups (O13). This is a host foreign body response to an acellular device in rats, not recognition of graft cells, so it only scopes the macrophage component of Gate3 for device-delivered grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (survival of islet cells under peri-transplant hypoxia and inflammatory cytokine exposure)
edges.claim_summary: Primary human islets cultured at 2% O2 for 3-4 days had higher overall survival with 5 µg/mL etanercept (47.2 ± 6.8% vs 28.6 ± 6.3%; O10), lower ROS (O9), and lower measured TNF-α/IP-10 release (O14/O15), with improved static stimulation index (O11). This provides an in-vitro bridge to the frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 stress-resilience objective; it does not validate the edited SC-islet product, an oxygen source, immune protection, or a clinical ETA regimen. Claim-specific incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate4 / M1 (endocrine function and dose-limited anti-inflammatory cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: In primary donor islets, 5 µg/mL ETA improved static stimulation index in normoxia (O2) and hypoxia (O11/O12); 20/40 µg/mL depleted intracellular insulin content (O20), had lower numerical SI without a significant high-dose SI test reported (O24), and increased basal release with unresolved Results/caption p-threshold reporting (O25). High doses also impaired morphological integrity (O3/O4/O19/O22/O23/O30/O31). This qualifies dose selection if ETA is considered alongside the Blueprint: static 2→20→2 mmol/L incubations do not establish §1.2 Gate1 biphasic GSIS, rapid shut-off, or exact-product function. M1 applies to the drug perturbation; primary-islet culture does not justify M2. Specific adoption is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (possible interaction with Locus 3 CXCL10::SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1 induction)
edges.claim_summary: ETA reduced IP-10/CXCL10 protein release from hypoxic primary donor islets (O15). If ETA is considered as an adjunct, a bounded hypothesis is to test whether it changes the actual Locus-3 payload induction described in frozen Blueprint §4.3 and ranker Decision Experiment #3. The paper measured released protein and no promoter activity, payload or edited product; protein reduction alone does not establish transcriptional damping. GRAVEYARD_001 concerns specific IFN-pathway edits and NF-κB bypass, so it cannot be treated as empirical proof of an ETA interaction. Claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic integrity; Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: After Cas9 RNP cleavage, large on-target deletions were considerably lower in undifferentiated iPSCs than in T cells and HSPCs (O1), yet one of 52 iPSC clones still carried a one-allele deletion (O16), with no loss of heterozygosity (O17) and no mega-deletions by qPCR (O18). On-target large deletions are therefore a cell-type-dependent failure mode to screen for in nuclease-edited hPSC clones; no islet-lineage cells were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 knock-in and nuclease-only knockout steps)
edges.claim_summary: An HDR donor present at the Cas9 cut reduced AAVS1 deletion indexes by 90% with AAV6 in T cells (O10) and by about 52% with ssODN (O6), and a short dsODN insertion reduced deletions by about 60% in T cells and HSPCs (O14). Hypothesis: co-delivering a donor or dsODN at nuclease-only edit steps could reduce on-target large deletions in hPSC engineering; effects were shown in T cells and HSPCs, and in iPSCs ssODN and AAV6 gave no significant change from low baseline (O7, O12).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex nuclease editing genomic-integrity safety)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O6, O8, O10, O14 and O16: Cas9 double-strand-break editing favored pre-existing p53-mutant and KRAS-mutant cells over wild-type cells in leukemia lines, RPE1 cells and cell-line datasets, supporting DSB-based editing as a Gate5 genomic-safety concern. Shown only in cancer or immortalized lines (no hPSC or islet cells), so the bridge is the generic DSB-p53 damage response.

edges.claim_summary: O11 and O12: most (71.9–82.9%) in vivo ITR-Seq off-target sites were absent from in vitro GUIDE-Seq calls, suggesting the genomic-safety panel should add an in vivo or orthogonal off-target readout for transplanted edited cells rather than rely on a single in vitro nomination assay. ITR-Seq needs AAV delivery, so it is not directly applicable to hPSC editing.

This supports including oncogene-locus off-target and nuclease-independent integration checks in Gate5 safety work; mouse liver with AAV, not hPSC.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (choice of off-target nomination assay for Islet-1 gRNAs)
edges.claim_summary: Against the initial hybrid-capture reference, GUIDE-seq precision was 0.225 versus 0.007 and 0.014; read-count/editing R2 was 0.7 versus 0.36 and 0.01, while nominated-site identity reproducibility was 30% versus 72% and 60.4% (O8-O10, O13-O17). Since Blueprint section 9.4 already names GUIDE-seq, the incremental hypothesis is to qualify a cell-matched, replicated nomination-plus-computational workflow with orthogonal confirmation of low-frequency/low-complexity calls, informed by six of 152 rhAmpSeq sites above 0.2% and the probable single hybrid-capture artifact (M2359_O18-M2359_O19). Transfer to actual Islet-1 hPSC guides and nucleases is unvalidated; adoption of these study-specific assay-choice criteria is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe: tumorigenic risk of residual undifferentiated hPSCs)

This supports a clonogenic fail-safe for residual pluripotent cells, bridged from CMs rather than SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularized graft integration; 72-hour oxygen-bridge relevance is a transfer hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 associate 14-d preimplantation endothelial/fibroblast scaffold culture with increased graft-host anastomosis, approximately eightfold host-vessel penetration and sixfold graft perfusion; exact comparator and postimplantation timing are not reported. The frozen Blueprint already specifies pre-lumenized iEC:iPericyte fragments and direct Stage-2 lumen-patency/inosculation qualification (section 4.5), while the ranker bundles a vascular niche prior. Incorporation of these specific abstract findings is unknown; this non-islet scaffold evidence does not validate the exact edited islet product, a 72-hour anastomosis threshold or bridge sufficiency.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 (thrombo-inflammatory scope), Gate5 / M3, M7 (prevascularized graft maturity and thrombosis failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O6 provide a qualitative maturity-associated thrombosis boundary: short-term/less mature scaffold constructs showed thrombus accumulation and elevated vWF/TF, whereas developed networks prevented clot accumulation. The abstract supplies neither exact short-term arm assignments nor a quantitative coagulation endpoint, and O4/O5 overlap. Blueprint section 1.2 includes thrombo-inflammatory Gate3 scope and section 4.5 requires lumen-patency/inosculation qualification; incorporation of this specific maturity-vWF/TF boundary is unknown. This scoped link does not establish NK/macrophage protection, IBMIR causality, a numeric maturity release criterion or exact-product safety.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation: beta-cell marker expression and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: hiPSC-derived islet organoids under perfused 3D culture showed enhanced PDX1 and NKX6.1, increased INS and C-peptide expression, more sensitive GSIS and higher Ca2+ flux than static culture (O1-O5). Supports Gate1 maturation readouts in the right cell type, but the abstract gives no magnitudes, stimulation index, n or statistics.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biomimetic perfusion as an added maturation lever)
edges.claim_summary: The authors attribute the improvements to biomimetic mechanical flow promoting endocrine differentiation and maturation (O1-O5). Hypothesis: test perfused or flow-based culture as an added maturation condition for Islet-1 SC-islets; chip format is not the Blueprint manufacturing format and no magnitudes are available.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage 4-6 SC-beta differentiation: Hippo/YAP inhibition as a protocol lever)
edges.claim_summary: Stage-dependent YAP inhibition is a Gate1/M2 differentiation hypothesis: verteporfin increased the C-peptide+/NKX6.1+ fraction from 27.5 +/- 4.2% to 38.6 +/- 3.9% (mean +/- SEM), whereas early progenitor inhibition impaired NKX6.1 specification (O1-O4). Static secretion normalized to insulin content increased at basal and stimulated conditions, but SI did not differ significantly (O10-O11); neither nonsignificance nor higher basal output proves improved dynamic GSIS, rapid shut-off, or yield per starting hPSC. Blueprint section 1.2 and purification section 6.4 require endpoints not measured here; claim-specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3; Gate5 / M5 (residual SOX9+ progenitor depletion as a bounded safety-proxy hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: Verteporfin reduced SOX9+ and Ki67+ populations in vitro; 12-week SCID-beige kidney grafts contained ~17% SOX9+ cells in controls versus an average 3.1% after verteporfin differentiation (O13-O17; SOX9/DAPI fraction, n = 4 animals per histology group). Both groups had reported 8-week glucose responses, without an established between-group equivalence test or GSIS n. This supports a testable progenitor-depletion manufacturing hypothesis and a Gate5/M5 safety-proxy bridge; no clonogenic escape, tumor prevention, pan-lineage iCasp9 response, or oxygen bridge was measured. M3 denotes in vivo graft evidence. Blueprint section 7 already distinguishes marker burden from effective clonogenic safety denominators; adoption of this specific YAP intervention remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation; functional GSIS benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: In hiPSC-derived S7 cells, TKi improved IF composition (O1, O2) and proteome distance to adult islets (O10), yet static GSIS (O9), hormone levels (O15) and ion-channel levels (O17) were not improved, so composition or proteome shifts do not equal functional maturation. Only static GSIS was assayed here, not dynamic perifusion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-7 maturation additive to lower bi-hormonal cells)
edges.claim_summary: TKi (G007-LK, 5 umol/L, 4 h) at S7 raised the insulin+ fraction and lowered the bi-hormonal fraction versus untreated S7 (O1, O2) with a mild viability cost (O18), proposing Wnt inhibition as a candidate lever against bi-hormonal cells. Evidence is modest, three hiPSC lines, IF counts not numerically stated in text, and no GSIS gain (O9).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex base-editing genomic safety: guide-independent off-target RNA editing and indels)
edges.claim_summary: HEK293T ABEmax overexpression increased RNA A-to-I editing above endogenous background, including Cas9-fusion-independent TadA activity (O1-O3, O6-O9); indels can remain despite inactive TadA* DNA base editing (O21). This bounds safety-scoping for a future ABE implementation, while frozen Blueprint §5/GRAVEYARD_006 and the ranker already address broader DNA structural/nickase risk. Adoption of this specific RNA-screening boundary is not established; cell-line results do not quantify hPSC/SC-islet or multiplex risk.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (adenine base-editor variant choice, ABEmaxAW)
edges.claim_summary: ABEmaxAW reduced cell-line RNA editing, candidate-site DNA off-target editing and indels relative to ABEmax (O10-O16), with a lower mean on-target rate (36 ± 1.4% versus 47 ± 3.9%; O12) and exposure-dependent RNA observations (O19-O20). This is a conditional editor-comparison hypothesis for an ABE-dependent Islet-1 edit; hPSC/SC-islet manufacturing performance, long-term protein consequences and product safety are untested. The frozen references do not establish adoption of this specific editor choice.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M3 (intrinsic cytoprotection and pre-transplant conditioning of islet cells)
edges.claim_summary: Ferroptosis inducers caused roughly 20-24% LDH release and lower stimulation index in primary human islets (O1-O4), rescuable in vitro by Fer-1 or DFO (O6, O7, O9, O11), but erastin challenge or Fer-1 pre-treatment did not change engraftment in RAG-/- recipients (O16-O18). In vitro rescue should not be assumed to give graft benefit; primary islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (GPX4-glutathione-iron ferroptosis axis as a possible cytoprotection element)
edges.claim_summary: Human islets are susceptible to GSH-depletion (erastin, CHAC1 up, O14) and GPX4-inhibition (RSL3, O3) ferroptosis, so a GPX4/GSH/iron node could be tested as an addition to Gate4 stress-resilience elements for SC-islets. Evidence is in vitro in primary islets only, and the in vivo readouts were null (O16-O18).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe; residual undifferentiated cells in a differentiated hPSC graft)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O18: untreated hiPSC-CM grafts in NOG mice formed tumours in 9/15 (subcutaneous) and 5/6 (heart) mice with high Ki-67-positive cell density, whereas brentuximab vedotin-treated grafts formed none (0/16, 0/8), consistent with the Gate5 premise that residual pluripotent cells in a differentiated hPSC product are tumourigenic. The product is cardiomyocytes in immunodeficient mice, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 + M2 (non-genetic pre-transplant purge of CD30-positive residual pluripotent cells as a layer beside iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O10: CD30 was on 91.2 ± 10.9% of hiPSCs vs 0.4 ± 0.4% of hiPSC-CMs, and brentuximab vedotin killed hiPSCs (> 85% death in Ff-I14) and lowered Lin28 in CMs. Hypothesis: a CD30-ADC purge step could add a genome-edit-free layer for the Gate5 residual-pluripotent fraction of SC-islets; CD30 status and MMAE tolerance of SC-islet cells were not tested here, and CM tolerance had a narrow window (O11, O14).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (primary-islet endocrine-function readouts; bridge to SC-islet M2)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O4 provide primary-human-islet evidence for morphology/GSIS/first-phase readouts: up to 2.5-fold higher GSIS (p < 0.001) and a qualitatively more pronounced first phase, without proving morphology equivalence or SC-islet maturity. Gate1 already requires dynamic endocrine testing (frozen Blueprint:61,245-247), but incorporation of these exact HDCM findings is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (size-controlled SC-islet reaggregation; transfer from primary-islet M7 evidence)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3 report up to 4.0-fold rat and 2.5-fold human GSIS gains, whereas O5/O6 provide species-unresolved size dependence and up to six-fold insulin content per cell; these do not identify an SC-islet optimum or prove an oxygen benefit. Controlled reaggregation and size caps are already explicit in frozen Blueprint:61,65,246 and ranker:490-495,5596-5611, so blanket novelty is rejected; adoption of this exact 250-cell HDCM protocol/effect remains unknown.

edges.claim_summary: O3, O4: PEC proliferation declines with CDKN1A and CDKN2A up-regulation, and reducing either in a defined time window increased proliferation and GP2+ yield. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex-editing genomic-safety release criteria: karyotype, aneuploidy and identity QC)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O5, O10, O12, O17: hiPSCs with reactivated reprogramming transgenes (LU07+Dox) formed embryonal carcinoma-like OCT3/4+/NANOG+ tumours in NSG mice yet showed no aneuploidy by qPCR in tumours, 1 of 20 cells with +12 before injection, and normal PluriTest results. edges.claim_summary: O2, O3, O17, O18: the NSG teratoma/xenograft assay separated malignant LU07+Dox and hEC tumours from normal teratomas, while PluriTest flagged only hEC. Hypothesis: add an in vivo xenograft malignancy readout and monitoring of integrated-cassette reactivation to hPSC line release criteria for Gate5; shown on undifferentiated lines, not SC-islet products.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (differentiation-linked cassette silencing and pan-lineage fail-safe expression)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O6, O15 and O16 supply murine SFFV.eGFP retention evidence for the already recognized differentiation-silencing failure mode: SG retention is 7%/4% in mESC/miPSC assays, 1–5% at ROSA26 and 31–42% at TIGRE. Frozen Blueprint §4.4 and §7 explicitly recognize differentiation-linked methylation/silencing and require qualification; ranker Shared_Promoter_Epigenetic_CpG_Methylation requires post-differentiation stress challenge. Incorporation here concerns that failure-mode principle, not adoption of these mouse percentages as iCasp9 escape rates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (locus/promoter context and differentiation-specific expression qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O15–O18 qualify transfer across loci and cell states: C-SG retains 7–15% at ROSA26 versus 71–89% at TIGRE after differentiation, with distinct pluripotent behavior. The frozen Blueprint already treats the exact 455-bp HNRNPA2B1-proximal candidate as function pending and requires head-to-head lineage qualification against the published CBX3-side fragment (Layer-2 status, §4.4). These murine ROSA26/TIGRE reporter findings reinforce that qualification boundary; they neither test AAVS1/EEF1A1/iCasp9 nor establish failure of the current human construct.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (CpG-preserving scrambled CBX3 comparator for anti-silencing qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O11–O13 motivate a bounded comparator hypothesis: test a CpG-preserving scrambled element beside the published 679-bp CBX3 and the distinct current 455-bp HNRNPA2B1-proximal candidate. CscrCpG gives 33%/47% post-differentiation relative reporter retention versus SG 8%/3% despite almost absent autonomous promoter activity; fully scrambled Cscr has no significant protection in this assay, which is not proof of zero activity. Blueprint already uses an anti-silencing candidate and requires the published-CBX3 comparison; incorporation of this exact scrambled comparator is not established by the inspected frozen references. No human SC-islet, AAVS1, EEF1A1 or iCasp9-functional validation is supplied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (avascular oxygen diffusion limits; slab and Krogh-type size physics)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3, O4: in rat islet-cell aggregates cultured in medium, the dead-cell area ratio rose from 0.11 ± 0.02% (49.5 ± 4.9 μm) to 11.26 ± 5.13% (222.8 ± 16.6 μm), hypoxic core cells increased with size, and the authors infer hypoxia-linked death above 150 μm, consistent with diffusion-limited core hypoxia. Rat cells with oxygen from culture medium, not an avascular graft oxygen bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (size-controlled SC-islet clusters for GSIS and alpha/beta architecture)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O6, O7, O11, O12: 49.5 μm pseudo-islets showed less cell death, insulin-central/glucagon-peripheral arrangement and higher day 7 high-glucose insulin release than larger aggregates, but the GSIS advantage was gone by day 14 (O12) and delta cells and dynamic perifusion were not assessed. Hypothesis: engineer SC-islet cluster size as a Gate1 manufacturing lever; untested in hPSC-derived cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (human-islet reference values normalised per IEQ for secretion and viability benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O5, O6: conventional IEQ overestimated large-islet tissue volume by nearly double and gave different viability and insulin secretion concentrations than a cell-number method, so absolute per-IEQ human-islet reference values are size-dependent. This qualifies any Gate1 comparison of SC-islet output with per-IEQ human-islet values; ratio indices such as the stimulation index were not tested in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (cell-number-based normalisation of SC-islet cluster dose and GSIS data)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2: human islets are non-spherical (smallest/largest diameter ratio 0.73 in large vs 0.85 in small) and diameter predicts cell number with R(2) = 0.99, supporting a hypothesis to normalise SC-islet cluster dose and secretion by counted cells rather than assumed spherical volume. Not tested on SC-islets, whose shape and size distribution are unmeasured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (Locus 4 AAVS1 safe-harbor insertion with constitutive expression persisting through differentiation)
