edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic integrity of the hPSC starting line; multiplex-editing genomic safety)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O3 report that enzymatic single-cell passaging of hESC lines produced karyotype abnormalities, copy number variations and DNA double-strand-break association within five passages. This qualifies Gate5(b) genomic-integrity readouts: lesions in an edited line may arise from culture method rather than from editing, and the cheatsheet does not state this culture-induced failure mode. The bridge is from unedited hESC lines to hPSC-derived islet manufacturing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (release testing of banked hPSC lines beyond routine karyotype)
edges.claim_summary: O4 (the authors' recommendation) proposes adding microarray-based subchromosomal copy number screening to routine karyotyping; applied to Islet-1 banks this is a hypothesis for the genomic-safety release panel, with no data in this abstract on islet-fate cells or edited lines.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease-induced genomic rearrangement hazard)
edges.claim_summary: O14-O16 support the existing precaution that nuclease-induced DSBs can participate in translocations, deletions and inversions. Frozen Blueprint Stage 4 and section 8 GMP-editing row, plus GRAVEYARD_006, already require sequential editing and structural-genomic QC; this link concerns that incorporated hazard, not adoption of O1/O7 cell-line magnitudes. The study tested individual Cas9 RGNs in U2OS/HEK293, not simultaneous Islet-1 multiplex editing, HiFi-SpCas9, AsCas12a, base editing or prime editing; it cannot calibrate their product-specific rates or the ranker penalty.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (scope and empirical qualification of genome-wide off-target mapping and translocation QC)
edges.claim_summary: O10-O12 distinguish GUIDE-Seq cleavage mapping from the historical MIT/E-CRISP predictions and dCas9 binding maps. O19/O21 validate different assays in tagged versus RGN-alone cells, while O22 shows recovery was not complete. The general empirical-testing principle is already explicit: frozen Blueprint section 9.4 names pending Cas-OFFinder / GUIDE-seq and NOT_ENUMERATED genome-wide status, Stage 4 requires CAST-Seq, and GRAVEYARD_006 specifies structural QC. Therefore empirical mapping is not a new absent safety layer; transfer of this GUIDE-Seq protocol and its sensitivity to exact edited hPSC clones remains unvalidated, with no validated Islet-1 detection limit supplied by this study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (candidate truncated Cas9-guide comparison at CXCL10 and AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O18 supports testing truncated versus full-length Cas9 guides at intended Islet-1 loci, using empirical genome-wide and on-target validation; O22 prevents assuming complete off-target recovery. Frozen Blueprint section 9.4 specifies 20-nt HiFi-SpCas9 spacers for CXCL10 and AAVS1, so the proposed truncated-guide comparison is a distinct candidate experiment beyond that specified design. The paper tested VEGFA and EMX1 guides, not Islet-1 loci or HiFi-SpCas9; no efficacy/safety transfer is established. Its Cas9 result does not directly justify truncating the 23-nt AsCas12a B2M/CIITA guides.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual undifferentiated hPSC release testing alongside the iCasp9 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O11, O13 and O14 show a LIN28/ddPCR assay detecting 0.001% hiPSCs spiked into cardiomyocytes (12.4 copies versus LLOD 6.0) with LIN28 below 1.5 copies in all tested normal tissues including pancreas. Hypothesis: add a LIN28/ddPCR residual-pluripotent-cell release assay for SC-islet batches; bridge is the shared pluripotency-marker logic, but SC-islet background was not measured and the cheatsheet does not state such a release assay.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (assay detection limit versus clinical cell dose; tumorigenicity fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O10 and O17 give a theoretical limit of one cell in 500,000 and the authors' statement that this is insufficient for a dose of at least 109 cardiomyocytes, so a negative residual-cell assay cannot alone demonstrate safety. This qualifies reliance on in vitro detection for Gate5(b) next to the cheatsheet's <1e-6 iCasp9 escape threshold (different quantities); the dose is cardiac-specific and an islet dose was not assessed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture: beta-cell Ucn3 to delta-cell somatostatin negative feedback)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3, O4, O5 and O7 show that beta-cell Ucn3 acts on delta-cell Crhr2 and that Ucn3-null mouse islets have fewer delta cells, less somatostatin content and release, and exaggerated insulin release; O13 shows Ucn3 stimulating somatostatin release from human islets. This supports the Gate1 paracrine-architecture element (delta cells in the 60:30:10 reference) as functional; the cheatsheet does not state this Ucn3 feedback mechanism, and no SC-islet material was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet release functional testing: somatostatin feedback)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10 and O11 show somatostatin release depending on Ucn3-Crhr2 signalling and Ast2B acutely raising insulin secretion in perfused mouse islets. Hypothesis only: perifusion with a Crhr2 antagonist could test whether SC-islet batches contain functional delta-cell feedback; this was not tested in SC-islets or human perifusion here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (stability of maturation and function readouts in a hyperglycemic host)
edges.claim_summary: O14, O17 and O18 show beta-cell UCN3 lowered in ob/ob mice, Type 2 diabetic donor islets and high-fat-diet macaque islets, and O16 shows restoring Ucn3 worsened glycemia in ob/ob mice. This qualifies reading beta-cell marker expression as a fixed maturity readout for a graft placed in a hyperglycemic or insulin-resistant host; no graft or SC-islet data are in the packet.

edges.claim_summary: O8, O11 and O12 show a germline SNV creating a two-mismatch allele edited at 36.7% (reference allele 1%), and O15, O17 and O18 estimate ~1.5-8.5% SNV-created off-target likelihood from in silico analysis. This qualifies guide off-target screens that rely on the reference genome only: for the Islet-1 line, line-specific genome sequence is needed before guide selection; the cheatsheet does not state this failure mode.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (durability of insulated iCasp9 cassette at Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O4 and O5 show A2UCOE stabilizing transgene expression with viral promoter/enhancer elements. Hypothesis only: test A2UCOE flanking or substitution for the iCasp9 promoter to guard against silencing and escape; the cheatsheet names an insulated iCasp9 cassette but not A2UCOE, and the abstract used retroviral transgenes, not safe-harbor knock-in.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter silencing as a failure mode of integrated cassettes in hPSC)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O10 and O12 show the SFFV-eGFP lentiviral vector strongly silenced in hESCs (below 10% of day-8 eGFP+ cells at day 36) with nearly 90% promoter CpG methylation. This supports promoter silencing as a real Gate5(b) failure mode in hPSC; the bridge is the shared hPSC epigenetic machinery, but this is a viral promoter in semi-random lentiviral integrations, not a safe-harbor cassette, and the cheatsheet states no such magnitudes.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (sufficiency of insulation for the iCasp9 cassette at Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10 and O12 show that even the best insulator left residual silencing: SE-IS2 kept only more than 40% of day-8 eGFP+ cells at day 36 and SE-IS2Rev retained 50% promoter CpG methylation. This qualifies the assumption that an insulated cassette is silencing-proof for a suicide-switch escape threshold; lentiviral SFFV data in hESCs, not AAVS1 knock-in.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (insulator choice for suicide-switch and cytoprotection cassettes)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O9, O14, O15, O16 and O17 show the chimeric IS2 (HS4-650 plus SAR2) outperforming SAR2 and HS4 elements on silencing, variability and expression in hESCs and hematopoietic progeny, at the cost of about half the titer in K562 (O18). Hypothesis only: test IS2-type insulators for Islet-1 knock-in cassettes; no islet-fate cells or safe-harbor loci were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (NKX6-1+/INS+/MAFA+ beta-cell identity and stimulus-responsive endocrine function)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O4-O6 support the biological rationale for Gate1's existing mature beta-cell identity and regulated secretion requirements: NKX6.1-high progenitors produced stimulus-responsive, nuclear-MAFA-positive insulin-positive grafts with diabetes reversal in mice. Incorporation refers only to the explicit identity/function requirements in frozen Blueprint section 1.2, not these study-specific timings or proportions; in-vivo progenitor maturation in a Theracyte device does not establish edited Stage-7 product performance, biphasic GSIS, low-glucose shut-off, immune protection, or clinical qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hypothesis: pre-transplant NKX6.1 progenitor fraction as an in-process characterization criterion)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4 associate approximately 80% versus 25% pre-transplant NKX6.1 expression, with approximately 85%-90% PDX1 expression in both protocol-derived populations, with different subsequent graft outcomes. This motivates testing progenitor-stage NKX6.1 fraction as an in-process characterization criterion; two modified differentiation protocols do not isolate NKX6.1 causality or establish a release cutoff, and the Islet-1 edited Stage-7 protocol was not tested. Frozen Blueprint sections 1.2 and 6 already specify mature identity and intracellular NKX6-1/C-peptide QC, but adoption of this distinct progenitor-stage criterion is not established by the supplied references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O4 show that HLA-E presenting leader-like peptides engages CD94-NKG2 and that some UL40 peptides inhibit target lysis via CD94-NKG2A, consistent with the NKG2A-engagement mechanism of the Locus 1 HLA-E design. Evidence is from viral peptides and human NK clones, not islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E peptide dependence, NKG2A vs NKG2C readout)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O5 show that HLA-E engagement of CD94-NKG2 depends on the presented peptide sequence (reduced affinity with non-HLA-identical variants) and that peptide variants can inhibit via NKG2A while barely activating via NKG2C, qualifying the HLA-E design: the peptide identity in the HLA-E construct matters, and NKG2C+ subsets should be tested against it. Abstract gives no quantitative values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection, candidate anti-Fas/caspase-8 element)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 show that TOSO (Faim) blocks Fas-pathway beta-cell apoptosis in human islets and that its loss induces apoptosis, proposing TOSO as a candidate Gate4 cytoprotective element that the cheatsheet Gate4 list does not name. Evidence is in primary human islets in vitro (not SC-islets) and O6 shows a limited replication capacity.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hPSC pancreatic-lineage manufacturing and in vivo functional maturation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O9 and O19 support scalable CyT49 Stage-4 pancreatic-progenitor manufacturing followed by functional maturation in ordinary SCID/Bg mice (228/240 with a reported glucose response). Nonsignificant bank means in O7 do not prove equivalence. This is a bridge to Gate1/M2 and in vivo M3 evidence: it does not qualify the Blueprint’s edited mature Stage-7 60:30:10 product, perifusion dynamics, or immune protection. Specific adoption status is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification and off-target cell elimination baseline)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O6/O22 describe unsorted Stage-4 progenitor populations containing immature endocrine/poly-hormonal, PE and PDX1-only fractions, followed by human C-peptide responses developing over weeks in vivo (O8-O12/O19). This provides a delivery-stage qualification for Gate1 maturation/purification discussions, not evidence to relax the Blueprint’s mature Stage-7 sorting, SLC18A1 purge or dynamic-function gates; no sorted-versus-unsorted comparison or human immune protection was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety, hPSC bank karyotype)
edges.claim_summary: O17 documents post-thaw mosaic aneuploidy and disqualification of one bank expansion without a reported genome-editing intervention, relevant as a baseline-manufacturing caveat alongside the Blueprint’s Gate5 genomic QC. Separately, mature grafts could contain ductal cysts (O16/O21), whereas rare OCT4+/SOX2+/NANOG- cells were observed in early day-5 differentiating aggregates (O18), not demonstrated as pluripotent cells in mature grafts. These findings do not measure tumor incidence, iCasp9 escape, or safety of the exact edited product; specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (candidate adjunct for hPSC genomic QC; no GRAVEYARD_006 translocation-risk validation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O7 support only a hypothesis to assess bead-based whole-pool DNA karyotyping as a routine adjunct for hPSC chromosomal QC. Abstract concordance and low-input claims are qualitative; the packet establishes no numeric mosaic detection threshold, balanced-rearrangement coverage or edited-product performance. The reviewed Blueprint Stage-4 QC and GRAVEYARD_006 already require orthogonal genomic surveillance; this assay is not a demonstrated replacement, and incorporation of this specific assay is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (baseline hESC chromosomal abnormalities and passage-aware genomic QC)
edges.claim_summary: O8-O12 document abnormal G-banding entries in hESC samples without a described genetic-edit intervention, providing baseline context for edited-line QC rather than evidence of editing-induced damage, culture-acquisition timing or passage-dependent incidence. Sample and G-banding passages are distinct, including H9 P99/P112 entries karyotyped P60. Blueprint Stage-4 and ranker genomic-surveillance sections already address longitudinal/pre-existing clonal QC; incorporation of these exact specimen findings remains unknown and they do not contradict GRAVEYARD_006.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (promoter silencing, EEF1A1-driven insulated cassette at a defined safe-harbor-type locus)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 report that cHS4 double-insulator-flanked single-copy EF1alpha-GFP and CAG-GFP cassettes kept constitutive expression through prolonged culture and directed differentiation including pancreatic endoderm, consistent with using an insulated EEF1A1 cassette. The cargo is GFP at chromosome 13q32.3 in hESC lines, not iCasp9 at AAVS1 in SC-islets, and no silencing or escape frequencies are given.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytokine-resistance element: SOCS-1 / IFN-gamma-IRF-1 axis, beyond TNFAIP3/A20)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show beta-cell SOCS-1 expression made mouse islets more resistant to TNF-alpha with or without IFN-gamma, with IRF-1 inhibition correlating with protection, proposing SOCS-1 as a Gate4 cytoprotection candidate absent from the cheatsheet list. Evidence is from transgenic mouse islets only, with no human or SC-islet data and no values in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (single cytoprotective factor in a fully allogeneic setting)
edges.claim_summary: O5 shows the cytokine-resistant SOCS-1 islets delayed rejection of an allograft by at least 2 weeks rather than preventing it, and O4 shows only an impairment of IFN-gamma-induced class I MHC upregulation, so one cytoprotective transgene does not substitute for class I ablation or other layers. Mouse strain-mismatch model only; abstract gives no rejection-free duration.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (insertion-locus vetting for Locus 4 AAVS1/GAPDH and other cassette loci)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 show only about 10% of random lentiviral integrations met five position-based safe harbor criteria, with one named clone meeting all five (O4), and O2 and O3 report high-level expression without neighboring-gene perturbation at such sites. This proposes auditing each Blueprint insertion locus against explicit position criteria (gene proximity, cancer genes, miRNAs, ultraconserved regions). Evidence is a lentiviral globin vector with erythroid readout in thalassemia iPSCs, not targeted knock-in in SC-islets.

edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4 and O5 describe a roughly 200 microL stirred chamber whose OCR scales with viable cell number and tracks membrane integrity, proposing small-sample OCR measurement to parameterise and release-test the oxygen demand used in avascular oxygen-bridge modelling. It was characterised on betaTC3 cells and islets, not SC-islets, and the abstract gives no OCR values or precision numbers.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (KIR2DL1-HLA-C missing-self axis, KIR+ NKG2A-negative NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: O10, O16 and O17 provide a structural rationale for the Gate3 KIR2DL1–HLA-C axis: P8Lys is 68% surface-exposed, residue 80 lies in the proposed receptor-facing patch, and the separately analyzed ligand/receptor surfaces have complementary polarity. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (existing Plan B'-SCT C2 HLA-C/peptide candidate for KIR2DL1+ NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: The frozen Blueprint line 125 already names the Plan B'-SCT C2 candidate, and frozen rank_islet1_stacks.py lines 4372–4409 explicitly incorporate PMID:10429675 and HLA-C*04:01/QYDDAVYKL SCT with product-specific qualification gates. O10/O16/O17 supply native-ligand structural rationale but do not validate tethering, Y84A engineering, KIR-subset inhibition or SC-islet protection; the proposal is an existing unvalidated candidate rather than a newly uncovered upgrade.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (KIR2DL2/3 engagement of HLA-C, KIR+ NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: The KIR2DL2/Cw3 structure shows KIR contacts peptide positions 7 and 8 and an Asn 80-dependent allotype contact (O2, O4), giving a structural basis for the KIR axis the Blueprint evaluates. It is a recombinant-protein structure with no cellular NK assay in the abstract, and the cheatsheet does not state these contact determinants.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (scope of HLA-C retention for inhibiting KIR+ NK cells)
edges.claim_summary: KIR contact requires peptide position 8 to be smaller than valine and depends on an allotype-specific Lys 44 to Asn 80 hydrogen bond (O1, O2), so HLA-C-mediated KIR inhibition is gated by allotype and peptide rather than by HLA-C presence alone. This qualifies any assumption that a retained HLA-C molecule universally inhibits KIR+ NK cells; the abstract does not test engineered cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 with Gate4 (XIAP cytoprotection versus iCasp9 suicide-switch kill)

The cheatsheet lists XIAP as a Gate4 cytoprotective element and iCasp9 as the Gate5 suicide switch, so XIAP-mediated caspase-9 inhibition could blunt suicide-switch kill if XIAP is raised; the abstract tests neither iCasp9 nor islets, and whether iCasp9 retains the XIAP-binding linker is not stated in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (immunogenicity of the peptide carried by a single-chain trimer)
edges.claim_summary: Single-chain trimers carrying an antigenic peptide were potent stimulators of peptide-specific CTL and antibodies (O5, O6), so a trimer scaffold is not immunologically inert and its tethered peptide must be chosen to avoid recognition. This qualifies an assumption of inertness only; the abstract tests classical class I with antigenic peptides, not an HLA-E trimer with a leader peptide in a graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E allele choice in the Locus 1 single-chain HLA-E trimer)
edges.claim_summary: The two major HLA-E alleles had similar steady-state protein but different cell surface levels, peptide affinity and thermal stability (O1, O2, O4, O5), so the HLA-E allele used is a design variable for surface HLA-E that engages NKG2A. The abstract does not say which allele is higher, does not test a single-chain trimer or hPSC-derived islet cells, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether the Blueprint already fixes an allele.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M7 (structural invariance of HLA-E across peptides and alleles)
edges.claim_summary: Crystal structures showed no significant change in HLA-E architecture on binding different peptides or on the position 107 substitution (O3), which supports treating the HLA-E scaffold as structurally stable when the tethered peptide or allele changes. The abstract gives no RMSD values and does not assess NKG2A recognition of those peptides.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (indirect host-APC priming pathway)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show in mice that DC cross-presentation via an MHC class I tyrosine-based routing signal contributes to CTL priming against viral epitopes (no numbers in the abstract), which is mechanistic background for host-APC (indirect) priming against graft antigens in Gate2B. The study uses viral antigens in mice, not allogeneic islets, and the cheatsheet names only indirect CD4+ presentation, so whether the Blueprint covers host-DC CD8 cross-priming cannot be settled.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 / M7 (residual class I conformation and alloreactive CTL recognition after beta 2m loss; B2M Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show conformed mouse Db heavy chains on beta 2m-negative cells and alloreactive CTL lysis of Con A blast targets even in serum-free conditions (O2), qualifying any absolute claim that beta 2m loss abolishes direct class I recognition. This is a justified mechanistic bridge to Gate2A B2M-edited human SC-islets, without human-islet validation or quantitative effect estimates. The frozen ranker already cites PMID:1512546 for residual-heavy-chain/exogenous-beta2m concerns and a proposed W6/32 plus CTL challenge (lines 4562-4571), while Blueprint section 4.1 and graveyard 010 retain categorical direct-presentation elimination language; incorporation of the distinct serum-free susceptibility finding is therefore unknown.

Transfer of a disulfide trap to the Locus-1 HLA-E*01:03(VMAPRTLVL) SCT remains a hypothesis: the supplied abstract provides no HLA-E, NKG2A/NKG2C, NK-protection, human-islet or graft evidence. The frozen Blueprint specifies the HLA-E tethered-peptide architecture (section 4.1), but incorporation of this particular HLA-E disulfide-trap hypothesis is not established; the ranker's explicit DT-1 comparator concerns HLA-C, not HLA-E.

edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 provide murine SCT engineering rationale for a disulfide-trapped peptide comparator, with no human HLA-C/KIR functional validation in the supplied abstract. The frozen ranker already cites PMID:17475856 for its planned DT-1 HLA-C(Y84C, A139-WT) plus L1-Cys2 comparator in the Plan B'-SCT Gate 0B-SCT panel (rank_islet1_stacks.py:4373-4395); those human construct details and proposed SPR tests are project design context, not outcomes extracted from this abstract. Incorporation here means inclusion as a planned comparator, not adoption or demonstrated protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement, macrophage phagocytosis)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O4 support a cross-species mechanistic bridge: NOD mouse SIRP-alpha binding to human CD47 and its expression on host macrophages support human hematopoiesis. The general CD47-SIRPalpha/macrophage protection mechanism is already explicit in the frozen Blueprint (sections 1.2 and 4.1); this abstract provides no SC-islet, exact-product, human-recipient, phagocytosis-rate, or immune-protection qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M7 (SIRPA allelic variation as a mechanistic determinant of CD47 efficacy)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show that the host mouse Sirpa allele/genetic background conditions human HSC engraftment and NOD SIRP-alpha binding to human CD47; this is a mechanistic model-context qualification, not a quantified CD47 intervention effect. The frozen Blueprint already specifies human SIRPA V1/V2 coverage and leaves pan-allelic protection unverified (sections 1.2, 4.1 and Layer 3), but incorporation of this precise NOD-versus-other-mouse-allele qualification is not established. The abstract tests neither human SIRPA variants nor SC-islets, so transfer to human recipients remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, single-chain HLA-E trimer, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O5 support peptide-dependent HLA-E/CD94-NKG2 recognition as a Gate3 design parameter, at a structural/mechanistic bridge level. This bounded peptide-choice principle is already accounted for: frozen Blueprint section 4.1 specifies VMAPRTLVL, its X1 definition explicitly discusses the VMAPRTLFL comparator and requires exact-trimer SPR, while frozen GRAVEYARD_005 and the ranker leader-swap satellite explicitly recognize weak/non-functional VMAPRALLL leader context. This abstract itself compares HLA-Cw*07 VMAPRALLL with HLA-G*01 VMAPRTLFL; it does not test Blueprint VMAPRTLVL, establish receptor-specific NKG2A versus NKG2C selectivity, assign four-digit HLA-C alleles, or demonstrate exact-product NK protection. already_accounted_for applies to the bounded design principle, not adoption of every structural detail or qualification of the product.

The actual frozen Blueprint (Complex 4, line 298) already distinguishes PD-1 trans binding and PD-L1:CD80 membrane cis heterodimerization; the supplied abstract establishes neither binding topology nor the product-relevant functional consequence of this affinity hierarchy, so incorporation of this exact finding remains unknown. O4 and O5 describe antibody-blocking selectivity and activation-associated T-cell PD-L1 induction without establishing a graft-protective effect.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M7 (extracellular CD47 IgSF-domain recognition of SIRPalpha)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 structurally support extracellular CD47 IgSF-domain recognition of SIRPalpha, the molecular recognition element already explicit in frozen Blueprint sections 4.1 and 9.2. O3 and O4 provide receptor-family specificity context, but already_accounted_for here applies only to CD47-SIRPalpha recognition, not to adoption of each related-receptor detail. The abstract-only packet establishes neither engineered CD47-IgV-GPI function, macrophage inhibition, pan-allelic SIRPA protection nor graft protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (WPREmut6 undesired-ORF suppression and expression-cassette safety; Blueprint section 4.1 and Locus1/Locus3 construct ledger)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablating classical HLA-A/B/C, including HLA-C)
edges.claim_summary: In human kidney allografts, HLA-C mismatch was associated with decreased graft survival in presensitized recipients (O1, P<0.001), consistent with HLA-C being an allorecognition target that B2M KO removes. Kidney transplantation under standard care, not an hPSC-derived islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M4 (clinical benchmark: HLA-C relevance depends on recipient presensitization)
edges.claim_summary: The HLA-C mismatch effect was seen in presensitized (O1, P<0.001) but not non-presensitized (O2, P=0.75) kidney recipients, so any benefit of removing HLA-C may be concentrated in presensitized hosts; the transfer to SC-islet recipients is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3; PD-1/PD-L1 engagement strength)
edges.claim_summary: Human PD-1 binds PD-L1 weakly in vitro (Kd 8.2 +/- 0.1 uM forward, O1; 7.5 +/- 2.2 uM reverse, O3), and the synapse simulation shows PD-L1 dominating PD-1 engagement on mature DCs (about 80,000 vs 5000 copies/cell, O13; 5-fold fewer PD-L2 complexes, O14). This qualifies PD-L1 as an allo-T-cell brake: effect likely depends on surface density, but recombinant proteins and a T cell - DC simulation are not an islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M7 (species dependence of PD-1/PD-L1 constants in rodent test systems)
edges.claim_summary: Mouse PD-1 bound mouse PD-L1 at Kd 29.8 +/- 6.8 uM (O6) and PD-L2 at 38.4 +/- 7.1 uM (O7), versus 8.2 and 2.3 uM for the human pairs (O1, O2), and simulated mouse complex formation fell about 3-fold (PD-L1) and about 20-fold (PD-L2) (O15, O16). PD-L1/PD-1 readouts in immunocompetent rodent models may therefore not scale to human T cells.

For a graft, CD47 protection may matter mainly when opsonization or other pro-phagocytic signals are present; shown on tumor cells only.

edges.claim_summary: After islet transplantation recipient cross-dressed cells outnumbered donor passenger leukocytes (about 10 times; O14, O15) and after heart grafting reached more than 90,000 per million spleen cells (O12). Absence of passenger leukocytes (as in SC-islets) therefore does not by itself prevent direct-pathway presentation if graft cells shed MHC-bearing vesicles; vesicle origin in parenchymal cells was not established here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (single-patient clinical glycemic-function benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O5, O10 and O13 provide a clinical benchmark in one recipient of primary deceased-donor islets on the omentum under systemic immunosuppression: insulin was discontinued at day 17, 12-month 7-day CGM mean was 109+/-15 mg/dL, and HbA1c was 6.0% versus 6.8% at baseline. O21 documents low baseline stimulated C-peptide only; no numeric post-transplant stimulated C-peptide or calculated CGM time-in-range is supplied. Transfer to edited SC-islets remains a bridge; the Blueprint's citation of this PMID for site choice does not establish adoption of this exact glycemic benchmark.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmark durability under systemic immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: O11 and O12 report decreased insulin secretion and increased glucose after the 6-month evaluation and functional decline at 12 months; the authors speculate about the tacrolimus-to-sirolimus switch (O23), without testing causality. These findings qualify functional durability in this single recipient; they do not measure graft mass retention. Reported regular exercise and a low-carbohydrate diet, continued systemic immunosuppression, and the unresolved O13-versus-F1 low-glucose wording limit transfer to a drug-free engineered product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (clinical omental-site precedent only)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O14 and O22 support a bounded clinical precedent for omental placement of 602,395 IEQ (6.5 ml packed tissue) with a plasma/thrombin scaffold in one immunosuppressed patient, with insulin stopped at day 17 and no reported surgical complications. The frozen Blueprint explicitly cites PMID:28489987 for omental site choice (roadmap Stage 4 and Surgical Site Scaling); already_accounted_for applies only to that site rationale. This packet does not validate a folded prevascularized engineered pouch, its proposed area or areal loading, measured vascularization or 72-hour oxygen performance, retrieval, or a suicide switch.

This is a mechanistic bridge to Gate2A, not an allogeneic islet experiment. The general contact-checkpoint strategy is already present in frozen Blueprint §4.3 and GRAVEYARD_008 replacement_solution; no alloreactive protection, systemic immune selectivity or exact-product qualification follows. O21/O23/O24 are assay descriptions with endpoint-specific directions unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1, M7 (Locus-3 PD-L1 post-translational stability and recycling)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3/O10-O13 establish CMTM6-dependent PD-L1 abundance, lysosomal protection and recycling in cancer-cell models. Frozen Blueprint §4.3, lines 151-152, explicitly cites PMID:28813417 for CMTM6 recycling and includes surface PD-L1 recycling in Decision Experiment #3; frozen ranker lines 2888-2889 and 6184-6186 likewise incorporate that rationale. Seat1/Seat2 claim that this mechanism is not yet accounted for is rejected. The study does not test SC-islets, autoimmune memory or indirect host APC presentation, nor demonstrate that cassette-tail orientation or CMTM6 augmentation works in the exact product; those transfers remain unvalidated. No new construct upgrade or IIP acceptance is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O11-O13 provide human mechanistic context for the Gate3 HLA-E/NKG2A strategy: HLA-E and imputed HLA-A correlate in 58 donors, and within HLA-B -21M/M donors HLA-A associates positively with Raji-stimulated NKG2A+ licensing but inversely with HIV-target CD107a degranulation. Other reported correlations being nonsignificant does not prove subset specificity or a between-subset difference. Blueprint §4.1/§6/§8 already specify the SCT and residual NKG2A-negative KIR/NKG2C assay boundaries; these HIV/T-cell-blast results do not validate engineered-islet protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M7 (Locus 3 CXCL10::SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1: protease-mediated PD-L1 loss)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O13 establish cell-free recombinant PD-L1 degradation by MMP-7/MMP-13 and partial membrane-PD-L1 recovery with CL82198 in HNSCC lines; they do not establish a cell-surface cleavage site, SC-islet immune protection or an effective product intervention. The frozen Blueprint §4.3 explicitly cites this study beside its shedding/effluent panel; frozen ranker lines 5735-5741 already require a MMP-7/MMP-9/MMP-13 surface-retention/soluble-protein challenge. Thus the bounded failure-mode assay rationale is already incorporated, not a novel upgrade. Its exact numeric assay acceptance limits are project specifications, not values demonstrated by this paper. CL82198 dose and spread conflicts remain unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inducible PD-L1: membrane abundance versus transcript/total-protein readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 distinguish transcript/total-lysate PD-L1 from membrane-extracted PD-L1: OSC-20 membrane PD-L1 is 22.3-fold over KD versus 96.08-fold for OSC-19, while abstract/Discussion state higher OSC-20 total-lysate PD-L1. O21 records supernatant ELISA nondetection without an assay limit, so degradation does not demonstrate soluble PD-L1 abundance or activity. Frozen Blueprint §4.3 and ranker lines 5735-5755 already distinguish surface retention, soluble abundance and a separate functional effluent assay. This supports that bounded measurement boundary only; the tumour-line findings do not validate cassette performance or alloimmune evasion in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (evaluation of NKG2C+ NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2: adaptive NKG2C+ NK cells are a distinct human NK subset whose recognition, expansion and differentiation depend on HCMV strain peptides, consistent with the Blueprint's plan to evaluate NKG2C+ NK subsets in Gate3. The abstract mentions no HLA-E, islet or graft data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NKG2C+ NK subset assays: donor HCMV serostatus and strain context)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3: because UL40 peptide variants plus inflammatory signals shape NKG2C+ NK expansion and heterogeneity among HCMV-seropositive people, Gate3 NKG2C+ assays may need to record donor HCMV serostatus or strain context. Hypothesis only; the abstract gives no quantitative data and no test of any graft cell.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M7 (QPCTL-dependent CD47 processing; exact CD47-IgV-GPI qualification hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4 support QPCTL-dependent CD47 pyroglutamate formation and recombinant SIRP binding in tumor/immortalized cell systems. Testing processing and functional SIRPα engagement of the exact Blueprint CD47-IgV-GPI in SC-beta/iEC lineages is an unvalidated qualification hypothesis, not an islet result or a clinical instruction to avoid QPCTL inhibitors. Blueprint §4.1 already requires exact-construct functional comparisons; pyroglutamate-specific incorporation is not established by the reviewed reference passages, so remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (generic CD47-SIRPα restraint of macrophage phagocytosis)
edges.claim_summary: O9 and the abstract support CD47-pathway restraint of antibody-dependent phagocytosis of Raji tumor cells by primary human macrophages; SEN177 plus opsonization enhances phagocytosis without caption-derived effect sizes. The generic SIRPα/macrophage protection mechanism is explicitly accounted for in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 and §4.1 (lines 63,134) and ranker primary readouts (lines 5809-5810); exact SC-islet construct efficacy and thresholds remain unvalidated by this paper.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (neutrophil antibody-dependent tumor-cell killing: transfer boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O10-O12, O17 and the abstract report enhanced antibody-dependent tumor-cell killing after QPCTL disruption/inhibition, including a rodent peritoneal model without a reconstituted human immune system. These data identify a possible neutrophil challenge context for a CD47-protected graft; they do not establish human SC-islet protection, a graft-release threshold, NK efficacy, or the unresolved depletion/ratio contrasts in O13-O15. Whether this specific neutrophil boundary is incorporated is unknown; it is separated from the already-accounted-for macrophage mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (multiplex editing genomic-integrity panel; Locus 4 AAVS1 knock-in)
edges.claim_summary: AAV sequences were captured at Cas9 target sites in murine neurons and tissues (O2, O4, O5, O7) and human U2-OS cells (O21); targeted no-gRNA qPCR lacked amplification in U2-OS (O16), without excluding background integration elsewhere. Hypothesis: explicitly quantify unintended on-target AAV/ITR capture when evaluating the Blueprint AAV6 donor workflow (including AAVS1 Locus 4), alongside existing long-read and clonal QC. AAV1/2 murine or tumor-cell results are a justified mechanism bridge only: hPSC, AAV6 HDR and SC-islet editing rates were not tested, and incorporation of this specific assay is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (nuclease off-target genomic integrity)
edges.claim_summary: In hippocampal genome-wide AAV mapping, 11-19 unique sites per condition and similar descriptive integration levels did not show an increase with Cas9/gRNA, while recurrent sites lacked gRNA-target homology (O10, O13, O15). These pooled and limited non-dividing mouse-brain measurements do not establish equivalence, absence of off-target genomic damage, or safety of hPSC/AAV6 editing; they cannot replace the Blueprint longitudinal clonal QC or the GRAVEYARD_006 precaution. Incorporation of this exact empirical boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (Locus 3 inducible PD-L1; PD-1 engagement on T cells)
edges.claim_summary: In these reconstitution/cell-line assays, cis-CD80 blocked PD-L1:PD-1 engagement by 80% at 3.5-fold excess (O4) and reduced PD-1 clustering/signaling (O5–O6), whereas the low-CD80 context retained similar PD-1 enrichment (O7). This qualifies transfer of Locus-3 PD-L1 efficacy to an untested SC-islet CD80/PD-L1 density state; no islet protection was measured. Frozen Blueprint §9.2 Complex 4 already acknowledges this paper’s cis-PD-L1:CD80 mechanism and leaves exact-product membrane 2D Kd null; incorporation of the full quantitative density/functional boundary is not established, so remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 at Locus 3; indirect host-APC pathway)
edges.claim_summary: PD-L1 co-expressed with CD80 preserved the reported CD28 responses (O8–O9), restricted CTLA-4 binding/homodimer avidity (O10–O12), and protected APC CD80 from trans-endocytosis (O13–O19); anti-PD-L1 depleted CD80 in 4T1/CT26 tumor APCs, with anti-CTLA-4 recovery in CT26 DCs (O18, O20–O21). These APC-intrinsic cis effects do not demonstrate that graft PD-L1 protects against host indirect antigen presentation; intermembrane PD-L1:CD80 binding was not detected in O1. Blueprint §4.2, ranker Gate2B and GRAVEYARD_010 already retain an indirect-APC hazard/assay boundary, but incorporation of this specific cis/CTLA-4 costimulation mechanism is not established; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (PD-L1/PD-1 NK-cell target availability; separate HLA-E/CD47 innate shield)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O2 report lack of PD-1 on human/mouse NK cells under the sampled conditions despite activation/regulatory-marker upregulation. This qualifies an assumption of direct PD-L1-to-PD-1 inhibition of NK cells; it does not test PD-L1-engineered islets, NK killing, HLA-E or CD47 protection, establish universal NK PD-1 absence, or prove that PD-L1 cannot have indirect effects. Blueprint §1.2/§4.1 assigns separate innate protection to HLA-E/CD47; incorporation of this specific expression boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (contextual PD-L1 checkpoint-target relevance; Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O4 show qualitative PD-1 expression and greater prominence of tumor T cells relative to NK cells, identifying T-cell versus NK-cell target availability in the studied tumor contexts. Gate2A/Gate2B routing reflects the shared PD-L1 checkpoint context in the frozen cheatsheet and ranker; tumor T-cell expression neither establishes suppression of alloreactive or T1D-autoreactive T cells nor tests indirect host-APC presentation or islet-graft protection. Incorporation of this specific tumor-derived boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Locus 1 CD47 / SIRPalpha engagement; macrophage phagocytosis)
edges.claim_summary: In the tested mouse-macrophage systems, CD47 suppression was partial and depended on IgG density (O1-O2); integrin activation with manganese or ICAM-1 bypassed suppression (O14-O15), with complementary CD47+ RBC and L1210 findings (O16,O18). These are bounded Gate3/M1 qualifications, not proof that the human CD47-IgV-GPI SC-islet construct fails. Blueprint §4.1 addresses SIRPalpha-mediated protection and exact-product uncertainty; the ranker includes recipient-serum opsonized ADCP, but incorporation of the specific integrin-bypass boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement, mechanism)
edges.claim_summary: CD47-SIRPA binding suppressed engulfment (O3-O4), CD47 retained SIRPA at the cup (O5), and SIRPA positioning and beta2-integrin/F-actin perturbations support a mechanism involving integrin activation (O8-O9,O12-O13,O27-O29). Blueprint §4.1 already states the generic SIRPalpha-mediated macrophage-protection rationale, but incorporation of these specific synapse/integrin mechanisms is not established. Mouse synthetic-target findings are a justified mechanistic bridge; human SIRPA alleles, human immune cells and SC-islets were not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (PD-L1 at Locus 3 as a possible additional NK-restraining axis beside HLA-E-NKG2A and CD47-SIRPalpha)
edges.claim_summary: Human NK cells carry low but functional PD-1, and PD-L1 overexpression on K562 targets suppressed NK function (O1, O3), so the Blueprint PD-L1 element could be tested for NK restraint as well as T-cell suppression. Targets here are tumor lines, not islet cells, and the abstract gives no magnitudes or n.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (KIR2DL2/3+ NK missing-self; NKG2A-negative KIR+ NK subsets)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-C1 allotypes inhibited degranulation of KIR2DL2/S2+ and KIR2DL3+ primary NK cells (O14), consistent with KIR2DL missing-self sitting inside Gate3 scope and with evaluating NKG2A-negative KIR+ subsets. Targets are .221 transfectants, not islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK potency assays: KIR2DS2 and HLA-C1 allotype stratification)
edges.claim_summary: C1 allotypes differed in inhibitory potency for KIR2DL3+ NK cells (O15) and KIR2DS2+ NK cells showed elevated activation on HLA-C transfectants (O16), so Gate3 NK assays could stratify donors by KIR2DS2 and report the HLA-C1 allotype tested. This extends the evaluation of KIR+ subsets beyond what the cheatsheet states.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M7 (complement arm of Gate3; acidosis as a mechanistic failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: Native plasma C5 was not cleaved by thrombin, but acidification to pH <= 6.8 permitted cleavage (O2, O4), so peri-graft acidosis could be tested as a condition that enables thrombin-driven complement activation. The abstract involves healthy blood and no islets or grafts, so this is a hypothesis only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: The structure is of the cleaved, relaxed form of human serpin B9 (O1, O4) and the abstract reports no granzyme B inhibition or cell data, so it adds structural detail about the Blueprint SERPINB9 element without testing its protective function in islet cells.

edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports purified-component kinetics of TAFI activation by thrombin-thrombomodulin (O2-O5) and its effect on tPA-induced fibrinolysis (O6), with no islet, immune-cell, complement or graft endpoint. It does not bear on a Blueprint gate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cell-intrinsic nature of SERPINB9 protection)
edges.claim_summary: PI-9 is cytosolic and not secreted and sits apart from granzyme B (O5, O6), so protection is presumably confined to cells that express it; each graft cell would need its own SERPINB9. This is an inference from the localization data, not a protection assay.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Locus 1 single-chain HLA-E trimer, NKG2A engagement)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-E binds a tightly defined set of near-identical hydrophobic leader-derived peptides (O3), which is consistent with building the Blueprint HLA-E element as a peptide-presenting single-chain trimer. The abstract is structural only and tests no NK cells or islet cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inhibitory co-signalling to CD4+ T cells; PD-L1 at Locus 3 as the Blueprint's analogous checkpoint axis)
edges.claim_summary: O4 and O5 state that an inhibitory CTLA4 signal to CD4+ T cells is required for DST plus anti-CD154 tolerance and can block alloimmune MLR responses, consistent with the premise behind inducible PD-L1 that inhibitory co-signals can suppress allo-T-cell responses. CTLA4 is a different axis from PD-L1, the data are qualitative, and the species and graft are not hPSC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (adaptive alloimmunity benchmark: recipient presensitization and host-directed tolerance)
edges.claim_summary: O1 reports that pretransplant DST presensitization accelerates islet allograft rejection, and O2 and O3 report that anti-CD154 co-treatment prevents this and permits subsequent islet or cardiac engraftment; this is a host-directed, systemic costimulation-blockade result in a rodent model, not a graft-intrinsic edit, so it only qualifies the Gate2A benchmark with a recipient presensitization risk.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (granzyme/FAS effector pressure on target cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4 show that primary mouse cardiac myocytes upregulate Fas on viral infection, are killed via Fas by FasL-expressing cells, and are lysed by cardiac T cells, supporting Fas-mediated killing as a real effector axis of the type listed in Gate2B. The target is a non-islet mouse cell type and no beta cell was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition at CXCL10 Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: O5 reports predominantly Fas-mediated killing by gamma delta+ T cells and Fas-dependent killing capacity in alpha beta+ T cells, a route that a granzyme B inhibitor such as SERPINB9 would not address by itself; the cheatsheet names SERPINB9 but not a Fas-specific protective element, and this is only a cardiac-myocyte qualitative result with no beta-cell data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression by delivered costimulation-blocking molecule; Blueprint benchmark is PD-L1 at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4 show that CTLA4-Ig delivered by a dendritic cell line prolonged mouse islet allograft survival (mean 20 days versus 11-12 days) without prolonging third-party grafts, supporting allo-T-cell suppression by an immunoregulatory molecule as a lever relevant to Gate2A. Mouse fully allogeneic model, cell-therapy delivery rather than a graft-intrinsic edit.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (protection from recurrent autoimmune destruction in NOD recipients)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 report that a co-transplanted cell population prolonged syngeneic islet graft survival in autoimmune NOD recipients (median 11 to 32 days) and the authors describe a Fas ligand-independent protective component, supporting that autoimmune destruction of islet grafts is amenable to graft-side modification in an autoimmune model. Mouse islets and neonatal Sertoli cells, not hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CD8+ cytolytic effector pathways; Gate2B SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition as the perforin/granzyme arm)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 report that primed mouse CD8+ T cells rejected established islet allografts without individually needing perforin or Fas ligand but critically needing IFN-gamma production, which qualifies how much protection against cytolytic effectors alone (such as granzyme B inhibition) can be expected against CD8+ rejection. Qualitative mouse SCID-transfer result; the cheatsheet does not state this IFN-gamma dependence and the graft-side IFN-gamma target is not identified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (direct CD8+ T-cell allorecognition as the rejection route addressed by the B2M KO)
edges.claim_summary: O1 to O3 describe rejection of established islet allografts by purified alloreactive CD8+ T cells alone in SCID recipients, supporting CD8+ T cells as sufficient rejection effectors of the type Gate2A targets. The study does not test MHC class I ablation or any hypoimmune edit, and the system is mouse allografts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (alloimmune tolerance benchmark; host-level liver-induced tolerance rather than graft-intrinsic edits)
edges.claim_summary: O1 to O3 show that a donor-strain liver allograft modified rat islet allograft outcome in a timing-dependent and partial way (rejection delayed with simultaneous liver; long-term survival in three of seven animals with liver 1 month before, and three of seven cases with liver on day 4), with four animals dying of liver rejection. This is a host-level organ co-transplant in rats, not a graft-intrinsic hypoimmune design, so it only qualifies what tolerance benchmarks Gate2A can draw from it.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (in-graft suppression or deletion of alloreactive T cells as a tolerance correlate)
edges.claim_summary: O6 associates islet graft tolerance with FasL up-regulation, apoptosis of alloreactive leukocytes and donor-specific MLR suppression, and O4 shows infiltrate intensity did not track outcome, consistent with the premise that suppression of alloreactive T cells within the graft is what determines acceptance. The evidence is correlative, in rats, with no FasL manipulation, and FasL is not among the cheatsheet's named Blueprint elements.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization and prevascularized device; the 72-hour avascular oxygen bridge covers the interval before vascularization)
edges.claim_summary: O1 to O3 show that bFGF-releasing gelatin microspheres plus a collagen sponge in a PET mesh bag produced a capillary network and higher tissue hemoglobin at 7 days, and subsequent allogeneic islet grafts maintained normoglycemia for more than 40 days where control groups were ineffective, supporting prevascularization as a route to graft survival. Rat allogeneic islets with no oxygen tension measured, immunosuppression unstated, so it does not test the avascular oxygen bridge itself.

edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 report that islets co-transplanted with 1 x 10(7) testicular cells containing FasL-expressing Sertoli cells kept all animals normoglycemic throughout follow-up (P < 0.05) with apoptosis of infiltrative lymphocytes, supporting graft-local protection from allo-T cells in rats. It is an accessory-cell, not graft-intrinsic, approach; follow-up length and n are not stated.

edges.claim_summary: Peripheral-blood cytotoxic lymphocyte transcript monitoring (granzyme B best, O1, O2) led rejection by 83--197 days in rhesus islet allograft recipients, so it could be proposed as a pre-symptomatic rejection readout alongside C-peptide/CGM benchmarks for clinical SC-islet grafts. The cheatsheet states only C-peptide and CGM time-in-range benchmarks; evidence is four monkeys with anti-CD154 withdrawal and needs human validation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (local allo-T-cell suppression; inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: A beta-cell line secreting CTLA4-Ig survived 20 days in 7 of 12 DST-sensitised allogeneic mice while all 10 parental grafts were rejected within 14 days (O1); protection persisted without detectable serum CTLA4-Ig and was lost when the CTLA4-Ig graft was removed (O2, O4). This supports locally expressed inhibitory immunomodulators for allo-T-cell suppression, but it is a mouse insulinoma line in mice (not hPSC islets), protection was partial and short-term, and CTLA4-Ig is a different molecule from the Blueprint PD-L1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (candidate secreted CTLA4-Ig payload alongside B2M/CIITA KO and PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: Local secretion of CTLA4-Ig by graft cells was protective against DST-accelerated rejection in mice and was CTLA4-dependent (O1, O3); this could be proposed as an extra costimulation-blockade payload for SC-islets. The cheatsheet does not mention CTLA4-Ig, and nothing here tests it in human or SC-derived cells, with HLA edits, or beyond 20 days.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (immune-privilege ligands as cloak elements)
edges.claim_summary: FasL delivered by cotransplanted testicular (Sertoli) cells kept all animals normoglycemic for 60 days (O2, O3), whereas FasL expressed directly on the islets accelerated rejection (O4); this qualifies any proposal to add FasL as an islet-intrinsic immune-privilege element, since the cheatsheet lists no FasL element. Evidence is rodent allograft with a cotransplanted non-islet cell type, so it is not a direct test of the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) / M3 (vascularization of the avascular graft period; prevascularized site)
edges.claim_summary: In pancreatectomized swine, vascularized islet-kidney composites at 5,000 IE/kg gave normoglycemia (<120 mg/dl) and insulin independence for >3 months (O2, O4), whereas nonvascularized islets at 7,000 IE/kg left recipients hyperglycemic (O6). This supports vascular supply as a determinant of islet engraftment, but it is adult swine islets in a kidney-capsule composite and does not test an oxygen bridge or hPSC-derived islets; the cheatsheet cannot settle whether the Blueprint adopts prevascularization.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell evasion without genetic cloak)
edges.claim_summary: Vascularized IK recipients across minor and full MHC mismatch kept normoglycemia for >3 months after only a 12-day CyA or FK506 course, with in vitro donor-specific unresponsiveness (O2, O5), but nonvascularized islets given the same CyA course failed (O6). This qualifies Gate2A by showing graft site and vascularization can confound allo-rejection outcomes in a non-gene-edited model; the abstract gives no mechanism or controls separating immune from engraftment effects.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3; allo-T-cell suppression benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Soluble dimeric PD-L1Ig alone failed to prevent DBA/2 islet allograft rejection in C57BL/6 mice; long-term survival required concurrent anti-CD154 (O5, O6), although PD-L1Ig inhibited CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell proliferation in vitro (O1, O2). This qualifies reliance on PD-L1 as a Gate2A element: in this model PD-1 engagement was not sufficient on its own. The reagent is a systemic Ig fusion protein, not graft-expressed membrane PD-L1 within an HLA-edited stack, so the bridge is mechanistic (PD-1 engagement) only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CD8+ effector allorecognition evasion; B2M KO + CIITA KO)
edges.claim_summary: Fully MHC-mismatched mouse islet allografts were rejected with a median survival of 12 days in wild-type recipients (O2), and CCR2 deficiency in the recipient reduced CD8+ but not CD4+ effector generation (O3, O4) yet only delayed rejection to 24 days with eventual graft loss (O2, O5). This is a recipient-side mouse manipulation, so it is a bridge to, not a test of, graft-intrinsic HLA evasion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: Intragraft CXCL-10 expression, with CXCL9, CCL5, CCL8 and CCL9, rose steadily during mouse islet allograft rejection (O1), consistent with an allograft-rejection inflammatory milieu in which a CXCL10-responsive promoter would be expected to be active. Abstract gives no magnitude, so the induction level is not quantified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmark; CD8+/CD4+ allorecognition evasion)
edges.claim_summary: In fully MHC-mismatched mouse islet allografts, single-agent costimulation or mTOR blockade only delayed rejection (O1), ICOS expression rose in rejected grafts (O2), and adding anti-ICOS mAb improved survival (O3) and suppressed acute alloreactive T-cell expansion and function (O6) but without donor-specific tolerance or regulatory T-cell activity (O4, O5). This is recipient-side pharmacology in mice, so it is a bridge to, not a test of, graft-intrinsic HLA evasion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (HMOX1 cytoprotection; pre-transplant conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: Inducing HO-1 or giving CO to the mouse donor, the islets or the recipient improved allogeneic islet survival (O1, O2), with long-term survival after donor-only CO (O3) and suppressed inflammatory and apoptotic gene expression (O5). The cheatsheet lists HMOX1 and pre-transplant conditioning in Gate4; this is a pharmacologic mouse primary-islet result, not an edit of hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (granzyme B and FAS effector pressure; SERPINB9 + PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0026:L2 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O5,O6 | text_sha256=92d66d619f649b52761c6f4574fff59f6251efcbe7f953317f4f167b52069ace]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate injury: complement and CD11b+ myeloid infiltration; endothelial coating as an additional cloak)
edges.claim_summary: Coating primary human islets with human aortic endothelial cells reduced complement and coagulation activation and CD11b+ cell infiltration in clots in ABO-identical blood (O1, O2, O4) in proportion to coverage (O5). The cheatsheet states Gate3 complement and macrophage mechanisms only via HLA-E and CD47, not endothelial coating; the data come from primary human islets in an in vitro blood model, not hPSC-derived islets, so a composite-graft addition would be untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell functional maturation; glucose-stimulated insulin secretion)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT-8 was restricted to insulin-producing beta cells in human islet cells (O1, O2), and its overexpression in the rat INS-1E line raised intracellular zinc (O3, O4) and enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion only above 10 mM glucose (O5). The functional data come from a rat cell line, so this is a mechanistic bridge to the Gate1 GSIS machinery of hPSC-derived beta cells, not a test in them.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CD8+ allorecognition; B2M KO ablating HLA class I)
edges.claim_summary: In fully MHC-mismatched mouse islet allografts, CTLA4/Fc monotherapy did not clearly beat no treatment (O1) whereas IL-15 antagonism gave 100% acceptance (O2) with fewer intragraft and proliferating CD8+ T cells (O3, O5), indicating CD8+ T cells can escape costimulation blockade; this is consistent with the Gate2A premise that CD8+ allorecognition must be addressed, but it is a systemic-drug mouse result, not a test of graft-intrinsic edits.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adjunct control of CD8+ T cells beyond HLA edits; IL-15/IL-15R pathway)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0029:L2 | relation=novel_upgrade_hypothesis | applicability=unvalidated_transfer | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O2 | text_sha256=4e08bdd100533f5bc167d65dc5036688186bd7ccc0d64d0d073ab859bef48883]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (IAPP oligomer and amyloid toxicity as a post-transplant failure mode; Gate1 coordinate secretion)
edges.claim_summary: In isolated human islets, h-IAPP oligomers disrupted cell-to-cell adherence and coordinate insulin secretion and, per the title, induced apoptosis and impaired secretion (O1-O4); the abstract notes islet amyloid accompanies declining secretion after islet transplantation. The cheatsheet Gate4 and M7 lists name hypoxia, ER/oxidative and cytokine stress but not IAPP amyloid, so IAPP-oligomer toxicity is a candidate extra failure mode to examine in SC-islets; it was not tested in them.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and endocrine function benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0031:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=matched_domain | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O1,O3,O5,O6 | text_sha256=6e359fa5354732a964b42390e913dd62e1c2d6a02b51e045b66843271c6eea07]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell control; recurrent T1D autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: Long-term cytopiloyne prevented spontaneous diabetes in NOD mice (O1, O2) with a Th2 shift, fewer CD4+ T cells in pancreatic lymph nodes and spleens, and preserved total antibody responses (O3-O5), supporting that T1D autoimmunity is T-cell driven and pharmacologically modifiable. These are endogenous islets with no graft or recurrence test, so transfer to autoreactive T-cell attack on hPSC-derived islets is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (inflammatory cytokine exposure incl. IFN-gamma; intrinsic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: The cheatsheet lists IFN-gamma under the inflammatory cytokine exposure that Gate4 cytoprotection must withstand; this study shows IFN signalling in primary human islet cells also induces antiviral genes (O1) and protects against Coxsackievirus replication (O3), so IFN responsiveness is not purely a damage pathway. The abstract names no IFN subtype and tests primary islets, not hPSC-derived islets, so it qualifies rather than contradicts Gate4.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme-B inhibition; granzyme/FAS effector pressure)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: in this CD8+ T-cell islet allograft model neither perforin nor Fas disruption alone had much effect, but disrupting both prevented rejection in most recipients (abstract, no counts). This suggests protection that targets only one contact-dependent effector route could be insufficient; the cheatsheet lists granzyme/FAS effector pressure under Gate2B but does not state whether the Fas route is covered, and the model is rodent rather than hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (direct-pathway CD8+ T-cell allorecognition evasion)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4: direct-pathway alloreactive CD8+ T cells depended on contact-dependent perforin and Fas routes to reject islet allografts, and the transferred T cells persisted at the graft site without rejecting it in most recipients when both were disrupted. This is mouse effector biology, not evidence for any specific edit in the Gate2A stack.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks; CD28/B7 and LIGHT/HVEM costimulation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3: in fully allogeneic BALB/c mice with C57BL/6 islets, CTLA4-Ig alone gave 55 days, LTbetaR-Ig alone 27 days and the combination more than 100 days, indicating that a second costimulatory axis (LIGHT/HVEM) adds to CD28/B7 blockade. This is a systemic-biologic benchmark in mouse islets, not a test of the B2M/CIITA/PD-L1 edits, and the cheatsheet does not state costimulation-blockade values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; donor-specific tolerance via regulatory T cells)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0035:L2 | relation=novel_upgrade_hypothesis | applicability=unvalidated_transfer | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O5,O6 | text_sha256=a6b0751f7a3c0cd15af4a64507966b7e1b16c2ed5827809a30ac4ecb4f826981]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmarks beyond stimulated C-peptide: early-failure markers)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O5: in 17 long fx versus 20 short fx human islet allograft recipients, higher insulin resistance and altered proinsulin processing accompanied early failure long before it occurred. This suggests, as an untested hypothesis, that post-transplant insulin resistance and proinsulin processing could be added as early-warning readouts alongside the stimulated C-peptide / CGM TIR benchmarks the cheatsheet lists; the cohort is primary-islet allografts, not hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M4 (T-cell allorecognition evasion; scope of early-failure mechanisms)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4: early failure was accompanied by lower soluble IL-2 receptor (a T-cell activation marker) and higher soluble FasL (an apoptosis marker), so in this cohort early failure was not marked by higher systemic T-cell activation. This qualifies reading early failure solely as T-cell alloreactivity; the abstract does not address causation or immunosuppression effects.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; effector T-cell trafficking via CXCR3)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3, O8-O9 and O18 support a bounded mouse mechanism bridge to Gate2A: systemic CXCR3-173 delayed islet allograft rejection (median 12.5 to 21 days, p<0.05), combination therapy with rapamycin yielded 80% long-term islet engraftment, cardiac CD4/CD8 infiltration was reduced, and in vitro chemotaxis blockade was ligand-selective and incomplete. These are not tests of edited human SC-islets or drug-free protection. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9 already target inflammation and graft CXCL10; the exact anti-CXCR3-plus-RPM finding's adoption is not established, so incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (CXCL10-inducible Locus 3 SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: O12-O13 qualify transfer from day-7 mouse cardiac transcripts to the Gate2B shared CXCL10-inducible shield: IFN-gamma mRNA was lower under CXCR3-173 monotherapy while CXCL10 was not significantly reduced; ischemia/reperfusion is the authors' explanation referencing prior work, not a directly measured early induction time course here. Frozen ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9 explicitly uses native IFN/NF-kB control, and GRAVEYARD_001 acknowledges a TNF-alpha/IL-1beta NF-kB bypass, so the current framework does not assume exclusively IFN-gamma induction. This study does not test engineered human promoter output, autoimmunity or indirect APC presentation. O19 adds significant combination-versus-PIP-plus-RPM tests without caption-defined direction. Exact incorporation of the cardiac finding is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks; B7/CD28 costimulation blockade via CTLA4-Ig)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5: CTLA4-Ig-expressing dendritic cells inhibited T lymphocyte proliferation in vitro and, in streptozotocin-diabetic C57BL/6 recipients of BALB/c islets, prolonged allograft survival with a Th1/Th2 cytokine shift. This supports cell-delivered costimulation blockade as an allo-T-cell suppression strategy, but it is an abstract-only mouse result with DCs rather than graft-cell expression, and the cheatsheet states no CTLA4-Ig element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (immunoprotective factor expression and allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O6: in mice, primary Sertoli cells extended islet allograft survival to 61.1 +/- 6.9 days versus 26.9 +/- 2.1 days, but the MSC-1 line, although it expressed clusterin, Fas ligand and TGF-beta1, gave 29.8 +/- 3.3 days. This cautions that expressing some known immunoprotective factors on a cotransplanted helper cell did not by itself protect allografts; it is an abstract-only mouse result with cotransplanted cells, not edited islets, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether the Blueprint addresses it.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (intrinsic cytoprotection and mechanistic failure modes of transplanted islets)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0040:L1 | relation=scoping_qualification | applicability=unvalidated_transfer | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O1 | text_sha256=f5229c555dd21f79cd6f3a6d1144a9a7565fd03dd7d9a2fe3c3768ce74b3065c]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (in-vivo omental graft and late vascularization)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4, O12, O16, O18: primary cynomolgus islets on a VICRYL/PDS scaffold in an omental pouch gave long-term CP-positive function, loss of CP after removal in four explanted auto/allograft recipients, and late explant vascularization. Frozen Blueprint section 4.5 surgical-site scaling explicitly includes a portal-draining prevascularized omental pouch, so the general site strategy is already present; incorporation of this study-specific scaffold and durability evidence is not established. This bridge does not show that the scaffold is essential (no free-floating omental control), quantify oxygen/perfusion, or validate the edited SC-islet/iMVF/PDMS-CaO2 product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (early oxygen bridge versus delayed functional recovery)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (drug-covered NHP allograft benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10, O14, O15, O17-O20: primary NHP allografts received systemic FK506, rapamycin and Zenapax; autologous animal 1 received no immunosuppressive drugs. Allograft attrition, descriptive histology, infection/death and selected durability denominators provide a contextual in-vivo benchmark, not a direct allo-T-cell mechanism assay or immune-cloak efficacy test. Blueprint section 1.2 and ranker allogeneic comparator definitions distinguish the immunosuppression-free target; these findings cannot validate B2M/CIITA/HLA-E/CD47 protection or establish site-specific immune privilege. Specific study incorporation is unknown; M3 replaces M4 because this is a primary NHP graft study, not a clinical/regulatory benchmark.
