edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (STAT1-dependent cytokine apoptosis; compatibility with inducible checkpoints)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O9, O14 and O16-O18 show enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation with PTPN2 knockdown and reported 56%/67% protection by STAT1 knockdown in INS-1E rat cells. They do not test SC-islets or checkpoint-promoter compatibility. The frozen Blueprint §5 GRAVEYARD_001, graveyard entry 001 and ranker already flag clonal STAT1 loss paired with STAT1-dependent GAS/ISRE checkpoints; therefore this is a bounded mechanistic finding, not an established novel product upgrade. Incorporation of the exact acute siRNA protection magnitudes is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (preserving the PTPN2 brake against cytokine-associated islet-cell death; GRAVEYARD_007)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O11 support the specific existing caution that loss of the PTPN2 brake sensitizes beta-cell/islet-cell models to cytokine death: the human result is a reported 30-38% exacerbation in dispersed primary islet cells, not a beta-cell-specific absolute death rate. Frozen Blueprint §5 GRAVEYARD_007 and graveyard entry 007 explicitly cite PMID:19336676 for this loss-sensitization mechanism, and the ranker enforces the related block. This incorporation ruling covers that qualitative hazard, not quantitative calibration, siRNA-to-full-KO equivalence, or SC-islet/product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (preliminary DNA vector-based PTPN2 overexpression toxicity boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O19 reports preliminary, data-not-shown 30-50% apoptosis at 36 h after DNA vector-based PTPN2 overexpression versus <8% in control-transfected INS-1E cells. It cautions against assuming that more PTPN2 is protective, while the authors explicitly require primary rat/human confirmation. Promoter/constitutive expression and safe expression levels are unreported; this does not establish that all overexpression strategies are toxic or that STAT1 targeting is safe. Frozen GRAVEYARD_007 addresses PTPN2 loss; adoption of this separate gain-of-expression boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (isolated-islet GSIS as the functional readout)
edges.claim_summary: In mouse Slc30a8 knockouts isolated-islet GSIS was reduced ~33% (O16) with unchanged islet insulin content (O15), while fasting glucose (O8, O9) and IPGTT (O14) were unchanged; this supports reading secretory competence from isolated-islet GSIS rather than whole-body glucose measures. The bridge from mouse islets to hPSC-derived islets is by shared beta-cell secretory physiology only; no SC-islet data here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (granule zinc handling, SLC30A8/ZnT-8 as a maturation readout)
edges.claim_summary: Loss of ZnT-8 markedly reduced islet zinc (O1, O2) and plasma insulin (O10, O11); this motivates testing SLC30A8 expression and islet zinc content as candidate Gate1 maturation or granule-competence readouts for SC-islet lots. This is a hypothesis only: the data are from a mouse global knockout and the Gate1 baseline in the cheatsheet does not list ZnT-8 or zinc.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate blood-mediated injury at blood-contacting sites; adjunct to the genetic cloak)
edges.claim_summary: In primary human islets exposed to ABO-compatible human blood, IBMIR clot, platelet and neutrophil injury (O1, O2) was prevented by rhAPC (O4) and by tirofiban plus low-dose rhAPC (O5) but not by tirofiban alone (O3). This proposes pharmacologic platelet plus coagulation co-inhibition as an adjunct for blood-contacting graft sites; the cheatsheet lists no IBMIR element, SC-islets were not tested, and the abstract gives no values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1, M3 (THBD adjunct and early thrombo-inflammatory loss in intraportal mouse islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O6–O10 support the general thrombomodulin adjunct rationale for reducing early intraportal thrombo-inflammatory loss: IV lipo-TM improves early mouse graft function and fibrin, PMN and liver-cytokine readouts; O4 is only a descriptively favorable >100-day trend (p=0.06). The frozen Blueprint already includes SA-THBD adjuncts (Stage 2; §4.2), so blanket novelty/absence is rejected. Incorporation of this exact 1 mg/kg IV liposomal formulation and its quantitative effects is not established by the inspected references. Primary murine islets and this route/site do not qualify SC-islet, surface-bound THBD/microgel, adaptive protection or clinical performance.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (primary-human islet and human-blood loop thrombo-inflammatory readouts)
edges.claim_summary: The primary-human 60-min loop supports a bounded bridge for THBD-mediated suppression of islet-blood thrombotic responses: TAT falls 98%, F1+2 95% and β-TG approximately threefold; TAT remains above the no-islet control, while F1+2 prose/non-equivalence and table-print tensions remain explicit (O11–O17). Gate3 already includes the thrombo-inflammatory shield and SA-THBD is present in the full Blueprint; adoption of this precise loop/formulation result is unknown. This is neither SC-islet product validation nor evidence that the systemic IV, direct-surface SA-THBD and PEG-microgel delivery forms are interchangeable.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 at Locus 3 restraining autoreactive CD8+ T cells)
edges.claim_summary: In NOD mice, transient PD-L1 upregulation on host lymphoid cells prevented expansion of PD-1+ diabetogenic CD8+ T cells and delayed onset (O3), supporting the PD-L1/PD-1 axis behind the inducible PD-L1 element listed for Gate2B. The ligand here is on host lymphoid cells after viral infection, not on a graft, and the abstract gives no values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 plus regulatory T cell support for long-term tolerance)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0048:L2 | relation=novel_upgrade_hypothesis | applicability=unvalidated_transfer | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O3,O4,O5 | text_sha256=8fc0849db21875456c9bda7a7a4994e9a24ffee5f43fb57d09807f3005d69351]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 / PD-1 negative costimulation against allogeneic T cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and the blockade readouts O7/O8 support a necessary role for PD-1:PD-L1 signaling in prolonged murine intratesticular islet-allograft survival and local T-cell suppression. This is a justified mechanism-level bridge to the existing PD-L1 component in Blueprint section 4.3 and the Gate2A PD-L1/A20 ranker branch, but not proof that engineered human graft PD-L1 is sufficient: O3 localizes PD-L1 mainly to host testicular cells, and O2 reports only nonsignificant acceleration of already acute renal-capsule rejection. The specific site-dependent empirical boundary is not established as incorporated; general PD-L1 inclusion alone does not resolve that claim.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (donor-specific memory CD8 T-cell readout for PD-L1 strategies)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O4/O5, and the blockade contrasts O7/O8 motivate donor-specific memory-CD8 generation/proliferation and graft-infiltrating T-cell proliferation/apoptosis as candidate mechanistic readouts for a PD-L1 strategy. Their transfer to the exact human SC-islet product is unvalidated, and O6 has no named comparator in the abstract. Blueprint section 6 and the ranker primary-readout block already cover allogeneic survival and other immune/apoptosis assays, but do not establish adoption of this exact donor-specific-memory and infiltrating-T-cell readout combination; incorporation remains unknown. Allomemory does not itself establish Gate2B autoimmunity or indirect-APC protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (accessory-cell bystander immune suppression as a complement to the genetic cloak)
edges.claim_summary: Xenogeneic neonatal porcine Sertoli cells extended allo-islet survival in unsuppressed rats from 5.67+/-0.94 days to 8.33+/-0.58 and 16.33+/-1.53 days (O1, O2) with reduced lymphocytic infiltrate (O3), independent of Fas ligand (O5). This proposes cotransplanted immune-privileged accessory cells as an adjunct to Gate2A edits; survival stays at about 2 weeks, rat/porcine cells only, and the cheatsheet lists no such element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS-based functional criterion for SC-islet maturation)
edges.claim_summary: In ZnT8(-/-) mice, glucose-induced insulin release, insulin content and glucose tolerance were preserved on control diet (O2, O4) despite loss of zinc release and rare mature dense core granules (O1, O3); a defect appeared only after high-fat diet (O5, O6). This qualifies how far a normal GSIS result alone can establish granule-level maturity for Gate1 (the cheatsheet lists dynamic GSIS and C-peptide benchmarks); mouse knockout, abstract only, no SC-islet data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (ZnT8-dependent granule maturation and stimulated zinc release as SC-islet QC readouts)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT8 loss removed stimulated zinc release (O1) and mature dense core insulin granules (O3), suggesting stimulated zinc release and dense-core granule ultrastructure as candidate Gate1 maturation QC readouts, optionally with a metabolic stress challenge (O5, O6). This is a hypothesis only; the cheatsheet lists neither, and no human or SC-islet data are given.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmark in an MHC-mismatched islet graft)
edges.claim_summary: In a fully MHC-mismatched mouse islet allograft, adding EP1013 to CTLA4-Ig gave 16/18 long-term survivors vs 40% with CTLA4-Ig alone (O3) alongside reduced CD4+/CD8+ infiltration, fewer IFN-gamma ELISPOT responders and no IgM/IgG alloantibody (O8, O10-O12, O17, O18). This is drug-based immunomodulation in mouse, a mechanistic bridge to Gate2A allorecognition but not an edited-cloak test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection, anti-apoptotic strategy)
edges.claim_summary: Caspase inhibitor alone did not prolong allograft survival (O1) yet changed T-cell responses and raised intragraft Foxp3+ cells (O7, O9, O15), so survival benefit from an anti-apoptotic agent in an allogeneic setting cannot be attributed to graft cytoprotection alone; graft apoptosis was not measured in this paper. The cheatsheet does not state this confound for Gate4 anti-apoptotic elements.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biphasic GSIS by perifusion and beta-cell maturation, PDX1/MAFA)
edges.claim_summary: In mouse ZnT8BKO islets first-phase insulin secretion was reduced while second-phase and arginine responses were not significantly different (O4-O6), with reduced Pdx1/MafA transcripts and increased proinsulin (O8-O11). This supports using dynamic perifusion and insulin-processing readouts as maturation criteria; evidence is mouse genetic loss-of-function, with human islets used only for TEM localization.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate QC readouts: ZnT8, zinc content, proinsulin handling in SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT8 loss lowered islet zinc and dense core granules and raised proinsulin (O7-O9, O13) while sparing arginine-stimulated secretion (O6). Hypothesis only: ZnT8 expression, zinc content and proinsulin handling could serve as additional SC-islet maturation checks; this was not tested in SC-islets and the cheatsheet does not mention ZnT8.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity: CD4+/CD8+ T-cell pressure on an islet allograft)
edges.claim_summary: In rat islet allografts, intravenous Sertoli cell infusion gave the longest MST (41.6+/-4.20 days, O1) with fewer CD4 and CD8 T cells and lower IL-2 (O2-O4), consistent with T-cell-driven rejection being the lever Gate2A targets. The strategy is systemic tolerance by infused accessory cells in an abstract-only rat study, not an edited-graft cloak, so transfer to SC-islets is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (human-immune-system humanized mouse as allorejection testbed for human islets)
edges.claim_summary: HSC-engrafted NRG-Akita mice rejected 8/13 human islet allografts (P = 0.03 vs non-engrafted, O13) with human CD45+ graft infiltration (O14), against 8/9 restored without a human immune system (O12). The test is on unedited primary human islets, and rejection was incomplete (5/13 did not revert, O16), so an unedited control arm is needed in each cohort.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo function readout of human islets in a spontaneously diabetic host)
edges.claim_summary: Spontaneously hyperglycemic NRG-Akita mice (O1) were restored to euglycemia by 4,000 IEQ human islets and by mouse islets (O2, O3), with function lasting over 300 days in some cases (O4). Primary human islets stand in for SC-islets here; the authors state the model is intended for validating stem cell-derived beta cells, which this paper does not test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (in vivo maturation of hPSC-derived pancreatic endoderm; stimulated C-peptide and GSIS benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: hESC-derived pancreatic endoderm in athymic nude rats gave islet-like structures in only 50% of implants with beta-cell area 0.8 +/- 0.3% (O1, O2), very low human C-peptide and insulin (O3, O4) and no rise after glucose challenge (O5). This is consistent with requiring demonstrated glucose-responsive function (Gate1) rather than assuming in vivo maturation of progenitors; the cells are an early progenitor stage in a rat host.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (device-housed progenitor graft maturation)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0056:L2 | relation=scoping_qualification | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O1,O6 | text_sha256=cc4e62881226525f5557ce846ece806c539a4084d9ab0e52b061d9b50cc869e6]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmark for an MHC-mismatched islet graft)
edges.claim_summary: Systemic prolonged mATG+CTLA4-Ig delayed rejection of fully allogeneic islets (MST 54 vs 8 days, O1; 30% >70 days, O7) and suppressed alloantigen IFN-gamma (O8, O9), but heart allografts were eventually rejected (O14) and treated-donor splenocytes still rejected donor skin (O12). It is a drug-based benchmark in autoimmune NOD mice, not a graft-intrinsic cloak.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (recurrent T1D autoimmunity, IGRP-reactive T cells)
edges.claim_summary: The same regimen suppressed IFN-gamma responses to BDC2.5 and IGRP peptides (O10), prevented adoptive transfer of diabetes (O11), kept syngeneic islet grafts from rejection (O16) and reversed new-onset diabetes in 10/10 mice (O17). This shows autoimmune pressure on islets can be controlled systemically in NOD mice; it does not test a graft-intrinsic protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1, Locus 3 inducible PD-L1 and allo-T-cell suppression)
edges.claim_summary: Mobilized murine hematopoietic cells express PD-L1 (O14); WT HSC-enriched cells suppress the MLR (O15), whereas PD-L1-KO HSCs are reported not to do so (O16). CXCR4 treatment adds no statistically detected graft-survival benefit in globally PD-L1-deficient recipients (O17). These findings provide a mechanistic bridge to the PD-L1 allo-T-cell inhibitory axis, while direct CXCR4 drug effects (O3), global rather than HSC-specific knockout, and nonexclusive ACK2 effects prevent isolating an HSC-specific causal mechanism. Blueprint §4.3 and ranker Locus-3 entries specify graft-cell PD-L1; incorporation of this particular host-HSC mechanism is not established and remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (graft-expressed inducible PD-L1, Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: Untreated globally PD-L1-deficient recipients have longer survival than WT controls (22 versus 12 days, O18), and CXCR4 treatment produces no statistically detected additional benefit in KO recipients (O17). The net model result therefore qualifies an unconditional PD-L1-is-protective interpretation without testing graft-expressed inducible PD-L1 in human SC-islets. Blueprint §4.3 and ranker effluent clauses already distinguish pathway activity from cellular-source attribution, but whether this particular recipient-KO boundary is incorporated is unknown. Skin rejection in both treated and control mice (O13) also prevents extending the islet result to systemic donor-specific tolerance; no autoimmune/indirect-APC or unrelated-immunity qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (CXCL10 as an islet-intrinsic inflammation-inducible chemokine; Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible cassette)
edges.claim_summary: Primary human islets secrete IP-10/CXCL10 after enterovirus-driven innate activation, which 17β-estradiol reduced (O1) but not the poly(I:C)-induced secretion (O2), consistent with CXCL10 being an islet-intrinsic inducible signal as assumed for the Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible design. Primary islets in vitro rather than SC-islet grafts, and secretion rather than promoter activity, were measured.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (CXCL10-inducible Locus 3 trigger specificity)
edges.claim_summary: Because enterovirus and poly(I:C) induce CXCL10 and innate genes in human islets (O1, O3, O4), CXCL10-gated expression need not be triggered only by autoimmune cytokines but may also respond to viral or dsRNA innate signals; this was not tested at an engineered locus, and the cheatsheet does not state whether viral triggers are considered.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks; donor-specific hyporesponsiveness)
edges.claim_summary: ECDI-SP donor-cell tolerance protected 80% of scaffold islet allografts beyond 150 days vs rejection of all grafts by day 20 without it (O1), with donor-specific MLR hyporesponsiveness (~60% decrease, O10; third-party ns, O11) and local Treg accumulation (O9). This is a murine host-directed tolerance benchmark in non-autoimmune STZ-diabetic mice, not graft editing or hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (implantation-site dependence of immune protection)
edges.claim_summary: With the same ECDI-SP regimen, protection was similar for scaffold vs kidney capsule grafts (O2, P = 0.4) but better for scaffold than intra-portal grafts (O3, P = 0.014), so allograft protection depends on implantation site. This qualifies carrying any Gate2A benchmark across sites; it was not tested for hypoimmune hPSC islets, and the cheatsheet does not say whether the Blueprint addresses site dependence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (surface-marker purification of beta-cell lineage cells; CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment)
edges.claim_summary: Several cell-surface proteins (SEZ6L2, LRP11, DISP2, SLC30A8, FXYD2, TSPAN7, TMEM27) keep an islet-specific expression in the adult pancreas (O4), and DNER and DISP2 antibodies worked in cell sorting (O6), consistent with surface-marker immunoisolation of islet lineage cells. The abstract is from developing and adult pancreas plus mouse and human islet cells, not hPSC-derived islets, and gives no purity or function data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate enrichment or depletion markers beyond CD49a/ITGA1)
edges.claim_summary: DISP2 and DNER (antibodies used in cell sorting, O6) and DDR1 (overlaps early PDX1+/NKX6-1+ progenitors, O3) are untested candidate surface handles to evaluate on hPSC-derived stages alongside CD49a/ITGA1; the cheatsheet names none of these markers, and the abstract reports no sorting purity or hPSC data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (graft-intrinsic allo-T-cell suppression; inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3 as a graft-displayed immunomodulator)
edges.claim_summary: A transient graft-surface immunomodulatory ligand (SA-FasL) with a 15-day rapamycin course kept all 45 allogeneic islet grafts functioning vs acute rejection of controls (O4), through Treg-dependent localized tolerance (O12, O13, O14), consistent with graft-displayed ligands restraining T-cell allorecognition. This is FasL protein display on murine islets in non-autoimmune recipients, not a genetically encoded ligand on hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (benchmarks for graft-intrinsic immunomodulation without systemic immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: The graft-displayed ligand alone gave only ~18% long-term graft survival (O3) and robust protection needed concurrent rapamycin (O4); tolerance was localized, with donor skin rejection (O7) triggering loss of the islet graft (O8), and it was lost on Treg depletion (O12, O13). This qualifies reading a graft-intrinsic ligand as sufficient or systemic; the cheatsheet does not say how the Blueprint treats immunosuppression or Treg dependence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation; dynamic GSIS benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Early hESC-derived insulin+ cells showed defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, reduced glucose-induced Ca2+ uptake and an immature-endocrine genomic signature despite similar TF and glucose-sensing/exocytosis gene expression (O2, O3, O5, O6), consistent with the Blueprint's reliance on Stage-6/7 maturation and GSIS benchmarks. Abstract-only evidence from an early differentiation protocol (up to 25% insulin+ cells); no quantitative values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification and off-target / multihormonal cell elimination)
edges.claim_summary: Even INS:GFP-reporter-purified insulin+ cells were often multihormonal (insulin plus glucagon granules) and functionally heterogeneous (O1, O4), indicating that insulin-positivity alone does not ensure monohormonal beta-cell identity. The cheatsheet states CD49a enrichment and SC-EC elimination but does not state this polyhormonal failure mode.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell endocrine function: insulin biosynthesis and secretion)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP as an intrinsic cytoprotection target)
edges.claim_summary: Pharmacological TXNIP repression with verapamil reduced TXNIP in INS-1 cells, human islets and mouse islets (O1-O3, O9, O18) and was accompanied by lower beta-cell apoptosis and better glucose control in STZ and ob/ob mice (O8, O10-O17), consistent with TXNIP as a Gate4 cytoprotection target. The protection data are in native mouse beta-cells; the human-islet evidence is TXNIP reduction only, and the cheatsheet lists TXNIP without these quantitative results.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (conditional pharmacological TXNIP repression as a possible adjunct)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: because verapamil lowered TXNIP at 11.1 but not 5 mmol/L glucose (O4) and acts through a Ca2+/calcineurin/ChREBP E-box route (O5-O7), an oral calcium channel blocker could be tested as a glucose-conditional TXNIP-lowering adjunct for hPSC-derived islet recipients. This was not tested in grafts or SC-islets here, and the cheatsheet states no such pharmacological element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS-based functional readouts of beta-cell secretion)
edges.claim_summary: In this mouse knockout, fasting insulin was lowered in females (about 20%) but static GSIS and glucose tolerance were unchanged, and the male fasting-insulin and GSIS phenotypes seen on a mixed background vanished on C57BL/6J (O5, O6, O11, O13-O15), so single secretion readouts can dissociate from each other and depend on sex and genetic background. This is a mouse global knockout of a non-Blueprint gene, not an SC-islet result, and the cheatsheet does not state how Gate1 GSIS benchmarks handle such dissociation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP as an intrinsic cytoprotection target; ER-stress-driven beta-cell death)
edges.claim_summary: Txnip deletion protected MEFs and mouse islet beta-cells from ER-stress-induced apoptosis and reduced hyperglycemia and beta-cell apoptosis in the Akita proinsulin-misfolding mouse (O10-O13), and TXNIP induction required IRE1α and PERK but not ATF6 (O2-O4). This extends the cheatsheet's TXNIP Gate4 element to ER-stress death in rodent beta-cells; there are no human islet or SC-islet data and no graft setting.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (upstream IRE1α RNase inhibition as a possible alternative route to lower TXNIP and IL-1β)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis only: the IRE1α RNase inhibitor STF-083010 blocked TXNIP production in INS-1 cells and Tg-induced IL-1β secretion in THP-1 cells (O17, O18), so upstream IRE1α inhibition could be tested as a peri-transplant adjunct to TXNIP lowering. Evidence is in vitro in cell lines and the authors note the compound class may be unstable in vivo; the cheatsheet states no IRE1α element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity is not solved by intragraft cytoprotection alone)
edges.claim_summary: NF-κB-blocked allografts were promptly rejected in an MHC-mismatched mouse model despite better histology (O3, O5), and only adding low-dose rapamycin extended mean survival from 20 to 81 days (O6), so intragraft cytoprotection does not substitute for allo-evasion. This is a mouse allograft model with intact MHC, not an HLA-edited hPSC-derived graft; the cheatsheet does not settle whether the Blueprint already states this boundary.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (T-cell-mediated beta-cell injury; adenosine/CD39 as a candidate protective element)
edges.claim_summary: Tissue-restricted CD39 overexpression protected mice from T-cell-mediated MLDS diabetes with less insulitis and no islet cytokine-gene upregulation (O1, O5, O8-O10), acting through A2A and A2B receptors (O14-O16), so CD39/adenosine generation could be tested as an additional Gate2B protective element. This is a mouse chemical-plus-T-cell model, not an allograft or recurrent-autoimmunity setting, and the cheatsheet lists no CD39 element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (boundary between intrinsic cytoprotection and extrinsic immune modulation)
edges.claim_summary: CD39TG islets were equally susceptible to IL-1β, TNF-α and IFN-γ in vitro as WT islets (O11) while CD39 overexpression still protected in vivo (O1, O10), so this protection does not look like Gate4-type intrinsic cytokine resistance and should be classed as extrinsic immune tempering. Mouse islets and a single in vitro viability assay; the cheatsheet does not state how the Blueprint classifies adenosine-pathway effects.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (SERPINB9 granzyme B inhibition against autoreactive CD8+ T cells)
edges.claim_summary: Human beta cells coexpressing HCMV US2 and SERPINB9 were highly protected from patient-derived autoreactive CD8+ T-cell clones in vitro and kept insulin and C-peptide output when coimplanted with beta-cell-specific cytotoxic T cells in immunodeficient mice (O2-O4), supporting SERPINB9-based Gate2B protection. This is abstract-only evidence in primary human beta cells (not hPSC-derived), SERPINB9 was combined with US2 rather than the Blueprint's PD-L1 pairing, and the cheatsheet does not state this combination or result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (FAS-axis immunomodulation of auto- and alloreactive T cells; transient rapamycin)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (3D extracellular-matrix-mimetic culture for islet-like cluster survival and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: Rabbit adipose-stem-cell-derived islet-like clusters on a 3D dextran-gelatin scaffold showed significantly higher glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and viability than on 2D plates (O3, O4), suggesting a hypothesis that an ECM-mimetic 3D scaffold could be tested for SC-islet viability and function. The cells are rabbit adipose-derived (not hPSC-derived or human), evidence is abstract-only with no values, and the cheatsheet states no scaffold-based culture element for Gate1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell identity gene dosage: SLC30A8/ZnT8)
edges.claim_summary: Human genetics shows heterozygous SLC30A8 truncation is protective against T2D (O1-O3, O8), so SLC30A8/ZnT8 dosage is a candidate genotype to consider when choosing or editing SC-islet lines; the cheatsheet states no such SLC30A8 element for Gate1 and lists ZnT8 only as a Gate2B autoantigen. Untested in SC-islets or T1D, and the study measures T2D risk in population cohorts only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M3 (in vivo maturation of hESC-derived islet progenitors in an encapsulation device)
edges.claim_summary: Encapsulated CyT49 hESC-derived islet progenitors matured in vivo to secrete human insulin (detectable by 7 weeks, 17-fold rise over 8 weeks) and ameliorated alloxan-induced diabetes by 20 weeks (O1, O2, O4). Evidence is abstract-only, in mice with strain and n not stated, and alloxan diabetes is not an autoimmune model.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (graft containment and biomass as safety readout)
edges.claim_summary: BLI showed constant biomass during insulin maturation and full containment of hESC-derived cells in devices up to 150 days (O3, O5). Physical containment is a different safety layer from a genetic suicide switch, so this bears on the Gate5 safety aim only by a bridge, and abstract-only data give no n.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization of a subcutaneous site as oxygen/engraftment support)
edges.claim_summary: Prevascularization of subcutaneous pockets was required for islets to rapidly revert hyperglycemia, which was not seen in nontreated subcutaneous sites (O1); this is consistent with vascularization as part of the avascular-site problem. Rat islets in STZ rats, abstract only, no counts, so bridge to hPSC-derived grafts is by mechanism only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (site-dependent allograft acceptance without immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: Long-term allogeneic survival without immunosuppression in prevascularized subcutaneous sites, versus transient function in liver (O2, O3), suggests testing whether a prevascularized site lowers alloimmune pressure on edited hPSC-islet grafts. Untested in humans or hPSC cells, and the STZ rat model carries no autoimmunity, so Gate2B is not informed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 axis for allo-T-cell suppression)
edges.claim_summary: PD-L1 augmentation was part of the combined arm that reached (92.27±9.65) days allograft survival versus (6.51±0.27) days for control, and the combined arm outlasted Ad-PD-L1 alone at (40.64±3.95) days (O1, O3). PD-L1 is delivered systemically by adenovirus in mouse recipients rather than expressed on the graft, so transfer to a Locus-3 SC-islet design is by mechanism only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (OX40-OX40L co-stimulation blockade as an additional layer)
edges.claim_summary: Combining OX40L knockdown with PD-L1 outperformed either single treatment (O3, O4; OX40L-RNAi-LV alone (55.14±5.48) days), suggesting OX40L co-stimulation blockade as a candidate add-on to a PD-L1 cloak; the cheatsheet lists no OX40/OX40L element. Evidence is mouse, recipient-side systemic vectors, abstract-only, so untested on graft-side edits or human cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-beta maturation, GSIS benchmark, monohormonal architecture)
edges.claim_summary: The unedited SC-beta protocol supports a bounded Gate1/M2 manufacturing and endocrine-function claim: repeated static GSIS (O1-O3), NKX6-1/C-peptide coexpression (O6), predominantly monohormonal C-peptide cells (O7-O8), adult-like transcriptional clustering (O10-O11) and a source-reported proinsulin/insulin ratio (O20). This does not qualify the Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS, <3-minute shut-off, MAFA, SC-EC limit or 60:30:10 exact edited product; per-cell secretion means remain lower than the adult comparator and transcriptional differences persist. Specific empirical incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (rapid in vivo function of SC-beta grafts in immunodeficient hosts)
edges.claim_summary: Human insulin was detected at the earliest tested two-week graft time point (O13); responder proportions were 27/37 SC-beta and 9/12 human-islet recipients without a between-group rate test (O14), while the within-SC-beta insulin increase had p=0.0008 (O21). In NRG-Akita mice, fasting glucose averaged <200 mg/dl across the reported trajectory, insulin responsiveness persisted at day 126, and fewer recipients died over >4 months (O16-O17, O19). These are immunodeficient non-humanized rodent endocrine bioassays, not immune protection, human clinical efficacy, or qualification of the Blueprint oxygen/device/exact-product stack; specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (residual pluripotent cells and tumor formation as safety readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O9 reports no residual OCT4-type pluripotency-marker cells observed, and S5 reports no SC-beta graft masses/tumors compared with later PH graft masses (O18). Neither observation supplies a residual-cell detection limit, tumor denominator, exact S5 host/cohort, or sufficient later follow-up to bound risk, and the authors explicitly require further transplants/histology. This scopes preliminary cell-product safety evidence; it does not validate the Blueprint quantitative residual-PSC/clonogenic escape, pan-lineage suicide-switch, genomic-integrity or 72-hour oxygen contract. Specific empirical incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (complement and blood-contact injury of islet clusters; pig xenograft context)
edges.claim_summary: Pig NICC with GTKO/CD46 or GTKO/CD46/CD39 edits showed antibody binding, shortened coagulation time and reduced viability in human blood with no genotype difference (O1-O4). This is a xenogeneic natural-antibody setting with no hPSC-derived or human islets, so it tests none of the NK or macrophage elements of Gate3 and is recorded only as a domain-mismatched note on complement.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine purity, single-hormone architecture and progenitor removal)
edges.claim_summary: A modified hESC protocol gave ICs with 73%-89% endocrine cells, mostly single-hormone insulin-positive cells, and a simple enrichment gave aggregates of 93%-98% endocrine cells with 1%-3% progenitors (O1-O3). Abstract-only data with no n, no in vitro GSIS value and no beta:alpha:delta composition, so it supports purity and enrichment feasibility only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (device-loaded SC-endocrine product function in vivo and cryopreservation)
edges.claim_summary: Enriched ICs in macroencapsulation devices functioned in mice similarly to the VC-01 product, and endocrine aggregates could be cryopreserved with retained functionality (O4, O5). Mouse strain, n and functional values are not in the abstract, and the device's immunoprotection is asserted in the Significance text, not measured.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 maturation benchmark vs in vivo-dependent maturation)
edges.claim_summary: ICs showed relatively low maturity-associated markers and a time to function similar to PEC-01 cells, so they needed cell-autonomous maturation after in vivo delivery (O6). This product therefore does not meet an in vitro Stage-6/7 maturity benchmark and should not be read as evidence for a mature, immediately functional graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization of a subcutaneous site; prevascularized device)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (complement activation and innate leukocyte injury of human islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: Complement activation products (iC3b, C4d, C5b-9), innate cell infiltration (CD11b+, CD66b+) and cytokines accompany early human islet graft damage, and APT070 reduced them in vitro and in hu-NSG mice at day 5 (O3-O8, O10-O13). Primary human islets rather than SC-islets, 5-day horizon, no placebo-vs-SC-islet comparison; the cheatsheet places complement inside Gate3 but names no complement-regulator element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (membrane-localizing complement regulation as an add-on to the immune cloak)
edges.claim_summary: A membrane-bound C3 convertase inhibitor on islets cut complement deposition and C-peptide/LDH release (O6, O7, O11, O12), suggesting a complement-regulatory layer could be tested alongside HLA-E/CD47 for SC-islets. The benefit was transient (IFN-γ difference gone by day 9; O16) and did not give a significant graft-survival gain (O18), so this is untested on SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-1/PD-L1 axis and tolerance maintenance)
edges.claim_summary: In a fully mismatched mouse islet allograft model, PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade abrogated CD3 Ab tolerance (median survival 33.7 ± 1.5 and 28.6 ± 5.1 days) and anti-PD-L1 at day 100 precipitated rejection (O10-O12), with PD-L1 raised on intragraft CD8+ T cells (O8). PD-L1 acts here on recipient T cells during antibody-induced tolerance, not as a graft-expressed cloak on beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (adaptive allo-rejection of islet grafts under immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: Inflammatory cell infiltrates were present in all biopsied islet allografts despite immunosuppression (O6), which the authors read as graft rejection detectable by endoscopic biopsy; infiltrate cell types are not stated, so the link to T-cell allorecognition is indirect and the cells are pig islets, not hypoimmune hPSC islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive CD4 T-cell antigen repertoire; PPI-derived epitopes)
edges.claim_summary: The cheatsheet lists PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8 and IA-2 as Gate2B autoantigens; this study shows CD4 clones from NOD mice (O1, O2, O3) and from islets of T1D organ donors (O13, O14, O17) recognize hybrid insulin peptides formed by fusing proinsulin C-peptide fragments to other granule peptides, with murine HIPs detected by MS (O7, O8). HIP formation in hPSC-derived beta cells was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (residual autoreactive CD4 memory; HLA class II dependence)
edges.claim_summary: Islet-derived human CD4 T cells from two T1D organ donors responded to HIPs (O13, O17), restricted by HLA-DQ8 and blocked by anti-HLA-DQ antibody (O15, O16), consistent with Gate2B's premise of autoreactive CD4 memory. Presentation was by B-cell lines rather than beta cells, so it does not show a graft-level effect.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate4 / M3 (thrombo-inflammatory site burden and acute islet-distress surrogates)
edges.claim_summary: Primary syngeneic rat site comparisons found a lower 1 h insulin peak and lower 24 h leptin and α2-macroglobulin in the intraomental scaffold (O7, O9, O10), while C-peptide lacked a significant difference (O8), and MCP-1/CCL2, IL-6 and haptoglobin were described as comparable (O20, O21). O10 retains the Results pg/mL versus F5 μg/mL conflict. These systemic surrogates bridge Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 thrombo-inflammation and Gate4 stress; they do not measure NK/macrophage protection, β-cell loss directly, or a cytoprotective gene effect. Precise incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 / M3 (allogeneic graft outcome under conventional immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: Four fully MHC-mismatched rat recipients initially achieved normoglycemia but returned to hyperglycemia with rejection by up to 5 weeks under the stated immunosuppressive protocol (O13); one immunosuppressed NHP showed peri-insular CD3 infiltrate at POD 49 (O17). These data qualify extrahepatic graft feasibility under conventional immunosuppression; no no-immunosuppression comparison isolates scaffold immune protection, and no hypoimmune hPSC or autoimmune/indirect-APC protection is established. Blueprint §1.2 retains independent alloimmune cloaking; exact outcome incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate5 / M3 (dose-dependent extrahepatic function and late vascular engraftment)
edges.claim_summary: Primary rat intraomental grafts supported glycemic control and author-described comparable glucose clearance at tested adequate doses and purities (O1–O6, O11, O12, O19), but 450 IEQ favored intrahepatic metabolic-control success in unshown data (O22). Late vascular histology (O3, O18) and improved glycemia/C-peptide in one NHP ending at death on POD 49 (O14–O16) support feasibility only. Blueprint §4.5 uses a folded prevascularized omental pouch plus separate oxygen/packing qualifications: these data do not establish measured 72-hour pO2, oxygen delivery, vascularization onset, edited SC-islet performance, or fail-safe function. Exact incorporation of these dose/purity/endpoint findings remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inducible PD-L1, Locus 3; allo-T-cell suppression)
edges.claim_summary: Loss of PD-L1 on donor islets shortened median allograft survival from 13 to 9 days (O2) and increased graft-infiltrating CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (O7, O8), splenic effector CD4+ T cells (O12) and alloreactive IFN-γ responses (O14, O17) while Foxp3+ cells fell (O9, O18). This is a mouse primary-islet knockout in unmodified immunocompetent allogeneic recipients, supporting a protective role of islet PD-L1 against alloreactive T cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 design element: necessity vs gain-of-function)
edges.claim_summary: The evidence is germline PD-L1 loss in donor islets (O2), which shows necessity of donor PD-L1 for normal allograft survival but not that PD-L1 overexpression or cytokine-inducible PD-L1 in hPSC-derived islets is sufficient to extend survival. PD-L1 on passenger donor cells in the islet preparation is not separated from islet-cell PD-L1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and maturation; NKX6.1+ monohormonal β-like cells and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: In hESC-derived β-like cells, ~15% CPEP+ cells (O13), ~80% of them monohormonal (O14), gave GSIS of around 2 fold (O15), which sits at the low end of the cheatsheet's stimulation-index reference range. NGN3−/− cells lacked NKX6.1 co-expression in most CPEP+ cells (O16) and GSIS (O17), and NGN3 induction worked in all stages, strongest at S4 and S5 (O18); the cheatsheet does not state NGN3 dependence.

edges.claim_summary: O1–O6 and O19–O21 support cell-class feasibility of generating insulin-secreting SC-β cells from the tested T1D and ND hiPSC lines. The 2/20 mM static challenge and SCID/Beige graft bioassays do not test Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 dynamic biphasic secretion, 16.7→2.8 mM shut-off, engineered tri-hormonal product or donor-population equivalence; incorporation of these exact patient/assay findings is not established.

edges.claim_summary: O5-O6: bilirubin raised PD-L1 on mouse macrophages and their coculture with splenocytes expanded Foxp3+ Tregs, suggesting a host-APC-side tolerogenic conditioning to pair with graft-side PD-L1 at Locus 3. edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4, O6: a four-drug regimen downregulated T-cell and infection-defence genes in recipient blood, while CXCL10 and MX1 rose with early rejection-associated signals and early single GalT-KO losses. A small-volume blood immune-gene panel could be tested as a non-invasive rejection readout in Islet-1 preclinical work; it is not validated against graft function in this abstract and comes from xenografts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (maturation and functional readouts of hESC-derived beta-like cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 and O18-O21 distinguish preserved marker/content measures from impaired secretagogue responses and mouse glucose control after these biallelic knockouts. WT static GSIS of 2.3±0.8-fold coexists with an approximately 30-40% glucose-Ca2+ responder fraction whose genotype is not stated; the >70% primary-beta-cell comparator is external literature. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 already requires dynamic biphasic GSIS and rapid shutoff, so this qualifies transfer from older static assays rather than contradicting that requirement. The specific static/Ca2+ observation is not established as incorporated; no threshold or product qualification is inferred.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (CDKAL1-null-context FOS/JUN inhibition hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O11-O17 support T5224/FOS-pathway perturbation within the CDKAL1-null model: stress-death rescue, reduced apoptosis, restored secretion and acute mouse GSIS, with the reported lack of effect in WT contexts. Results paragraphs 16-19 additionally describe FOS genetic rescue of secretion and separate long-term/in vivo assays; these are contextual support, not extra replicated outcome records. A head-to-head test in this susceptible platform is a hypothesis for Gate4, not a validated upgrade for unedited donor lines, common GWAS risk alleles, immune pressure or the exact OpenIslet product. Claim-specific adoption is unknown after checking the frozen Blueprint/ranker/graveyard resilience scope; keyword absence is not adoption evidence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5(b) / M5 (whether a sustained, insulated high-expression iCasp9 cassette alone reaches the <1e-6 escape threshold)
edges.claim_summary: O11, O12, O17: retransduction restored iC9 expression to parental level (O11) yet CID sensitivity only incompletely (O12), and CID plus BCL2 inhibition did not eliminate the cells (O17). This qualifies any reliance on expression insulation alone for the escape threshold: expression was necessary but not shown sufficient in these lentiviral hiPSC, so a separate non-silencing escape route (BCL2) must also be addressed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 vs Gate5 / M5 (compatibility of BCL2/XIAP cytoprotection payloads with the iCasp9 fail-safe)
edges.claim_summary: O13-O16, O18: BCL2 was high in iC9-resistant hiPSC while XIAP was similar, ABT737 augmented caspase-9/-3 activation (with drug-alone toxicity, O16), and SMAC mimetics did not help. A BCL2 cytoprotection payload (Gate4) could raise the apoptosis threshold for the Gate5 switch; BCL2 here was upregulated in a selected subpopulation, not engineered, so this is a compatibility check to run, not a demonstrated conflict.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (ZnT8 autoantigen) and Gate1 / M2 (GSIS function)
edges.claim_summary: Isolated mouse islet GSIS was lost only with combined Slc30a7 and Slc30a8 deletion (O5, O6). Untested hypothesis: if ZnT8 were ever edited out as an autoantigen in SC-islets, ZnT7 would need to stay intact to protect GSIS. Evidence is mouse deletion data from an abstract only; human or SC-islet transfer is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO removal of HLA class I recognition by CD8+ T cells)
edges.claim_summary: Mature hESC-derived endocrine cells carried normal HLA class I (O3) and were killed by alloreactive and CMV-specific CTLs (O12, O13), while low-HLA progenitors became CTL targets once IFNγ upregulated HLA (O2, O10). This supports the rationale for removing HLA class I via B2M KO; the assays used unedited cells and in vitro CTL clones only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (complement arm of innate immunity; antibody-dependent killing)
edges.claim_summary: Mature hESC-ECs resisted alloantibody plus rabbit complement lysis (O18; CD46, CD59 and a higher CD55 than PEs, O6-O8) but were sensitive to alloantibody-driven cellular cytotoxicity (O17). This qualifies Gate3 complement scope: in this in vitro assay complement was not the vulnerability of mature cells, while antibody-directed cytotoxicity depended on HLA targets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate2B (CXCL10 Locus 3 induction strength; donor or cell-line IFIH1 genotype)
edges.claim_summary: TC donor islets showed higher type III IFN, ISG and secreted CXCL10 responses than TT islets (O11, O12, O13) with similar virus load (O15, O16). Untested hypothesis: the IFIH1 rs1990760 genotype of the source hPSC line could modulate how strongly a CXCL10-inducible cassette fires during viral challenge; no hPSC-derived material was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1+NKX6.1+ progenitor to beta-like cell manufacturing yield)
edges.claim_summary: Losing one GATA6 allele cut NKX6.1+PDX1+ PP2 cells from about 55% to about 20% (O7) and C-peptide+ beta-like cells from 15% to about 3.5% (O9), and GATA6/GATA4 compound dosage loss blocked PDX1+ cell formation (O17, O18). Untested hypothesis: the GATA6 and GATA4 copy state of an Islet-1 edited line should be verified, since dosage loss would cut the beta-cell yield.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic GSIS stimulation index benchmark SI >= 2.0-3.0)
edges.claim_summary: hPSC-derived beta-like cells made with a 2nd-generation protocol showed a static high/low glucose C-peptide ratio of about 2-fold in both WT and GATA6-/+ lines (O11), at the lower edge of the Gate1 stimulation-index benchmark in the cheatsheet. Measured by static incubation, not dynamic perifusion, so it does not show the upper range.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive CD8+ T cell memory; autoantigen panel for Gate2B testing)
edges.claim_summary: T1D patients carry CD8+ T cells against a nonconventional insulin product that can kill human beta cells (O2, O3), an autoantigen outside the cheatsheet Gate2B list (PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8, IA-2). Untested hypothesis: include such alternative-ORF epitopes in the autoreactive T-cell panels used to challenge edited SC-islets. Abstract only: HLA restriction and whether SC-islets express the product are unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (islet paracrine architecture: beta:alpha:delta composition and alpha-cell function)
edges.claim_summary: In mice, pancreatic but not intestinal Gcg reactivation restored the Ex9-sensitive glucose regulation (O11, O16, O17), pointing to islet alpha-cell GLP-1 as a paracrine contributor. Untested hypothesis: when assessing SC-islet alpha-cell content under Gate1, also check GCG processing to GLP-1 and Ex9 sensitivity of GSIS. Mouse in vivo data; authors flag possible species differences.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation timing and endocrine induction via NEUROG3)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 and O5-O6 show in an in vitro hPSC-derived pancreatic differentiation model that an activating STAT3 mutation induces NEUROG3 (and INS/GCG) prematurely, and O4 reports complete reversal on CRISPR correction, adding qualitative evidence that endocrine-induction timing is a regulated variable in iPSC-to-islet protocols. The abstract gives no magnitudes, it is a disease-mutation context, and it does not measure maturation or GSIS.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E single-chain NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 support the mechanism that HLA-E single chains can inhibit NKG2A-dependent human NK killing of B2M-edited hESC-derived CD45+ cells; blockade increases killing, and the lower-NKG2A donor shows only partial reversal. O6 supports a bounded NK-92/CD45+ mouse bridge; the separate teratoma exposure comparison is qualified by p=0.096 (O22). Incorporation here refers to the HLA-E/NKG2A mechanism and subset boundary already explicit in Blueprint Locus 1 and Decision Experiment 2, not adoption of each experimental magnitude. The study trimer uses VMAPRTLFL, whereas the current exact Blueprint construct uses VMAPRTLVL with additional CD47/promoter engineering; SC-islet and exact-product protection remain unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M-null CD8+ T-cell evasion, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O9, O11 and O21 support reduced EB-primed allogeneic CD8+ lysis/infiltration after removal of polymorphic class I, with O13/O19 providing CDC assay evidence and one trimer-c6 serum exception. O12 reports WT necrosis without establishing a comparative necrosis burden. The incorporated claim is the B2M/class-I allo-CD8 and DSA-evasion strategy in Blueprint section1.2/Locus1, not quantitative adoption of every assay result. HLA class II absence remains an explicit source limitation; WT-EB CD8 priming is not proof of protection from host-APC indirect CD4 presentation or T1D memory. This is a bridge from hematopoietic/RPE cells and teratomas, without SC-islet or current-product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (B2M-editing line quality, karyotype and clone selection; residual class I also qualifies Gate2A / M1)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O18 and O20 qualify B2M-editing line selection: original-vector H1 alleles leaked inducible class I; two selected pure complete-KO Elf-1 clones were abnormal (including tetraploidy) and had lower hematopoietic suspension output; analyzed PCR+ second-step knockout cohorts differ from selected final clones. Selected HLA-E dimer/trimer clones had normal karyotypes, but >89% CD45+ is a fraction, not proof of normal absolute yield or SC-islet differentiation. This supports clone-specific residual-HLA, genomic and growth QC as a justified hPSC bridge. Generic Blueprint QC is present; incorporation of this particular AAV/B2M failure pattern is unknown, and the experiment does not prove a universal causal B2M hazard or a nuclease-derived genotoxicity rate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (unmodified allogeneic cells in immunocompetent hosts as the rejection benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O12, O14 and O15 show loss of detectable GFP+ allogeneic murine MSC grafts by day 28 with earlier inflammatory infiltration and shorter persistence than syngeneic grafts (O10; P < 0.01 allogeneic-versus-syngeneic comparison). This supports a Gate2A allorecognition benchmark for immunocompetent hosts; inflammatory infiltrates are not cell-typed and the experiment does not isolate direct from indirect pathways. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §4.2 address alloimmune cloaking, but these MSC data do not qualify a human SC-islet cloak. Claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (non-hPSC fetal progenitor differentiation into hormone-expressing glucose-responsive islet-like clusters)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 support hormone-positive cluster formation and a qualitative glucose response from expanded human fetal pancreatic progenitors. This M2 differentiation bridge does not establish hPSC Stage-6/7 maturity, composition, biphasic dynamic GSIS or low-glucose shut-off; the separate Fig1d progenitor-comparator p-value is not the high-versus-low glucose p-value.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (intraportal graft function with recipient renal benefit in diabetic rats)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O9 support week-16 graft presence, endocrine markers, serum human C-peptide and lower glucose in ordinary Wistar rats. O10-O13 and O18-O25 describe recipient renal benefit with partial transcript/marker recovery despite insulin-associated glycemic improvement; nonsignificant insulin renal contrasts do not prove equivalence, and neither glycemic matching nor causal C-peptide/pathway attribution is established. O3/O8 overlap and renal assays are not graft intrinsic cytoprotection tests.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (developmental HLA and xenogeneic graft immunogenicity observations)
edges.claim_summary: O8/O14-O17 are bounded early-fetal developmental-HLA, rat lymphocyte-lysate and xenograft-presence observations. They do not establish human allorejection protection, donor-specific antibody absence, recurrent autoimmunity, indirect-APC protection or innate resistance of an engineered mature SC-islet product. O16 has unusual positive-control wording; O17 assay specificity is unresolved. The Blueprint human adaptive/innate assay requirements cannot be replaced by these rat observations.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (non-genetic local Treg-containing prevascularized subcutaneous site for allogeneic islets)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 report 8 of 10 allogeneic rat islet recipients with long-term graft survival without immunosuppression in a regulatory T cell-containing granulomatous pocket, adding evidence that local site conditioning can limit alloimmune rejection in rodents. The abstract has no control arm, no follow-up duration and no human SC-islet data, so transfer to Gate2A cloaking is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (graft function in a prevascularized subcutaneous site)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 report vascularized pockets 10 days after agarose-SEK rod implantation and nonfasting blood glucose confirming graft survival in 8 of 10 recipients. Function is judged by blood glucose only (no C-peptide, GSIS or perifusion in the abstract), in rat islets rather than SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 target; M7 source boundary (marker positivity versus measured glucose responsiveness)
edges.claim_summary: The bounded incorporated claim is the need to measure endocrine function separately from marker identity: murine embryonic-progenitor pancreatoids express Insulin and beta-cell markers yet show no glucose-stimulated c-peptide increase (O1, O4–O5, O9–O12). Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 (line 61) separately requires NKX6-1/INS/MAFA identity and dynamic biphasic GSIS/low-glucose shut-off; this functional requirement is already accounted for. This static murine assay is domain-mismatched to human SC-islets and does not test the Blueprint’s dynamic endpoints, establish product qualification, or establish incorporation of this protocol or its numeric values. The ranker Gate1 maturation priors and Graveyard004 are context only, not evidence that this murine protocol was adopted.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (macrophage phagocytosis arm; CD47-SIRPalpha engagement)
edges.claim_summary: In rhesus recipients, macrophage infiltration of islets rose from 1 to 24 hours irrespective of islet type (O6) and was greater for GTKO porcine islets than alloislets at 7 days despite costimulation blockade (O16, p=0.02), consistent with an innate macrophage arm that adaptive-targeted regimens do not control. Porcine xenoislets, not hPSC-derived islets, and no CD47 or SIRPalpha intervention was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (early peri-transplant islet stress and loss)
edges.claim_summary: Within 24 hours of intraportal infusion, WT porcine islets showed more caspase 3 activity (O1, 1 hour) and more TUNEL-positive cells (O4, p=0.03) than rhesus alloislets, while ex vivo cultured WT NPIs had minimal caspase 3 activity (O3), pointing to early in vivo apoptosis rather than an intrinsic defect. Xenogeneic primary islets in the liver, so transfer to hPSC islet grafts is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (ZnT8 autoantigen; autoimmunity protection)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT8, which the cheatsheet lists among Gate2B autoantigens, was immunogenic in knock-out mice (O1) and accessible to human type 1 diabetes patient antibodies on live rat INS-1E cells, with a ZnT8 knock-out specifically reducing the binding (O3, O4). The finding is humoral and in a rat cell line, whereas Gate2B is framed around T-cell memory, and pathogenicity is only raised as a possibility (O5).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP; hypoxic and inflammatory stress resilience)
edges.claim_summary: In MIN6 cells, hypoxia up-regulated ROS and TXNIP (O3, O4) and activated the NLRP3 inflammasome with cell death in LPS-primed cells (O1, O2), with an ROS-TXNIP-NLRP3 axis concluded (O5, O6); the cheatsheet lists TXNIP among Gate4 elements but does not state this inflammasome mechanism. Mouse insulinoma line framed around type 2 diabetes, abstract only, no graft or hPSC islet data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (oxygenated macroencapsulation and mass-transfer failure boundaries); Gate4 (injury/amyloid context)
edges.claim_summary: Primary allogeneic islets in the refillable-oxygen βAir device showed surviving beta cells alongside central necrosis/amyloid (O16–O18), low intact-device secretion and partial recovery of slab responsiveness (O15,O20), undetectable intradevice PET signals within finite observation windows (O14), and little clinical function (O10–O13,O19). These observations qualify any inference that oxygen provision alone secures endocrine performance; impaired nutrient/hormone transport is an interpretation, not a measured permeability. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.5 and ranker macrodevice branches already account for general diffusion/foreign-body hazards, but incorporation of this trial’s exact PET/slab/patient findings is not established. This active refillable primary-islet device does not directly test the Blueprint’s 72-hour passive PDMS-CaO2/catalase bridge, SC-islets, or fail-safe.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical endocrine efficacy benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: The uncontrolled four-patient phase 1 primary-islet device study provides a negative clinical endocrine benchmark: 3-month MMTT C-peptide peaked at 0.06 nmol/L in one patient and was <0.003 nmol/L in the other three (O11); authors report no significant HbA1c change, no CGM variability change and no reduction of insulin needs (O12,O13,O19). These findings do not establish equivalence, insulin independence, or SC-islet manufacturing performance. Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and ranker Gate1 macrodevice diffusional-lag branch establish relevance; the specific trial values’ incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A, Gate2B / M3, M4 (physical-isolation sensitization observations); Gate3 (peridevice macrophage context)
edges.claim_summary: Behind a physical macroencapsulation barrier without systemic immunosuppression, no HLA immunization and no change in GAD/IA2/ANA autoantibody frequency were reported (O2,O3), with no immune-cell islet infiltration restated in Discussion (O4), despite peridevice foreign-body/macrophage/T-cell accumulation (O5–O7). Antibody-frequency observations do not prove elimination of recurrent autoimmune T-cell activity or host-APC indirect presentation. Blueprint §1.2 Gate2A/2B and GRAVEYARD_010 explicitly retain these pathways; physical isolation does not validate B2M/CIITA-edited exposed cells or a CD47 innate cloak. Exact clinical observation incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (primary adult progenitor lineage-output qualification; off-domain for SC-islet manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: O11/O17/O18/O19/O20 show residual progenitor/possible ductal fractions, acinar-biased RNA-seq preparations and variable differentiation in sorted adult hNEPT-derived cultures. These findings bound the lineage-purity and reproducibility claims for that alternative route; they do not contradict the hPSC SC-islet Gate1 protocol, establish a clonogenic hazard, or prove a need to replace the Blueprint live endocrine-sorting workflow (§1.2; §6 item 4, Step 1 at line 245). The Blueprint already requires lineage checks, but incorporation of these particular adult-progenitor findings is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive CD4+ T-cell memory and neoepitope antigen repertoire)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4, O5: CD4+ T cells from patients with type 1 diabetes recognize tTG2-modified (deamidated) beta-cell epitopes, so the autoreactive repertoire relevant to Gate2B extends beyond the native antigens the cheatsheet lists (PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8, IA-2). Evidence is human islets and insulinoma cells plus patient T cells, not hPSC-derived beta cells, and the abstract gives no counts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER-stress resilience, MANF/TXNIP, linked to Gate2B immunogenicity)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3: ER stress raised cytosolic calcium and tTG2 activity in insulinoma cells and stressed islets elicited T-cell responses to modified peptides. Hypothesis (untested here): ER-stress mitigation in graft beta cells could also reduce neoepitope generation, a Gate2B benefit of Gate4 payloads that this abstract does not test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (clinical benchmarks: insulin independence, stimulated C-peptide)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O5, O6: in forty islet allograft recipients, clinical graft-function endpoints (insulin independence, metabolic benefit defined as <25% CV fasting glycaemia with >331 pmol/l C-peptide) varied with recipient BMI, SLC30A8 genotype and HLA-A*24 (p = 0.012-0.046). This qualifies the use of such clinical benchmarks for comparison with SC-islet trials: recipient covariates matter. Evidence is deceased-donor islets, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 paired with SERPINB9; sufficiency of PD-L1 alone)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O4, O16: endogenous β cell PD-L1 appears reactively with T cell infiltration (absent in Rag1-/- islets) and, per the authors' Discussion, did not prevent diabetes in most NOD mice, so PD-L1 alone should not be assumed sufficient against autoimmunity. This is an interpretation from mouse data without a PD-L1 loss- or gain-of-function arm.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (graft-local, non-genetic adjunct to the B2M/CIITA/PD-L1 adaptive-immunity stack)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O5, O14: in fully allogeneic mouse recipients, co-transplanted SA-FasL microgels with a short rapamycin course gave 12/13 grafts surviving 200 days and Treg-dependent acceptance. Hypothesis only: a graft-local Fas-ligand/Treg-promoting biomaterial could be tested as an adjunct against residual T-effector pressure in hPSC-islet grafts; not tested against edited cells or in human-immune-system models.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (what local immune protection requires)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O6, O11, O14: protection was conditional in this model: SA-FasL alone gave MST = 31 days (about 25% over 200 days), rapamycin alone MST = 36 days, systemic donor-antigen responses stayed intact, and Treg depletion rejected all grafts. Graft-local ligand display should not be read as a stand-alone, drug-free immune cloak; evidence is mouse allografts, not hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (mono-hormonal β-like cell manufacturing, mature marker panel)
edges.claim_summary: A hESC protocol giving 85–95% mono-hormonal INS+ cells (O1) with high PDX1/NKX2.2 but only 50.8% NKX6.1 and 63.6% UCN3 (O2) and a GSIS response given only qualitatively (O3) is consistent with Gate1 manufacturing aims. It is a minimal disease-modeling protocol, not a benchmarked SC-islet product, and no stimulation index is reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (β-cell secretory capacity; SLC30A8 loss-of-function as a candidate edit)
edges.claim_summary: R138X mice secreted more insulin under S961 hyperglycemia (O8) with no change in chow GIIS, proliferation or mass (O6, O11, O12), suggesting an SLC30A8 loss-of-function edit as a testable secretory-capacity upgrade for SC-β cells. This is a mouse study with residual Slc30a8 mRNA (O1), protein not excluded (O3) and homozygosity unconfirmed, and human SC-islet effects are untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CIITA transcript only)
edges.claim_summary: Ciita was 2.47-fold higher in R138X mouse islets in bulk RNA-seq (O18), alongside other hematopoietic-lineage genes. No class II, T-cell or immune-evasion readout was measured, so it does not inform the CIITA knockout design.

edges.target_gate_or_module: None of Gate1-Gate5 / M7 (biophysical binding constants only)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports anti-ZnT8 antibody affinity, selectivity, Fab-mediated transport inhibition and an HTRF assay (O1-O6) as research tools. It reports no β-cell function, graft, immune or safety readout, so it bears on no Islet-1 gate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 element, Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: Native T1D insulin-containing islets showed PDL1 expression (O1-O4) associated with an insulitis context (O18); this supports biological plausibility of the PD-L1 element already included in frozen Blueprint §4.3/§6 X3, which cites PMID:30269996, and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9. Incorporation is only the qualitative PD-L1-shield rationale, not adoption of these tissue counts or proof of protection. These observational/native-human and expression results did not test immune killing, indirect APC suppression, SC-islet grafts or exact-product efficacy.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / Gate4 / M1 (native PDL1 regulation and Locus 3 signaling/promoter compatibility boundary)
edges.claim_summary: Native PDL1/reporter induction depends on the tested cytokine and pathway context: IFNα/IFNγ versus IL-1β (O5-O7), JAK1/ruxolitinib (O9-O11), compensating single-STAT knockdown versus combined STAT1/2 knockdown (O12-O14), and the native PDL1 promoter IRF1 site (O15-O16). Complete abolition at 4 µM ruxolitinib is EndoC-specific; primary-islet PDL1 was severely inhibited. Frozen Blueprint §5/§6 X3×X4 and GRAVEYARD_001 already recognize a general signaling/promoter hazard, but incorporation of these exact native-promoter, siRNA and pharmacologic boundaries is not established. Acute partial siRNA knockdown, native CD274 promoter reporters and JAK inhibition do not directly establish clonal STAT1/TYK2 knockout behavior or performance of CXCL10/synthetic PD-L1 cassettes; exact SC-islet cassette testing is an unvalidated transfer.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (local sustained release of a maturation factor from an extrahepatic scaffold)
edges.claim_summary: Exendin-4 release from a PLG scaffold raised human C-peptide 15.7-fold over blank scaffolds (O5) and gave insulin-dominant graft composition at weeks 4 and 8 (O9, O10) for stage-4 progenitors in the fat pad, suggesting local maturation cues as a testable device element. Evidence is H1 progenitors in immunodeficient NSG mice with insulin pellets, not Stage 6/7 SC-islets or an immune-competent host.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (in vivo maturation toward mono-hormonal beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: Blank-scaffold fat-pad grafts drifted to glucagon-dominant composition by week 8 (O8) with glucose of approx. 400–600 mg/dL versus approx. 100–250 mg/dL under the kidney capsule (O1), while exendin-4 scaffolds were insulin-dominant (O9, O10). This supports Gate1's need for mono-hormonal maturation but shows site and local cues can dominate the outcome in this stage-4 progenitor model.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2, M3 (ER-stress resilience of SC-beta cells; survival-only endpoints)
edges.claim_summary: Human INS-mutant SC-beta-like cells had low basal apoptosis without a detected genotype difference (O6, O14), despite reduced early proliferation, INS+ fraction, insulin content, cell size and graft C-peptide (O1, O4, O9–O12, O15–O18). The proliferative difference gradually disappeared after transplantation as corrected-cell proliferation declined (O26). This bounds survival-only interpretations of Gate4: genetic proinsulin stress can affect development/output without detected excess basal apoptosis. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 already names unfolded-proinsulin stress and §4 separates survival from survivor function; adoption of this mutation-specific developmental boundary is not established. Normoglycemic non-humanized NSG hosts do not test exact-product cytokine/hypoxia resilience or immune protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (endogenous MANF stress-response marker in SC-beta-like cells)
edges.claim_summary: MANF immunoreactivity increased with BIP/GRP170 under mutant-proinsulin stress in human SC-beta-like cells and grafts (O5, O13), but overnight MANF secretion showed only a nonsignificant tendency and circulating human MANF was below detection (O24–O25). No MANF perturbation tested protective function. This source-checks an endogenous stress-response observation; it does not validate MANF addition as a Gate4 intervention. The cheatsheet mentions MANF; current adoption of this specific empirical boundary is not established by the inspected Blueprint/ranker stress and recovery sections.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-7 SC-islet composition and functional maturity)
edges.claim_summary: Stage-7 aggregates averaged 18 ± 6% SD INS+NKX6.1+ cells across lines (O2), with INS+ fractions 31 ± 10% SD mutant and 49 ± 13% SD corrected (O1). Static secretion with 1 µM forskolin showed minimal glucose fold responses (1.15 mutant, 1.05 corrected), preserved pharmacological responses, and nonsignificant genotype differences in fractional release despite 5.2-fold lower mutant insulin content (O8–O9, O19; same experiment). Corrected-graft C-peptide rose from month 2 (O11), consistent with expansion/maturation but not separating these mechanisms. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 requires dynamic biphasic GSIS and rapid shutoff; this disease model provides a bounded immaturity/metrology example and does not qualify those functions or a production lot.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M7 (scope of intrinsic cytoprotection across death mechanisms)
edges.claim_summary: Propargite preferentially depleted hESC-derived INS+ cells (O2) and damaged primary human islets (O4, O5); PS translocation/caspase-3 activation were not induced in β-like cells (O7, O8), and GSH rescued human-cell survival/death endpoints (O11, O12). The ROS-null observation and DNA-damage-before-HMGB1 timing are MIN6 mouse-cell results (O13, O9). This supports a justified mechanistic scope check for the frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and ranker Gate4 branches (CXCL10/SERPINB9/PD-L1, A20, RNLS/IAPP): apoptosis-oriented or oxidative-stress protection cannot be assumed to cover this pesticide-detoxification context. None of those Blueprint interventions was tested here, so their failure or efficacy is not established. Specific incorporation is unknown; reviewed Gate4 architecture is insufficient to establish adoption of this finding.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M7 (candidate source-line GSTT1 context and GSH-dependent xenobiotic resilience)
edges.claim_summary: Across ten hPSC lines, double-null GSTM1/GSTT1 status correlated with lower propargite survival (O14, O21); isogenic GSTT1-null β-like cells had IC50 1.17 μM versus 2.15 μM for the matched WT clone (O15), with more DNA damage (O16). EndoC-βH1 GSTT1-targeting effects were also observed in vitro (O19) and in NSG xenografts (O20; T5, no human immune reconstitution). Recording GSTT1 context and testing an explicitly bounded xenobiotic challenge in candidate source-line resilience work is an unvalidated transfer hypothesis: the study does not establish benefit from GSTT1 overexpression, genotype-based line exclusion, GSH supplementation in the Islet-1 product, or peri-transplant protection. GSTM1 cannot be assigned the same causal effect from the population correlation. Incorporation is unknown after bounded review of the frozen Blueprint/ranker Gate4 scope; no ranking or graveyard change follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1, M3 (localized SA-FasL adjunct with transient systemic conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: The broad approach of a localized SA-FasL biomaterial adjunct under transient rapamycin is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §4.2 (lines 144–146) and ranker lines 2852–2856. O2 and O10–O12 support this approach only in mouse allografts with the stated regimens; the no-rapamycin group had mixed outcomes and is not a clean rapamycin-only contrast. This is not a new human HLA-ablation upgrade or validation of protection from autoimmunity/indirect APC presentation, and exact PLG-specific dosing incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (alloimmune barrier and locally protected rodent islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: Fully mismatched BALB/c-to-C57BL/6 islets without SA-FasL were rejected under transient rapamycin, whereas SA-FasL presentation prolonged graft function (O2, O10–O12). Recipient CD8+ responses were described as similar and CD4+ responses greater than naive controls for donor/third-party MLR stimuli (O4–O5), qualifying claims of systemic donor unresponsiveness; these assays do not establish broad unrelated immunity. No direct T-cell-deletion mechanism, B2M/CIITA edit efficacy or human-product protection was isolated here; exact study-specific benchmark incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (function of mouse islet grafts on immunomodulatory PLG scaffolds)
edges.claim_summary: PLG scaffold-associated mouse grafts restored glycemia and long-term recipients had authors-described IPGTT similarity to naive mice (O1, O3, O13–O14); this does not establish SC-islet manufacturing, biphasic GSIS or equivalence. O16–O17 characterize fluorescent-SA binding to biotin-PLG scaffolds, with unresolved Results/caption dose units; A20 apoptosis is a separate bioactivity endpoint (O8–O9). Neither 72-hour oxygen bridging, fail-safe/genomic safety, nor validated off-the-shelf storage was measured. Exact PLG-material and binding-dose incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3 (stimulated C-peptide and in vivo glucose-control benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: Gene correction restored insulin-positive cells, insulin content and KCl-stimulated secretion (O2, O6, O9), with graft-supported glucose regulation in immune-compromised mice (O10-O14). This is a justified bridge to Gate1/M2 differentiation and M3 graft function, not qualification of the frozen Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS/rapid shut-off or 60:30:10 product: in vitro GSIS was explicitly not evaluated, and no human immune-protection result is established. O20 supplies raw glucagon composition without demonstrating equivalence. Incorporation of these exact study findings is unknown.
