edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (basal insulin-production-associated UPR marker in differentiated human beta-like cells)
edges.claim_summary: Insulin-negative mutant beta-like cells contained less spliced XBP1 than corrected insulin-producing cells (O19), suggesting an association between insulin production and basal IRE1alpha/UPR activity. This provides context for Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 ER-stress assessment, but it does not demonstrate a cytoprotective intervention, resilience to a stress challenge, or a causal benefit of lowering sXBP1; generic caption significance is not assigned to a specific contrast. It does not calibrate the ranker’s Gate4 stress-resilience offsets (rank_islet1_stacks.py:212-224). Incorporation of this specific finding is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (islet-intrinsic cytokine/interferon signaling tone; MAFA as maturation-linked stress readout)
edges.claim_summary: Human cadaveric-islet MAFA co-expression is inversely associated with IFN-response genes (O1, O5); T5 MafA loss raises basal Ifnb1/Mda5 and reduces day-3-minus-day-0 CVB3 production (O10, O11, O16), with no reported infected-genotype viability difference (O17). A MAFA/IFNAR1/IFIH1/DDX58 panel is an untested SC-islet stress-QC hypothesis, not a protection intervention or evidence that suppressing anti-viral priming is beneficial. Frozen ranker DEC-053 already requires intact MDA5/RIG-I/MAVS signaling and functional viral challenge (lines 5983-6009); incorporation of this specific MAFA panel is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 (MAFA-positive maturation-marker interpretation) / M1 (intrinsic interferon-response mechanism)
edges.claim_summary: Blueprint section 1.2 uses MAFA positivity within its mature SC-beta-cell description. The present human co-expression/protein observations and T5 loss experiments show MAFA also associates with intrinsic interferon tone; they do not test SC-islet differentiation, functional maturation, or show that maintaining high MAFA prevents autoimmunity. O20 reports opposing selected T1D-risk/HLA-gene correlations without universal per-gene signs, and O21 adds DLK1 association. This qualifies marker interpretation as a hypothesis for SC-islets. Gate2B host-APC/autoreactive protection remains unmeasured; the study does not discharge GRAVEYARD_010. Specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytokine-exposure stress panel; type I IFN-α not among the cytokines listed in the cheatsheet; upstream of Gate2B autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: Abstract-only evidence (O1-O4) that IFN-α drives PNPT1/miR-26a/TET2-dependent DNA demethylation and upregulation of inflammatory/immune pathway genes in primary human islets, and (O5, O6) that β-cell IFN-α expression precedes T1D in transgenic mice. Untested hypothesis: add an IFN-α exposure arm and a methylation/hydroxymethylation readout to cytokine stress testing of SC-islets; primary islets are a bridge, SC-islets and graft settings are not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO, Locus 1/2 HLA class I and II ablation)
edges.claim_summary: Cells carrying B2M and CIITA disruption plus CD47 survived long-term in fully MHC-mismatched allogeneic mouse recipients without immunosuppression (O5-O7, O3) and, for hiECs, in BLT-humanized mice (O15: four of five grafts vs all WT rejected), supporting the B2M+CIITA adaptive-evasion element. Caveats: non-islet derivatives (ECs, SMCs, CMs), the three edits are never separated, and humanized-mouse Elispot and BLI panels give no stated direction (O9, O10, O12-O14).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 / SIRPalpha engagement; HLA-E axis not tested)
edges.claim_summary: CD47 overexpression is part of every engineered survival outcome (O3, O5-O7, O15), consistent with the CD47 element of Gate3, but the packet states no NK- or macrophage-specific result (O11 direction not given) and the design contains no HLA-E, so the separate contribution of CD47 and the HLA-E/NKG2A axis are not tested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe for residual undifferentiated cells)
edges.claim_summary: Immune-evading B2m-/-Ciita-/- Cd47 tg miPSC grafts survived and formed teratomas in allogeneic immunocompetent BALB/c mice in 100% of grafts (O4, n = 11), i.e. engineered undifferentiated cells are not cleared by the allogeneic immune system, which supports the need for an independent clonogenic kill switch for any residual pluripotent cells in a hypoimmune product. Undifferentiated iPSC grafts, not SC-islets.

edges.claim_summary: Primary human islet/MIN6 NU9056 exposure impaired GSIS (O15/O16); MIN6 Kat5/Dmap1/Brd8 deletion increased intracellular insulin while reducing basal fractional secretion and GSIS (O18/O19/O17). These findings motivate testing the NuA4/Tip60 axis and retaining separate content, basal secretion and glucose-response readouts; they do not establish that activating the axis improves SC-islet maturation. Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and §4.5 already require dynamic function, but adoption of this specific mechanism is not established. M6 denotes actual screen/omics and M7 the functional-proxy failure boundary; no SC-islets tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M6 (observational human beta-cell stress-signature context)
edges.claim_summary: Hypoxia/glycolysis/HIF1A gene-set upregulation and aerobic-respiration downregulation accompany both disease trajectories (O9); heat-shock alpha/beta populations are mainly in two donors (O3), without observed association of the identified minor populations with BMI/T2D (O4). These are observational transcriptome references for the intrinsic-stress domain in Blueprint §1.2 Gate4, not controlled hypoxia exposure, survival benefit or cytoprotection qualification. No immune/indirect-APC outcome is measured, and adoption of these specific signatures is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1-driven maturation program in hPSC-derived beta-like cells: PDX1, NKX6-1, MAFA, UCN3, GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: In this in vitro hPSC-to-beta-like-cell protocol, PDX1 haploinsufficiency and homozygous P33T impaired PP2 differentiation, S7 endocrine yield and static GSIS. This supports the relevance of genotype-dependent differentiation/function readouts to Gate1, whose frozen contract explicitly requires NKX6-1/INS/MAFA maturity and dynamic GSIS (Blueprint §1.2). Static 60-minute low/high-glucose secretion does not validate biphasic dynamics or shut-off. The empirical PDX1 variant mechanism is source verified; its claim-specific incorporation is unknown. No graft or immune-protection endpoint is tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (manufacturing benchmarks and line genotype)
edges.claim_summary: Patient-derived P33T/+ and C18R/+ lines gave about 8% versus about 25% control C-peptide-positive yield and weaker static glucose responsiveness. Isogenic homozygous point-mutant lines support a variant effect, but do not isolate the effect size of either heterozygous patient genotype from donor background. This scopes Gate1 manufacturing interpretation to tested lines/protocols. Blueprint §1.2 and the HIP-Core yield/QC workflow address endocrine function and clone variation; those provisions do not establish whether this specific PDX1-variant boundary is already incorporated. Incorporation is therefore unknown, and this is a qualification rather than a contradiction of a numerical Gate1 acceptance threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP as an intrinsic cytoprotection target; TXNIP-NLRP3 inflammasome pathway)
edges.claim_summary: Abstract-only evidence in the INS-1 rat insulinoma line that Ang II lowers viability and promotes apoptosis (O1, O2) with TXNIP up-regulation (O3), and that MCC950, TXNIP silencing or Telmisartan reduce the apoptosis (O4-O6), is consistent with TXNIP being a useful Gate4 cytoprotection element. Ang II is a different stressor from graft hypoxia or cytokines, the cell line is rodent and not hPSC-derived, and the cheatsheet does not state the NLRP3 mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3, M6 (SC-EC persistence/lineage and CD49a manufacturing boundaries)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O9/O11/O12/O18 identify SC-EC cells, their persistence at eight weeks in non-humanized SCID beige grafts, and an inferred late common-intermediate lineage; O19-O21 distinguish single-pass antigen enrichment, absolute recovered-cell counts, and the two-pass method statement explicitly unused in presented results. The Blueprint explicitly targets SC-EC exclusion and yield measurement (lines 61,245,247), but this does not establish incorporation of these specific persistence/lineage and sorting recovery details. Incorporation remains unknown; no toxicity, lineage-restricted switch escape rate or immune-protection inference is made.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 maturation and GSIS benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O4/O5/O8 qualify in-vitro stage-6 maturity: glucose responsiveness persisted for about five weeks and SI was described as in the human-islet range, yet secretion magnitude was lower and UCN3/MAFA/SIX3 expression remained absent. The Blueprint already requires MAFA-positive cells, biphasic GSIS and rapid shut-off (line 61), but incorporation of this source-specific marker/absolute-secretion limitation is not established by the broad Stage-6/7 label; incorporation remains unknown. These findings do not show that the later Stage-7 protocol fails or meets Gate1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (general TXNIP glucotoxic-stress node)
edges.claim_summary: The molecular OGT/OGA perturbation and TxNIP-NLRP3/cleaved-IL1beta findings support the general rationale for investigating TXNIP as a glucotoxic-stress node. That general rationale is already explicit in frozen Blueprint section 6 X5 (TXNIP+/+ versus TXNIP-/-) and rank_islet1_stacks.py X5; this study does not itself test TXNIP knockout, survival rescue or the engineered SC-islet product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (specific O-GlcNAc/TXNIP mechanism and human-islet transfer limits)
edges.claim_summary: Human primary-islet Results report 4-fold TxNIP induction, 1.6-fold cleaved IL1beta induction and a further 2.9-fold with PUGNAc; INS1 reporter Results additionally report about 30-fold glucose induction and 50% OGA-associated reduction. These are assay-specific molecular observations, with unresolved time/normalization details and no demonstrated SC-islet protection; WGA recovery alone is not modification-specific evidence (Discussion). The frozen general X5 TXNIP factor does not establish incorporation of these specific findings, so their incorporation is unknown.

edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O4, O7: SC-beta cells assembled with HUVECs on undiluted Matrigel (84±4% vs 6±1% on dilute-Matrigel plastic; p<0.0001) while suspension reaggregation failed to incorporate ECs, suggesting hydrogel-based EC co-assembly as a route to prevascularized SC-islet constructs. Only in vitro assembly of HUVECs with Matrigel (mouse sarcoma-derived) is shown, with no perfusion, oxygenation or graft data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (TNFAIP3/A20 element; Gate2A adaptive alloimmunity readout)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4: A20 overexpression gave permanent allograft survival in about 45% of recipients and above 80% with subtherapeutic rapamycin, survival was Treg-dependent and antigen specific, and the I325N loss-of-function variant caused acute rejection, supporting A20 as a Blueprint protective element. The abstract names neither recipient species nor control arms, so A20 alone did not protect every graft and the transfer to hPSC-derived grafts is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (regulated SC-islet function; SLC30A8 allelic-series test rationale)
edges.claim_summary: Human genetic/physiology findings (O1-O5, O19/O21/O22; T1) and EndoC assays (O10-O13, O23; T5) motivate a bounded SLC30A8 allelic-series function test. That test concept is already explicitly planned in frozen ranker DECISION_EXP_5, including low-glucose shut-off and basal leak; this incorporation label does not mean the individual numerical results or a beneficial edit are adopted. Increased basal secretion (O10), absent significant glucose-only gain (O11), and reduced conductance (O12) prevent claiming an established SC-islet function upgrade. No SC-islet GSIS or immune protection was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hiPSC beta-like-cell formation and expression boundary)
edges.claim_summary: Stage-7 edited hiPSC beta-like cultures show reduced SLC30A8 expression (O6/O7/O20), absent or undetectable ZnT8 protein (O8), and fewer INS/SLC30A8 transcript-positive cells (O9). This qualifies pre-differentiation loss-of-function testing; it does not resolve formation versus expression or establish a manufacturing yield magnitude. The frozen Blueprint requires lineage maturity/yield and the ranker notes dense-core concerns, but adoption of this exact hiPSC developmental finding is not established by those broader boundaries.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER-stress cytoprotection perturbation: SLC30A8 knockdown)
edges.claim_summary: SLC30A8 knockdown improved an ER-stress MTT viability proxy in EndoC-βH1 (O14, p = 0.032; T5), supporting a bounded cytoprotection hypothesis. Exact stress exposure, survival mechanism, mature SC-islet protection and in-vivo benefit are unresolved. The frozen Blueprint Gate4 establishes ER-stress resilience as a goal, but the supplied references do not establish adoption of this specific SLC30A8 MTT result. M1 applies to the actual cytoprotection perturbation; M2 would require a differentiation/maturation endpoint.

edges.claim_summary: TSQ zinc-dye live-cell sorting labeled >80% of insulin+ cells in a reporter line (O1) and is proposed as an antibody-free enrichment and monitoring option beside CD49a enrichment; the packet gives no purity, GSIS or function data for TSQ-sorted cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5; M3 (SOX2-targeted iC9/AP1903 residual-hPSC depletion and NSG assay)
edges.claim_summary: In H1 hESCs, SOX2-linked iC9 after Puro excision gave an AP1903 IC50 of 0.1242 ± 0.0083 nM (O1), apoptotic killing (O4/O19) and selective depletion from in-vitro mixtures and S7 spike-ins (O5/O17). NSG pretreatment yielded teratomas lacking detectable GFP+ cells, not absence of teratomas (O6). Blueprint §4.4/§7 already specifies a pan-lineage biallelic AAVS1-EEF1A1 iCasp9 architecture and clonogenic qualification; incorporation of this specific SOX2/H1 potency dataset is not established. These assays do not qualify Blueprint escape thresholds or established-graft ablation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5; Gate1 / M2 (locus/cassette dependence and pancreatic differentiation boundary)
edges.claim_summary: Puro retention coincided with absent AP1903 killing (O2/O3); SOX2 reactivated during pancreatic differentiation (O14), and SOX2+ non-beta S7 cells retained iC9 protein yet persisted after drug (O15). BCL-2 increased at S7 but its causal role was not tested (O16); NPCs were sensitive (O9), whereas beta-like-cell markers were not significantly changed and spiked undifferentiated cells were depleted (O12/O13/O17). This source qualifies selective pre-transplant purging, without testing pan-lineage safe-harbor function. Frozen Blueprint and ranker already address silencing/apoptosis-resistance risks; incorporation of these specific SOX2/Puro/BCL-2 observations is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (bounded paired-nickase genomic observations; GRAVEYARD_006 scope)
edges.claim_summary: Targeted sequencing reported no nucleotide changes at the top five predicted sites per sgRNA and a chromosome 8 candidate; normal edited-cell karyotypes were also reported (O7/O20), with supplementary data and assay sensitivity unavailable. These single-locus H1 findings do not quantify genome-wide off-target rates or test multiplex base/prime editing. Frozen Blueprint §5 GRAVEYARD_006 and the actual graveyard warn about multiplex editing, while §8 requires deeper genomic QC; this paper does not overturn those precautions. Incorporation of this precise negative dataset is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (conformal hydrogel coating geometry and confined graft sites)
edges.claim_summary: A PEG conformal coat of 25.45 ± 11.43 μm (O5) had text-described comparable OCR/viability (O6/O10), with external-layer death (O7) and reduced absolute insulin output (O9/O27); central necrosis is reported in larger ALG/PEGALG microcapsules (O11), without a measured CC protection effect size or isolated oxygen mechanism. Blueprint §4.5 explicitly accounts for diffusion geometry, and frozen ranker NICHE_UNEDITED_MACRODEVICE_ENCAPSULATION describes >150–200 μm barriers, but this thin-coat experiment does not validate a 72-hour PDMS-CaO2 oxygen bridge or establish adoption of its numerical findings.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet reaggregation purity, batch heterogeneity and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: Reaggregation increased NKX6.1+C-peptide+ fractions (O2/O3) while live-cell yield fell to 21–42% (O1). Static SI text mean 3.6 (O4) conflicts with six listed batch values (O21); Table 1 also includes CHGA 84.5% despite >90% Results generalization (O20). This bounds manufacturing/assay interpretation, not qualification of Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS, 60:30:10 architecture or <3-min shutoff; frozen ranker co-primary dynamic SI >=3.0 is a different assay domain.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (dose-dependent time to function in immunodeficient fat-pad grafts)
edges.claim_summary: At 2.5k IEQ naked SC islets reversed diabetes later than HI (MRT 58 versus 1 day, p = 0.007; O13). CC comparisons do not establish superiority (O14/O25), and caption CC MRT duplicates remain unresolved. Long-term glucose values (O16/O26) describe selected responders and lack assay-specific n; NOD-scid fat-pad graft function, macrophage density/fibrosis-marker nonsignificance (O17/O28), and IPGTT (O30/O31) do not demonstrate human immune protection or exact-product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (transient SA-FasL adjunct and systemic-conditioning context)
edges.claim_summary: At the level of adjunct choice and conditioning caveat, the frozen Blueprint §4.2 already evaluates SA-FasL microgels and explicitly retains short-course systemic rapamycin context; this is not a new adjunct proposal. The present mouse direct-islet-surface study supports the rationale through local OT-I suppression, alloreactive T-cell death and 100-day allograft survival with 15 daily rapamycin doses (O1-O4), but does not validate human SC-islets, SA-THBD combinations, microgel delivery, zero-systemic-conditioning efficacy, or the exact product. Fig. 1 OVA assays inform a model-antigen pathway rather than recurrent T1D memory.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 / M3 (spatiotemporal and antigen-dependent limits of localized graft protection)
edges.claim_summary: Mouse protection was donor-specific and initially extended to simultaneous distant donor islets, but maintenance retained systemic donor reactivity and failed to protect a later distal graft despite rapamycin (O5,O9-O10,O17). Anti-CD25 treatment, delayed same-site retransplantation, and rejection of donor-matched skin/heart challenge conditional durability (O11-O16,O21); antigen clearance itself was not measured and the authors qualify the tissue-specific interpretation in Discussion. The exact boundaries are not established as incorporated by the reviewed Blueprint §4.2/ranker decision-experiment context; incorporation remains unknown. The GRAVEYARD_010 indirect-pathway warning and human exact-product assays are not cleared.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M3 (phagocyte-dependent tolerogenic induction, not blanket macrophage suppression)
edges.claim_summary: Clodronate-sensitive phagocytes and peri-transplant TGF-β were required in this mouse SA-FasL system (O6,O8), and a separate OT-II/apoptotic-body assay showed macrophage uptake with cytoplasmic TGF-β staining (O7). Day-3 immunoregulatory transcripts rose (O19), while IL-10 induction blockade and TGF-β maintenance blockade did not impair reported survival (O20,O18). This is a bounded warning that phagocyte clearance can support tolerance; the study did not test CD47/SIRPα blockade, innate-cloak combinations, quantitative TGF-β secretion, or human APC protection. Exact incorporation of this mechanism into the frozen Blueprint/ranker/graveyard is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation; dynamic perifusion GSIS benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Inducible LIN28B knockout from day 3 gave about 2-fold greater static GSIS stimulation index, higher markers and depletion of a juvenile gene set in hESC-derived eBCs (O10, O12, O13, O15), while let-7 induction alone did not improve GSIS (O16, O18). The cheatsheet does not state LIN28B depletion as a maturation lever, so it is a candidate Gate1 maturation upgrade, limited to in vitro hESC eBCs, with an unspecified early-start cost on INS-GFP+ yield (O9) and higher low-glucose secretion (O14).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (maturation gap between in vitro SC-islet cells and adult or in vivo matured beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: hESC beta-like cells had lower let-7 and higher LIN28B than in vivo matured beta cells and human islets, with eBCs intermediate (O1-O6), consistent with the Blueprint's premise that Stage-6/7 maturation of SC-islets is incomplete. The cheatsheet cannot settle whether this specific let-7/LIN28B marker axis is already tracked.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1; Gate1 / M2 (cytokine/ER-stress resilience and endocrine phenotype)
edges.claim_summary: In unedited stage-7 human iPSC-derived aggregates, IFNγ + IL-1β increased apoptosis around twofold, reduced endocrine-phenotype transcripts and induced ER-stress markers (O2, O6, O12, O15); ruxolitinib pre-incubation nearly prevented apoptosis in the reported supplementary Results (O16). Frozen Blueprint §1.2 already recognizes these failure-mode classes, but incorporation of these particular magnitudes, maturation boundaries and drug observations is not established. The study does not test the Blueprint’s edited product or prove A20/MANF/BCL2/XIAP efficacy.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (classical HLA surface-expression boundary and cytokine-induced PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: O7/O10/O11 show cytokine-associated HLA-ABC mRNA/surface increases in unedited human iPSC-derived endocrine cells; ICC response to IFNα occurred in three of six experiments (O20), distinct from flow cytometry. PD-L1 and total STAT1 expression increased (O14), but antigen presentation, T-cell killing, B2M editing, PD-L1 function and graft protection were not tested. This supplies expression-context evidence for Blueprint §4.1/§4.3, not validation of the immune cloak.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS; SI >= 2.0-3.0 benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Healthy-donor human islets in the perifusion system had SI after high glucose of 3.5 ± 1.3 and after KCl of 5.1 ± 0.9, versus 2.3 ± 1.1 and 3.4 ± 2.1 in T2DM islets (O5, O6), and a 5-8 mM glucose threshold (O9). This is consistent with the dynamic perifusion SI benchmark the cheatsheet states for Gate1; it is primary-islet reference data, not SC-islet data, from only three healthy donors.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biphasic GSIS as a maturation readout for islet-like structures)
edges.claim_summary: Day-7 HLSC-ILS (liver stem-cell derived, not hPSC derived) were glucose-responsive with a robust first phase (SI~5) but a lower response amplitude than healthy islets, an earlier 4 mM threshold and an oscillatory second phase (O7, O10, O14, O15), showing dynamic perifusion exposes immaturity features that single-timepoint SI would not. The finding is from a different islet-like cell type and transfers to hPSC-derived SC-islets only as an assay-design precedent.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (virus-induced class I expression context for B2M/CIITA cloaking)
edges.claim_summary: In unedited HUES8-derived SC-beta cells, CVB4 increased HLA-A/HLA-B/B2M/TAP1 proteins and MHC-I transcript pathways (O4, O12); O19 quantifies the HLA-B component at 48 h and is nested evidence, not an independent effect. O10 is a Discussion-reported lack of class II increase in this immune-cell-free setting. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §4.1–4.2 already specify B2M/CIITA ablation, but incorporation of this particular viral-challenge phenotype is unknown; the study tests neither edits nor antigen presentation, allorecognition, or immune protection, and does not show CIITA is dispensable.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic antiviral stress and secretion-versus-content failure boundary)
edges.claim_summary: CVB4 challenge of unedited human SC-beta cells reduced INS transcript and basal-normalized stimulated secretion, increased the annexin V+/7-AAD+ population, and produced a nonsignificant total insulin-content comparison (O8, O13–O18); it does not establish equivalence of insulin content or quantify how much dysfunction is independent of cell death. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and ranker Gate4 entries address inflammatory/ER stress and protective modules, but this experiment does not test those modules, prove type I IFN causes the injury, or qualify viral resistance of the exact product. Claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS and in vivo function of SC-β cells)
edges.claim_summary: Planar-protocol hPSC-derived SC-β cells showed second-phase-capable dynamic GSIS in the 1013–4FA line approaching human islets (O11) and reversed STZ diabetes in immunodeficient mice within about two weeks with glucose below 200 mg/dL to week 36 (O13, O15); consistent with the Gate1 dynamic GSIS benchmark, but in NSG mice with no immune challenge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation: transient actin depolymerization at endocrine induction as a manufacturing lever)
edges.claim_summary: A 24-hour latrunculin A pulse at the start of stage 5 rescued SC-β specification and GSIS in plated cultures (O5, O6, O8) while reducing off-target lineage markers (O7); proposes testing a stage-5 cytoskeletal-depolymerization step and a planar format as differentiation/manufacturing upgrades. The cheatsheet does not state this element; supporting numbers are mostly figure-only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 maturation: MAFA and UCN3 gap)
edges.claim_summary: Despite functional GSIS, planar SC-β cells still had low MAFA and UCN3 expression relative to human islets (O10), and stage-4 latrunculin A or nocodazole drove premature endocrine or exocrine-like fates without NKX6–1 (O1, O2); qualifies how far this protocol closes the maturation gap and stage-timing dependence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 axis, Locus 3: allo-T-cell suppression)
edges.claim_summary: Recombinant mouse PD-L1 displayed on mouse islets inhibited alloreactive 4C T-cell proliferation in vitro (O2, p < 0.001) and promoted Treg conversion (O1, p = 0.004), consistent with the cheatsheet's rationale for PD-L1 in Gate2A. Domain limits: mouse protein and mouse cells, exogenous protein display rather than genetic inducible expression in hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 as local immunomodulator at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: SA-PDL1 display alone prolonged allograft survival only from MST 14 to 28 days with all grafts eventually rejected (O6); sustained survival in > 90% of grafts at 100 days needed a 15-day rapamycin course (O7), and long-term recipients showed no systemic tolerance (O10, O11). Qualifies reliance on PD-L1 alone as a Gate2A mechanism; mouse allogeneic model with a transient protein coat, so transfer to genetically expressed PD-L1 in SC-islets is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biphasic SC-β GSIS as an endocrine-function requirement)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O5 support assaying first- and second-phase GSIS in human SC-β preparations, a requirement explicitly present in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 (line 61). This incorporation claim concerns the existing assay requirement, not adoption of the WS4-specific 8.9±2.1x effect or qualification of the OpenIslet product. O6-O10 are non-humanized NSG functional bioassays and establish no immune protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (WFS1-dependent ER stress and mitochondrial/insulin-processing failure boundaries)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O17 and O19-O25 bound WFS1-associated SC-β ER/mitochondrial stress and processing defects, with thapsigargin also reversing corrected-cell function. Transfer from this predominantly WS4 disease model to healthy-donor engineered stacks is a bridge; MANF/TXNIP expression is observational here and does not test their therapeutic manipulation. Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 (line 64) and ranker Gate4 priors (lines 212-222) address intrinsic stress, but do not by themselves establish incorporation of these specific WFS1 effects; no new weight or protective target is adopted.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (genotype-local differentiation/purity and associated overgrowth observations)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O14 and O18 compare differentiation fractions in WS4 corrected versus unedited preparations; O13 reports overgrowths without endpoint denominators. These qualify transfer of yield/purity expectations across disease genotypes, not healthy-donor yields or a quantified clonogenic-safety risk. The main mechanistic/transplant study focuses on one WS4 donor; there is no packet basis for the original single-patient-family claim. Blueprint Gate1 and §7 require lineage/purity measurements, but incorporation of these specific WFS1 boundaries is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation: beta versus delta cell allocation at the endocrine progenitor stage)
edges.claim_summary: Loss of RA signaling in NEUROG3+ endocrine progenitors impaired mouse beta cell differentiation with ectopic delta cell genes including somatostatin (O1, O2), and RA pathway inhibition in hESC-derived progenitors impaired insulin expression (O3). Hypothesis only: maintain or tune RA (and Wnt) signaling around the NEUROG3 stage to protect the beta cell fraction and limit delta cell drift; the delta cell phenotype is mouse-only and the packet is abstract-only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: TYK2 inhibitors prevented IFNα-induced CXCL10 mRNA in EndoC-βH1 cells (O2) and CXCL10 secretion by human islets (O8), and reversed established CXCL10 expression (O4). This qualifies the CXCL10-inducible Locus 3 design: concurrent TYK2/JAK inhibitor therapy could blunt the IFN arm of its induction. Only the endogenous gene was measured, not an engineered promoter, and no SC-islets were used.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (functional readout and mechanistic interpretation boundary for SLC30A8 perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2 report no apparent 10-week genotype difference in glucose tolerance or 15-min circulating insulin, while O13/O18 report lower 4-min circulating insulin in KO mice. O20 shows why this does not isolate secretion kinetics: insulin clearance was only inferred and processing is another possible explanation. The frozen Blueprint §1.2 already requires dynamic first/second phases and low-glucose shut-off, and ranker Decision Experiment 5 includes an SLC30A8 allelic series, but neither establishes incorporation of this precise age/time/clearance boundary; hence incorporation remains unknown. This supports a bounded readout caution, not human SC-islet efficacy, a shut-off defect, or a new numerical gate. M7 denotes mechanistic failure modes; M2 SC-islet differentiation/maturation was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: No direct Islet-1 gate endpoint (systemic ZnT8 EHR and hematologic context)
edges.claim_summary: O8-O11/O19 are observational human rs13266634 associations, not ZnT8 inhibition or SC-islet graft interventions; O16/O17 are murine systemic blood counts. They retain human provenance and extra-pancreatic drug-target context but do not demonstrate graft endocrine performance, intrinsic stress protection, or immune evasion. The apparent T1D association elsewhere in Results is attributed by the authors to diagnosis-code ambiguity. No inference of T1D protection or qualification of an SLC30A8-edited graft follows. Ranker autoantigen-stack and Graveyard 007 restrictions concern broader perturbations and are not overturned by these associations.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine composition, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference and off-target endocrine cells)
edges.claim_summary: MAFB loss left PP-stage efficiency and total CHGA+ cells unchanged (O3, O11) but cut INS-GFP+ and C-PEP+ NKX6.1+ cells (O1, O2), raised SST+ and PPY+ cells and lowered GCG+ cells (O12-O14, O18), and the MAFB−/− grafts gave no glucose-responsive human C-peptide (O5). This shows that late-stage specification of β:α:δ composition depends on a specific transcription factor in hPSC-derived islet cells, a failure mode the cheatsheet does not state.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (MAFB-MAFA axis and β-cell maturation readouts)
edges.claim_summary: Doxycycline-driven re-expression of one MAFB allele at the PP stage partly restored INS-GFP+ cells and raised MAFA expression in MAFB−/− cells (O15, O16), suggesting MAFB as a candidate upstream checkpoint or QC readout for MAFA-linked maturation in Stage-6/7 SC-islets. This is an inference from an engineered knockout-rescue system, not a tested manufacturing intervention.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (β-cell glucose-sensing set-point and fasting-hypoglycemia risk)
edges.claim_summary: In G6pc2 KO mice, which lack glucose cycling (O10), blood glucose fell to hypoglycemic levels on a ketogenic diet and after a 24-hr fast (O1, O2) while fasting insulin and the glucose-stimulated insulin rise did not differ (O4, O8, O12). This suggests testing the glucose set-point of SC-islet grafts under fasting or low-carbohydrate challenge, not only insulin output; it is a mouse germline-KO result and not tested in human SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 (candidate additional protective edit: RNLS deletion)
edges.claim_summary: RNLS loss let NIT-1 and primary NOD.scid islet cells survive splenocyte-driven autoimmune killing (O2-O4) and made NIT-1 cells resistant to thapsigargin and IL-1β plus IFN-γ (O8, O9), and RNLS-knockout hiPSC gave normal SC-beta cells (O12, O13) that resisted thapsigargin (O14). This suggests testing RNLS deletion as an extra autoimmunity and stress-resilience edit, but autoimmune protection was shown only with mouse cells in mouse hosts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER-stress and cytokine resilience, TXNIP)
edges.claim_summary: Cytoprotection against ER stress and inflammatory cytokines (O8, O9) was accompanied by reduced Txnip and Chop mRNA after thapsigargin (O10) and reproduced in human SC-beta cells for thapsigargin (O14), consistent with the Gate4 premise that intrinsic stress resilience, including TXNIP, protects beta cells. The Txnip change is a correlative readout downstream of RNLS loss, not a TXNIP manipulation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A vs Gate2B (positioning of an autoimmunity-protective edit)
edges.claim_summary: Rnls deficiency left MHC class I and II unchanged (O5), weakened the autoreactive CD8+ T-cell response (O6) but did not prevent allo-rejection of grafts in C57BL/6 mice (O7), and pargyline likewise did not (O18). An RNLS-type edit would therefore address Gate2B and Gate4 but would not substitute for Gate2A HLA ablation; this rests on small mouse allograft groups (n=3).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hPSC-to-endocrine differentiation yield: insulin+ cell formation, MAFB/PAX4)
edges.claim_summary: Deleting the lncRNA LINC00261 in H1 hESCs cut insulin+ cells by 30-50% (O6) with lower insulin content and INS mRNA (O7, O8) and MAFB/PAX4 downregulation (O11, O12), independent of its sORFs (O14, O16). Hypothesis: LINC00261 RNA expression is a candidate dependency or QC readout for endocrine-stage yield in H1-derived lines; evidence is one hESC line in early monolayer endocrine cultures, not mature SC-islets or grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine-stage differentiation robustness to non-coding locus deletions)
edges.claim_summary: Nine of ten lncRNA deletions left endocrine cell development intact (O1-O3), with no loss of definitive endoderm formation (O4) and no change in neighboring lineage TFs (O5, O10), expanding the evidence base on which non-coding loci can be deleted without impairing insulin+ cell formation in H1 hESC monolayer differentiation (LINC00261 being the exception).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (PD-L1 immune cloak, Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: Lentiviral PD-L1 overexpression in hiPSC-derived islet-like organoids sustained glucose control for >50 days in immune-competent mice (O6) and over a human T cell repertoire in Hu-PBMC-NSG-SGM3 mice (O9), with fewer graft CD45+ cells (O7) and more retained insulin+ cells (O8, O11). Constitutive overexpression, organoids rather than SC-islets, and 27-50 day follow-up limit the bridge to the Blueprint's inducible Locus 3 PD-L1.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (pre-transplant cytokine conditioning and cytoprotection; endogenous PD-L1)
edges.claim_summary: Ex vivo multiple pulse IFNgamma priming gave sustained endogenous PD-L1 (O13, O18) without compromising GSIS (O14), protected against IL-1beta dedifferentiation (O15) and extended glucose control to >40 days (O16) with fewer activated CD4+CD3+ graft T cells in humanized mice (O17). Hypothesis: a pre-transplant IFNgamma pulse conditioning step could complement the Blueprint's inducible PD-L1; shown only in HILOs with short follow-up.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation benchmarks; in vivo graft maturation, MAFA/G6PC2)
edges.claim_summary: Stage 6 SC-beta cells under-express maturation genes (only 2.09% and 1.20% express MAFA; O9) and acquire them after 6 months in kidney-capsule grafts in STZ-diabetic NSG mice (O1, O7, O8, O12, O13), with residual differences from native beta cells (O14, O15). Qualifies Gate1 maturation benchmarks: transcriptional maturity here emerged in a vascularized 6-month graft, not from the in vitro product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (elimination of off-target SC-EC cells; CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment)
edges.claim_summary: SC-EC cells arise in the six-stage protocol, are absent from cadaveric islets, and persist with further EC-gene changes 6 months after transplantation (O18), supporting the need to remove them before grafting. The study did not test CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference composition)
edges.claim_summary: In this protocol SC-alpha cells averaged 51.8% of cells at stage 6 and 11.1% in grafts (O17), so stage 6 composition sits far from the 60:30:10 reference and shifts in vivo; graft cell composition cannot be inferred from the in vitro product. Beta cell proportions are not given in the packet text.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 (a) vascularization / M3 (prevascularized graft as adjunct to the 72-hour oxygen bridge)
edges.claim_summary: Fusing microvascular fragments into mouse islet organoids improved take rate, functional capillary density and day-3 microvessel blood flow, and 250 PI + MVF restored normoglycemia where 250 FI did not (O6, O11-O14). This suggests prevascularized SC-islet organoids as an untested adjunct to the oxygen bridge; no pO2, hPSC-islet, human in vivo or allogeneic-immune data were collected.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (HMOX1 antioxidant cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: Co-aggregated MVF increased the vital-cell fraction (92 ± 4% vs 79 ± 1% CI and 72 ± 4% PI), lowered reaggregation-induced mitochondrial ROS and raised HO-1 expression in mouse islet organoids (O1-O3), with no caspase-3 difference in grafts (O18). The data are associative (HO-1 not perturbed) in mouse islets under culture and reaggregation stress, not peri-transplant hypoxia.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (preservation of glucose-responsive insulin secretion)
edges.claim_summary: Adding MVF to primary islet cells left the mouse stimulatory index and human C-peptide secretion unchanged (O5, O10), although DNA-normalized glucose-stimulated insulin secretion was lower than PI (O4) and in vivo plasma insulin at 180 min was unchanged (O16). Static assays in primary islets only; no SC-islets, dynamic perifusion or stimulatory index values in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation: monohormonal endocrine fate and glucose-responsive C-peptide release)
edges.claim_summary: Moving the final differentiation stage from 2D to 3D suspension clusters gave monohormonal endocrine cells, a higher INS-positive fraction and a 2-fold high-glucose C-peptide induction (PECs-2D showed no sensitive response) in hESC-derived cells (O3-O8). It is a static 2 mM to 20 mM assay in an early-stage protocol, not dynamic perifusion, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether 3D clustering is already part of the Blueprint.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 at Locus 3 as T-cell evasion element)
edges.claim_summary: PDL1 overexpression in INS:CD19 beta-like cells gave only partial protection against CD19 CAR-T cells in NSG mice (n = 4), with less CD8 infiltration and reduced IL-2 in coculture (O11-O13). This supports including PD-L1 but indicates it is not sufficient alone; the model uses constitutive AAVS1 PDL1, a synthetic CD19 antigen and CAR-driven rather than TCR-driven killing, so transfer to the inducible Locus 3 design is a bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytokine and ER-stress death pathways: GSDMD-CASP4 pyroptosis)
edges.claim_summary: Reactive T-cell conditioned medium upregulated GSDMD, tunicamycin raised cleaved GSDMD, and a caspase-4 inhibitor reduced GSDMD cleavage more than a caspase-1 inhibitor in human beta-like cells (O14-O16). This suggests testing CASP4 or GSDMD inhibition or knockout as an addition to Gate4 cytoprotection; cell survival was not measured and the exposure was in vitro.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet identity, purity and off-target cell content; scRNA-seq as M6 readout)
edges.claim_summary: By single-cell RNA-seq, the iPSC-derived endocrine cells had high homology with mature islets and the abstract reports no residual pluripotent, ectodermal or mesodermal cells (O2-O4), while pseudotime shows a non-endocrine branch (O5), in line with the Gate1 need for purification. Abstract-only evidence: no cell numbers, detection limits or functional data are available, and the cheatsheet cannot settle whether this specific non-pancreatic endoderm content is already addressed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1/NKX6.1 progenitor-stage readouts of SC-islet differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: Deletion of LAMA1 or CRB2 (or their progenitor-specific enhancers) in hESCs left PDX1+/NKX6.1+ percentages at PP2 similar to control (O7, O8, O10, O11), whereas lama1 and crb2a/b knockdown reduced beta-cell number in zebrafish (O14, O15, O16, O18). This qualifies how far PP2 PDX1/NKX6.1 readouts can stand in for later beta-cell yield, but the zebrafish-to-human step is unvalidated and the cheatsheet states no progenitor-stage QC criterion.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell differentiation yield; candidate ECM/cell-polarity levers LAMA1 and CRB2)
edges.claim_summary: Reduced beta-cell numbers after lama1 and crb2a/b knockdown (O14, O15, O16) and the enhancer-dependent PP2 expression of LAMA1 and CRB2 (O5, O9) suggest ECM and cell-polarity gene dosage as untested modulators of beta-cell yield in the Gate1 differentiation protocol. This is a zebrafish morpholino result with no human beta-cell yield measurement, so it is a hypothesis only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP and inflammatory-cytokine stress resilience of beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: In streptozotocin-diabetic rats, oral verapamil was accompanied by inhibition of the TLR4/TXNIP/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, lower vitreous TNF-α and IL-1β, and preserved pancreatic islet diameter (O2, O3, O4, O6), consistent in direction with the Gate4 inclusion of TXNIP among cytoprotection targets. The evidence is qualitative, drug-based (verapamil is not TXNIP-specific), measured in rat islet morphology rather than hPSC-derived beta cells, so the transfer is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (MANF cytoprotection element)
edges.claim_summary: In SKMEL28, MC-38 and HepG2 tumor lines, IFN-γ raised extracellular MANF (O1, O6, O7) without a detectable rise in MANF mRNA or intracellular protein (O2, O3, O8, O9), the secretion was dantrolene-sensitive and accompanied by diminished thapsigargin-releasable ER calcium (O13, O14), and IL1B alone did not induce it (O10). If this holds in SC-beta cells it would mean the MANF element of Gate4 should be judged by secreted MANF and ER-calcium state, not transcript level; the study never tested beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3 (functional maturation of SC-beta cells; GSIS stimulation-index benchmark SI >= 2.0-3.0)
edges.claim_summary: In this hPSC protocol, beta-like cells reached only <2-fold insulin secretion in vitro (O5), while WT cells matured for 23 weeks under the mouse kidney capsule secreted insulin with a fold change of at least 2 and C-peptide of at least 1.5 (O6, O7), consistent with the Gate1 requirement for a GSIS stimulation-index benchmark and in vivo maturation. The cheatsheet states the SI target but not this protocol-specific in vitro failure and 23-week maturation time; static fold change here is not a perifusion SI.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (diagnostics for non-responsive SC-beta cells: glucose uptake, ATP, GLUT2, HNF1A targets)
edges.claim_summary: HNF1A+/H126D beta-like cells matched WT in progenitor and beta-cell formation (O1, O2, O3, O4) and in Ca2+/KATP channel secretagogue responses (O9, O10, O11) yet failed GSIS in vivo (O8) with lower glucose uptake, ATP:ADP ratio and GLUT2 (O12, O13, O14, O15), suggesting glucose-uptake and ATP readouts as extra diagnostics when SC-beta cells differentiate normally but do not respond to glucose. This comes from a monogenic-disease line, not a standard manufacturing failure, hence a bridge and a hypothesis only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO, Locus 1/2: classical HLA-I ablation)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O13 and O18: B2M-KO sBC lacked surface HLA class I and gave no stimulation of a PPI 15-24/HLA-A*02:01-restricted CD8 TCR reporter even with exogenous peptide. The effector is a murine-IL-2 TCR transductant (no killing, no NK testing), hence a bridge from the SC-islet side only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 at Locus 3; endogenous PD-L1 non-induction in sBC)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O6: sBC did not upregulate PD-L1 after 6-day chronic cytokines whereas human islets did, while O12 and O17 show DOX-induced PD-L1 raised surface PD-L1 and reduced PPI-specific T-cell stimulation. Effector T cells express mouse PD-1 and the Tet-On at AAVS1 is not CXCL10-inducible, so transfer to the Locus 3 design is a bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet manufacturing compatibility of edits)
edges.claim_summary: O10, O11: the AAVS1 Tet-On PD-L1 knock-in plus B2M KO line (iP-BKO) differentiated to INS-GFP+ sBC without statistical differences versus iP at any stage, with about 40% GFP+ cells at the end. No GSIS or functional maturity was measured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1; definitive endoderm to pancreatic progenitor transition)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O5 and O6 state that a PDX1 5'-UTR variant is necessary and sufficient for a DE-stage differentiation block with decreased early-PP PDX1 expression in patient iPSCs, supporting PDX1 as a hard requirement of the early pancreatic differentiation path. Single patient-derived line, abstract only, so a bridge to healthy-donor SC-islet manufacturing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (leucine and mTOR sensitivity at DE to PP; donor-line genotype screening)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 report leucine hypersensitivity and defective leucine-sensitive mTOR signalling at the DE to PP transition in a variant line (O5). Hypothesis for the protocol: test leucine and mTOR sensitivity at DE to PP and screen donor lines for PDX1 5'-UTR variants. Not tested in healthy SC-islet lines here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (long-term SC-β-cell graft retrieval yield under the kidney capsule)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3: about 5 million transplanted SC-β-cells yielded 1-2 million retrievable human cells per graft after 5-12 months, with a graft about 0.5 cm across. This is a recovery count after dissociation and sorting, not a survival fraction, and the host is immune-compromised.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine-progenitor regulatory network: NEUROG3 targets NEUROD1, NKX2-2, PAX4, NKX6-1)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O5, O10 and O14 map NEUROG3 occupancy (863 sites, 1263 genes) in hiPSC-derived endocrine progenitors, recovering known targets and binding near NKX6-1, supporting NEUROG3 as a direct regulator of the endocrine program used in SC-islet differentiation. Binding is not functional proof, with one sample per antibody and one line.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (maturation: early NEUROG3 binding of insulin-secretion genes GCK, ABCC8/KCNJ11)
edges.claim_summary: O16 and O17: NEUROG3 binds secretory-machinery genes (GCK, ABCC8, KCNJ11) but no hormone genes at the PEP stage, so PEP-stage NEUROG3 timing might influence later GSIS competence (Gate1 dynamic-perifusion benchmark). Hypothesis only; no GSIS or perturbation of NEUROG3 timing was tested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (classical HLA class I and CIITA ablation; HLA-E surface dependence on HLA signal peptides)
edges.claim_summary: O6, O7, O15, O16: deleting HLA-A/B/C (except HLA-A2) plus CIITA lowered rejection by T cells in PBMC-reconstituted mice (O15), while HLA-ABCnull cells lost HLA-E surface expression until an HLA-A2 leader peptide was supplied (O6, O7). The model used HLA-A2+ donor PBMC and had no NK cells at 4 weeks (O16), and the strategy retains HLA-A2 rather than a B2M KO, hence a bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (edit compatibility with β-like cell differentiation and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4: HLA-ABCnull and HLA-A2R (CIITA-edited) lines gave similar β-like cell composition and a similar glucose-stimulated secretion increase as WT, so these HLA edits did not impair function in one parental hESC line. No values in the text.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation; 3D culture, beta-cell identity and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: 3D orbital-shaking culture raised the mCherry+/INS+ fraction (O11, O12), glucose-recognition gene expression (O13) and insulin content (O14), and the hESC clone showed a static GSIS increase (O15, O16, O17). In vitro, static assay only, no stimulation index.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic GSIS benchmark; cell-line dependence of maturation)
edges.claim_summary: Glucose responsiveness was achieved only in the hESC SC30 clone (O16) and not in the iPSC NSC20 clone in 2D or 3D (O18), and 2D cultures showed KCl- but not glucose-triggered release (O4). The Gate1 functional benchmark should be read as cell-line specific, and these assays are static, not perifusion SI.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification of the differentiation product)
edges.claim_summary: MACS enrichment of SOX9+ progenitors at d12 via a knock-in H-2Kk reporter raised insulin and C-peptide content ~4-fold (O3) but did not restore glucose-triggered release (O4), so progenitor-stage purification alone does not deliver Gate1 function; it is a different handle from the Blueprint's CD49a enrichment.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (in vivo graft monitoring; peri-transplant graft persistence readout)

The iron signal rose from day 1 to 7 and is not validated as viable beta-cell mass, with no glycemic data in non-diabetic NOD/scid recipients.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-G1 ILT2/ILT4 inhibitory-ligand axis as an add-on or alternative to HLA-E/NKG2A + CD47; Gate2A T-cell readouts)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-G1 on porcine cells lowered IFN-γ in human macrophages (O10; p=0.0045) and, without stated p, in NK and T cells (O11, O12), and reduced human and monkey T-cell proliferation (O13, O14, O16, O17). This proposes HLA-G1 as an extra Gate3/Gate2A inhibitory ligand, but data are porcine cells in bulk PBMC co-culture, several effects sit near p=0.05 (O3, O4), and a GTKO background effect is present.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (islet function compatible with an immunomodulatory transgene at a ROSA26 safe-harbor-type locus)
edges.claim_summary: Islets from GTKO/HLA-G1+ pigs reversed diabetes in athymic STZ-diabetic mice as did GTKO islets (O8), so ROSA26-driven HLA-G1 did not obviously impair islet function; the beta-cell fractions of the preparations differed (O9). Porcine islets in nude mice without an immune challenge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo functional benchmark: glycemia, IVGTT, stimulated C-peptide)
edges.claim_summary: After intrapleural allogeneic islets the NHP showed non-fasting BG of 56-200 mg/dL, 1-3 units of insulin per day (O1, O2), IVGTT disposal mimicking a healthy NHP and C-peptide comparable to the naive state (O3, O5). One animal, primary islets rather than SC-islets, no insulin independence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; benchmark immunosuppression context)
edges.claim_summary: Graft survival to day 92 with no CD3 infiltration (O12) occurred under rATG, anti-CD20 and rapamycin that depleted circulating T and B cells (O15). This single animal cannot inform graft-intrinsic evasion and shows that this NHP benchmark depended on systemic lymphodepleting immunosuppression.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune T-cell pressure; Treg count vs effector balance as a tolerance readout)
edges.claim_summary: TLR3+/- NOD mice had more PLN Foxp3+ Tregs (O10) but also more IFN-γ+ CD4+ T cells (O11) and were not protected from CB4-induced T1D (O2), while reduced MDA5 gave protection (O3). Treg numbers alone therefore did not predict protection in this endogenous-islet model, a caution for Gate2B tolerance readouts; no graft was studied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (local type I interferon tone as a graft-site stress perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: Reduced MDA5 versus TLR3 sensing gave distinct IFN-α and IFN-β signatures (O4, O8, O9, O14) and virus tropism changed the PLN T-cell response (O15, O17, O18). This proposes testing local type I interferon challenge as a Gate2B perturbation, but the evidence is indirect, in NOD host islets and not in grafts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M4 (adaptive alloimmunity; immunosuppression as clinical comparator)
edges.claim_summary: The cohort used a systemic immunosuppressive regimen with non-immunoprotective devices, and O5 shows immunosuppression-related shifts in circulating T-cell subsets. The abstract reports no rejection or graft-loss endpoint, so it cannot show allorecognition evasion by edited cells and only scopes the benchmark to an immunosuppressed setting.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP as a cytoprotection target)
edges.claim_summary: For the broad TXNIP glucotoxic/redox-stress target rationale, O3-O5 and O15-O16 provide rodent/cell-line corroboration, while frozen Blueprint section 6 explicitly includes X5 TXNIP+/+ versus TXNIP-/- and ranker X5 names the oxidative-stress shield. This is not a TXNIP knockout or rescue/epistasis study and does not establish direct miR binding, TXNIP mediation, human SC-islet benefit, or an adopted miR-17-5p intervention.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (stress-resilience readouts beyond TXNIP: NLRP3 inflammasome and GSDMD pyroptosis)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O10 and O16-O18 associate miR-17-5p perturbation with reduced NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD readouts and flow-defined pyroptotic cells, alongside rodent functional improvement (O2, O11-O12, O14). A bounded hypothesis is to evaluate beta-cell pyroptosis readouts during glucotoxic stress in human SC-islets; there is no TXNIP/NLRP3 rescue or epistasis establishing necessary mediation or GSDMD dependence. Frozen ranker already includes macrophage NLRP3 IL-1beta in the IAPP challenge, so blanket NLRP3 absence is false; incorporation of this distinct beta-cell/miR-17-5p mechanism is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 / G6PC2 (GRAVEYARD_003 glucose-set-point precaution)
edges.claim_summary: Human BioVU association with lower random glucose plus G6PC2 expression/activity impairment in rat 832/13 cells gives a mechanistic bridge to the Gate1 precaution for G6PC2 disruption. This mechanistic precaution is explicitly incorporated in frozen ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md §5 (line 189), graveyard GRAVEYARD_003 (PMID:34954144, precautionary_mechanistic_hazard), and ranker GY003 WARN logic; already_accounted_for applies only at that level, not to adoption of every table coefficient. This study measures neither fasting/exercise hypoglycemia nor low-glucose insulin shut-off in edited human SC-islets, and does not test immune protection, G6PC2 promoter safety switches or product qualification. The study’s random-glucose endpoint qualifies the references’ broader fasting-glucose phrasing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M4 (clinical maturation and stimulated C-peptide benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 and O19 provide a human clinical benchmark that hESC-derived pancreatic progenitors can engraft, mature and yield low measurable meal-responsive C-peptide under systemic immunosuppression in an open subcutaneous device. Responder strata are outcome-defined, and the Results >0.1 ng/mL criterion coexists with displayed 0.1 values. This class-level benchmark does not validate the Blueprint edited 60:30:10 product, its dynamic GSIS/shut-off requirements, or immunosuppression-free protection (frozen Blueprint section 1.2). Specific incorporation of these data is not established by the inspected reference context.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (C-peptide detection versus clinical glycemic benefit)
edges.claim_summary: O17 preserves the report of no statistically significant glycemic pre/post differences despite C-peptide detection in 6/17; Table S1 and exact test estimates are absent, so this is not equivalence. O16 reports average graft-cell fractions of 40% versus 26% within fibroblast-dominated explants. These observations qualify using detectable C-peptide alone as evidence of clinically useful function; they do not transfer exact efficacy or cell-fraction bounds to the Blueprint product. The frozen ranker separates clinical modalities at lines 2981-3002, but specific incorporation of this PEC-Direct finding remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 / M5 (late device vascularization and observed off-target growth safety)
edges.claim_summary: O13 reports a 10-fold CD34 density association between cellular and non-cellular lumen regions at late explant, and O11 qualitatively reports no observed teratomas/metastatic growth with unresolved ascertainment n/window. This open immunosuppressed subcutaneous device measures neither the Blueprint section 1.2 72-hour oxygen bridge nor the pan-lineage iCasp9 clonogenic escape requirement; no oxygen tension, acute inosculation kinetics or triggered switch test is supplied. GRAVEYARD_002 is a lineage/switch qualification boundary, not validated by absence of observed tumors here; specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (candidate intrinsic cytoprotection node: PTPN2, not in the cheatsheet's Gate4 element list)
edges.claim_summary: O5 reports partial protection from ER stress-induced beta-cell death by PTPN2 overexpression, and O3 and O4 place PTPN2 in interferon and Ca2+-dependent unfolded-protein-response control in human stem cell-derived beta-like cells. Hypothesis only: test PTPN2 as an added Gate4 cytoprotection element in hPSC-derived islets; the abstract gives no magnitudes and does not name the cell type used for overexpression.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (HNF1B dosage as a candidate PP-stage lever; hypothesis only)
edges.claim_summary: HNF1β-mCherry overexpression partially rescued PDX1+ progenitors and INS+ cells in a single MODY3 line (O17, O18), while HNF1αMUT overexpression reduced HNF1β targets in WT organoids (O16). This only suggests testing HNF1B level as a lever in the HNF1A-truncated background; it is untested in wild-type SC-islet protocols.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference and SC-EC elimination)
edges.claim_summary: After the extended S7 stage this hESC protocol gave ≈40% INS+, ≈40–50% GCG+ and ≈4% SST+ cells (O1, O3, O4) and SC-EC cells fell from ≈13% to ≈6.5% rather than to zero, with the fall dependent on ZM (O6, O7). So extended S7 maturation alone did not reach the 60:30:10 reference or eliminate SC-EC in this protocol; this qualifies what the Gate1 composition baseline needs beyond S7 maturation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic perifusion GSIS maturation in vitro)
edges.claim_summary: Biphasic GSIS appeared from S7w2, the glucose threshold reached ≈5 mM by S7w3, polyhormonal INS+GCG+ cells fell to <5%, and removing ZM or NAC attenuated GSIS (O2, O8, O9, O10). This supports in vitro functional maturation as a Gate1 endpoint, but metabolic coupling stayed immature (no glucose-induced respiration; pyruvate responsiveness; O11, O12) and no stimulation index is reported in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo graft function in immunodeficient host) and M6 (scRNA maturation trajectory)

The host is an immunodeficient NSG mouse with no alloimmune or device context, so it bridges to Islet-1 graft expectations only for maturation, not for immune evasion or oxygenation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide and time-in-range clinical benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: In the ViaCyte trial (NCT03163511) patients on immunosuppression showed increased fasting, glucose-responsive and mixed meal-stimulated C-peptide, reduced insulin requirements, more time in target range and mature beta-cell phenotype in explants (O4, O5, O6). The abstract gives no values, n or follow-up, so it supports the clinical benchmark categories only qualitatively.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M3 (SC-islet maturation and graft-site/dose function)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O13 and O19-O22 establish source-bounded site/dose dependence of HUES8 stage-6 SC-islet function in male immunodeficient NSG mice. In O7, the IM stimulation-index mean exceeds KC despite lower absolute secretion and failure to reverse diabetes; an index alone does not qualify graft function. Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 explicitly requires mature cells and dynamic first/second phases with rapid shutoff, and §4.5 specifies a different full-product microenvironment: these mouse static/in vivo assays do not qualify that contract or a clinical dose. KC is explicitly nontranslatable in the paper; SQ/IM used Matrigel and KC delivery differed. Claim-specific incorporation of these site/dose results is not established, rather than inferred from keyword absence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (host hyperglycemia and intrinsic-stress transfer boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O17 report similar or nonsignificant C-Peptide, proinsulin/insulin ratio and MAFA findings in STZ versus no-STZ KC hosts. This is a bounded host-state observation, not equivalence or cytoprotection. The STZ grafts reached euglycemia by week 6, so later maturation is not evidence of continued chronic hyperglycemic stress; MAFA n = 8/4 counts SC-islets in one graft per condition. Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 concerns inflammatory/hypoxic intrinsic injury, and §4.3 a specified SERPINB9/PD-L1 perturbation. Neither that perturbation nor cytokine, hypoxia or immune challenge was tested. Incorporation of the specific host-state observation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (descriptive absence of observed graft overgrowth/tumor)
edges.claim_summary: O18 preserves only the Discussion statement that overgrowth/tumor formation was not observed, without a safety-specific denominator, ascertainment protocol or duration. Blueprint §4.4/§7, ranker effective_denominator_definition and GRAVEYARD_002 require pan-lineage residual-clonogenic/switch evidence; this study has no iCasp9, escape assay, residual-PSC quantification or genomic-safety measurement. It cannot qualify the fail-safe or establish a zero tumor rate. Incorporation of this specific descriptive observation is unknown; source-checked readiness does not establish product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-5/6 endocrine progenitor to beta-cell induction and maturation)
edges.claim_summary: WNT5A (about five-fold INS+ cells at 500 ng/ml, O10) and WNT5A + Gremlin1 (16-fold, O16; GCG+ cells down 1.5-fold, O18) could be proposed as EP-stage additions to improve beta-cell yield, with effect seen across three other protocols (1.5-2.2-fold, O12). Limits: in vitro only, 12-day WNT5A gave no extra INS+ cells (O13), and factor treatment stayed below M-E20 coculture (O17).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference)
edges.claim_summary: Endocan raised SST+ cells more than four-fold in hESC-derived EPs without a stated change in GCG+ cells (O11), so it could be proposed as a lever for the delta-cell fraction, while WNT5A/Grem1 lowered GCG+ cells (O18). In vitro, small N = 3 for Endocan, and no composition ratio is reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS-competent beta-cell manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: Stage-matched fetal pancreatic M-E coculture increased INS+ cells (30% vs 3%, O3), gave a static GSIS stimulation index of 23.4 not significantly different from cadaveric islets at 29.2 (O4, O5), and acted at EP stage (O6, O7). Static 2.8 vs 16.7 mM assay in a non-scalable coculture, so not directly comparable to perifusion benchmarks.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (local, non-genetic T-effector control for adaptive alloimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: Co-delivered SA-FasL microgels gave graft survival of >180 days mean versus 27.7 days for control microgels under transient rapamycin (O2), with more graft-site FoxP3+ cells (O9), minimal infiltration (O10) and no change in systemic frequencies, donor antibodies or donor MLR (O11, O12, O15, O16), which could be proposed as an add-on to genetic allo-evasion. Limits: unmodified NHP islets, n = 4 vs 3, rapamycin cover, mostly haploidentical pairs, no autoimmunity, no insulin independence (O4).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks in a large-animal model)
edges.claim_summary: Control NHPs given unmodified allogeneic islets with rapamycin monotherapy rejected at around day 30 (O2, O8) with increased anti-MHC class II antibodies (P = 0.0326, O13) and CD8+ donor MLR response (P = 0.0057, O14), giving an NHP rejection phenotype that an allo-T-cell suppression benchmark can reference. Small n = 3 control group.
