edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP axis in hypoxic beta-cell stress resilience)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4 report that reducing the NLRP3-TXNIP interaction in hypoxic mouse beta-cells triggers nuclear shuttling of MafA and PDX1 and insulin gene expression, consistent with TXNIP being a Gate4 stress-resilience target. Mouse islet data only; the cheatsheet lists TXNIP but not the NLRP3 interaction, so incorporation cannot be settled.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 / M3 (pre-transplant NLRP3 inhibition as a hypoxia-resilience and revascularization element)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O5 show improved revascularization and normoglycemia restoration with Nlrp3-/- or CY-09-exposed mouse islets, suggesting transient NLRP3 inhibition of islet cells before transplant as a candidate Gate4 conditioning element. NLRP3 inhibition is not among the Gate4 elements in the cheatsheet; evidence is mouse-only and abstract-level with no values.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (biphasic GSIS and exocytosis machinery; candidate CD59-IRIS readout)
edges.claim_summary: O5, O6 and O4 show lower IRIS-1/IRIS-2 protein in T2D donor islets and lower IRIS-1 after glucotoxicity, and O10 assigns IRIS-1 to first-phase and IRIS-2 to later-phase release in rat INS-1 CD59-KO cells, suggesting IRIS expression as a candidate exocytosis-competence readout for Gate1 SC-islet maturation. Phase assignment comes from a rat cell line and human data are expression-only; no SC-islet data and CD59 is not named in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (insulated cassette at AAVS1: promoter silencing through differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: O16 reports no significant difference in iRFP720 mRNA through 13 days of pancreatic progenitor differentiation for a cHS4-insulated CAG cassette at AAVS1 (n = 3), with slightly lower fluorescence (O17). This supports an insulated AAVS1 cassette staying expressed to the progenitor stage in human iPSCs; the cargo is a reporter (not iCasp9), the promoter is CAG (not EEF1A1), and no endocrine or SC-islet stage was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety and clone QC of AAVS1 knock-in, Locus 4 step)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O4 report very low HDR knock-in yield (0.001% puromycin-surviving, 0.0002% precise, three correctly integrated clones) and O7 an extra integration elsewhere in clone A5-04, while O8 found no cleavage at four predicted off-target sites. This qualifies any assumption of a clean single-copy AAVS1 knock-in: clone-level junction PCR, Southern and off-target screening are needed; single line, reporter cargo rather than an iCasp9 cassette.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9 zygosity at Locus 4 AAVS1)
edges.claim_summary: O5 and O6 find monoallelic iCASP9 escapees at 3.6 × 10^-8 and 2.5 × 10^-8, while O7 and O8 find none among 5.2 × 10^8 and 3.14 × 10^8 CID-treated biallelic cells; O9 shows transgene loss, probably LoH, as one monoallelic route. This suggests specifying biallelic iCasp9 knock-in at AAVS1 for the clonogenic fail-safe; zygosity is not stated in the cheatsheet, and the bridge is from undifferentiated hiPSCs, a CAG promoter and a dTomato co-cassette.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 / M7 (promoter silencing of the iCasp9 cassette; CAG vs EEF1A1/insulated design)
edges.claim_summary: O11, O12 and O13 show CAG promoter methylation (2/2 analyzed hCBiPS2 resistant subclones) that tracks loss of reporter expression and CID resistance and was reversible, so promoter silencing is a real escape route for an AAVS1 iCasp9 cassette. This supports listing promoter silencing as a Gate5 failure mode; the cassette was not insulated and EEF1A1 was not tested, so the data do not show the Blueprint design avoids it.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (in vivo clearance versus the <1e-6 escape threshold)
edges.claim_summary: O3 shows 2/5 NOD/SCID mice with monoallelic iCASP9 teratomas kept human tumor-like tissue after AP1903, although in vitro escape frequencies were far below 1e-6 (O5, O6); the authors suggest CID-resistant clones. This qualifies reading a sub-1e-6 in vitro frequency as proof of complete in vivo clearance for a monoallelic switch; the mice carried a large teratoma burden from 10^6 undifferentiated hiPSCs, not an SC-islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet beta-cell specification and maturation)
edges.claim_summary: In H1 hESC-derived pancreatic endocrine cells, TET loss cut PDX1/NKX6.1 co-expression (O1) and PAX4 induction (O3), and TET1 loss alone reduced INS+/C-peptide+ cells (O9) and graft C-peptide in SCID-beige mice (O11, O12); full-length TET1 restored beta-cell determinants (O15). The cheatsheet states no TET or epigenetic-regulator dependency, so incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 + M3 (candidate TET1-PAX4-enhancer demethylation readout for SC-islet manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: PAX4 enhancer 5mC rose to 35-50% in TET1KO and 60-65% in TKO (O17) alongside loss of graft function (O11, O12), and TET1 interacted with FOXA2 (O18); this proposes PAX4 enhancer hypomethylation as a testable in-process marker of beta-lineage competence and flags TET1 as a locus to avoid disrupting in edited lines. Untested in Stage-6/7 SC-islets; evidence is from PE-stage cells and bulk assays.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP lowering as intrinsic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0206:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=unvalidated_transfer | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O2,O4,O5 | text_sha256=1d3308b7bfa2b54e50749e74fb6ce642c2e5088b096251fda819f46311cd914f]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (upstream ChREBP handle on TXNIP transcription)
edges.claim_summary: Celastrol lowered Txnip transcription by promoting ChREBP degradation (O6), which proposes ChREBP as an alternative upstream control point for TXNIP-based beta-cell cytoprotection and could also reduce IL-1β from islet macrophages (O3). Untested in human cells or SC-islets and stated only qualitatively in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (granzyme B effector pressure; SERPINB9 + PD-L1 at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0207:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O13,O16,O9 | text_sha256=7751dc5ec0b690b8ffd9c7be8fa2ffe31b72743d875896b63ba26a0df2580e1b]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks)
edges.claim_summary: Treg upregulation at the graft site (O6, O10) did not secure allograft survival (O16) and a higher IL-2D dose shortened graft function (O14, O15), so Treg counts alone are a weak pass criterion for allo-T-cell suppression benchmarks. Mouse data with local protein delivery and no systemic immunosuppression; the cheatsheet does not specify benchmark content, and the Teff results (O7, O8) are contradictory between text and caption.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation, CD49a/ITGA1, dynamic and static GSIS stimulation index)
edges.claim_summary: In hESC-derived SC-β cells, ZnT8 LOF cells were overrepresented along the maturation trajectory with ITGA1 (CD49a) enriched (O1, O2), had higher static and perifusion stimulation indices (O4, O6) and better in vivo GSIS (O9). The cheatsheet states CD49a enrichment and a GSIS SI benchmark but not the ZnT8 edit or these values, so incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 + M3 (candidate SLC30A8 LOF cytoprotection edit for the stress-resilience stack)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT8 LOF SC-β cells resisted PA, SA, LA and glucose toxicity (O10-O13), showed lower ER stress gene expression (O14) and restored normoglycemia in 11 of 15 versus 6 of 14 diabetic mice at 90 days (O17), proposing SLC30A8 LOF as an added Gate4 element. Shown only in SCID-Beige mice without immune challenge, and the cheatsheet does not list this edit; its interaction with the multiplex editing stack is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1+NKX6.1+ progenitor competence upstream of beta-cell formation and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: ALKBH5 loss in hPSCs left DE and PF formation intact (O3, O4) but reduced PDX1+NKX6.1+ PPs (O5), C-peptide+ mono-hormonal beta-like cells (O10) and hILO GSIS (O12), with rescue only by catalytically active ALKBH5 (O13, O14). This supports a PP-stage regulatory dependence upstream of Gate1 readouts; in vitro hILOs only and the cheatsheet does not mention m6A regulation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dm-αKG and ALKBH5-YTHDF2 mRNA-stability axis as a PP-stage differentiation lever)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0209:L2 | relation=novel_upgrade_hypothesis | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=not_yet_accounted_for | outcomes=O15,O16,O17,O18 | text_sha256=038965060a926b092ca84eed3fa828f923bba1dacb28bcb4375ea0a912417f46]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: In this mouse allograft model, PD-L1 alone and IDO alone failed to reverse STZ diabetes (O3) and PD-L1 plus IDO co-expression gave only transient recovery (O4), whereas the PD-L1-IDO fusion reversed it (O5, O6), dependent on host CD4 (O12). This qualifies any assumption that PD-L1 expression alone is sufficient for Gate2A protection, but it used constitutive lentiviral expression in mouse islets, not inducible PD-L1 in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (Locus 3 PD-L1 module, autoimmune setting)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis: testing a PD-L1 module with IDO tethered to its cytoplasmic tail (PIDO-like) in SC-islets, motivated by NOD relapse 20% vs 100% (O9), CD8 suppression and a Treg-rich plug milieu (O14, O16) and the local, non-tolerizing action (O11). Mouse islets with lentiviral constitutive expression only; the human SC-islet transfer is untested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (macrophage phagocytosis arm)
edges.claim_summary: PIDO-engineered islets recruited fewer F4/80+ and CD11b+ macrophages into Matrigel plugs (O15), a local innate-cell effect relevant to the Gate3 macrophage scope. No CD47 or SIRPalpha arm was tested and the readout is cell counts in a mouse plug, so it supports only the idea that engineered local immune modulation can lower phagocyte infiltration.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (dynamic GSIS release criteria for SC-islet maturation)
edges.claim_summary: Bounded diagnostic hypothesis: compare depolarizing-secretagogue (tolbutamide or KCl) responses and Fura-2 calcium with existing dynamic GSIS to localize secretory defects. HNF1A KO cells had impaired GSIS (O2) and lower calcium (O4), with secretion described as comparable to WT under tolbutamide/KCl (O3); CACNA1A and SYT13 KOs partly reproduced the phenotypes (O5–O7). The frozen Blueprint already requires dynamic insulin function (§1.2, §6); adoption of this specific calcium/secretagogue diagnostic combination is not established. Genetic disease models do not validate a product-release assay, and comparable secretion is not demonstrated equivalence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (stimulated C-peptide as functional benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: In the HNF1A-null NSG graft model, substantial C-peptide (O11) coexisted with virtually undetectable human insulin (O12), an author-reported 18-fold lower insulin:C-peptide ratio (O13; Results/caption time-window discrepancy retained), and >90% enlarged granules (O15). This qualifies interpretation of C-peptide as a proxy for insulin delivery in this disease context. The Blueprint already requires dynamic insulin GSIS and paired insulin/C-peptide output (§1.2, §6); this does not show that its actual multi-readout gate fails, establish the clearance mechanism, or establish incorporation of this specific HNF1A boundary.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic and oncology safety of hPSC-derived grafts)
edges.claim_summary: Observed hPSC-derived cluster teratomas support the general need for residual-clonogenic/outgrowth control, explicitly already addressed in Blueprint §1.2 Gate5 and §7 and GRAVEYARD_002. O9 reports 92.5% (49/53) hESC-recipient teratoma freedom; O10 reports 87.9% (51/58) freedom for the pooled R200Q/corrected group versus 61.5% (8/13) formation for the pooled 460ins/control group, with different endpoint directions preserved. These pooled, line-associated rates are not genotype-specific causal estimates or Blueprint product-risk estimates. No suicide switch was tested; the study does not qualify iCasp9 kill depth, and its NSG hosts lack human immune reconstitution. Incorporation refers to the general safety need, not adoption of these specific rates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (donor/line-dependent robustness of SC-islet differentiation protocol)
edges.claim_summary: A published protocol and a commercial kit generated no NKX6.1/PDX1-positive cells in the lines tested, with only one later protocol working (O1), and multihormonal cells (O5) and a patient-line organoid defect (O6) appeared despite similar progenitor and hormone percentages (O3, O4). This qualifies any assumption that a Gate1 differentiation protocol transfers across iPSC lines; it is a single patient line, no GSIS, and a different protocol from the Blueprint stages.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (ER stress and UPR resilience of beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: In MIN6 insulinoma cells the mutant INS isoform inhibited growth (O14, O15) and activated UPR reporters, with the GRP78/BiP promoter almost three times higher than wild type (O16, O17), supporting ER stress as a failure axis within Gate4 scope. No protective intervention (such as MANF) was tested and the data come from a mouse cell line overexpressing human cDNA, not hPSC-islets under transplant stress.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytokine-resilience edit candidates beyond A20 and XIAP: RIPK3 necroptosis axis)
edges.claim_summary: RIPK3 loss or inhibition protected NIT-1, INS-1 and primary mouse islet cells from TNFα+zVAD death (O7, O8, O14, O15) and Ripk3-/- mice had lower glucose after low-dose STZ (O17, O18). Hypothesis: test RIPK3 (or RIPK3-MLKL) knockout or inhibition as a Gate4 cytoprotection perturbation in SC-islets under TNFα; evidence is from rodent cells, an artificial pan-caspase block and a whole-body knockout, not human SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (IAP/XIAP-mediated protection against TNFα death)
edges.claim_summary: The IAP antagonist BV6 amplified TNFα-induced death in NIT-1 cells and mouse islet cells and strongly amplified TNFα+zVAD death (O3, O6, O12), supporting a protective role of IAPs against TNFα, which fits the XIAP element listed in Gate4. BV6 is described as a cIAP/SMAC-mimetic antagonist and XIAP was not tested, and primary islet cells resisted TNFα alone (O11).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A + Gate3 / M1 (CXCL10 depletion; component-level bridge to the Locus 3 swap)
edges.claim_summary: The pooled-screen CXCL10 signal (O4/O5), lentiviral depletion result (O8), C10G immune-cell co-cultures (O13/O19), and PBMC-humanized graft observations (O15–O18) support CXCL10 depletion as an allogeneic immune-evasion component; NK protection was tested in vitro, not in the long-term mouse immune compartment. Results describes HDR CXCL10-GFP null mutations, but the frozen evidence does not establish the asserted biallelic P2A-GFP sequence. Anti-CXCR3/anti-CXCL10 controls and the TLR4-blockade result (O11/O21/O22) bound mechanism: recruitment abolition is not measured. Frozen Blueprint §4.3 specifies the target cassette, and ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9 explicitly incorporates CXCL10 deletion. Transfer to the exact SERPINB9-GSG-P2A-PD-L1 cassette is a component bridge, not construct validation; no current autoimmune or host-APC indirect-presentation efficacy is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M depletion and classical HLA-I allorecognition)
edges.claim_summary: B2M, HLA-A and TAP1/2 gRNAs were enriched in the pooled hPi screen (O4), and B2M depletion was reported to improve SC-β viability by more than 2-fold under allogeneic PBMC attack (O9). This supports the classical HLA-I component rationale explicitly represented by B2M-disrupting Locus 1 in frozen Blueprint §4.1. It does not validate the combined HLA-E/CD47 cassette, indirect host-APC protection or in vivo NK resistance; the long-term PBMC-humanized model is T-cell dominated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A + Gate3 / M1 (STAT1-loss trade-off; Gate4 inducible-shield transfer qualification)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0214:L3 | relation=scoping_qualification | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=already_accounted_for | outcomes=O12,O14,O20 | text_sha256=cf895b601b3d853cca0450c47b9860b94d88a4065dcb3d981799474c5b1f3708]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0215:L1 | relation=scoping_qualification | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O12,O13,O14 | text_sha256=56ec41764d84cd16bd3a9c54b26f2f38294e5a688bc430f527aa6528d50d079a]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PPI-directed CD8+ T-cell activation); Gate2A / M1 (classical HLA class I / B2M bridge)
edges.claim_summary: NLRC5 knockdown decreased HLA class I/antigen-processing expression and partially reduced PPI-specific CD8+ T-cell CD107a activation in H1-derived islet-like-cell coculture (O3-O7, O16). The direct functional endpoint is autoimmune antigen-specific degranulation (Gate2B), not allorecognition or target-cell killing; the Gate2A/B2M-KO connection is a mechanistic bridge from partial siRNA effects. Host-APC indirect presentation was not tested, and claim-specific incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate2B / M1 (CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1, Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: NLRC5 knockdown reduced endogenous IFNα-induced CXCL10 mRNA/secretion (O8-O9, O29), reduced endogenous PDL1 mRNA at 24 h (O11, O15), and had no reported PDL1 effect at 8 h (O10); siNL#1 and siNL#2 also differ in EndoC viability (O19, O22). These are perturbation-specific constraints rather than evidence that the engineered Locus 3 promoter or shield fails. Blueprint §4.3, §5/GY-001 and the ranker already distinguish IFN-pathway/promoter interactions, but incorporation of these NLRC5-specific results is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E protection and NKG2C+ NK escape boundary)
edges.claim_summary: O7, O8 and O19 support the receptor/effector-subset boundary, not pan-NK protection. The boundary is explicitly represented in frozen Blueprint Gate3 and the ranker residual-risk/Decision Experiment #1 entries. Paper Methods[10] uses a peptide-B2M-HLA-E*01:03 single-chain construct with HLA-G-derived VMAPRTLFL and R107G; Blueprint Locus1 uses VMAPRTLVL with different cassette/CD47 architecture. Exact peptide, construct, numeric lysis and product efficacy are not thereby incorporated or qualified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (B7-H3/CD276 and CD155/PVR loss on a B2M-null background; proposed transfer to Blueprint cloak)
edges.claim_summary: Ligand knockouts reduced NK lysis in one edited iPSC clone and its pancreatic derivatives (O11, O13–O16), with acute PP-graft signal/retention evidence (O17/O18, cohort caveat retained). These knockouts were tested as alternatives on B2M-null cells without HLA-E, not as a combined add-on to the Blueprint HLA-E/CD47 cloak. Combined-stack interactions, long-term function, unrelated immune protection and exact Blueprint adoption remain unestablished; absence is not inferred from keyword search.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M disruption and direct allogeneic CD8 recognition)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O4 support the bounded direct-CD8 recognition mechanism that frozen Blueprint §4.1 already assigns to B2M disruption. O5 finds no detected change after ligand KO (p > 0.99), not equivalence. Fig3 assays used three independent experiments with different donors and MOLT-4 priming; donor identity/HLA metadata are unavailable. This iPSC in-vitro evidence does not establish the full edited SC-islet product or Gate2B autoimmunity/indirect-APC protection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage-6/7 SC-islet maturation; SC-EC elimination)
edges.claim_summary: Loss or early inhibition of TYK2 lowered endocrine precursor markers and β-like output (O1, O2, O3, O8, O10: 31.1% vs 15% β-like cells; O4: about 32% fewer INS+ cells) while mature-cell secretion was unchanged (O6), so any TYK2/JAK perturbation must be timed after S5; the incidental SC-EC reduction (O5) is a side observation, not a validated purification route.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO; IFN-induced HLA class I and class II)
edges.claim_summary: In SC-islets IFNα raised surface MHC class I (O14: 83.1% in WT vs 0.69% in TYK2 KO) and class II genes DQB1/DRB1 (O15), and IFNα pretreatment increased peptide-specific CD8+ lysis (O16), which TYK2 inhibition reduced only partially (O17); this supports the rationale for removing class I and II but tests TYK2 blockade, not B2M/CIITA KO, with a flu-peptide CD8 line rather than allogeneic or autoreactive T cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: IFNα-induced endogenous HLA-E transcript rose in WT but not TYK2 KO SC-islets (O13) and IFNα-induced PD-L1 was partly lost with TYK2i (O18), so endogenous protective-molecule induction depends on type I IFN signalling through TYK2; this is a transcript-level observation with no NK assay and does not test the constitutive Locus 1 HLA-E trimer.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell memory; ZnT8 as a T1D autoantigen)
edges.claim_summary: In a global Slc30a8-null NOD background, complete loss accelerated spontaneous T1D (O1/O2; Fig. 1 caption-versus-Results p discrepancies retained) and was associated with more early insulitis than heterozygosity (O6). This qualifies the idea that removing a T1D autoantigen necessarily protects beta cells; it does not isolate a beta-cell-autonomous mechanism, demonstrate indirect-APC suppression, or test a human SC-islet edit. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 recognizes ZnT8 autoimmunity and ranker AUTO_NONE avoids SLC30A8-null dense-core concerns, but incorporation of this specific NOD boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection under inflammatory cytokines; metabolic and mitochondrial conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: Partial ZnT8 loss is a candidate metabolic-resilience hypothesis: cytokine-treated NOD.SCID HE islets increased content-normalized high-glucose secretion (O7) and respiration (O13–O15), while the female maximal-capacity result and ATP comparisons were nonsignificant (O21–O25). Basal secretion rose (O8), proton leak rose independent of treatment (O16/O17), and secreted proinsulin:insulin increased across genotypes (O20); these do not establish improved survival or safe endocrine function. The frozen ranker already proposes SLC30A8 allelic-series shut-off/OCR testing, but adoption of this specific effect and mechanism is unknown; no human or SC-islet validation is supplied.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet cluster manufacturing and function)
edges.claim_summary: The abstract reports that collagen-functionalized wet electrospun scaffolds gave smaller ILCs (70 ± 20 μm vs 300 ± 10 μm, O1) with enhanced insulin secretion and viability (O3, O4), loosely consistent with manufacturing-level control of cluster size; the cells are adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell derivatives of unstated species, with no GSIS index, values or p-values, so the link is weak.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive PPI-specific CD8 T cell recognition of HLA class I on SC-beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: In an in vitro co-culture, PTPN2 KO sBC stimulated HLA-A*02:01-restricted autoreactive preproinsulin TCR transductants more than WT sBC (O17, O18), alongside higher HLA class I (O12, O13), consistent with HLA class I on sBC being the substrate for autoreactive CD8 recognition. The bridge is a risk-gene KO with mouse T cell transductants in vitro, not a graft setting.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablation of classical HLA-A/B/C, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: HLA class I surface expression on sBC was higher in PTPN2 KO than WT at steady state and after IFN-gamma (O12-O15), with the IFNγ response gene set upregulated (O8); this is indirect evidence that HLA class I on sBC is inducible by interferon signalling, the target of B2M KO. No B2M-edited cells were tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation of an edited hPSC line)
edges.claim_summary: An hPSC line carrying a CRISPR-Cas9 PTPN2 deletion differentiated to insulin-GFP+ sBC (on average 14% GFP+) with no significant difference from WT in lineage markers or proinsulin/insulin content (O1-O4). This is a single-gene KO of a T1D risk gene, not an Islet-1 edit, and the authors note the sBC yield was lower than they reported previously.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablation of classical HLA class I, Locus 1/2)
edges.claim_summary: B2M-KO sBC showed essentially no HLA class I in vitro (O4), and in HLA-A2-matched autoimmune NOD mice the BKO groups had more surviving insulin+ cells than the first-experiment HLA-A2+ groups (O17, cross-experiment, no test stated), with BKO + DOX having the most animals with detectable signal late (O9). Domain limits: human cells in immunocompetent mice without a human immune system, 2-week follow-up, signal lost in most mice by day 14 (O10), no NK assay.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3 with SERPINB9, T cell effector pressure)
edges.claim_summary: DOX-inducible PD-L1 alone gave a significant bioluminescence benefit only at day 1 and 3 for HLA-A2+ sBC (O6) and at day 9 for B2M-KO sBC (O7), with no change in CD3+ number (O14), heavy infiltration (O11) and signal lost in most mice by day 14 (O10). This qualifies PD-L1 as a stand-alone Gate2B element; the system was DOX-driven, not the Blueprint's CXCL10-inducible PD-L1 with SERPINB9.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (unpurified SC-islet composition and functional benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: The transplanted sBC clusters were about 40% cPEP+ and about 25% NKX6.1+/cPEP+ (O1, O2) and grafted iP sBC did not reverse hyperglycemia within the 2-week study (O18), so this study provides no Gate1 functional benchmark; it measured immune-mediated survival, not graft function.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune effector pressure on beta cells: IFN-γ+CD4+ T cells, perforin+CD8+ T cells, TNF+ macrophages)
edges.claim_summary: In intact NOD mice, host-side MDA5 perturbations had distinct autoimmune phenotypes: partial-function ΔHel1 delayed spontaneous and CVB3-accelerated T1D (O1, O3, O7), whereas KO did not protect females and accelerated spontaneous male T1D (O2, O4, O6). ΔHel1 had reduced pancreatic inflammatory-cell counts and type-I IFN (O10–O16), lower day-7 pancreatic viral titer (O19, O21), and increased M-MDSC frequency without demonstrated suppressive function (O17); KO had still lower IFNs without equivalent disease benefit (O20, O22, O23). This qualifies infection-state and signaling-depth assumptions for Gate2B/M1; it does not measure indirect APC presentation, establish a viral-challenge requirement, or quantify protection by any human SC-islet graft. Actual frozen Blueprint §1.2, ranker Gate2B branches and GRAVEYARD_010 already recognize autoimmune/host-APC hazards, but adoption of this particular MDA5 boundary remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1,M3 (local pharmacological allograft suppression in a prevascularized device)
edges.claim_summary: Primary rat-islet allografts under local CTLA4Ig + ALS achieved euglycemia in 8/12 rats versus 5/8 under systemic IS (O1); no equivalence test is supplied. Local dosing yielded lower plasma exposure (O9-O10), preserved circulating T-cell levels (O11), and less graft cytotoxic-T-cell infiltration than active rejection (O13), with two failures attributed to release problems (O16). Healthy NHPs provide only 14-day histologic/immune observations (O17-O18). This is a pharmacological benchmark for allograft suppression, with no direct evidence for drug-free hypoimmune SC-islets or autoimmune protection; claim-specific incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3,M7 (prevascularized site and oxygen-bridge evidence boundary)
edges.claim_summary: Islets were loaded after 6 weeks of NICHE site prevascularization; rat endpoint islet vessel area was 12.02 ± 2.06% versus 7.58 ± 1.63% in native pancreas (O8), and the separate NHP device cohort supplied 4/6-week vascularization data (O21-O22). Neither early post-loading islet perfusion nor 0-72-hour oxygen was measured, so prevascularization does not establish absence of an avascular interval or replacement of an oxygen carrier. The frozen Blueprint Gate5 explicitly combines a prevascularized retrievable site with a 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/catalase bridge; these NICHE-specific measurements do not qualify that product or its fail-safe, and their specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (primary rat-islet in vivo graft-function readouts)
edges.claim_summary: In euglycemic rat subsets, grafts supplied HbA1c described as comparable to healthy rats (O5), improved glucose tolerance versus diabetic controls (O6), and higher fasting C-peptide versus diabetic controls (O7); no equivalence is established. These are primary rat-islet graft readouts, not SC-islet manufacturing, biphasic dynamic GSIS/rapid shutoff, human stimulated C-peptide, or clinical CGM evidence. T2 is a study-level designation for the separate NHP experiments and does not upgrade these rat outcomes. Specific Blueprint incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate NK and macrophage evasion by the HLA-null CD47 hypoimmune stack)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0224:L1 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O11,O9 | text_sha256=e82086816b29d26d185c72f502efbfc28dcf47147a7e997ea70c9a594757d527]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (antibody-mediated rejection layer added to the B2M KO + CIITA KO + CD47 hypoimmune stack)
edges.claim_summary: Adding CD64t could protect hypoimmune SC-beta cells from IgG-mediated ADCC and CDC: CD64t beta cells were resistant to anti-HLA-A2 ADCC and CDC (O15), grafts survived antibody challenge in NSG mice with NK cells (O16) and glucose sensing and insulin production were intact (O14); CD64 also protected HIP iECs against anti-MICA (O6) and in humanized mice (O11). Evidence is commercial iPSC-beta cells and non-islet cells, mostly in vitro with supplementary-only beta cell data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (scope of HLA-null hypoimmune protection: antibody-mediated killing)
edges.claim_summary: HLA-null HIP iECs escaped CDC from anti-HLA recipient sera (O4) but remained killed by NK ADCC and CDC with anti-MICA IgG1 (O5), so B2M KO + CIITA KO protects against HLA antibodies only; CD64 itself did not alter primed CD8+ T cell killing (O12) and its antibody protection was saturable at low expression (O13). Endothelial cells in vitro, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO, Locus 1/2 HLA class I ablation; CIITA KO not tested here)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O12, O13: B2M−/− SC-islets (class I ablation without CIITA KO) survived PBMC co-culture better than WT in vitro, but in PBMC-humanized diabetic NSG-MHC-null mice rejection was only delayed (WT destroyed within 2 weeks; some graft function at 7 weeks), qualifying class I ablation alone as insufficient in this CD3-biased PBMC model; O3 reports B2M−/− and BEC jointly.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1; CD47-SIRPalpha)
edges.claim_summary: O4-O6: HLA-E restored survival of HLA-deficient cells against NK-92 MI, which are ∼96.1% NKG2A+/NKG2C−. O7, O8: with IL-2 pre-activated primary NK cells (in vitro) and in Scid/beige mice, no significant survival difference was seen between WT, B2M−/− and BEC lines. O9-O11: SC-β cells lack MIC/ULBP-type activating ligands and anti-SIRPα/anti-TIGIT blockade lowered survival, so HLA-E necessity is qualified in short assays.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (local Treg-recruiting cytokine secretion: IL-2 mutein, TGF-β, IL-10 at GAPDH)

edges.claim_summary: RREB1KO/KO hiPSCs generate NKX6.1+/C-peptide+ BLCs while showing higher NEUROG3 and endocrine-progenitor gene enrichment (O10–O13). edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment of SC-islet beta cells)

Static SI is not the dynamic perifusion SI named in the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (maturation marker panel for SC-islet release criteria: UCN3, MAFA, CHGB, G6PC2, IAPP, ENTPD3)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O9, O13: UCN3 was high in fetal islets and polyhormonal cells and Pro B SC-islets with high UCN3 still had SI 1.2, so UCN3 should not serve as a maturation criterion; SC-islet MAFA mRNA was 100 to 250-fold below primary islets. A fetal-vs-adult marker panel is a hypothesis for Gate1 QC, with human tissue data bridged to SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (alloimmune surveillance of an extrahepatic graft; pharmacologic immunosuppression comparator)
edges.claim_summary: O8-O13: graft survival in animals 1 and 2 occurred under a lymphocyte-depleting regimen (thymoglobulin, anti-CD20, rapamycin) with T cells and B cells depleted and no alloantibodies except one confounded rise, while animal 3 had DSAs about 50 times over naive and failed. This scopes any in vivo benefit to heavy systemic immunosuppression; genetic cloaks (B2M, CIITA) were not tested, and n = 3 NHPs with primary islets limits transfer.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (preclinical insulin independence and C-peptide benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3, O5: two diabetic NHPs given allogeneic islets on a bioengineered omentum had normal fasting BG (30-110 mg/dL), no exogenous insulin after day 28, and insulin and C-peptide comparable with naive levels over 90 days. This is a primary-islet NHP benchmark for M4, not an SC-islet result, with n = 2 responders.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (omental pouch as a revascularizing extrahepatic graft site; Gate5 vascularization context)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O15, O16: grafts on the fibrin-matrix omental pouch showed CD31+ and beta-III-tubulin+ cells at autopsy and a glucose-disposal improvement in animal 2 between 1 and 3 months. Revascularization was assessed only at about day 90; the early avascular oxygen-bridge window named in the cheatsheet was not measured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (macrophage phagocytosis; transient surface-displayed innate modulator as an alternative to the CD47-SIRPalpha axis)
edges.claim_summary: O4, O6: SA-TM on rat splenocytes lowered engulfment by a mouse macrophage line (p = 0.0256) and on MHC-deficient NSG bone marrow lowered innate clearance in allogeneic C57BL/6 recipients (p <0.0001). Thrombomodulin is not among the cheatsheet Gate3 elements, so a protein-display add-on to HLA-E and CD47 is a hypothesis only; data are mouse and rat cells, SA-TM persisted about 6 hrs on cells in vivo (O2), and human SC-islets were not tested.

edges.claim_summary: In this hiPSC protocol, pre-transplanted islets and 1-month grafts were K+-responsive but glucose-unresponsive for [Ca2+]i (O1), and glucose responses appeared only after 2 months in vivo (O2). This qualifies how far in vitro Stage-6/7 maturation alone can be assumed to meet the Gate1 glucose-responsiveness benchmark for this line; [Ca2+]i, not insulin secretion, was measured, and animal number is not stated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (SLC30A8 loss of function as a zinc-depletion cytoprotection candidate)
edges.claim_summary: O15–O17 show a significant TPEN-induced TUNEL increase in WT and no significant within-genotype increase reported in KO or R138X; this does not supply a resolved mutant-versus-WT protective effect test. O14 reports elevated free cytosolic zinc in KO, not an identical mechanism proven for both alleles. This supports testing zinc-depletion-specific resilience as a candidate for Gate4, not demonstrated protection from the Blueprint §1.2 cytokine/hypoxic stressors or in-vivo death. Ranker already recognizes SLC30A8 loss and dense-core defects; adoption of this precise chelation-resilience claim is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 and M3 (SLC30A8-edit differentiation and endocrine-function scope)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O2/O19 and NSG graft serum results O8/O9 did not reveal the reported differentiation/output deficits; O20 adds polyhormonal composition and O21–O23 bound processing/content claims. These are endpoint-specific comparisons, not manufacturing equivalence or full Gate1 qualification. O4/O5 show dense-core disruption and O13 reports an incompletely genotype-assigned rise in low-glucose insulin secretion; biphasic GSIS, rapid shut-off, and the specified tri-hormonal product were not qualified. The ranker AUTO_NONE description already recognizes SLC30A8 dense-core defects, but incorporation of these exact quantitative and functional findings is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (scope of ZnT8 autoantigen-edit hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: The actual Blueprint §1.2 names ZnT8 among autoimmune targets, and ranker AUTO_FULL_KO_G6PC2_SLC30A8_PLUS_BASE_INS_GAD2_IAPP_CXADR already includes SLC30A8 deletion in a broad candidate stack; the target idea is not newly established here. This study reports undetectable ZnT8 staining and retained endocrine outputs, but no immune-reconstituted host, autoreactive T-cell, or host-APC assay. Negative staining does not establish loss of every antigenic peptide; Results also suggest a partially active two-transmembrane-domain protein in R138X cells. No autoimmune protection, removal of all autoantigenicity, or reversal of the broader Graveyard 007/010 constraints is demonstrated; adoption of this precise bounded claim is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (hypothesis: JNK1/BIM suppression as a cytokine-resilience edit for TNF-alpha and IFN exposure)
edges.claim_summary: PTPN2 silencing raised IFN-alpha/TNF-alpha cytotoxicity by 20-50% in human beta cell models including iPSC-derived islet-like cells (O1), and silencing JNK1 or BIM abolished the proapoptotic effect after PTPN2 inhibition (O2, O3), pointing to the JNK1-BIM arm as a candidate Gate4 cytoprotection target. This is shown only in PTPN2-silenced cells, with siRNA for 48 h and IFN-alpha/TNF-alpha rather than the full IL-1beta/IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha/CXCL10 set, and no graft data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (static GSIS evidence versus dynamic endocrine qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O12-O14 concern static one-hour 2/20 mM GSIS: an index >1 and a significant within-condition high-vs-low response only consistently reported for S6D1 do not establish dynamic first/second phases or rapid shut-off. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 (line 61) requires those dynamic functions, and rank_islet1_stacks.py lines 5582-5584 specifies a co-primary SI >=3.0 and shut-off <=3.0 min; these study measurements do not establish Gate1 passage. Study-specific incorporation is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (extrahepatic scaffold graft endocrine function in non-humanized NSG mice)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O18 give bounded preclinical evidence of cell presence at 14 days, lower but unnormalized glucose, and increasing post-glucose human C-peptide through 6 weeks after extrahepatic PLG-scaffold grafting. These outcomes are in non-humanized diabetic NSG mice with endpoint-specific n and unknown cohort overlap. They do not establish immune protection or function of the edited human Blueprint product; transfer to that product/site/device and its Gate1 contract is unvalidated (Blueprint §1.2 lines 59-65). Specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (process-specific recovery versus percentage enrichment)
edges.claim_summary: The higher C-pep/NKX6.1-positive percentage in O1 must be interpreted beside the approximate 50% reaggregation process loss in O19; it does not prove higher absolute beta-cell yield or measured selective off-target removal. This H1 process cannot calibrate the distinct Blueprint §6 step-2 handling/capture-loss assumptions (line 246), and internally inconsistent O20 is not a resolved recovery estimate. Specific incorporation of this process boundary is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M6 (SC-EC lineage interpretation and CDX2 perturbation trade-off)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O7 support computational and immunostaining relatedness of SC-ECs to a transient fetal serotonin-producing pre-beta-cell state; they do not establish lineage fate or dispensability of SC-EC depletion. CDX2 knockout reduces SC-ECs but also reduces beta-cell relative abundance and ENP3 NKX6-1 expression/the NKX6-1+ population (O8–O14, O19, O21). This qualifies the biological interpretation of the actual Blueprint Gate1 SLC18A1+ off-target purity requirement (Blueprint lines 61, 245) without showing that its <1% threshold is unnecessary or unsafe. Whether this specific lineage/trade-off finding has been incorporated is unresolved; the ranker purification workflow and GY-002 are distinct manufacturing/switch precautions, not direct tests of CDX2 or SC-EC fate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 / M6 (SC-beta-cell maturation programs versus primary beta-cells)
edges.claim_summary: O15–O16 show that SC beta-related cells separate from primary beta-cells and have less enrichment of signal-dependent TF motifs/programs, including STAT3, ARNTL, AR and THRA, supporting the Gate1 maturation problem. This is omics/GRN evidence, not a causal rescue of those programs or proof of mature final-product function. The study does include GSIS assays and reports maturation during culture (Methods 28–29; Results 3,13); those observations must not be erased by claiming there was no GSIS readout anywhere in the study. Specific program-level incorporation into the frozen Blueprint is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (DHT as a candidate SC-beta-cell expansion intervention)
edges.claim_summary: O17–O18 support testing daily 10 nM DHT from D14 or D21 for an increased D32 SC-beta-cell percentage and EdU-positive fraction in the H1 differentiation system. These measurements do not establish greater absolute beta-cell yield, DHT-mediated functional maturation/GSIS rescue, long-term proliferation safety, or benefit in the edited Blueprint product. Incorporation of this specific intervention is unknown; this is a bounded manufacturing hypothesis, not adoption or qualification.

edges.claim_summary: O4 reports approximately 180,000-220,000 CD47/cell in edited primary human islets, and O21 reports >600,000/cell in human HIP iPSCs/derived islets. edges.claim_summary: O6-O12 and O17 support the B2M/CIITA-deficient CD47-overexpressing allogeneic rhesus benchmark explicitly included in Blueprint Benchmark 1 (line 120) and ranker lines 185-208/369-374. iPSC survival is up to 16 weeks with perioperative methylprednisolone in Methods[28]; primary-islet BLI persistence is 40 weeks in one recipient and does not establish NHP diabetes correction. O22/O25 are separate human-to-rhesus immune assays using rhesus CD47. O13 concerns teratomas from undifferentiated iPSCs, not demonstrated tumors in islet products; no fail-safe efficacy, recurrent T1D/indirect-APC protection or exact Blueprint construct qualification is established. Detailed secondary-endpoint incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (off-target SC-EC cell elimination; SC-EC and SC-beta lineage continuum)
edges.claim_summary: The cheatsheet lists elimination of off-target SC-EC cells as a Gate1 baseline element; O1 finds SC-EC and SC-beta cells form a continuum of states, O6 finds SC-EC numbers fall only from month 6 in vitro (with SC-alpha loss by month 12), and O9 reports no major composition shift after 6 months in NSG mice. This qualifies how cleanly SC-ECs can be removed as a distinct population; no purification experiment was run here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (chromatin-regulator levers for beta identity: ARID1B knockdown, CTCF)
edges.claim_summary: O14 and O15 show ARID1B shRNA knockdown raised INS, DLK1 and IAPP expression and the C-peptide+ fraction in SC-islets, and O11-O13 show CTCF overexpression shifts cells toward an EC-like fate. Hypothesis: ARID1B knockdown (or restraining CTCF) as a Stage-6/7 maturation or SC-EC-reduction lever; O18 shows no clear gain at 20 mM glucose (P = 0.27), O16 and O17 directions are unstated, and CTCF knockdown failed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 + M3 (SC-beta maturation gap versus primary beta cells; transplantation versus extended in vitro culture)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 show SC-beta cells keep more off-target features and less restricted chromatin than primary beta cells; O8 and O10 show 6 months in NSG mice moved SC-beta cells closer to primary beta cells, whereas O5 and O7 show extended in vitro culture improved insulin secretion only until week 4 and lowered beta-cell TF activity by months 6 and 12. This supports a persisting Gate1 maturation gap, with one sample per time point and no stated GSIS stimulation index.

Renalase is not among the Gate2B elements in the cheatsheet; the finding is a qualitative, abstract-only mouse result and is not shown in hPSC-derived beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (HLA-E-NKG2A axis, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10, O13 and O14 show that primary NKG2A+NKG2C- NK cells and NKL cells respond to HLA-E-VL9 on .221 targets in a pattern that tracks CD94/NKG2A reporter engagement, consistent with the HLA-E-NKG2A inhibitory axis. Targets are the .221 B cell line and BLCLs, not islet cells; the bridge is the shared HLA-E-CD94/NKG2A interaction.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Locus 1 HLA-E trimer: peptide content versus NKG2A engagement strength)
edges.claim_summary: NKG2A engagement is not set by HLA-E surface level alone: only 6 of 16 classical SPs are functional (O1), SP-6B gives high HLA-E but the lowest recognition (O3, O4, O15) and reporter activity did not track HLA-E expression on pulsed targets (O17). This qualifies any assumption that HLA-E abundance predicts NK inhibition; the cheatsheet does not state which VL9 peptide the Locus 1 trimer carries.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NKG2A-negative, NKG2C+ NK subset evaluation)
edges.claim_summary: O11 and O12 show that primary NKG2A-NKG2C+ NK cells from HCMV-seropositive donors respond differentially to the SP set and mirror JurkatNKG2C reporter activity, so NKG2C+ subset behavior depends on the HLA-E-presented peptide. This supports evaluating NKG2C+ subsets, but the cheatsheet does not say whether peptide dependence of that response is already considered.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell threat: IGRP-specific CD8+ T cells against beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O11/O24 directly report cytolysis of the immortalized HLA-A2+ βLox5 line by clone-32 IGRP-reactive human CD8+ avatars; O8/O9/O12/O13 show stronger activation and effector output after TRAC KO. The bounded general threat of IGRP-reactive CD8+ autoimmunity is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate2B (line 62); this does not incorporate these exact magnitudes, establish protection by any edit, or test indirect APC presentation. One HLA-A2-restricted clone, possible cross-reactivity/incomplete HLA matching, and a beta-cell line limit transfer to human SC-islet products.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (engineered autoreactive T-cell avatars as a challenge assay for protected beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: Specific TRAC-KO clone-32 avatars could be investigated as a stronger autoreactive challenge reagent: O4/O5/O6 establish improved pairing/binding and O10 greater target killing. Frozen ranker line 5811 already specifies autoreactive PPI/IGRP/GAD65 CD8+ TCR survival assays, so an engineered challenge assay cannot be called absent from the project using cheatsheet silence. Whether this exact TRAC-KO implementation is incorporated is unknown. Transfer to protected SC-islet targets, protective-edit discrimination, multi-clone/HLA coverage and donor standardization remain untested; this is an assay hypothesis, not an accepted upgrade or therapeutic TRAC-KO recommendation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (SLC30A8 allelic effects and compartment-specific metal metrology)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O6 and O14/O15 show that islet zinc and bulk pancreatic zinc are distinct endpoints in native male R138X mice; O17 supplies only an unquantified secretion tendency with unresolved cohort labels. These findings scope mechanistic interpretation of SLC30A8 perturbation and bulk-metal proxies, but do not validate endocrine function or protection in edited human SC-islets. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 requires dynamic GSIS and low-glucose shutoff; ranker AUTO_NONE explicitly mentions avoiding SLC30A8 dense-core defects and Decision Experiment 5 names an SLC30A8 allelic series. Claim-specific incorporation of this study’s metal-redistribution magnitudes is unknown. The paper supplies no immune-protection, intrinsic stress-challenge, or exact-product qualification result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1 engagement, Locus 3)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O11 show delayed rejection with biomaterial-presented SA-PD-L1 plus rapamycin in diabetic NOD mice under autoimmune and combined allo/autoimmune challenge. The broad PD-L1 component is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §4.3 (Locus 3) and ranker lines 1736-1740; incorporation does not extend to these exact mouse survival figures or to qualification of genetically encoded PD-L1 in the human product. Median labels and unspecified ± terms remain as reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (durability of PD-L1-based protection under recurrent autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports a source-defined >30-day syngeneic survival fraction of 4/11 (36%); O12 reports the Discussion delayed-rejection fraction of 46% in allogeneic recipients; O17 reports 5/6 allogeneic responders had fully rejected by day-60 analysis. These distinct outcomes and outcome-defined responder subgroups demonstrate partial, transient benefit under a 30-day rapamycin course with retained insulin pellets. They qualify transfer of local biomaterial PD-L1 results to durable drug-free human protection; exact claim-level incorporation is not established by the frozen references, despite general Gate2B residual-hazard treatment in GRAVEYARD_010.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (macrophage compartment; PD-1+ M2-like macrophages versus the CD47-SIRPalpha arm)
edges.claim_summary: Syngeneic responders had more F4/80+CD206+PD-1+ macrophages (O9); allogeneic Results/Figure 6 distinguish the F4/80+PD-1+ comparison (O23) from separate CD206+ M2-like gating (O15). The source Discussion speculates about reduced phagocytosis but explicitly says delayed-rejection mechanisms were not characterized, and late sampling may be confounded by rejection kinetics. This yields an unvalidated mechanistic hypothesis for comparison with the Blueprint Gate3 CD47-SIRPalpha phagocytosis requirement, not evidence of macrophage protection or synergy; exact incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (static GSIS as a bounded endocrine-function transfer claim)
edges.claim_summary: O8 reports static high/low-glucose insulin-secretion indices of 2.71-fold and 1.79-fold (RBP) in adult human omentum-MSC-derived beta-cell spheroids, with higher INS1/GLUT2 transcripts (O3/O4). This supports a within-source culture comparison but does not establish the Blueprint Gate1 hPSC-derived tri-hormonal product's dynamic biphasic GSIS, low-glucose shut-off or basal-leak performance; static index 2.71 is not a Gate1 pass. M2 denotes the target differentiation/maturation question, not source identity. Exact claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate matrix and cell-contact cue for SC-islet maturation)
edges.claim_summary: Higher maturation and junction/adhesion transcripts on MBP-FGF2 (O2/O9), plus qualitatively enhanced Cx36/Cx43/E-cadherin protein expression in actual Results, motivate testing an immobilized-FGF2 culture cue in hPSC-derived SC-islets. The source uses adult omentum MSC derivatives, not Blueprint Stage-6/7 hPSC SC-islets, and contains no causal perturbation of junction signaling or functional SC-islet transfer test. The frozen ranker uses a Stage-6/7 maturation baseline; this does not establish adoption of the specific MSC matrix claim, so incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (graft-dependent glycemic regulation in an immunodeficient-mouse bioassay)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O12/O15 support graft-dependent glycemic regulation through 30 days and plasma human-insulin detection after 120 MSC-derived spheroids were placed under the kidney capsule of diabetic athymic nude mice. This is a bounded functional-bioassay bridge, not exact-product or immune-protection qualification. Results also describe qualitative peri-graft blood vessels at day 30; vessel density, perfusion, oxygen and vascularization kinetics were not quantified, and faster glucose regulation cannot establish angiogenic causation. No C-peptide benchmark or human immune reconstitution is supplied; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive T-cell evasion benchmarks; non-genetic CXCL12-alginate immune protection)
edges.claim_summary: In NHPs without systemic immunosuppression, xenoantigen-specific CD4+/CD8+ T-cell IFNγ/TNFα changes were minimal (O2) and cytokine changes limited to 2-6-fold (O1), per the abstract. Porcine adult islets in alginate microbeads are a different strategy and cell type from edited hPSC SC-islets, with n = 4 plus 1 and no stated non-CXCL12 comparator.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 and Gate3 / M1 (graft-localized pharmacologic immunomodulation; adaptive T-cell and macrophage infiltration)
edges.claim_summary: Local CsA microparticles prolonged murine primary-islet allograft survival vs empty particles (O1) and reduced abstract-reported T-cell/macrophage infiltration (O8/O9). With short-course systemic CTLA4-Ig, 55 vs 25% function at day 214 and author-labelled MST values (O2/O19, same cohort) did not establish an incremental survival advantage (log-rank p = 0.13). This supports a local immunomodulation concept, not genetically edited human SC-islet evasion, drug-free protection, NK protection or reduced macrophage phagocytosis specifically. The frozen Blueprint §1.2 requires immunosuppression-free multi-gate performance; claim-specific incorporation of this regimen is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (donor-specific challenge and limits of pharmacologically induced operational tolerance)
edges.claim_summary: Donor-matched BALB/c skin rejection was delayed (O16), while third-party C3H skin rejection was described as comparable to controls (O17). Donor-matched skin was ultimately rejected and apparently followed by islet graft rejection (O25), limiting the authors' operational-tolerance interpretation. FoxP3 staining (O15) is associative and not proof of suppressor function or causal tolerance. No autoimmune-memory or indirect-APC assay, permanent donor-skin acceptance, or edited human SC-islet qualification was shown. Frozen Blueprint §4.2 and ranker Decision Experiment #2 cover host APC/adjunct regimen constraints; incorporation of this particular challenge boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet identity and manufacturing QC: hPSC line genotype, polyhormonal cells, insulin content)
edges.claim_summary: PAX4 variant donor-derived SC-islets showed polyhormonal-cell increases and reduced insulin content (O12,O13); correction reduced polyhormonal cells and increased insulin content in both correction series (O14,O15). This supports a testable Gate1/M2 donor-line genotype or correction hypothesis in T4 in vitro cells. It does not demonstrate mature GSIS rescue, clinical graft benefit, or product qualification: O18 is a Discussion limitation, and O23 shows glycolytic-reserve rescue only for His192. The frozen Blueprint Gate1 contract and manufacturing QC are relevant, but adoption of this exact PAX4 line-selection claim is not established; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (differentiation yield and composition metrics vs identity metrics)
edges.claim_summary: In this in vitro model, similar stage proportions (O9) and no measured p.His192 hormone-transcript difference (O11) coexisted with polyhormonal-cell, insulin-content and maturation-gene findings (O8,O12,O13). These qualify the information supplied by individual differentiation readouts; nonsignificance is not equivalence. Frozen Blueprint section1.2 already requires lineage purity and dynamic GSIS, and its Stage7 sorting/QC includes hormone staining and starting-hPSC-normalized beta yield. The study does not establish that current Blueprint QC misses this defect, nor whether this precise PAX4 boundary is incorporated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-cell identity: repression of the alpha-cell program)
edges.claim_summary: PAX4 knockout derepressed an alpha-cell signature in Protocol A SC-islets (O6); Protocol B showed directionally consistent but nonsignificant alpha-gene changes (O7). PAX4 knockdown in EndoC-betaH1 cells raised GCG transcript 2.7-fold and abolished GSIS (O3,O5). These provide bounded support for the importance of endogenous PAX4 function to Gate1 beta-cell identity in T4 SC-islet and T5 cell-line contexts. They do not establish a beneficial PAX4 overexpression strategy, edited-product function or clinical efficacy; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.claim_summary: Capillaries were already present in the graft area at the earliest time sampled, 1 week, and polyhormonal cells fell from 66 to 24 cells between 1 and 2 weeks (O16, O17). Sampling began at 1 week, so these data cannot test the Gate5 short-hours avascular bridge target; vessels are mouse host-derived at a kidney-capsule site.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet GSIS and maturation readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 show CD47 signaling restrains insulin granule exocytosis via Cdc42 in human and mouse β cells, so GSIS and exocytosis readouts of CD47-expressing or CD47-overexpressing SC-islets should be tested against a CD47-low condition. Human β cells share exocytosis machinery with SC-β cells, but SC-islets were not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoimmune host-model endpoint qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O12/O15 report no overt T1D in the respective HLA/TCR cohorts, while O4/O7/O13/O14/O17 and O8 retain insulitis or impaired glucose-challenged plasma insulin readouts. These mouse-islet models can therefore inform selection of autoimmune endpoints, without establishing a hyperglycemic efficacy model or qualification of an edited human SC-islet product. Blueprint §1.2/§2 requires Gate2B protection and exact-product preclinical qualification, but adoption of this particular model/endpoint limitation is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (insulin/C-peptide-reactive T-cell pressure)
edges.claim_summary: O4/O7/O13/O14 and O8 qualitatively support an insulin/C-peptide-reactive autoimmune threat in HLA-DQ8 transgenic mouse-islet hosts; that generic PPI-reactive threat is explicitly recognized in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate2B and §4.2. This claim does not assert that the study is incorporated quantitatively or that it measures donor-MHC-null SC-islet survival, indirect host-APC presentation, memory-cell recurrence, or the efficacy of PD-L1/SERPINB9. Frozen ranker Gate2B coefficients and Graveyard 010 remain separate mechanistic priors, uncalibrated by this study.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (HLA/TCR-transgenic autoimmune host limitations: peripheral selection and myocarditis)
edges.claim_summary: O19/O21 show markedly lower peripheral CD4+ yield in the scid 20D11 context yet persistent insulitis; O20/O22 report myocarditis in DQ8-based hosts and reported absence in DQ8-A2–20D11, without myocarditis incidence counts or proof of causal elimination. These findings qualify autoimmune host selection and interpretation of morbidity. They are not Gate2A allorejection or long-term graft-survival validation: no graft, human immune reconstitution or edited SC-islet product was tested. Incorporation of these exact host-specific limitations is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 + M7 (PDMS-CaO2 oxygenation and scaffold oxygen transport; no switch/genomic endpoint)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O5-O8 support in-vitro oxygen delivery by CaO2/PDMS disks in collagen/Matrigel scaffold culture: release persists beyond 20 d in water, definitive-endoderm bottom oxygen rises to 89% central and about 95% peripheral air saturation versus about 74% and 75%, and pancreatic-progenitor central bottom oxygen is around 50% versus 27%. The frozen Blueprint §1.2 and Stage2 already require a 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/catalase bridge, but these water/culture measurements do not qualify exact-product kinetics, avascular graft pO2, peroxide, pH, or viability over that bridge. Incorporation of these protocol-specific quantitative observations is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation, maturation-marker composition, and static GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O11, O13 and O15-O23 support an oxygen-supply lever during IMR90 scaffold differentiation: INS/PDX1/NKX6.1/GCG/SST transcript increases, higher static stimulation index, and altered semi-quantitative endocrine-marker fractions. O12 provides no significant benefit of day-19 oxygenator replacement; the authors infer an early-stage effect without stage-isolated timing tests. These results suggest a manufacturing experiment, but do not test the frozen Blueprint §1.2 dynamic biphasic GSIS and less-than-3-minute shut-off gate, its sorted 60:30:10 input mixture, absolute lineage yield, or counterregulation. O14 author-described similarity to human islets is not equivalence; O23 dual-positive enrichment is not established maturation. Incorporation of this specific manufacturing protocol is unresolved.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (release criteria for beta-cell function: electrophysiology and coupling readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O6-O14 show MEA slow-potential and patch-clamp readouts can separate BLC function (coupling, KATP conductance, Ca2+-exocytosis coupling) from expression markers, suggesting these could be added as functional QC alongside perifusion GSIS for SC-islets. Tested only in BLC preparations and EndoC-βH1 comparators, not in current SC-islet lots.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP and inflammatory-cytokine stress resilience of beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: O8, O9 and O16 show TXNIP rising together with NLRP3, caspase-1 and GSDMD-N under high glucose or T2DM and falling with irisin-driven Nrf2 activation (O1-O4, O7), consistent with TXNIP being a stress node in the Gate4 element list. Only expression correlations in a mouse cell line and a diet/STZ model were measured; TXNIP was not manipulated and no hPSC islet or T1D cytokine context was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (peri-transplant pyroptosis readouts and Nrf2-based cytoprotective conditioning)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4, O9 and O15-O18 suggest pyroptosis markers (GSDMD-N, caspase-1, IL-1β) and an Nrf2-Trx/TXNIP axis could be added as stress-resilience readouts or a conditioning lever for SC-islets. Irisin is untested in human or SC-β cells and the evidence is mouse glucotoxicity, so this is a hypothesis only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (non-invasive localization and monitoring of SC-islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O10 show a DGCR2 PET tracer detects intramuscular SC-islet grafts in nude mice only early (SUV 0.79 ± 0.19 vs 0.31 ± 0.09 muscle at 10 min), with fast washout and kidney spill-over hiding abdominal grafts (O9, O16). DGCR2 imaging is therefore a candidate graft-monitoring readout for the Blueprint, not a validated one; graft function or survival was not correlated and group n is not stated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet beta-cell identity and persistence after engraftment)
edges.claim_summary: O11 and O12 show DGCR2 co-localizing with insulin in H1 hESC-derived SC-islets before transplantation and in grafts four weeks after intramuscular transplantation, and O4 shows SC-islet sections bound more tracer than human islet fraction sections. These are qualitative immunofluorescence and autoradiography findings without function readouts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularized subcutaneous site; vascularization timing)
edges.claim_summary: Islets in an untreated subcutaneous site did not reach euglycemia whereas bFGF-agarose prevascularized sites did (O2), with faster euglycemia after 2 wk than 1 wk (O3: 40.8 d vs 12 d) and CD31+ vessels infiltrating the capsule at 2 wk (O7). Supports site vascularization and its maturation timing as variables for a prevascularized device; no oxygen tension measured and no stem-cell-derived cells used.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation efficiency and maturation; PDX1/NKX6.1 progenitor quality)
edges.claim_summary: Deleting the lncRNA MIR503HG in H9 hESCs raised PDX1/NKX6.1 PP fraction (O1) and INS/NKX6.1 and CHGA/MAFA SC-beta fractions while lowering poly-hormonal cells in vitro and in grafts (O2-O4, O8, O9), with higher human C-peptide at 5 weeks (O7). Proposes an extra manufacturing edit to test; evidence is a single lab, n = 3-8, no stimulation index and a SCID-Beige host.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic and oncology safety of editing)
edges.claim_summary: After single-locus CRISPR/Cas9 deletion the KO hESCs showed no significant chromosomal mutations (O16) and recipients showed no tumorigenesis in major organs with fewer KI67+ graft cells (O14, O15). Weak support for editing safety: a single deletion, no off-target or translocation analysis stated, and Gate5 concerns multiplex editing.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M6 (glucose-dependent insulin secretion; repolarizing K+ channels Kcnb1 and Kcnh6)
edges.claim_summary: In mouse islets, blocking Kv2.1 or Kcnh6 raised insulin secretion at 16.7 mM glucose or in perfusion but not at low glucose (O2-O5), and lysine acted through Kcnh6 in patch-clamp, islet and mouse data (O10-O16). Repolarization biology is plausibly shared with beta cells generally, but no SC-beta cells were tested and the human-islet result is n = 3 (O17).

edges.target_gate_or_module: M6 (pooled CRISPR plus scRNA-seq screens in beta-cell models)
edges.claim_summary: A pooled all-K+-channel CRISPR/scRNA-seq screen in Min6 cells nominated Kcnb1 and Kcnh6, which inhibitor and KO-mouse experiments then validated (O2, O5, O6, O11). The screen itself is weak: the Ins1/Ins2 direction conflicts between text and Fig 2 caption (O1) and the authors state no non-targeting-sgRNA control was run.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER and integrated stress resilience of SC-beta cells; pharmacologic cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: WFS1-null SC-islets showed integrated stress response activation (O7-O9), and ISRIB 100 nM lowered stress granules, restored protein synthesis, raised the INS-GFP/NKX6.1-mCherry fraction and reduced beta-cell apoptosis (O10-O13). Suggests testing ISR inhibition as a Gate4 conditioning lever, but this is a genetic WFS1 disease model with no hypoxia, cytokine or transplant stress.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation and GSIS; stress-branch failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: In SC-islet beta cells a stress trajectory competes with the maturation trajectory; WFS1 loss shifted cells to the stress branch (O1, O2) with lower INS/NKX6.1 expression, reduced GSIS and lower insulin content (O3-O6). Supports stress-state beta cells as a maturation failure mode, though the trigger here is a disease gene knockout rather than manufacturing conditions.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO + CIITA KO hypoimmune stack, Locus 1/2)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 report engraftment of allogeneic B2M-/- CIITA-/- CD47+ primary p-islets in an immunocompetent diabetic NHP with no detectable immune response and no immunosuppression, consistent with the B2M + CIITA knockout baseline. Domain is NHP primary pseudo-islets, not hPSC-derived islets, and the abstract gives no per-edit attribution.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 component; the abstract does not test HLA-E)
edges.claim_summary: The engrafting construct in O1 and O4 includes CD47 overexpression but the abstract does not separate its contribution from the knockouts or test NK subsets, so it supports the CD47 element of the innate-immunity axis only at the level of the combined stack.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (functional graft in an immunocompetent primate)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 state stable endocrine function and insulin independence from an allogeneic hypoimmune islet graft in a primate; no quantitative function data are in the abstract, so this is a qualitative in vivo feasibility signal rather than a benchmark.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive IGRP-specific CD8+ T-cell effector pressure in T1D)
edges.claim_summary: O1/O19, O12, O14, O17 and O18 support a mechanistic bridge to Gate2B: Tyk2 deficiency or early BMS-986165 treatment reduced diabetes development and autoreactive IGRP-specific CTL pressure in female NOD/NY8.3 systems without an islet graft. The 12w drug-start cohort had no statistically detected diabetes-free survival-curve difference (p = 0.99) while later onset age was reported; this does not establish equivalence or loss of all drug activity. Autoimmunity was not abolished (O4), and the highly diabetogenic NY8.3 cohort retained 60% incidence (O20). The frozen references include TYK2/IL-12/IL-23 design factors and a TYK2-WT lead policy, but incorporation of these specific host/CTL and age-window data is unestablished. Systemic drug and whole-animal knockout effects do not establish protection from graft-local TYK2 editing or preserved unrelated immunity.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (PDX1/NKX6.1 progenitor competence and GSIS in hPSC-derived beta-like cells)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3, O8, O9, O11 and O12: a hypomorphic GLI2 variant lowered PDX1/NKX6.1 progenitor output (~70% fewer double-positive cells in HET), beta-cell marker expression and GSIS in iPSC-derived beta-like cells, and the homozygous line arrested at the endocrine progenitor stage, so endocrine yield and function depend on HH/GLI2 signalling. This is a disease-variant model in one iPSC background, not a manufacturing intervention.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (stage-specific non-canonical WNT5A signalling at the pancreatic progenitor stage)
edges.claim_summary: O15-O18: WNT5A exposure of control cells reproduced the mutant phenotype (lower PDX1/NKX6.1 and reduced GSIS) and the WNT5A antagonist BOX5 partially rescued GLI2P>L HET cells. This suggests testing whether limiting non-canonical WNT5A activity at the progenitor stage protects endocrine differentiation in the Blueprint protocol, but BOX5 was never tested in wild type control lines in this packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (graft oncology safety: proliferative non-endocrine by-products of differentiation, beyond edit-related clonogenic risk)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O3, O5, O6 and O7: iPSC-derived islet grafts in NOD-scid mice produced human, Ki67-high PMSC outgrowth lacking pancreatic markers in 13% (12/96 mice) of s7-iPIC and 84% (38/45 mice) of s6-iPIC grafts, with PMSC markers absent before implantation and PMSC-like cells in other published ESC/iPSC graft datasets. This extends the Gate5 safety scope to unedited differentiation by-products; no suicide switch or edited cell was tested and the host was immunodeficient.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (purification and release testing: EGF extended-culture detection assay and docetaxel removal of nonendocrine proliferative cells)
edges.claim_summary: O8, O12, O13, O17 and O14: a 4-week EGF-supplemented extended culture exposed a putative PMSC population, docetaxel reduced it without affecting CHGA+ endocrine cells, and docetaxel-treated s7-iPICs gave neither PMSCs nor cysts in 85 mice while human C-peptide exceeded 2,000 pmol/L. This suggests adding an extended-culture release assay and a pre-implant docetaxel step to Gate1 purification, but it was shown only in this protocol and not with CD49a-enriched or gene-edited cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization and graft oxygenation after the avascular bridge)
edges.claim_summary: In immunodeficient mice at 3 months, SC-islet kidney-capsule grafts were vascularized by recipient vessels only (O9, O10) with graft oxygen tension of 23.1 vs 11.6 mmHg for human islets (O12, P < 0.01). This is chronic, revascularized-state data and does not test the acute avascular oxygen bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (IAPP as a maturation and purification marker; aconitine induction)

IAPP-based sorting or reporter-guided induction could be tested as a Gate1 manufacturing upgrade; the cheatsheet does not list IAPP.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3 (in vivo maturation of SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: After kidney-capsule transplantation SC-beta cells lost the poly-hormonal population (O1), GSIS improved with unchanged fasting insulin (O2, O3), and the IAPP+ fraction of INS+ cells rose in vivo (O14, O15), consistent with post-transplant maturation. No perifusion stimulation index was reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate2B / M1 / M7 (SLC30A8/ZnT8 perturbation: functional boundary for a possible autoantigen edit)
edges.claim_summary: Gene-disrupted EndoC-βH3 cells showed no apparent culture survival/growth defect (O14) and no reported basal/stimulated secretion change (O15), with ZnT8 protein ablation unconfirmed. This is a bounded functional observation, not evidence of ZnT8 antigen removal, immune evasion, SC-islet safety or dynamic glucose shut-off. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 lists ZnT8 autoimmunity; the actual ranker already includes SLC30A8 KO in its high-burden autoantigen alternative and an SLC30A8 allelic-series decision experiment, so a new/unaccounted target cannot be claimed. Incorporation of this study-specific result is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 / M7 (local regulatory effects of genome editing; genomic-safety extrapolation)
edges.claim_summary: CTCF-site mutations and enhancer-region deletions at SLC30A8 changed nearby transcripts (O4/O5/O7); separate targeted loss of UTP23/RAD21/MED30 reduced viability (O11–O13). These experiments do not prove that the enhancer edits caused that viability loss, nor do they quantify off-target damage or test B2M/CIITA/CXCL10/AAVS1 product edits. Frozen Blueprint §4.4/§9.1 and GRAVEYARD_006 already address distinct chromatin-insulation and genomic-integrity questions; whether this precise cis-regulatory finding is incorporated is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M4 (stimulated C-peptide and CGM TIR clinical benchmarks; Gate2A humanized-mouse allo versus syngeneic design)
edges.claim_summary: The Figure 1 caption lists the benchmark types the cheatsheet names for M4 (CGM, TIR, HbA1c, MMTT C-peptide; O6-O8) for one autologous E-islet recipient with type 2 diabetes, but no values or directions are in the packet. An autologous recipient without alloimmunity or autoimmunity cannot serve as a benchmark for an allogeneic hypoimmune design; the humanized-mouse allo versus syngeneic readout (O4, O5) has no stated result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement; macrophage phagocytosis)
edges.claim_summary: Transiently displayed SA-CD47 (alone or with SA-TM) reduced macrophage phagocytosis in vitro (O7-O9) and inhibited clearance of MHC-deficient allogeneic donor cells in vivo in spleen and bone marrow (O10, O11), with the combination more effective than single proteins (O12, O13). This is mouse and rat cells with recombinant protein display, not hPSC-derived islets with a CD47 transgene, so it bridges only through the shared CD47-SIRPalpha mechanism the cheatsheet states.
