edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (diffusion-limited hypoxia and HIF-target response in dense avascular islet culture)
edges.claim_summary: In primary human islets cultured 2 weeks at 442 IEQ/cm2, diffusion-only static culture gave islet degradation, lower viability (P = 0.020) and a larger rise in GLUT1/GLUT3/VEGFA than vertical-flow culture (O6, O7, O10). This supports hypoxia as a survival failure mode (Gate4) but is from primary islets in vitro at 27 C, not SC-islets in vivo.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS stimulation index >= 2.0-3.0 benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: Dynamic culture improved raw insulin secretion (O13) but the GSIS stimulation index showed no statistical difference (O14), so the platform's function benefit registers in secretion output and not in SI. Qualifies reliance on SI alone when judging culture-condition effects, in primary islets rather than SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (avascular oxygen supply, diffusion-consumption physics)
edges.claim_summary: A diffusion-convection-reaction model gave 27.3 mmHg at the islet surface and 9.1% of islet volume below 1 mmHg with diffusion-only supply, versus 110.8 mmHg and 1.1% with 40 µl/min flow (O2, O3). Shows dense diffusion-only islet supply is hypoxia-limited; the geometry is a perfused culture insert, not an avascular PDMS-CaO2 graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation; secretory output alongside stimulation index)
edges.claim_summary: RFX6+/− H1 SC-islets showed 62% and 54% lower basal/high-glucose secretion (O10/O11), lower perifusion AUC (O14), but reported similar static stimulation index, beta-cell proportion and insulin content (O13/O8/O9). This empirically illustrates why SI/composition alone do not establish secretory capacity; no numerical OpenIslet gate pass is demonstrated. The general multi-readout boundary is already explicit in frozen Blueprint line 247 (output U, basal/first-phase and equal-output confirmation) and ranker lines 5801–5803; RFX6-specific adoption is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo SC-islet graft function readout)
edges.claim_summary: The heterozygous secretory deficit persisted in human SC-islet kidney-capsule grafts in non-humanized immunodeficient NSG mice: random-fed human C-peptide approximately half WT (O17), fasting C-peptide ~60% lower (O19), reduced IPGTT C-peptide AUC (O18), and delayed lowering to the human glycaemic level (O24). These matched graft-function readouts do not establish immune protection, clinical efficacy or superiority of a particular OpenIslet product; exact RFX6-specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (hPSC donor-line selection and genotype QC)
edges.claim_summary: Hypothesis, not a screening intervention tested here: heterozygous RFX6 loss can reduce human SC-islet secretory capacity while leaving reported composition and insulin content similar (O7–O11/O13), motivating evaluation of beta-cell transcription-factor loss-of-function variants during donor-line QC. The bridge from engineered isogenic lines and Finnish observational genetics to a general donor-line screening policy is an inference, not demonstrated screening benefit; exact policy incorporation in the frozen Blueprint is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (PD-L1-dependent protection against recurrent autoimmunity)
edges.claim_summary: Cxcl16 deletion reduced insulitis and intra-islet effector-associated CD8+ populations (O6, O10, O12), while donor splenocytes remained diabetogenic on transfer (O7) and anti-PD-1 overcame protection (O16). CD8 depletion adds tissue-local support (O24, O25). This suggests a checkpoint-blockade challenge condition to test for the Blueprint local checkpoint shield; it does not show that engineered PD-L1-dependent or whole-stack graft protection would necessarily be lost, or quantify that loss.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / Gate2B / M1 (islet-macrophage CXCL16-mediated OxLDL scavenging and local autoreactive CD8+ T-cell persistence)
edges.claim_summary: Mouse islet macrophages show surface CXCL16 (O3), and knockout reduces macrophage OxLDL uptake while increasing intact-islet OxLDL (O8, O9), alongside reduced local effector-associated CD8+ subsets (O10–O13). Human donor islets only establish CXCL16 expression (O4). Cxcl16 deletion did not significantly alter the assayed basal activation markers or insulin presentation (O26, O27); no TNF/NF-κB transcriptional shift is inferred. This qualifies macrophage–T-cell coupling in endogenous NOD islets, not SC-islet graft survival, NK evasion or a validated CXCL16 intervention in humans; the source reports global knockout and no successful macrophage-specific conditional deletion. The Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 graft-phagocytosis shield is a distinct endpoint; specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (iCasp9/AP1903 at AAVS1 clonogenic fail-safe, escape threshold < 1e-6)
edges.claim_summary: TYMS−/− thymidine auxotrophy sharply limited hiPSC growth without dTMP (O1, O3, O4) but was a partial brake: one mouse formed a small teratoma without supplementation (O7), teratoma Ki67 did not differ (O8), and graft Ki67 was lower only in the first 3 months (O12). No escape frequency was measured, so it cannot be compared with a < 1e-6 threshold, and it acts on cycling cells, not as a kill switch.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (transgene-free proliferation brake alongside iCasp9)
edges.claim_summary: Proposed, not tested here: because dTMP-supplemented TYMS−/− hiPSCs expanded like TYMS+/+ (O2) and gave functional SC-islets (O13–O17), a TYMS knockout could be trialled as a manufacturing-stage proliferation brake layered with the iCasp9 switch. This was never tested with iCasp9 or the immune edits, and it adds an extra edit to the multiplex genomic-safety burden.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet function after genome editing)
edges.claim_summary: TYMS−/− hiPSC-derived SC-islets expressed similar maturation markers and showed similar in vitro insulin secretion, graft C-peptide and glucose lowering to TYMS+/+ controls up to 5 months in NSG mice (O13–O17), with no stated functional penalty from the edit. Values were not reported in text, and the grafts were in immunodeficient hosts.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet lineage purity and off-target SC-EC control)
edges.claim_summary: The observed EC contamination (O10/O12), low beta-cell fraction in impure grafts (O9) and acinar contamination (O13) support the existing Gate1 requirement for lineage purification and SC-EC control (frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §6 Step 1). Incorporation refers to that qualitative requirement, not adoption of this study’s percentages as thresholds. No purification intervention, 60:30:10 comparison or clinical harm from EC cells was tested, so these data do not qualify the prescribed mixture or purity gate.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (measured C-peptide-to-graft-mass surrogate limitation)
edges.claim_summary: In a separate non-imaged kidney-subcapsular cohort of non-diabetic NSG mice, human C-peptide did not correlate with total engrafted volume (O16), and only residual secretion under hypoglycaemia weakly correlated with calculated beta-cell mass (O17); secretion fell approximately 90% during ITT (O18). This bounds C-peptide as a mass surrogate in this host/site, while intact mouse beta cells and separate PET and kidney cohorts limit transfer. It is not a clinical-trial or paired PET-versus-C-peptide accuracy result; exact incorporation of this metrology boundary in the Blueprint is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (graft-overgrowth monitoring as a possible fail-safe trigger)
edges.claim_summary: Impure graft expansion (O6/O7/O19) and exendin volume tracking (O3) motivate a hypothesis that PET surveillance could inform a Gate5 fail-safe intervention. O25 shows early non-detection, O21 shows cyst-sensitive FDOPA volume performance, and O14/O22–O24 composition correlations depend on histological volume correction; low tracer signal does not directly quantify off-target burden. No iCasp9 activation, eradication, clonogenic escape, oxygen bridge or exact-product protection was tested. Clinical transfer and exact incorporation of a PET-trigger rule are unestablished; existing pan-lineage switch requirements remain distinct.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (RNLS-associated NK regulation and checkpoint expression; not demonstrated CD47/SIRPalpha causality)
edges.claim_summary: RNLS loss is associated with higher endogenous CD47/CEACAM and reduced mouse NK proliferation/degranulation-marker expression (O5–O8, O11–O15), while mouse/human CD200 differs (O19–O20) and LAP induction, per-positive-cell intensity and secretion are distinct (O9, O21–O24). No ligand-specific block/knockout, SIRPalpha engagement assay, engineered CD47-IgV-GPI test, absolute surface-density qualification or macrophage endpoint is supplied; human mixed-PBMC protection does not establish NK-specific causality. Frozen Blueprint §4.1 already requires exact-construct NK qualification, and §5/GRAVEYARD_004 plus the ranker retain RNLS metabolic precautions; adoption of this specific RNLS-regulatory mechanism is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (indirect APC pathway, PD-L1 tolerogenic APCs, NK-APC cross-talk)
edges.claim_summary: NKp46-positive innate lymphoid-cell depletion removes the Rnlsmut paired-graft weight advantage and tolerogenic APC phenotype in mouse autoimmune-transfer experiments (O1–O3). Soluble-factor NK LAP/Tgfβ1 induction/secretion (O9, O21–O22) and human NK/T-cell surface phenotypes (O16, O23) suggest an RNLS-to-regulatory-NK/APC hypothesis; they do not prove Tgfβ1 mediates APC PD-L1 or human indirect HLA-DQ2/DQ8 protection. Frozen Blueprint §4.2 addresses host indirect APC presentation and the ranker Gate2B retains its residual-hazard discount; incorporation of this specific RNLS/NKp46/APC route is unknown, and this study does not remove the existing RNLS GSIS/OCR qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (functional maturation release criteria beside dynamic perifusion GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: BLCs from pioneer protocols had KATP conductance above primary beta-cells and limited glucose responsiveness on MEA (O3), and MEA slow potentials tracked insulin secretion (O1). Hypothesis only: add KATP conductance and MEA coupling as maturation QC next to perifusion GSIS; the abstract says KATP conductance 'may account' for the limited response, so causality is untested and the cells are not the Blueprint SC-islet protocol.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-beta cell functional resemblance to primary beta-cells)
edges.claim_summary: iPSC-derived BLCs were electrically coupled like primary beta-cells (O1) and had sodium and calcium currents comparable with primary beta- and EndoC-βH1 cells (O2). Abstract-only evidence from in vitro cells made with older protocols; no values reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M3 (early neutrophil-associated failure in prevascularized allogeneic grafts)
edges.claim_summary: In allogeneic primary-mouse islets in an MAA-prevascularized BALB/c subcutaneous site, the F1 caption describes neutrophils as predominant at 24 h (O3; Results calls neutrophils and macrophages prominent), while steroid plus fingolimod failed within 2 days (O9) and anti-Ly6G alone restored normoglycemia in all n = 3 mice (O10). This motivates testing early live-neutrophil-mediated graft inflammation alongside the Blueprint Gate3 NK/macrophage assays; the exact executioner-versus-messenger mechanism is unresolved (packet Discussion). Frozen Blueprint §1.2, ranker Gate3 branches and GRAVEYARD_009 concern NK/macrophage protection; the ranker also has a neutrophil-elastase surface challenge, which does not establish incorporation of this depletion experiment. Specific incorporation therefore remains unknown. No human SC-islet protection or systemic-depletion adoption is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate3 / M1 / M3 (combined innate and adaptive graft-protection context)
edges.claim_summary: The broad requirement to address both adaptive alloimmunity and innate graft injury is explicitly present in Blueprint §1.2 Gates2A/3 and separate ranker gate branches; already_accounted_for applies only to that architectural premise. In the mouse drug protocol, anti-Ly6G followed by rapamycin was associated with longer normoglycemia than anti-Ly6G alone (O13; n = 4 vs 3), with an unspecified subset surviving >75 days (O14, same cohort). This supports that broad premise without proving that the sequence is necessary, distinguishing direct from indirect allorecognition, or validating any human cell-edit stack; the exact drug regimen is not claimed as adopted.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularized graft context; no measured 72-hour oxygen-bridge qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O1 is an abstract-level claim of sufficient vasculature after 2 to 3 weeks of MAA-coated-tube prevascularization; Methods/F2A/F3A place the 600 IEQ allogeneic mouse grafts in a 14-21-day preconditioned site. This provides prevascularized-graft context for Gate5, whose general prevascularized-site/oxygen-support premise is explicit in Blueprint §1.2 and the ranker niche branch. It does not establish incorporation of this MAA regimen, quantify pO2 or oxygen flux, compare an unmodified site, or qualify the 72-hour PDMS-CaO2/iMVF human product. M3 is the explicit graft/oxygen/prevascularization module; M5 denotes switch/genomic safety and is unsupported here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation, paracrine architecture, glucose responsiveness)
edges.claim_summary: In hPSC-derived islet buds, the shift from bi-hormonal to mono-hormonal cells (O8), a majority core-mantle organization (O7) and more HG-responder buds (O12) occurred together from Stage 6 to Stage 7, yet most buds still did not respond to elevated glucose (O11). This is consistent with the Gate1 emphasis on maturation and architecture; the architecture-function link is correlative and in vitro only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine-stage readouts versus progenitor markers in SC-islet differentiation)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (developmental RFX6-CAT/apoptosis association in SC-islet differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: RFX6 deletion coincided with strongly reduced CAT transcripts/protein (O13-O15), increased Annexin V+ EPs (O10), and smaller organoids (O12). This is a justified bridge from developmental apoptosis to intrinsic-resilience questions at Gate4; CAT was not separately perturbed/rescued, STRING is a functional-association prediction, and inflammatory/hypoxic or peri-transplant protection was not tested. Blueprint §1.2 defines intrinsic stress resilience and separately uses extracellular catalase for Gate5 peroxide control; neither establishes incorporation of the specific developmental RFX6-CAT association, so that status remains unknown. O18 supports endocrine transcript rescue, not CAT-mediated survival rescue.

These findings do not isolate individual component causality or qualify mature dynamic glucose responsiveness, low-glucose shut-off, manufacturing yield or the OpenIslet product. edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture, 60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta reference)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization of an avascular graft site, prevascularized subcutaneous site)
edges.claim_summary: In STZ-diabetic BALB/c mice, 800 islets in a sponge reversed hyperglycemia and normalised IPGTT AUC only with one-week bFGF prevascularization (O2, O3, O6, O7, O10, O11), while non-angio-treated recipients showed no reversal. This supports vascularization of an avascular site as a gating requirement, but with mouse islets and no oxygen measurement, and the cheatsheet does not state this specific prevascularization result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (retrievable open-device subcutaneous platform for hPSC-derived islets)
edges.claim_summary: A commercial atelocollagen sponge kept islet viability >90% (O1), supported graft-dependent normoglycemia in immunodeficient BRJ mice (O12, O13, O14) and preserved histology and CD31 vascularization (O15, O17, O18). This suggests testing a bFGF-prevascularized, sponge-carried subcutaneous graft for hPSC-derived islets, which the cheatsheet does not state; it was only tested with mouse islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (stress challenge panel for SC-islets; enteroviral infection not in the cheatsheet's Gate4 stress list)
edges.claim_summary: SC-islets express the enterovirus receptors CAR and DAF and were successfully infected by CVBs (O4, O5), and Vemurafenib or its analogue reduced replication in most batches (O6). This suggests adding an enteroviral challenge to the SC-islet stress panel; it is an in vitro result only and the cheatsheet lists hypoxia, nutrient, ER/oxidative and cytokine stresses but not viral infection.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (ER-stress and IL-1β/IFN-γ/TNF-α cytokine resilience of iPSC-derived beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: In one WS1 patient-derived model, WFS1-variant iBeta had more early/late apoptosis than splice-site-corrected iBeta under TG/cytokines (O13/O14/O22), with an altered UPR marker pattern (O9–O12/O19/O21). This supports intrinsic stress vulnerability as a Gate4-relevant failure mode; corrected and disease-model cells are not the exact OpenIslet product. The specific WFS1/NMD mechanism is not established as an incorporated Blueprint component.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (stress-induced loss of NMD and PTC-transcript accumulation; B2M/CIITA knockout alleles)
edges.claim_summary: TG/cytokines reduced SMG7 expression and accompanied accumulation of PTC-carrying WFS1 isoforms (O16–O18); NMD inhibition in iPSCs also increased these isoforms (O5). A bounded hypothesis is to assay stress-conditioned transcript/protein products from any PTC-generating edited alleles. Transfer to B2M/CIITA knockout alleles is untested; neither those alleles nor NMD rescue/causal mediation were tested here, and accumulation does not by itself establish restored antigen expression or immune risk. Frozen Blueprint Gate4 and ranker Gate4 branches establish broad stress scope, not this claim-specific adoption; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (base-editor structural-genotoxicity hazard; GRAVEYARD_006 non-islet extrapolation)
edges.claim_summary: Cas9 and ABE structural-genotoxicity findings (O1, O4-O10), including B2M-targeting T-cell translocations (O10), support the existing genomic-safety precaution. Frozen Blueprint line 192 and GRAVEYARD_006 explicitly cite this exact PMID:39529170 as non-islet mechanistic evidence. This accounts for the broad hazard, not numerical transfer of T-cell/embryo rates to SC-islets. The paper does not test prime editing or simultaneous multiplex base editing plus >=4 DSB cuts, and does not calibrate ranker gamma_B=0.965 or establish product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5, M6 (genomic safety with single-cell CNV inference/WGS and high-fidelity ABE variants)
edges.claim_summary: The inferred CNV/WGS observations (O6-O10) and reduction of aneuploid ratio/SV numbers using PDCD1-targeting ABE8e-V106W (O17/O18), with residual SVs (O16), motivate evaluation of editor variants and these assays in the exact hPSC/SC-islet product. WGS/CAST-seq/optical genome mapping are already named in GRAVEYARD_006; whether this specific variant and scRNA-based approach are adopted is not established. Unknown incorporation concerns that specific proposal; transfer is unvalidated and neither assay readout nor residual-risk reduction qualifies the product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (mechanistic paracrine context for SC-islet mixture evaluation)
edges.claim_summary: O16 supports a general role for Sst in glucose-associated glucagon restraint in these global-knockout male mice. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and its endocrine-mixture protocol (lines 61, 244–247) specify SC-islet tri-hormonal architecture, but global mouse Sst deletion cannot isolate pancreatic delta cells from gastrointestinal/endocrine effects, validate the 60:30:10 ratio, or demonstrate human graft counter-regulation. The study-specific mechanism/quantitative boundary's adoption is not established; M7 describes the measured mechanistic evidence, while M2 is the untested target manufacturing domain.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (glycemic versus direct endocrine function readouts)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O6 show a 55% lower plasma-insulin OGTT AUC in CD-fed Znt8KO (p < 0.01) alongside a nonsignificant glucose-AUC difference (p > 0.05); this bounds glycemia as a proxy for endocrine output in this systemic mouse model, without establishing glucose equivalence or a measured insulin secretion rate. Blueprint §1.2 and lines 244–247 already require regulated dynamic endocrine measurements, and the frozen ranker decision experiment 5 includes SLC30A8 allelic-series functional testing (lines 6195–6198), so this is context for those checks, not evidence that the Blueprint relies on glycemia alone. Incorporation of this study-specific quantitative observation is unknown; clinical M4 evidence and SC-islet M2 manufacturing were not measured.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo human-islet and SC-derived beta-like-cell graft host model)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4-O5 support an abstract-reported, stable-hyperglycemic immunodeficient mouse platform for qualitative in vivo assessment of human stem cell-derived beta-like-cell graft function. M3 means In Vivo Graft, Oxygenation & Prevascularized Device. The supplied abstract does not describe a differentiation, purification, mixture or maturation experiment, so SC-derived-cell provenance does not justify M2. Blueprint section 1.2 Gate1 requires product-specific purity, tri-hormonal architecture, biphasic GSIS and low-glucose shut-off; those criteria and the exact edited OpenIslet product are not established here. The NSG model does not establish immune protection, 72-hour oxygen bridging, genomic safety or clinical efficacy. No quantitative graft-reversal metric or direct controlled comparison is supplied; O5 overlaps O3/O4. Specific adoption of this host model is not established by the bounded reference review, so incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC beta-cell percentages, survival proxies, intracellular insulin and dynamic GSIS; inceptor/IIR targeting hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3, O7-O8 and O15-O16 support testing inceptor loss or S5-S6 antibody targeting in human SC-islet differentiation/maturation: increased beta-cell percentage, author-described maintenance in extended culture, reduced apoptosis, higher insulin content and improved dGSIS are source-reported. These endpoints match the Gate1 function/manufacturing domain (frozen Blueprint section 1.2, line 61), but do not prove absolute manufacturing yield, edited-product qualification, the required low-glucose shut-off, no basal leak or graft function. The cellular FRET O19 is a secondary rat-cell mechanism, not a human SC-islet functional measurement. Claim-specific adoption is unestablished in the bounded frozen references; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (endocrine composition and processing-related qualification; 60:30:10 reference)
edges.claim_summary: O4 records lower SC alpha-cell percentages under genetic IIR knockout; O10 records a higher intracellular proinsulin:insulin ratio, whereas S5-S6 antibody treatment shows a slightly lower ratio (O17). O21 separately records only a tendency toward greater proinsulin secretion at high glucose. These findings warrant checking achieved endocrine composition, processing and secretion if inceptor targeting is tested; they do not establish an optimal mixture, a conversion defect, antibody superiority or reversal of the 60:30:10 reference. Frozen Blueprint lines 244-247 and ranker lines 5792-5803 already require achieved-composition and functional comparisons; whether these specific inceptor findings are incorporated is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (CD49a/ITGA1 SC-islet enrichment and off-target depletion)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O4, O5 and O6 support CD49a-based enrichment in HUES8 adherent-protocol SC-islets: relative to CD49a-, the C-peptide+ fraction was 4.0±0.4 times and SLC18A1+ fraction 0.26±0.05 times. This is depletion, not elimination or proof of the Blueprint absolute <1% SC-EC release criterion. Blueprint lines 245-247 and ranker lines 5602-5611 already specify live sorting, lineage QC and separate reaggregation; incorporation of this particular protocol and quantitative contrast is unestablished. No full Gate1 qualification follows from marker fractions or static GSIS.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (lineage recovery and controlled 60:30:10 input composition)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3 and O19 show that CD49a+ enrichment also depletes alpha cells and, relative to CD49a-, delta cells (GCG+ 0.38±0.03 and SST+ 0.48±0.09 times). These data qualify treating a beta-enriched fraction as an already assembled tri-hormonal product. Blueprint lines 245-247 explicitly separate lineage sorting and controlled input reaggregation, including measured achieved composition and mixture comparisons. The study gives no textual absolute fractions, alpha/delta functional comparison, or direct 60:30:10 test; it neither contradicts nor validates that reference. Incorporation of these exact source-specific ratios is unestablished.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (SC-islet graft functional bioassay in immunodeficient NSG mice)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0298:L3 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O13,O14,O15,O16,O17 | text_sha256=edc1beb58d2af486d4a193169b6cc95d01c08a43859a16d19a607fa0013e1301]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M disruption and PD-L1 immune-evasion components)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O6, O12, O18, O20-O21 and O24-O29 support lower immunogenicity on specified readouts after combined B2M editing plus PD-L1 overexpression in canine MSC-derived cells. O23 and O30-O33 retain nulls and differentiation-associated immunosuppression loss. This supports component plausibility, not sufficiency of a human hPSC-islet cloak: canine grafts co-transplanted companion ADSCs, assay host species is unspecified for spleen/peritoneal tests, and no single-edit arms identify marginal contributions. Blueprint sections 4.1 and 4.3 contain B2M disruption and PD-L1 respectively, but incorporation of these specific canine effects is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (residual NK and macrophage infiltration under the combined edit)
edges.claim_summary: O13, O16, O17 and O19 show delayed glycemic relapse with lower but persistent NK/macrophage graft-site infiltration and inflammatory cytokines in edited canine cell grafts. Day-80 site sampling used one dog per group, not six independent dogs per local assay. These counts are not NK killing or macrophage phagocytosis assays; no selective NK perturbation, missing-self causal test, or test of the Blueprint HLA-E/CD47 constructs is supplied. The frozen Blueprint section 1.2/4.1 specifies those innate barriers; these data neither isolate the relapse mechanism nor establish coverage of human innate subsets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularized graft site) / M5 (cell retention and fail-safe scope)
edges.claim_summary: O34 documents a vascularized canine scaffold pouch after a 30-day preparation interval; O35-O36 document subsequent cluster dispersion and migration into surrounding fat at Day 50. O13-O15 report function/expression in this site but cannot attribute efficacy to prevascularization because all groups shared preparation and there was no non-prevascularized comparator. Migration qualifies extrapolation from a local pouch to complete graft containment/removal; no explant completeness or 72-hour oxygen measurement is supplied. Blueprint section 1.2 requires a prevascularized retrievable site; frozen ranker en_bloc_retrieval_and_cell_retention_gate (lines 5979-5982) separately requires >=0.99 recovery with lower 95% CI >=0.99 and <10^-6 extra-capsular shedding. Specific incorporation of this canine migration result is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (lineage purity assessment and off-target control)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3, O8 and the CK19+ component of O6 support the existing Gate1 requirement to characterize lineage purity and control off-target cells in SC-islet differentiation. The already-accounted-for designation applies to that general requirement explicitly stated in the frozen Blueprint (section 1.2 Gate1 and section 6 Step 1), not to adoption of this protocol or its specific percentages. The abstract gives no common stage/denominator for the marker fractions and tests no off-target-removal intervention; O1 co-marker positivity alone establishes neither exclusive purity nor dynamic GSIS.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (candidate Vertical-Wheel suspension manufacturing route)
edges.claim_summary: O4 and O5 motivate evaluating Vertical-Wheel suspension differentiation as a manufacturing option: the abstract reports higher cell yield and an 88.8% cost reduction, while density units differ and the cost basis is unspecified. Transfer of these results from the reported healthy-donor iPSC protocol to the Blueprint edited, purified 60:30:10 product is unvalidated; the abstract provides no numerical GSIS, matched purity or post-purification yield. The frozen references do not establish adoption of this specific route or its numerical gains, so incorporation remains unknown rather than being inferred from keyword absence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-β-cell expansion and maturation lever: SPOCK2 loss or recombinant MMP2)
edges.claim_summary: MMP2 culture and SPOCK2 perturbation support a candidate SC-β-cell expansion/function hypothesis: reported cell-number and composition changes (O11/O12), total-cell-normalized secretion (O14), and immunodeficient-mouse function (O15/O17/O19). O11 leaves the 172% reference denominator unresolved; O15 has a C-peptide-versus-insulin label conflict. Adult primary-islet proliferation did not increase detectably (O18), and JNK inhibition attenuated the SC-β-cell effect (O21). Blueprint §1.2 and §6 require product-specific lineage/function/yield qualification; incorporation of this particular expansion mechanism is not established by the inspected passages.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (GSIS and maturation benchmarks against primary islets)
edges.claim_summary: SPOCK2-KD improves static secretion/SI against WT (O5/O6); authors describe primary-islet similarity for secretion and SI (O7/O22), and graft analyte similarity is reported with an unresolved label conflict (O16). These are not demonstrated equivalence or proof of Blueprint §1.2 dynamic first/second phase GSIS, <3 min low-glucose shut-off, regulated glucagon, or edited 60:30:10 product performance. The frozen ranker Gate1 branch likewise represents maturation assumptions, not this paper’s numeric effect estimates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M6 (TXNIP transcript association; intrinsic-protection transfer unresolved)
edges.claim_summary: TXNIP expression is lower in SPOCK2-KO scRNA-seq (O8), with other maturation-associated transcription changes. This does not manipulate TXNIP or measure cytokine, hypoxic, ER-stress, or survival resistance. Blueprint §6 X5 directly varies TXNIP wild type versus knockout; the correlative transcript result does not validate that intervention or its Gate4 protection. Claim-specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic stress resilience; enteroviral infection is not among the listed stressors)
edges.claim_summary: CVB1 killed EndoC-βH1 cells in a dose-dependent way (O17), was amplified in iPSC-derived islet-like cells (O8), and induced no IFNβ or ISG response in infected EndoC-βH1 cells (O14, O15). The cheatsheet's Gate4 stress list (hypoxia, nutrient, ER/oxidative, cytokines) does not name viral infection, so this scopes Gate4; evidence is in vitro in a fetal-like line and dispersed iPSC islet-like cells only, with no graft, immune or in vivo context.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 / M3 (murine MHC-depleted, Cd47-high allograft survival)
edges.claim_summary: Murine B2m/H2-Ab1 knockout plus Cd47 overexpression is associated with absent measured anti-HIP cellular/DSA responses and 29-day primary-islet graft function in fully allogeneic BALB/c recipients (O10-O19, O21-O22). Blueprint sections 4.1-4.2 and ranker Gate2A already include the analogous human B2M/CIITA/CD47 architecture, but incorporation of this specific short-term mouse result is not established. H2-Ab1 deletion differs from CIITA deletion; no recurrent-autoimmune challenge, long-term durability or exact human product qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (scope of Cd47 expression and ADCC evidence)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports approximately 45-fold HIP Cd47 MFI over isotype, not absolute molecules/cell. O13 and O22 show no measured NK ADCC against HIP islets in recovered-serum assays that also lacked detectable corresponding DSAs (O11/O19); they do not isolate missing-self resistance or causal Cd47 protection. The supplied experiments contain no macrophage phagocytosis or direct missing-self endpoint; Discussion attributes prior direct innate protection to reference 17. These mouse data do not satisfy Blueprint section 1.2/4.1 or Graveyard 009 Hour-0 human NK/macrophage and absolute-density requirements.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (primary murine islet graft endocrine function)
edges.claim_summary: O16 reports diabetes treatment in all HIP-islet recipients with fasting glucose stably below 200 mg/dL after 14 days through the 29-day study, and O17 reports restored C-peptide at day 29. This supports short-term function of primary mouse islet allografts; it does not establish human SC-islet differentiation, tri-hormonal mixture optimization, biphasic GSIS or low-glucose shutoff required by Blueprint section 1.2. M3 is retained for the in-vivo graft model; these primary islets do not justify M2.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (B2M KO ablating classical HLA-A/B/C; IFN-inducible HLA-B presentation)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoantigen panel: PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8, IA-2)
edges.claim_summary: Gate2B lists PPI, GAD65, IGRP, ZnT8 and IA-2 as autoantigens, yet the β-cell HLA-I immunopeptidome was dominated by granule proteins (CHGA, INS, SCG5, KIF1A, MAP1B), known antigens such as ZnT8, GAD2 and IAPP were underrepresented and IGRP absent, IFN-α added PTM and spliced epitopes (O3-O5), and islet-infiltrating T-cell lines from HLA-B40+ T1D donors reacted to HLA-B40 granule-peptide pools (O17). This scopes the Gate2B antigen panel as incomplete; evidence is from a β-cell line, non-diabetic islets and HLA-B40+ donors, not SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (late endocrine-progenitor differentiation and beta-cell identity; imeglimin maturation hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: In one human iPSC line, imeglimin exposure during late endocrine specification and extended culture did not show a secretion gain over Vehicle (O3/O5/O7), while RNA-seq generally increased mature beta-cell identity markers (O9). This supports a testable Gate1/M2 maturation-additive hypothesis, not demonstrated functional improvement or Blueprint manufacturing equivalence: the frozen Blueprint requires dynamic biphasic GSIS, rapid shutoff and a specified lineage composition. Maximal OCR (O13) does not establish lower basal oxygen demand; no ranker prior or graveyard rule is recalibrated. Exact claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (cytokine stress resilience of SC-islet cells)
edges.claim_summary: TNF-α + IFN-γ at 10 ng/mL each during Day 16–22 impaired INS expression (O14), and cMet further reduced it (O20). cImeg was described as Vehicle-like for INS expression (O15; no equivalence test) and contrasted favorably with cMet for KCl-responsive C-peptide secretion (O18), while its C-peptide-positive cell fraction was lower than Cytokine or cMet (O16/O17). This is a justified bridge to Gate4's cytokine-dedifferentiation concern, qualified by the developmental exposure and mixed endpoints; no mature graft-survival, granzyme, hypoxic or triple-cytokine protection was tested. Exact incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; diffusion-limited slab physics)
edges.claim_summary: In MIN6 alginate constructs with perfusion channels the viability radius was 0.55 ± 0.02 mm at 40 × 10^6 cells/mL and 140 mmHg, fell to 0.28 ± 0.01 mm at 40 mmHg, rose to 1.04 ± 0.06 mm at 10 × 10^6 cells/mL, and implied a critical oxygen tension near 1 mmHg (O3-O6). This gives measured density- and tension-dependence of diffusion-limited necrosis, bridged to hPSC islets by physics only because MIN6 is a rodent line.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 and Gate4 (human-islet oxygen limits at venous tension in thick, dense constructs)
edges.claim_summary: A model with literature-derived human-islet parameters gave a theoretical viability radius of 0.625 mm at a 20 mmHg cutoff (40 × 10^6 cells/mL, 140 mmHg perfusate) falling to 0.155 mm at 40 mmHg (O18), qualifying how thick or dense a diffusion- or channel-fed construct can be at venous oxygen. Model-only; the sole human-islet experiment was n = 1 (O16, O17).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (pre-in-vivo qualification of oxygenated device designs)
edges.claim_summary: The paper proposes its perfusion platform (CFD plus oxygen-transport model, real-time GFP imaging, at-line GSIS sampling) to de-risk bioartificial pancreas designs before in vivo work (O3-O9, O13); this could be tested as a pre-in-vivo gate for oxygen-bridge devices. Evidence is limited to MIN6 constructs cultured 2 to 7 days.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization route to oxygen supply; prevascularized device)
edges.claim_summary: A pre-vascularized iEC/lung-ECM scaffold carrying SC-islets restored normoglycemia in all transplanted diabetic NSG mice within 29 days (median 14 ± 1.9 days) vs 2 out of 13 for device-less ViβeSs, with graft vessels perfusable at 13 weeks (O9, O10, O18). Immunodeficient hosts and a xenogeneic rat-lung scaffold make this a bridge, not a direct test of the avascular oxygen bridge.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet functional maturation; dynamic GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: Within 7 days, SC-islets in a perfused vascularized ECM showed higher dynamic insulin release than batch-matched ViβeSs (peak AUC 8.352 ± 1.386 vs 5.527 ± 0.4257; O6, O7), suggesting iEC co-culture plus ECM and perfusion as a maturation adjunct. In vitro, commercial cells, no stimulation index reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (beta cell survival around transplant)
edges.claim_summary: Standard-culture SC-islets kept only 37.16% ± 10.38% live cells at day 7 (O1) and estimated beta cell death was 62.84% ± 10.38% vs 14.80% ± 9.11% in iVEP (O8), indicating substantial attrition that a perfused vascularized niche reduced. Death was measured by miR-375 release in vitro, not under graft hypoxia.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (RNLS cytoprotection; genetic perturbation versus PG pharmacology)
edges.claim_summary: NIT-1 Rnlsmut has increased glycolytic transcripts/ECAR and 2-DG-sensitive viability protection (O8, O10, O11), whereas PG fails to phenocopy the same metabolism and has hepatic MAO-B activity (O12, O13, O20); human KO did not show a significant apoptosis benefit in the stated single-stressor assay (O18). RNLS is already an optional Blueprint X6 modifier, so this is not a new target; incorporation of the specific 2-DG-dependent mechanism and PG-versus-genetic distinction is not established by the frozen references. Human exact-product cytoprotection remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (RNLS, Stage-6 sc-beta differentiation/function); Gate5 oxygen-demand precaution context
edges.claim_summary: This human SC-cell model retained poor static planar GSIS with WT and RNLS KO/PG (O17), while RNLS KO raised OCR in aggregates but not planar cells (O16). The RNLS metabolic precaution is already explicit in Blueprint GRAVEYARD_004/§6 X6, ranker Gate1 precaution and planned dynamic-perifusion comparison, and graveyard rule 004. The references call GSIS dynamic/aggregate, but actual packet Methods specify static planar GSIS; no KO-specific GSIS decrement, measured hypoxic harm, Stage-7 rescue, or cluster-size rescue is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TNFAIP3/A20 and HMOX1 cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: O3, O5-O8: co-aggregation of porcine islet cells with human BOECs reduced cell death and raised porcine HMOX1 (3.1 and 1.9-fold) and A20 (1.7 and 2.8-fold), the Gate4 effectors, but only as expression changes in porcine neonatal cells; protection by A20 or HMOX1 itself was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / Gate4 / M1 (INS-P rs3842752 seed-line hypothesis, ER stress and neoantigen-load rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O2-O8 and O15-O18 support a mechanistic rationale in primary-islet material and HEK293T/K562 surrogates for the INS-P seed-line hypothesis explicitly listed in frozen ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:125 (PMID:40112799). Frozen rank_islet1_stacks.py:4213-4215 already requires independent allele identity/direction and functional qualification; this incorporation is a Stage-0 hypothesis, not adopted or validated immune protection. No edited SC-islets, recipient APC response, immune killing or unrelated-immunity preservation were tested. GRAVEYARD_010 retains the residual indirect-APC warning even for INS-edited designs; the separately modeled INS leader/DRiP-initiation edit is not the rs3842752 intervention.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (primary-islet functional comparator and static-SI metrology limits)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O14 show that donor-genotype groups can differ in absolute secretion and metabolic bioassay timing while reported static stimulation indices and reversal rates remain similar. O19 and O21-O23 add nested single-donor descriptions, not independent replication. A static 2.8-to-28 mM assay cannot qualify the frozen Blueprint Gate1 dynamic biphasic response and <3-min shut-off after a 16.7-to-2.8 mM step-down (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61). Higher basal secretion is not inherently favorable; NOD SCID reversal among responders is not immune survival. Claim-specific incorporation of genotype-sensitive comparator/metrology limits is unknown. M7 denotes this measured proxy boundary; M2 is not used because no SC-islet differentiation, purification, mixture or maturation was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (assay kinetics; prospective M2 SC-islet maturation readout)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O11/O14-O18 support a candidate single-hESC-islet C-peptide readout: tracer equilibration must match residence time because the same KCl-evoked secretion gives antibody- and pearl-dependent normalized signals. The measured domain is M7 assay metrology; preparation of stage-7 hESC-islets is context, not a tested M2 differentiation, purification, mixture or maturation intervention. A prospective M2 maturation readout would require bridging this assay to the frozen Blueprint Gate1 biphasic glucose response and low-glucose shut-off requirements with glucose-waveform validation, which this packet does not supply. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 (line 61), ranker primary_readouts (lines 5800-5812), and GRAVEYARD_003 (lines 61-83) establish the dynamic-function context, but do not establish adoption status for this particular FAIA; incorporation remains unknown. Bounded semantic verification is not Gate1 or product qualification.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet purification and manufacturing)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4: the abstract claims a scalable, cytoarchitecture-preserving density-gradient enrichment of SC-islet clusters as an alternative to antibody-based single-cell sorting, so it could be tested as a purification step beside CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment at Gate1. All support is qualitative abstract text (no purity, function or yield numbers), and the cheatsheet lists CD49a/ITGA1 enrichment but no density-gradient step.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic stress resilience of SC-beta cells; ZNT8-mediated zinc transport and the integrated stress response)
edges.claim_summary: O5/O6 and O10/O13-O16 support a candidate intrinsic-stress hypothesis: ZNT8 deletion protected WFS1-deficient SC-beta cells, while low-dose anisomycin reduced human SC-beta/islet stress-apoptosis readouts. This bounded Gate4/M1 mechanism matches intrinsic cytoprotection, not adaptive or innate immune evasion. The protective genetic-loss experiment is WFS1-deficient; WT ZNT8-knockout add-back experiments separately test zinc transport. Anisomycin remains an optimization-stage hit; no exact-product transplantation, dynamic GSIS or immune challenge establishes adoption. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and ranker ER/autoantigen modules plus Decision Experiment 5 recognize stress/function tradeoffs and SLC30A8 testing, but do not establish incorporation of this specific WFS1/low-dose-anisomycin mechanism; incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-beta cell identity and yield under stage-7 stress)
edges.claim_summary: O4/O8/O11/O12 support a Gate1/M2 manufacturing hypothesis in WFS1-deficient stage-7 cultures: improved INS+NKX6.1+ fraction or INS reporter/transcript expression. These identity/fraction/omics readouts do not show dynamic GSIS, insulin content, secretion, mature function or absolute manufactured yield. Transfer to the frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 tri-hormonal/function contract is a justified bridge, pending function-under-protection tests; ranker Decision Experiment 5 explicitly includes an SLC30A8 allelic series, so novelty cannot be inferred from keyword absence and incorporation of this specific mechanism is unknown. The study does not overturn GRAVEYARD_007, which blocks a high-pLI multiplex stack rather than this isolated perturbation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A + Gate3 / M1 (B2M-/- CIITA-/- plus CD47 hypoimmune stack)
edges.claim_summary: Bounded support for the class rationale of MHC-I/II depletion plus recipient-compatible CD47 already specified in Blueprint §§4.1-4.2: HIP* endothelial assays showed no direct T/NK/macrophage or ADCC/CDC killing (O1-O4, O10, O20), while wt ADCC/CDC persisted (O5). This is not exact-product validation: human-to-macaque xenogeneic targets express macaque CD47, cynomolgus groups received a common multi-drug regimen, wt direct NK/macrophage assays also showed no reactivity (Fig6C-D), and O19 shows residual ABO/Rh antibody-mediated CDC vulnerability. Blueprint Stage5 already mentions ABO type-O compatibility for co-transplanted iECs; the paper-specific Rh(D) boundary is not established as incorporated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate panel beyond NK and macrophage: PMN cytotoxicity, CD99/CD200)
edges.claim_summary: Consider a Gate3 PMN challenge and CD99+CD200 research hypothesis: activated human PMNs killed allogeneic human wt/HIP endothelial targets (O21), and CD99+CD200 protected pig ECs against human PMNs while wt.99.200 remained susceptible to primed PBMCs (O17-O18; Fig8E-F). PMN inhibition accompanied HIP* BLI persistence and later PMN recovery (O11-O12), without a concurrent untreated HIP* cynomolgus control; authors considered the drug regimen too toxic for translation. Transfer to SC-islets and durable in vivo engineered-graft protection is unvalidated. Incorporation is unknown: the frozen ranker already contains membrane CD200 in an unscored complement/indirect-APC wildcard, which does not establish adoption of this PMN/CD99+CD200 mechanism.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (clonogenic fail-safe; residual pluripotent cells in hypoimmune grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O15 is a qualitative reminder of residual-pluripotent-cell safety: early teratoma areas occurred at both sampled wt and HIP* endothelial injection sites at day 10, with incomplete differentiation suggested rather than directly quantified. The broad need for pan-lineage residual-PSC control is already explicit in Blueprint §§1.2,4.4,7 and GRAVEYARD_002, and the ranker whole-product safety model includes the vascular compartment. This paper tests no iCasp9 construct, AP1903 regimen, escape threshold or SC-islet product; it neither demonstrates fail-safe efficacy nor proves a genotype-specific increase in tumor risk.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation; off-target enterochromaffin (SC-EC) cells)
edges.claim_summary: RFX3 loss in a single human iPSC background reduced endocrine markers and INS+/NKX6.1+ cell percentages, increased EC markers, and impaired static 20 mmol/l glucose-stimulated secretion; RFX3 overexpression in KO cells reversed some dysregulated mRNAs in PPs/EPs (O1-O13, O18). This supports testing RFX3 timing or level as a differentiation hypothesis, not a proven WT gain-of-function upgrade. Frozen Blueprint Gate1 already requires lineage-specific QC, EC depletion and dynamic GSIS (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:61,245; rank_islet1_stacks.py:5602-5613); incorporation of this specific RFX3 hypothesis is unknown. No EC depletion fraction, dynamic functional rescue or exact edited-product benefit is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (SC-islet developmental apoptosis and TXNIP association)
edges.claim_summary: Elevated TXNIP protein co-occurred with more Annexin V+ cells and smaller RFX3 KO organoids, while BrdU proliferation showed no reported difference (O14-O17). This provides supportive developmental association relevant to intrinsic apoptosis, with a bridge from differentiation failure to Gate4 stress resilience; TXNIP causality and benefit of its inhibition were not tested. Frozen Blueprint and ranker already include a TXNIP WT/KO redox factor (ISLET-1-BLUEPRINT.md:209; rank_islet1_stacks.py:4761-4768), but incorporation of this RFX3-specific association is unknown. No cytokine/hypoxia challenge, transplant survival or immune-protection result is inferred.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (TXNIP and ER-stress/cytokine resilience as an intrinsic cytoprotection edit)
edges.claim_summary: TXNIP-/- hESC-derived SC-islets gave no measurable gain over TXNIP+/+ islets in viability or composition in vitro (O8, O9) or in glycaemia, C-peptide, GTT and GSIS after engraftment (O13-O16), and the IFN-STAT1 data are internally contradictory (O11, O12). A TXNIP edit therefore showed no benefit without a stress or immune challenge, and TXNIP-/- HLCs had reduced BiP under thapsigargin (O7); NOD-SCID hosts and one cell line limit this.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (proliferation of edited undifferentiated hPSCs; Cas12a off-target check)
edges.claim_summary: TXNIP-/- H1-hESCs showed increased colony-forming proliferation (O3) without a viability change, so a TXNIP cytoprotection edit may raise the proliferative potential of residual undifferentiated cells, relevant to the clonogenic fail-safe; Sanger sequencing of predicted off-target sites found no unintended mutations (O2). Teratoma formation was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette)
edges.claim_summary: In human islets TYK2 inhibition blocked IFNalpha-induced CXCL10 (O4) and repressed CD274/PD-L1 mRNA (O11), and in RIP-LCMV-GP beta cells it lowered Cd274 and Cxcl10 mRNA at day 7 (O18). A cytokine-inducible CXCL10-locus PD-L1/SERPINB9 cassette would depend on IFN-TYK2 signalling, so co-therapy with a TYK2 inhibitor could blunt its induction; the engineered cassette was not tested and the native genes were measured in islets, EndoC cells and mouse beta cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (IFN-driven HLA class I and B2M upregulation, CD8 T cell recognition)
edges.claim_summary: In human islets and EndoC-betaH1/HLA-A2 cells IFNalpha raised HLA-ABC and B2M (O5, O6) and surface HLA-A/B/C (O7), and blocking this reduced HLA-A2 alloreactive CD8 T cell activation (O8), consistent with HLA class I display driving CD8 recognition of inflamed beta cells. Primary human islets and a beta cell line, not SC-islet grafts or B2M-edited cells.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (IFN-driven autoreactive T cell pressure on beta cells; pharmacological adjunct)
edges.claim_summary: TYK2 inhibition reduced activation of insulin- and preproinsulin-directed autoreactive T cells against IFNalpha-treated beta cells (O9, O10) and delayed diabetes with less insulitis in two mouse models (O15-O17). Hypothesis: a short course of TYK2 inhibitor could be tested as an adjunct against recurrent autoimmunity in hypoimmune grafts, weighed against the possible loss of PD-L1/CXCL10 induction (see the Gate4 link); not tested with SC-islet grafts, and mouse results do not transfer directly.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1-M2 (intrinsic cytoprotection under peri-transplant hypoxia; survival-oriented BCL2/XIAP, A20, MANF, TXNIP set)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O4, O7-O9: at 5% and 2% O2 the SC-beta INShigh share fell from 51% (21% O2) to 17% and 3%, and GSIS was impaired, while the paper reports no change in cell counts (minimal cell death). The hypoxic failure mode here is loss of beta-cell identity and function rather than loss of cells, which survival-type readouts alone would miss; the cheatsheet Gate4 baseline does not state this failure mode. In vitro SC-islets, scRNA-seq without replicates.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; chronic post-bridge hypoxia)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O5, O6: GSIS was impaired after 1 week at 5% O2 (the paper equates 5% with subcutaneous pO2) and lost after 1 week at 2% O2 (n = 8), so oxygen-limited graft conditions that persist beyond a short bridge can degrade SC-beta identity and function. The earliest functional readout is 1 week and no device or oxygen-carrier was tested, so the 72-hour window itself is not assessed; the cheatsheet states the 72-hour target but not this chronic-hypoxia consequence.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (inducible cytoprotection set; EDN3 not in cheatsheet baseline)
edges.claim_summary: O14-O18: lentiviral EDN3 overexpression kept about 40% of SC-beta cells insulin-high vs 14% in controls after 4 weeks at 2% O2, preserved IAPP/ITGA1 and 2% O2 GSIS (n = 5), and raised insulin expression in 1-week NSG grafts (n = 2). EDN3 is a candidate identity-preserving Gate4 element, untested in a hypoimmune stack, with no in vivo function or diabetes-reversal data; the authors state engraftment benefit is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization component; prevascularized graft)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10, O12: with a suboptimal SC-islet dose (about 0.4 million cells), 3 of 6 mice with pre-vascularized grafts vs 1 of 5 with non-vascularized grafts showed glucose reduction at 19 weeks, with higher human C-peptide and more SC-beta cell contact with basement membrane proteins. No pO2 or oxygen readout was made and O11 shows vasculature wraps but rarely penetrates SC-islets, so this supports pre-vascularization as a graft strategy rather than as a tested oxygen bridge; small n.

edges.claim_summary: O5-O8 and O10-O13 provide bounded human SC-islet manufacturing/function evidence: marker denominators and abstract purity remain unresolved, residual SLC18A1 is measured among CPPT+ cells, and the dynamic secretion peak remains below adult islets. The frozen Blueprint (lines 61,244-247) requires lineage-qualified purity and dynamic secretion/shut-off; this study does not establish those complete release endpoints or an optimal 60:30:10 mixture. Exact adoption of this dataset is not established by the reviewed references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (vascularization component of the oxygen bridge; pre-vascularized subcutaneous graft site)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O7, O12: a bFGF-loaded CGS pre-vascularized site gave 93.8% (15 of 16) engraftment of 200 syngeneic mouse islets at 100 days vs 0 of 4 with CGS alone, with higher capillary area fraction, and did not differ significantly from the bFGF-loaded agarose rod (P = 0.169) or IPTx (P = 0.328). Supports pre-vascularization as an engraftment lever, but with primary mouse islets in an immunocompetent syngeneic host, no oxygen or pO2 readout (the authors flag oxygenation as open) and a 2-week lead time, so it does not test the Blueprint 72-hour avascular bridge or hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (inflammatory cytokine resilience; TNF-alpha and IL-1beta exposure; extrinsic anti-inflammatory adjunct to the TNFAIP3/A20 set)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O4: an anti-TNF-alpha antisense nanoparticle reduced TNF-alpha in macrophages in vitro and protected stem-cell-derived islets in a diabetic mouse model compared with PLG NPs alone, with reduced Tnfα and Il1β expression. Hypothesis that a transient extrinsic TNF-alpha knockdown could supplement the cell-intrinsic Gate4 elements during the early post-transplant window; the abstract gives no magnitudes, n, host strain or time course, and the cheatsheet Gate4 baseline lists only cell-intrinsic elements.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytoprotective pre-transplant conditioning; adult primary islets and EndoC-betaH1 evidence)
edges.claim_summary: LIP pre-conditioning is associated with lower graft apoptosis and higher fasting/stimulated human insulin in female immunodeficient recipients (O3, O5, O7, O9-O10, O13, O21, O26). This supports a cytoprotection strategy class relevant to Blueprint §1.2 Gate4; it does not test the engineered SC-islet product, a defined cytokine/hypoxia challenge, or establish specific LIP incorporation. Frozen ranker Gate4 modules/prior branches concern other mechanisms; cocktail adoption cannot be established from this bounded comparison.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (recipient-sex and endpoint/time scope of subcutaneous pre-conditioning results)
edges.claim_summary: Female recipients showed sustained reported benefits, whereas male LIP results include a nonsignificant apoptosis trend (O4), nondetected area/stimulated-insulin differences (O11-O12, O14), and a transient 2-week fasting-insulin increase (O22-O23). These endpoint-specific observations constrain transfer; absence of reported formal sex-by-treatment interaction prevents claiming a proven universal sex mechanism. The specific boundary incorporation is unknown; TNF expression/enrichment does not establish mediation.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (candidate LIP/LIPHS conditioning of engineered SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: LIPHS increased stimulated insulin relative to LIP in male recipients of adult primary islets (O18); a separate barcode assay reported enhanced cell-survival activity (O17). Combined RAC1/PLK1/UNG CRISPR-a findings (O15, O19) are distinct perturbation evidence, not validation that the cocktail acts solely through those genes. Results/Discussion explicitly leave hPSC-derived islet-organoid benefit untested. M1 denotes the proposed cytoprotection intervention; M2 maturation was not tested. Frozen Blueprint/ranker/graveyard do not establish adoption of these specific cocktails, so incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M3 (SC-islet maturation and graft function after in vivo engraftment)
edges.claim_summary: H1 hESC-derived SC-islets in NSG mice lowered blood glucose to below 5.6 mmol/l by 3 months and matured metabolically, e.g. citrate labelling 12% to 28.7% and mitochondrial number 0.38 to 0.67 per µm2 (O1, O3, O4, O9, O10, O14). These time-resolved values are not stated in the cheatsheet; MafA stayed below human islets at M1 (O18).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2, M7 (pyruvate reactivity and MCT1 as SC-islet maturity and failure-mode readouts)
edges.claim_summary: Pre-engraftment SC-islets showed a pyruvate-to-glucose secretion ratio of 2.1 that fell to 0.5 at M4, alongside loss of membrane MCT1 (O15, O16, O17); a pyruvate challenge and MCT1 readout could be added to Gate1 pre-transplant maturity checks, because glucose-only perifusion would not flag this. The cheatsheet lists glucose perifusion and stimulated C-peptide benchmarks only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (elimination of off-target enterochromaffin cells)
edges.claim_summary: Enterochromaffin-like cells stayed at approximately 4% after engraftment (O7), so in vivo maturation does not remove them, consistent with the Blueprint's need to eliminate SC-EC cells before transplant. The persistence figure rests on an ESM panel not in the packet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (safe-harbor transgene-expression stability during hPSC-to-SC-islet differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: EF1α-driven CCL22-GFP at CLYBL showed 20.5% ± 2.09% GFP+ cells and progressive GFP loss with passaging, interpreted as suggesting silencing (O5-O6; CCL22-expression decline also in Results). This supports checking construct-specific expression stability. Frozen Blueprint §4.4 and ranker shared-promoter failure gates already address silencing risk, but incorporation of this exact CLYBL finding is unestablished; it does not demonstrate failure of the insulated 230-bp native EEF1A1-core/AAVS1-iCasp9 construct or measure clonogenic escape. No promoter-sequence equivalence or suicide-switch activity was tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation and endocrine function after CCL22 knock-in)
edges.claim_summary: The tested WA01-derived CCL22 lines differentiated to SC-islets, with no statistically detected differences in selected marker/normalized secretion readouts and with detectable graft-derived human C-peptide (O1-O4, O14-O15, O18, O21); PDX1 was higher (O2). This is bounded feasibility/compatibility evidence rather than equivalence, noninferiority, or qualification of the Blueprint product. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 requires dynamic biphasic GSIS and rapid shut-off; ranker co-primary Gate1 endpoints are dynamic SI >= 3.0 and shut-off <= 3 min, which these static secretion/homing experiments do not establish. Specific study incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (Siglec-sialic acid inhibitory axis as a possible addition beside HLA-E/NKG2A and CD47/SIRPalpha)
edges.claim_summary: Abstract-level, qualitative evidence that human-like α2,8 disialic acid on porcine endothelial cells enhances Siglec binding and reduces complement activation and cytotoxicity (O1-O3, O6). The cheatsheet's Gate3 elements list HLA-E and CD47 only; the abstract itself suggests application to human iPSC-derived islets, which was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (inhibitory-ligand route to reduce CTL killing, complementary to B2M and CIITA knockouts)
edges.claim_summary: ST8Sia6-expressing porcine cells showed reduced CTL-targeted killing with lower CD107a, perforin and IFN-γ (O4, O5), a Siglec/ITIM-linked effect that could be tested as an adjunct on hPSC-derived islets. The abstract reports correlations only, in porcine cells, with no quantities.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (local tolerance for allograft survival without systemic immunosuppression in a subrenal-capsule mouse graft)
edges.claim_summary: Prolonged graft survival, sustained insulin secretion and restored normoglycemia are claimed with local nanoparticles and no systemic immunosuppression (O3-O5). This is consistent with a Gate2A goal of protection without systemic drugs, but the abstract gives no figures and uses mouse allogeneic islets, not hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-IgV-GPI / SIRPalpha engagement, Locus 1)
edges.claim_summary: O1–O3 establish mouse kidney mismatch/recipient-CD47 perturbation effects, and O9/O12/O19–O21 associate human B→A SIRPA mismatch with adverse kidney outcomes. This is donor SIRPα engaging recipient CD47, not a direct test of engineered graft CD47 engaging host SIRPα, and does not show CD47 overexpression is harmful or fails in SC-islets. The bounded qualification that protection must be checked across SIRPA variants is already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate3 and §4.1 (PMID:40668892; V1/V2 pre-pilot), ranker primary_readouts and Decision Experiment #1, and GRAVEYARD_009 genotype-spanning assays; the kidney HRs are not validated SC-islet parameters.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M4 (recipient SIRPA genotype as covariate in CD47-based hypoimmune SC-islet trials)
edges.claim_summary: O9/O12/O15/O19–O24 support the rationale for existing SIRPA recipient/immune-donor genotype stratification. Frozen Blueprint Stage5 explicitly lists SIRPA V1/V2 typing citing PMID:40668892; §4.1 and ranker myeloid panel already predeclare genotype-spanning assays. This is a research rationale: kidney transplantation under systemic immunosuppression (UPMC 87.5% corticosteroid-free maintenance, not immunosuppression-free) provides no direct SC-islet efficacy evidence; 5-year Northwestern estimates remain imprecise (O16). The applicability is unvalidated_transfer because neither a predictive genotype effect nor treatment benefit has been demonstrated for SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 / M4 (exploratory paired donor-line/recipient SIRPA A/B mismatch annotation)
edges.claim_summary: Retain the untested part of the original second link separately: explore paired hPSC-line and recipient SIRPA A/B mismatch annotation when studying CD47-based grafts, motivated by the kidney donor-recipient mismatch associations (O9/O12/O19–O24). Existing frozen references establish recipient/immune-donor V1/V2 typing but do not establish adoption of this exact donor-line A/B mismatch covariate; incorporation is unknown. Explicitly map the paper A/B groups to project assay nomenclature and establish relevant SIRPα expression/topology before transfer. No SC-islet predictive utility, altered graft design, contraindication to CD47 overexpression or treatment benefit is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (hypoxic exposure, assay timing and insulin-content normalization)
edges.claim_summary: O14 and O16 show lower high-glucose insulin secretion and total insulin content after 48 hours at 1% O2 in primary donor islets; O17 reports no significant effect after content normalization. Assays followed exposure under normoxia without TCDD, and neither viability, later recovery nor protective conditioning was established. This is a bounded bridge to hypoxic-stress assessment, not qualification of the exact engineered SC-islet product. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and §4 post-bridge recovery already require stress resilience and distinguish survival from function, but incorporation of this specific 48-hour exposure and normalization result is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet MAFA maturity marker and model-specific GSIS competence)
edges.claim_summary: O5 shows reduced MAFA mRNA under hypoxia in the day-50+ INS-2A-EGFP WA01 SC-islet model. O14/O17 are primary-donor static secretion findings; Methods explicitly excludes SC-islets from GSIS because their glucose responsiveness was limited in this laboratory. These endpoints qualify transfer to Blueprint §1.2 MAFA-positive maturity and dynamic biphasic GSIS criteria; they do not demonstrate SC-islet functional rescue, failure of a qualified exact product, or a dynamic shut-off result. Incorporation of this model-specific combination is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (HMOX1 and MNSOD hypoxic transcriptional response versus cytoprotection)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O6 show HMOX1 (~24-fold) and MNSOD mRNA induction in SC-islets; O11 separately reports HMOX1 induction or trends in primary donor islets (prose 2.2–5.0-fold, with table/prose minimum discrepancy retained). Donor-islet MNSOD induction was not measured here. These are transcriptional stress responses; the study does not perturb HMOX1/MNSOD to establish protective efficacy, and donor secretion remained impaired before content normalization. They qualify interpretation of intrinsic-resilience claims without supplying a ranker protection coefficient; claim-specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet manufacturing: aggregate size control)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3 and O4 show micropocket hydrogel culture holds SC-islet aggregates at 136 μm (±31 μm SD) versus 275 μm ± 62 μm SD in suspension, with ~50× lower shear and no aggregate loss. Hypothesis: add aggregate-size control as a Gate1 manufacturing parameter; the abstract gives no function, endocrine-composition or yield data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M7 (fusion-driven oxygen limitation as a manufacturing failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O5 report that stochastic fusion grows suspension aggregates (114 to 275 μm) and can cause chronic oxygen limitation during differentiation, a failure mode of conventional SC-islet production. No oxygen measurements or threshold sizes are in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (cytokine-induced β-cell apoptosis; candidate resilience genes DLK1 and RASGRP1)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (oxidative stress and cytokine pathways; HMOX1/SOD2/CAT antioxidant layer)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2 and O18 show cytokine and CVB4 stress engage immune and apoptotic pathways in β cells and that ROS-production pathways are dysregulated in the apoptosis-prone DLK1−/− and RASGRP1−/− cells. This is consistent with an oxidative-stress component of Gate4 cytoprotection, but no antioxidant gene was perturbed in these experiments.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (IFN-driven inflammatory signature in β-cell models)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2 report that IFN signaling and antigen presentation are commonly upregulated across target tissues and that IFNα or IFNγ drive the signature in EndoC-βH1 cells, which supports IFN exposure as a stressor relevant to Gate4 cytokine resilience. The evidence is descriptive, and one cell type is a non-islet thyroid model.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (paracrine architecture, endocrine composition of SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3 and O4 report that PSC-islets reconstructed with all five endocrine subtypes spent far less time below 54 mg/dL (3% vs 59% of measurements) and showed restored counterregulation in diabetic mice, supporting the Gate1 emphasis on non-β paracrine architecture. The cheatsheet does not state this hypoglycemia-protection finding or the ε and γ subtypes.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (composition calibration beyond the β:α:δ reference ratio)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3 suggest that deliberately controlling the relative abundance of all five endocrine subtypes, including ε and γ cells that the cheatsheet β:α:δ reference ratio omits, may calibrate post-transplant hypoglycemia protection; this is a hypothesis drawn from a mouse abstract with no cell fractions, n or p given.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (virus-driven mitochondrial and identity-gene stress in primary human islets)
edges.claim_summary: O8, O10 and O12 show that CVB3 infection of primary human islets lowered INS expression, enlarged β cell mitochondria and altered OCR parameters that the paper reads as mitochondrial dysfunction, while whole-islet ROS did not change (O11). This adds viral infection as a stressor not named in the cheatsheet Gate4 list; it is an in vitro whole-islet result with no graft context.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate3 / M1 (HLA class I and HLA-E responses to viral IFN signaling)
edges.claim_summary: O3 to O6 show that HLA class I and HLA-E transcripts respond to CVB3 infection in a cell-type-specific way in primary human islets (ductal and α cells up, β cells HLA-A and HLA-C down at 48 h), so HLA expression is an infection-responsive axis relevant to the HLA-I and HLA-E edits. Transcript-level data only, with no T-cell or NK assay.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M6 (autoantigen and neoantigen repertoire of β-cells, including nuORF and INS-DRiP peptides)
edges.claim_summary: O2, O3 and O6 report INS-DRiP detection, 965 novel nuORFs in sBCs and HLA-presented, T-cell-tested preproinsulin and nuORF peptides, which suggests that Gate2B autoreactivity testing could include nuORF-derived and DRiP-type epitopes beyond the antigens the cheatsheet lists. The abstract gives no peptide counts or T-cell response values, and the T-cell assays are in vitro.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (HLA class I presentation of β-cell peptides; B2M KO rationale)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O6 indicate that antigen-presentation pathways are translationally regulated in sBCs and that HLA-presented β-cell peptides are immunogenic in coculture, consistent with the HLA class I dependence behind the B2M KO design. The abstract does not test any HLA edit, so this is indirect evidence only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate2B / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible module: JAK/STAT dependence of CXCL10 induction)
edges.claim_summary: The cheatsheet places a CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette at Locus 3. O2, O10 and O17 show that endogenous CXCL10 induction by IFN-α is driven independently by either STAT1 residue in HeLa cells, rises 721% after 24 h with PTPN2 silencing, and falls 97% with Baricitinib in primary islets, so CXCL10-promoter-driven output would depend on JAK/STAT signalling and shift with JAK-inhibitor co-treatment or PTPN2/BACH2 deficiency. Promoter-reporter behaviour was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (ZnT8 autoantigen deletion by SLC30A8 knockout)
edges.claim_summary: The cheatsheet lists ZnT8 among the Gate2B autoreactive-T-cell antigens. O3 and O4 report that humans with complete SLC30A8 loss mostly lacked type 2 diabetes, O16 and O18 show higher CIR30 and disposition index in LoF carriers, and O11 reports no significant MI or liver-enzyme association, which suggests (as a hypothesis) that SLC30A8 knockout in SC-islets could remove the ZnT8 antigen without an obvious function penalty. Caveats: germline loss in adults, a nominal angina association (O10), only two non-diabetic homozygotes in the OGTT analysis, and no immune or SC-islet data.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (insulin secretion capacity of SC-β cells, SLC30A8 as a candidate modulator)
edges.claim_summary: O7, O14, O16 and O18 show higher insulin and a higher corrected insulin response and disposition index in human SLC30A8 LoF carriers, suggesting SLC30A8 loss as a candidate way to raise glucose-stimulated insulin output of SC-β cells; the cheatsheet Gate1 text does not mention SLC30A8. The evidence comes from adult carriers with native islets, and transfer to SC-islets in T1D is unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (off-target enterochromaffin (SC-EC) cell elimination)
edges.claim_summary: NKX2.2 deletion suppresses EC markers and the EC scRNA-seq cluster (O11, O12) but the same deletion nearly abolishes NKX6.1+/INS+ beta-like cells and enlarges the mis-specified ARX+/INS+ population (O13, O14). NKX2.2 is therefore required for EC formation but cannot serve as an EC-removal handle in a beta-cell product; in vitro hESC evidence only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet differentiation; beta-cell identity and polyhormonal off-target fates)
edges.claim_summary: In an hESC-to-SC-islet protocol NKX2.2 loss leaves early PDX1+/NKX6.1+ cells unchanged (O4) but reduces PDX1+/NKX6.1+ and INS+ cells at S6d1 (O5, O6), lowers monohormonal INS+ cells and raises SST+, GHRL+ and polyhormonal cells at S6d14 (O7-O10), supporting NKX2.2 as an EP-stage requirement for beta-like identity (in vitro only).
