edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (alternative or complementary INS-linked surface-marker selection beyond CD49a)
edges.claim_summary: An INS-locus CD19Δ-mScarlet knock-in let MACS raise the mScarlet+ fraction from about 23-46% to about 61–80% (O8) with ∼3.5-fold higher basal and ∼2.5-fold higher total C-peptide secretion and a significantly improved stimulation index (O12-O14); proposes an engineered INS-linked handle as a CD49a alternative, limited by 50% surface display (O4), n=2-4 replicates, immature d25-d35 clusters and CD19/CAR-T regulatory concerns.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (60:30:10 beta:alpha:delta paracrine architecture)
edges.claim_summary: Positive INS-linked selection raised INS but lowered GCG and SST expression in CD19Δ-sorted clusters (O16-O18); if the product target keeps a 60:30:10 alpha/delta fraction, this purity-driven sorting would need alpha/delta add-back. NanoString expression is not cell proportion and no composition counts were reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection: genetic loss-of-function raising survival under ER, cytokine, lipotoxic and oxidative stress)
edges.claim_summary: Sec31A knockdown reduced stress-induced cleaved caspase-3 and improved survival of mouse alphaTC6 cells under TG, tunicamycin, Brefeldin A and cytokines (O3, O4, O6-O8) and a C. elegans UPRER response and survival (O12, O13), showing that a screen-derived COPII loss-of-function can raise stress resilience; the data are from alpha-cell and nematode systems, not beta-cell products.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (transferability of alpha-cell stress-resistance targets to beta cells; Gate1 insulin content)
edges.claim_summary: The Sec31A protective effect was cell-type specific: no survival difference in a mouse beta cell line (O5), SEC31A rose more in human alpha than beta cells under high glucose and cytokines (O15, O16), and SEC31A knockdown in EndoC-βH5 cells left GSIS comparable (O17) but significantly lowered insulin content (O18), so a screen-derived alpha-cell cytoprotective knockout should not be assumed to protect or be neutral in a beta-cell graft; cell-line evidence only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (NK inhibitory ligand axes beyond HLA-E-NKG2A and CD47; DNAM-1/PVR named in Gate3 scope)
edges.claim_summary: High-affinity CD155 (Ala67Thr) on sBC reduced NK cell-mediated lysis to 0.41-fold at 10:1 and NKG2D gMFI to 0.70-fold versus parental sBC, and anti-TIGIT blockade raised lysis 2.47-fold (O16-O18), proposing CD155-TIGIT engagement as a candidate inhibitory ligand to test alongside HLA-E and CD47; untested in combination with HLA-E/CD47, in NKG2A-negative subsets or in vivo, and CD226-Ig binding also rose (O7).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / Gate2B / M1 (checkpoint-ligand T cell suppression, as for inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3; autoreactive PPI-specific killing)
edges.claim_summary: On HLA-intact sBC (HLA-A,B,C still induced by IFN-γ, O8), CD155 Mut lowered allogeneic CD8+ T cell proliferation to 0.84-fold (O10) and PPI-specific lysis to 0.71-fold versus CD155 WT at 10:1 (O12), and protection was lost on TIGIT blockade (O14); these are partial effects in avatar and PBMC co-cultures, not a replacement for MHC-I removal.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet identity and GSIS preserved after genetic engineering)
edges.claim_summary: CAG-driven CD155 knock-in at AAVS1 did not change C-peptide or NKX6.1 frequencies at day 23 (O1, O2) or dynamic GSIS responses (O3) and expression was retained in virtually all modified sBC (O4), in vitro only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (Bri2 BRICHOS anti-IAPP-amyloid candidate cytoprotection perturbation)
edges.claim_summary: O12-O14 support testing low-titre Bri2 BRICHOS as an anti-amyloid strategy in human SC-islets: both titres reduced amyloid, but insulin-content restoration was reported only at low titre and static GSIS stimulation-index protection was reported at low titre. Figs5,6 report no detected respiration/death differences, not established cytoprotection or safety. This is a candidate bridge to Gate4, with in vivo and exact edited-product transfer unvalidated. The frozen Blueprint/ranker already include IAPP amyloid and an alternative IAPP-editing strategy; these inspected references do not establish incorporation of the specific BRICHOS findings, so incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M7 (IAPP amyloid under metabolic stress as an SC-islet failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O5 reports nearly doubled amyloid under high glucose in primary human islets; O6-O8 report stress-associated amyloid increases in SC-islets and O9 supplies TEM confirmation. These support the pre-existing Gate4 concern about IAPP amyloid under metabolic stress. Frozen Blueprint section1.2 line64 explicitly includes IAPP amyloid toxicity, and ranker ER_AMYLOID_MODULES plus its Gate0E-amyloid challenge explicitly incorporate the generic hazard. Incorporation applies to that hazard, not adoption of this study or its exact 20 mmol/l, 14-day culture parameters. No graft failure, immune injury or oxygen-bridge performance is measured here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet endocrine expression and static functional assessment)
edges.claim_summary: O3-O4 report INS mRNA at 50% and GCG mRNA at twice the primary-human-islet level; transcript abundance is not measured cell composition and does not validate a 60:30:10 ratio. O13-O14 distinguish restored insulin content from protection of the static GSIS stimulation index; O20-O21 report unchanged INS/GCG mRNA. These assays do not establish the dynamic biphasic secretion and rapid shut-off required by frozen Blueprint section1.2 line61, nor exact-product performance. Incorporation of these study-specific empirical details is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (functional maturation requires more than endocrine identity)
edges.claim_summary: O2/O3 show no detected difference in insulin/glucagon cell fractions, while O4/O5/O14–O17 show maturity-associated molecular differences and blunted static glucose-stimulated insulin secretion after defined EDC exposure. This supports the existing Gate1 requirement to assess functional maturation beyond endocrine identity (frozen Blueprint §1.2, line 61; ranker primary_readouts, lines 5808–5812). Incorporation refers only to that existing requirement, not adoption of this chemical challenge or marker panel. The unedited in vitro model and static 20/1.67 mM assay do not qualify an edited product, dynamic biphasic GSIS or low-glucose shut-off.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (defined chemical-exposure challenge as a candidate maturation-QC assay)
edges.claim_summary: O4/O6/O7/O17 and refined O19–O23 support considering a controlled chemical-exposure challenge during SC-islet differentiation as a candidate QC stress assay, based on the specified BPA/BPS/trans-nonachlor mixture. Actual manufacturing contaminants, cultureware leachates, acceptable exposure limits, rescue by contaminant removal and edited-product transfer were not tested. The bounded frozen-reference review establishes existing functional release checks, but does not establish whether this specific assay has already been adopted; incorporation remains unknown. No quantitative safety limit or design upgrade is accepted here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (ECM-supported graft integration and vascularization; oxygen-bridge scope qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O5 reports CD31-positive neovascularization and insulin staining, while O3/O4 are one reported site comparison favoring subcutaneous over intraperitoneal delivery in NOD-SCID mice. These bounded findings motivate graft-niche comparison but do not measure perfusion, inosculation timing, oxygen tension or 72-hour bridge survival. The frozen Blueprint already specifies Laminin-511 E8, iMVFs and PDMS-CaO2/catalase (Stage 2; Gate5), and the ranker NICHE_VASCULAR_MODULES models a composite niche; incorporation of this exact decellularized porcine lung scaffold and site-specific finding is not established. No ranking weight, oxygen-carrier substitution, immune protection or fail-safe qualification follows.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 (ESC-derived islet functional readouts; specific maturation mechanism unmeasured)
edges.claim_summary: O1 reports 1.4-fold-increased in vitro GSIS versus non-responsive free islets; O2 reports lower glucose in graft recipients versus unspecified controls. This supports functional investigation of ECM-supported ESC-derived islets within the bounded in-vitro/NOD-SCID domain. Frozen Blueprint Gate1 requires dynamic biphasic GSIS, tri-hormonal architecture and rapid low-glucose shut-off; the abstract provides no stimulation index, dynamic kinetics, cell composition or maturation mechanism. The reported fold increase is not an SI threshold result, clinical efficacy or proof of exact-product Gate1 qualification; incorporation of these specific findings is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (stage 6 WY14643 / PPAR-associated mitochondrial programming hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: In H1-derived stage 6 SC-islets, WY14643 increased C-peptide-positive and NKX6.1/C-peptide-positive fractions (O10/O12), bulk mature-marker transcripts (O15), and reported insulin secretion (O13); the glucose stimulation index was reported similar (O14), while PDX1 and OCR panels did not meet the stated significance criterion (O20/O21). Ten-day non-humanized NSG graft composition/content findings (O16/O17) do not establish glycemic control or transfer to the Blueprint’s edited, purified Stage 7 60:30:10 product. Blueprint §1.2 and §6 require dynamic biphasic function and rapid low-glucose shut-off; neither is qualified here. Claim-specific adoption of WY14643 is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (secretion, glucose responsiveness and mitochondrial-programming limitations in stage 6 SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: O2–O9 and O19 qualify the inference from insulin-positive cells or mitochondrial mass to mature glucose-regulated function: the tested stage 6 preparations had lower secretion/content and absent glucose-stimulated OCR despite no detected mass/architecture differences; bulk transcriptomic contrasts remain mixture-dependent. This is a justified maturation bridge to the Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and ranker dynamic GSIS SI >= 3.0 / shut-off <= 3 min criteria, not a direct test of its Stage 7 product, a quantitative oxygen-consumption parameter, or a revision of GRAVEYARD_004’s RNLS-specific precaution. Incorporation of these exact PPAR/mitochondrial findings is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation, GSIS and IAPP/MAFA maturity readouts)
edges.claim_summary: HUES8 SC-islets provide matched-domain evidence for Gate1’s need to assess function beyond morphology: DEC1 loss preserved author-described differentiation (O7) but impaired basal/glucose control, peak perifusion and maturity markers (O1–O8), with respiration and glucose-utilization defects (O20–O26). Frozen Blueprint §1.2 explicitly requires biphasic GSIS without basal leak, while the ranker’s Stage-7 niche prior and Graveyard 004 address broader maturation/metabolic tradeoffs. This supports that acceptance principle; it neither quantifies an Islet-1 gate probability nor establishes that its exact product incorporates DEC1 conditioning.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (DEC1-dependent circadian conditioning and metabolic rescue hypotheses)
edges.claim_summary: Synchronized WT SC-islets exhibited 24-h GSIS rhythms and an approximately 2-fold higher peak secretion fold change, driven by lower basal release (O9–O10); DEC1-null islets lacked this improvement (O11). Transplantation into ordinary immunodeficient mice did not remove the defect (O12). PMA, carbachol and metabolic-flux enhancers produced author-described rescue (O14–O18), while acute forskolin and ionomycin did not restore GSIS (O13, O27). These motivate controlled Gate1 maturation experiments; they do not show that DEC1 overexpression works, that restoration is statistical equivalence, or that the exact Islet-1 graft benefits. The frozen Stage-7 niche prior and RNLS-specific Graveyard warning are related context, not evidence of this specific intervention’s adoption.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (NHP functional and metabolic observations after SC-islet microencapsulation)
edges.claim_summary: Abstract-only pilot evidence: one diabetic NHP had serum C-peptide detectable through 13 weeks and a reported significant reduction in exogenous insulin requirement versus an incompletely described diabetic comparator (O2, O3); the healthy recipient remained stable (O7), and retrieved material was glucose-responsive and expressed endocrine markers (O8, O9). This supports feasibility in this encapsulated xenograft context, without establishing graft-specific serum C-peptide, insulin independence, edited-cell function, biphasic GSIS, rapid shut-off or the Blueprint 60:30:10 mixture (frozen Blueprint section 1.2). The specific pilot findings incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 / M3 (post-transplant viability attrition with unmeasured cause)
edges.claim_summary: Retrieved microencapsulated SC-islets had a reported significant decrease in viability versus pre-transplant levels (O6), despite qualitative glucose responsiveness and endocrine-marker expression (O8, O9). This is a bounded viability-loss observation relevant to the Blueprint section 1.2 Gate4 survival objective; no cause, magnitude, stress assay, or intrinsic cytoprotection comparison is supplied, so it does not validate or refute a Blueprint cytoprotection construct. Specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity against donor HLA class I and II)
edges.claim_summary: The bounded generic Gate2A claim is alloimmune sensitization to donor HLA: five of six recipients developed class-I DSA within one year and two of those patients showed class-II reactivity (O10/O11). Frozen Blueprint §1.2 explicitly includes DSA evasion, and ranker Gate2A registry/code already models HLA-I/II/DSA stealth; only that generic rationale is already accounted for, not adoption of this study’s incidence. The unedited, briefly immunosuppressed cadaveric graft does not test B2M/CIITA edits, prove rejection, or resolve the indirect-APC hazard in GRAVEYARD_010. Source positivity-threshold conflict is retained; no ranker parameter update is justified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (early peri-transplant beta-cell stress readout)
edges.claim_summary: Gate4/M3 hypothesis: source-reported biphasic circulating miR-375 (first hour and around day 5), unchanged miR-16, and transient inflammatory mediators (O15/O18) motivate testing a non-invasive early-stress readout alongside direct graft-function/injury measurements. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 addresses intrinsic stress survival; these unedited intraportal cadaveric-islet data neither validate that readout in SC-islet patches nor assign circulating miR-375 to donor rather than native cells. Matrix is inconsistent (serum in Methods/caption, plasma in Results). Incorporation of this particular hypothesis is unknown; keyword search does not establish absence or novelty.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (off-target SC-EC cells; PDX1, RFX6 and PAX6 as regulators that restrain SC-EC fate)
edges.claim_summary: Human SC-islet differentiation shows loss of PDX1, RFX6 or PAX6 biases endocrine composition toward SC-EC fate (O7–O10); O11 is only supporting mouse fetal expression evidence. The frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §6 already require <1% SLC18A1+ cells and lineage QC, so the general purity concern is accounted for; incorporation of this specific regulator-level mechanism and approximate endocrine-normalized ratio is not established. The study does not validate the Blueprint cutoff or a clinical release process.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (ISL1 as a candidate lever or QC marker to suppress SC-EC during SC-β differentiation)
edges.claim_summary: ISL1 KO reduces SC-β and increases SC-EC flow populations (O14–O15), while day-11 ISL1 OE suppresses the SC-EC h3 program across genotypes (O17) but restores the SC-β i5 program robustly only in WT and ISL1−/− (O18). This supports a hypothesis to test timed ISL1 manipulation or an identity marker during SC-islet manufacturing, not a qualified QC marker or product upgrade: bulk gene programs do not establish GSIS, persistence, graft benefit or genomic safety. Specific adoption of this mechanism is not established in the reviewed frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (candidate MEG3 cytokine cytoprotection, bounded by ER stress and identity findings)
edges.claim_summary: MEG3 silencing reduced cytokine-associated apoptosis in EndoC-βH1 and single-donor primary-islet hIsMTs (O6-O8, O13), with approximately 70% hIsMT knockdown (O21); it did not protect against thapsigargin (O12, O25). PDX1 decreased in one experiment (O11) but was not inhibited in confirmation experiments (O14), without resolving the repeated-48 h discrepancy. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§4.3 and ranker CYTOKINE_GRANZYME_MODULES define the cytokine-resilience target, but these sources do not establish adoption of this precise MEG3 perturbation; incorporation remains unknown. SC-islet perturbation, graft efficacy, durability and tumor-suppressor-loss safety were not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (MEG3–IFN-γ–STAT1–CXCL10 interaction with inflammation-inducible Locus 3)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (cross-lineage composition and basal secretion qualification of a candidate MEG3 intervention)
edges.claim_summary: Single-donor primary-islet hIsMTs showed preserved NKX6.1+ beta-cell fraction under cytokines (O19), decreased ARX+/alpha-cell fraction under untreated conditions (O20), and increased basal as well as stimulated insulin secretion after cytokines (O9-O10). These findings require separate lineage and secretion assessment before transfer to SC-islets; no absolute alpha-cell loss, glucagon defect, basal-leak threshold violation or optimal mixture is demonstrated. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 and §6 step 2/intermediate-mixture sub-study, and ranker bounded_intermediate_endocrine_mixture_comparison_substudy_iip_0006, retain 60:30:10 and require measured composition and whole-preparation/lineage-normalized function; those general safeguards do not establish adoption of this specific MEG3 finding.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (IFN-γ/JAK-STAT stress resilience; candidate effector PTPN2)
edges.claim_summary: PTPN2 loss amplified IFN-γ-induced STAT1 phosphorylation and ISG/HLA-I transcripts in hESCs (O3, O5) and raised inflammation markers while lowering β-cell markers in SC-islet grafts (O16, O17), with impaired post-STZ glycaemic control (O14). PTPN2 is not among the Gate4 effectors listed in the cheatsheet; keeping or raising PTPN2 is a candidate Gate4 element, but only loss-of-function was tested here, with no gain-of-function or immune-challenge test.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo functional readouts of edited SC-islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: A functional deficit in PTPN2−/− grafts was visible in glycaemia at 1000 SC-islets (O10) and after STZ (O14) and in insulin staining (O15), but not at 3000 SC-islets (O11) or in fasted C-peptide (O13) or week-8 C-peptide (O12). Graft dose and presence of endogenous β cells can therefore mask an edit-induced defect, which qualifies reliance on glycaemia or C-peptide alone in the Gate1 benchmarks; this is one edit in NOD/SCID mice, and group sizes are not stated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (β-cell-intrinsic resistance to autoreactive effector killing)
edges.claim_summary: Ripk1Δ NIT-1 cells showed halved death with diabetic NOD splenocytes in vitro (O7) and higher graft luminescence in NSG mice given diabetic NOD splenocytes (11-fold at day 14, >100-fold at day 19; O10, O11, O12), while splenocyte IFNγ and CD8 CD69 readouts were unchanged (O8, O9). This is consistent with the Gate2B premise that β-cell-intrinsic protection helps under autoreactive pressure, in a mouse cell line and not in hPSC-derived islets; whether the Blueprint already covers this node cannot be settled from the cheatsheet.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (Stage 5-7 SC-islet differentiation and long-culture maturation)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O5 support a matched in-vitro SC-islet manufacturing hypothesis: S5 DFO exposure increased cell death ~20-fold, later-stage aggregates showed reduced/delayed cell death, and LC static insulin secretion was reported preserved. Evaluate iron/transferrin sufficiency as a stage-dependent process variable; this study tested deprivation, not improved maturation from supplementation, and does not establish a safe supplementation dose, dynamic GSIS equivalence or graft protection. Frozen Gate1 maturation criteria and ranker Stage6/7 priors provide context, but adoption of this particular TFRC/iron claim is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 / M7 (intrinsic cytoprotection perturbation and iron-dependent mechanistic failure mode)
edges.claim_summary: O7-O15 and O19-O21 support iron-deficiency-associated intrinsic stress in mouse β-cells: impaired TFRC/iron acquisition, progressive β-cell loss, p53-associated expression, impaired respiration, and prevention of diabetes by iron dextran. Bridge to the human SC-islet product remains bounded: O1/O4 provide human in-vitro deprivation/omics support, whereas mouse rescue does not show that the Blueprint cloak or a particular cytoprotection edit protects against iron restriction. Frozen Gate4 covers intrinsic apoptosis/stress; the ranker has OXPHOS/ER and RNLS metabolic priors and GRAVEYARD_004 concerns RNLS/OCR, but none establishes incorporation of this specific TFRC/iron result.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (adaptive alloimmunity; intrinsic-cytoprotection edits as a Gate4-type hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O12-O14: neither Rnls nor Hivep2 knockout changed the clearance of β-TC-6 allografts in CD-1 mice (Hivep2 knockout showed only a modest, transient early radiance advantage, O13), so these CRISPR-screen hits for autoimmunity do not by themselves give alloimmune protection in this model. B2M/CIITA antigen-level edits were not tested; the model is a mouse insulinoma line in subcutaneous Matrigel with n = 4 mice per condition.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (innate immunity; xenograft model scope)
edges.claim_summary: O11, O16, O17, O18: in a pilot, human EndoC-βH1 spheroid grafts persisted and expanded over 35 days in SCID mice but fell below background by day 7 in CD-1 mice, and in CD-1 mice neither HIVEP2 nor RNLS knockout prevented loss. The authors read adaptive immunity as dominant for xenorejection here, which scopes what a human-to-mouse immunocompetent graft readout can say about the HLA-E/CD47 innate axes of Gate3; those axes were not tested, and the SCID pilot has no stated n.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (genomic safety of editing; DSB-associated integration profile)
edges.claim_summary: O9-O11: TLA of lentiviral DMF5 TCR integrations in Cas9-edited primary T cells found no breakpoints in TRAC or TRBC and about 5% exonic insertions (204 versus 179 sites per the Results text; the figure caption swaps group labels). This is a DSB-capture integration readout in primary T cells, not translocation, off-target or chromothripsis testing in hPSC-derived islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection; TET2/epigenetic perturbation of ER-stress and cytokine-induced beta-cell death)
edges.claim_summary: O13–O17 provide primary-human-islet in vitro evidence for testing TET inhibition as a Gate4 cytoprotection hypothesis; O2–O3 supply separate NOD-mouse evidence. Frozen Blueprint §1.2/§6 and ranker ER_AMYLOID_MODULES define the existing stress-resilience context, but do not establish incorporation of this specific TET result. Bobcat339 is not TET2-exclusive; mouse recipient Tet2 loss is not beta-cell-specific. No SC-islet differentiation, engineered graft, dynamic endocrine-function or long-term genomic/switch-safety qualification is established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 circuit)
edges.claim_summary: O9–O11 and the mouse closing-CRE results motivate checking whether a TET perturbation changes Locus-3 induction, because endogenous mouse Cd274/Cxcl10 decreased. Frozen Blueprint §4.3/§6, ranker CYTO_CXCL10_SWAP_PDL1_SERPINB9 and GRAVEYARD_001 explicitly recognize IFN/NF-kB promoter dependencies, but their STAT1/JAK1/TYK2 rules do not demonstrate a TET-specific deadlock or block. Endogenous mouse RNA/accessibility does not measure the engineered human cassette; this transfer and TET-specific incorporation remain unvalidated/unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (CD8+ cytotoxic, granzyme-mediated allograft rejection benchmark in a prevascularized subcutaneous device)
edges.claim_summary: Untreated rat allografts in a five-week-prevascularized NICHE showed falling local Treg frequencies, increased granzymeB+CD8+ frequencies and insulin-negative disrupted histology (O7–O9). Local CTLA4-Ig was associated with approximately 75% lower granzymeB+CD8+ frequency and insulin-positive histology (O10,O12), alongside reduced Tregs (O11). This is a bounded rat allograft benchmark for the Gate2A adaptive barrier described in frozen Blueprint §1.2, not causal proof of granzyme-mediated killing, qualification of B2M/CIITA/SERPINB9 edits, autoimmune/indirect-APC protection, or diabetic graft function; incorporation of this specific pharmacologic benchmark is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (transient local immunomodulation window for a prevascularized subcutaneous graft)
edges.claim_summary: Individual local agents produced distinct compartment concentration gradients and day-30 qualitative histology: CTLA4-Ig, ALS, anti-CD40L and anti-CD2 retained insulin-positive islets, whereas anti-IL6 did not (O6,O12,O15,O17,O19,O21–O23,O26,O28). Results[54] proposes an untested ALS plus anti-CD40L induction combination, optionally adding anti-CD2. Frozen Blueprint Stage 2 already specifies transient SA-FasL/SA-THBD microgels and acknowledges short-course rapamycin in cited studies; ranker Decision Experiment #2 and GRAVEYARD_010 already call for investigation of local/early APC protection. The specific NICHE-drug combination is therefore an unvalidated-transfer adjunct hypothesis with incorporation unknown, not an established missing local bridge or a demonstrated immunosuppressant-free therapy. No autoimmune, human edited-cell, donor-specific tolerance or diabetic graft-function test was performed.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47-SIRPalpha engagement, Locus 1 CD47)
edges.claim_summary: Transient SA-CD47 display alone only prolonged MST to 24 days vs 12 days (O5), with 2/6 grafts functioning at 53 and 82 days (O6), SA-TM alone did not differ from controls (O4), and 8/11 grafts survived 120–330 days only with both (O3). CD47-axis protection may be partial on its own in mouse allografts, and the CD47-specific contribution cannot be separated from the combination; the display is transient protein on mouse islets, not constitutive CD47 on hPSC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 layer plus a thrombomodulin-type coagulation/inflammation control for blood-contact transplant routes)
edges.claim_summary: TM alone had no survival effect (O4), yet TM plus CD47 gave durable survival (O3) with lower F3 (tissue factor), Hmgb1 and inflammatory-macrophage/NK signatures (O8, O9, O12, O15). A TM-type arm alongside the CD47 module could be tested where hPSC-islets contact blood (intraportal); IBMIR itself was not measured, the cheatsheet states no coagulation element, and no human cells were used.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (elimination of off-target enterochromaffin SC-EC cells; upstream differentiation levers)
edges.claim_summary: Raising PDX1+NKX6-1+ progenitors to a mean of 92% did not prevent SLC18A1+ EC-like cells (O3, O4); PD03 and LDN-containing conditions increased EC-like cells (O5, O10) while FGF2/BTC and BMP4 reduced them (O6, O8), though BMP4 days 13-16 lowered beta-like cells (O9) and FGF2/BTC did not raise them (O7). The cheatsheet lists SC-EC elimination (CD49a enrichment) but not these media-level levers, which are a candidate complement to purification; evidence is 2D planar H1-based culture without graft or function data for most arms.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (beta-like purity criteria: NKX6-1 and C-peptide co-expression)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-EC elimination and dynamic GSIS function)
edges.claim_summary: Beta-enriched hPSC-islets (about 700,000 beta-like cells of 1,600,000 per well, O12) secreted insulin better than EC-enriched hPSC-islets in static GSIS (O14), consistent with the Blueprint baseline of eliminating off-target SC-EC cells; static assay only (n = 9 sets), not the perifusion stimulation index benchmark.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant hypoxia resilience of SC-islet cells)
edges.claim_summary: iPSC-derived islet spheroids showed a far lower survival pO2 than primary human islets (0.01 vs 2.24 mmHg, O1; 0.01 vs 1.63 mmHg size-matched, O2), higher viability across sizes (O3) and far less variability (O5, O6) in a 48 h 1% O2 in vitro assay. Supports intrinsic hypoxia resilience of the SC-islet cell type under Gate4, but this is in vitro with a single iPSC line.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M7 (72-hour avascular oxygen bridge; spheroid-size diffusion limits)
edges.claim_summary: Lower hypoxic death threshold does not remove diffusion limits: the model predicts SC-islet central necrosis at 400 um (O14) and a viable limit of 200 um at 1% surface O2 (O13), against 150 um for primary islets, assuming OCR 1 pmol/min/IEQ (O17). Qualifies oxygen-bridge and spheroid-size design: the survival pO2 of SC-islets (0.01 mmHg, O1) is a model-derived input, not a verified in vivo bridge target.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M6 and M3 (transplanted SC-islet CRISPRa candidate nomination and site-specific host bioassays)
edges.claim_summary: The kidney-capsule NSG screen nominates candidates by 10-day guide enrichment (O1), not direct graft survival, mass or vascularization. FCAMR has subcutaneous glucose/C-peptide observations (O7–O8), transient opposite-direction kidney/muscle glucose effects (O12–O14), and greater body weight of unresolved mechanism (O15–O16, O23); GSTM3 has no significant measured subcutaneous glycemic/C-peptide difference (O9–O10). This supports only a hypothesis to test candidate perturbations under defined Gate4 stress and graft-survival assays. Frozen Blueprint Gate4 (§1.2), ranker ER modules and Graveyard_004 already distinguish survival rationale from metabolic qualification; incorporation of this specific FCAMR/screen proposal is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet endocrine identity, composition and regulated secretion after candidate activation)
edges.claim_summary: SIX3 is a top transplant-enriched hit yet reduces INS expression and impairs low/high-glucose sensing in vitro (O5–O6); transient lower mouse glucose (O22) does not rescue that endocrine deficit. FCAMR shows no significant identity/stress-gene change (O2) and FCAMR/GSTM3 no detected static-GSIS effect (O4), without proving equivalence; FCAMR shifts cell-type proportions (O17, O24–O25). This qualifies candidate selection using transplant enrichment alone. Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 already requires dynamic biphasic GSIS, low-glucose shutoff without basal leak, and specified endocrine composition; these static assays do not qualify that product. The specific SIX3/FCAMR finding's incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M6 / Gate1 (in silico single-cell perturbation screens for SC-islet differentiation regulators)
edges.claim_summary: A model trained on knockout scRNA-seq of hPSC-derived pancreatic differentiation ranked PDX1 first and recovered GATA6 and MAPK1 (O14), with AUC 0.79 vs 0.66 for expression-only ranking against a published pooled screen (O15). Proposes virtual screens to prioritise differentiation and maturation regulators ahead of wet CRISPR screens; computational, knockout-based evidence only.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M6 (reliability limits of virtual perturbation screens for editing-target selection)
edges.claim_summary: In the restricted strong-knockdown comparison, pertTF was reported better in 8 of 8 metrics, while all methods performed substantially worse than in earlier benchmarks. The full library had 50 genes with two in training; the caption describes a 10-strong-effect-gene evaluation, with Results/caption panel attribution unresolved. Selected-subset training overlap and analyzed-cell n are not given. This qualifies transfer to unseen genes/non-knockout edits; no graft or editing-stack performance was demonstrated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet manufacturing: SC-beta yield, SC-EC reduction, line-to-line robustness)
edges.claim_summary: Stage-1 F-actin depolymerisation is a source-supported manufacturing hypothesis in unmodified human hPSC lines: SC-beta fraction increased by ~5–10% as reported (O1), enterochromaffin fraction decreased by ~5–15% in Results for HUES8/WS4c/AN1.1 (O2; Fig1F caption names only HUES8/WS4c), GSIS improved (O4/O5), and parallel failed-control batches reached ~30–50% SC-beta cells (O9). H1 instead gained enterochromaffin cells (O3), its dose conflicts between prose and captions, and excessive latA impaired differentiation. Blueprint §1.2/§6 and ranker constant_isogenic_backbone prescribe purity, sorting, reaggregation and dynamic function; adoption of this specific early-stage lever is not established. Transfer to the edited 60:30:10 product, manufacturing yield and existing release gates remains unvalidated.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M5 (SC-islet graft tumor/overgrowth hazard and pan-lineage safety scope)
edges.claim_summary: Unmodified AN1.1-control grafts formed tumors by week 11, while latA-treated AN1.1 grafts had no reported overgrowth during 30 weeks (O17/O18); incidence counts and tumor origin were not resolved. O11 is HUES8 protein staining and must not be attributed to the AN1.1 graft cohort. This experimental hazard reinforces the residual/off-target clonogenic safety scope already explicit in Blueprint §7, ranker two_stage_orthogonal_psc_purge_requirement and GRAVEYARD_002. Specific incorporation of this AN1.1 observation is unknown. No iCasp9/AP1903, switch escape, edited-product safety or residual-PSC quantitative qualification was tested; the study does not contradict the existing pan-lineage requirement.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 / M7 (zinc-transport/AMPK stress-resilience hypothesis)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O3, O7 and O8 provide abstract-only mechanistic and directional support for testing chemical zinc-transport inhibition as an intrinsic stress-resilience intervention, relevant to Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 hypoxic stress. Transfer to the exact edited product, AMPK causal mediation, compound, transport target, dose, timing and safety are unestablished; the abstract does not identify SLC30A8/ZnT8 or support changing genetic-knockout penalties, and specific incorporation is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet functional maturation)
edges.claim_summary: O2 reports enhanced functional maturation of human SC-islets, directionally supporting the broad Gate1 maturation goal in Blueprint §1.2. O6 separately reports glycemic-control improvement in unspecified diabetic animals; neither claim establishes Stage-6/7 identity, biphasic GSIS, low-glucose shutoff, the 60:30:10 product or a numerical Blueprint acceptance threshold.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (SC-islet angiogenesis and endothelial integration)
edges.claim_summary: O4 states HIF1A-independent VEGFA expression facilitating endothelial integration and O5 reports accelerated angiogenesis in diabetic animal models, motivating testing of a chemical pre-adaptation adjunct to the vascularization goal in Blueprint §1.2 Gate5 and §4.5. No perfusion timing, oxygen measurement, 72-hour bridge duration, PDMS-CaO2 comparison, isogenic iEC:iPericyte result or fail-safe endpoint is reported; faster angiogenesis does not establish that the exact oxygen bridge can be shortened or replaced.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet manufacturing yield and source-line selection)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O2, O5, O9: in one isogenic pair, T2D-risk KCNQ1 alleles lowered the day-34 SC-β-cell fraction (10.95% fewer, P < 0.001) although PP generation was equal, so the loss arises at the endocrine-progenitor stage. This suggests (untested in other lines) that source-line genotype at T2D-risk loci could be screened as a Gate1 yield covariate; the cheatsheet states no genotype-dependent yield element.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1, M3 (short ex vivo conditioning of primary donor islets; RIPK1-associated stress pathways)
edges.claim_summary: O3/O13-O16 support testing 24-h Nec-1 conditioning as a hypothesis for primary donor-islet survival/engraftment: lower TUNEL staining and improved reported Rag-mouse glycemic outcomes. Transfer to the engineered SC-islet product, immunocompetent recipients and the intended implantation site is unvalidated. M1/O5 do not prove selective necroptosis inhibition, and Nec-1s staining benefit without glucose normalization limits simple mechanism-to-efficacy inference. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate4 and §4.3 define intrinsic protection; this specific regimen's incorporation is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (native CD47 and complement-associated transcripts; no innate-effector protection assay)
edges.claim_summary: O10/O11 show a lower complement pathway score and altered endogenous transcripts including lower CD47/CD40 and higher CD55 after Nec-1 culture. These are transcriptional observations, not functional complement resistance or engineered CD47/HLA-E protection. Frozen Blueprint §4.1 requires exact-construct surface/function tests and distinguishes its CD55 GPI-anchor segment from complement-regulatory domains; the native CD55 transcript finding cannot validate that anchor or the cloak. Incorporation of this specific pharmacologic interaction remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / Gate4 / M1, M3 (function alongside cytoprotection; glucose-responsive respiration trade-offs)
edges.claim_summary: M2/O19/O20 identify lower glucose-responsive respiration metrics and higher proton leak despite reported glucose-responsive insulin secretion (O6) and improved in-vivo glycemia; O12 also records reduced UCN3 transcript without inferred loss of maturity. This bounds a conditioning hypothesis and does not equate OCR with GSIS or survival with intact function. Frozen ranker Decision Experiment #5 and GRAVEYARD_004 already require paired functional/metabolic testing in other perturbation contexts; they do not establish incorporation of the specific Nec-1 trade-off or applicability to engineered SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M6 (proinsulin-ratio screening and functional-readout interpretation)
edges.claim_summary: The MIN6 screen/QTL study and EndoC-βH3 follow-up motivate testing proinsulin:insulin ratio alongside absolute hormone content and production, since PDIA6 loss can reduce the ratio while impairing proinsulin synthesis (O8, O10, O16). This is a candidate orthogonal Gate1 readout rather than evidence of improved SC-islet maturity or a PDIA6 intervention recommendation. Frozen Blueprint §1.2 Gate1 and ranker primary_readouts require regulated GSIS and shut-off; they do not establish this study-specific assay’s incorporation. Adoption of this precise ratio-plus-production boundary is unknown, and no specific graveyard rule is asserted.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection under IFN and viral stress)
edges.claim_summary: O9, O10, O18 and O5: ISG15 knockdown raised apoptosis in EndoC-βH1 cells and primary human islets, ISG15 overexpression reduced CVB1 damage in EndoC-βH1 cells, and ISG15 was lower in beta-like than alpha-like cells including hiPSC-derived datasets. This suggests ISG15 (with its partner USP18) as a candidate IFN-feedback cytoprotective element for the Gate4 stack; the cheatsheet Gate4 list (A20, MANF, TXNIP, BCL2, XIAP and others) contains no ISG15 element, and no SC-islet or transplant test was done.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (Locus 3 CXCL10-inducible SERPINB9-P2A-PD-L1 cassette)

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (classical HLA-A/B/C and B2M KO rationale)
edges.claim_summary: [Structured blueprint link R1_0373:L3 | relation=supports | applicability=justified_bridge | incorporation=unknown | outcomes=O14,O15 | text_sha256=6fb9221bf0c4cfdf9ec4a54fe77e5952d0ae5dd4e6dd2863f322ef1048ea48ac]

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (in vivo SC-islet graft site and function readout)
edges.claim_summary: O1-O3 (protocol claims only, no data in the abstract): an intramuscular, retrievable graft site with in vivo GSIS and histology could serve as an alternative preclinical read-out platform for hPSC-derived SC-islets in immunodeficient mice. The cheatsheet gives no graft-site element, so it cannot settle whether the Blueprint already covers this; graft survival, function and oxygenation at this site are not reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (intrinsic cytoprotection perturbation; BCL2/XIAP apoptosis axis)
edges.claim_summary: SLC30A8 R138X loss of function protected hESC-derived islet-like clusters from Zn2+-depletion-induced apoptosis (O1, O2) with lower CASP7/CASP8 and higher BCL2 (O3, O4). ZnT8 loss is a candidate extra cytoprotection lever not listed in the Gate4 elements; the stressor was TPEN chelation, so protection against hypoxia, cytokines or transplant stress is untested here.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation and GSIS)
edges.claim_summary: ZnT8 loss did not change INS+ cell numbers (O8) and shifted SC-islet clusters toward a more mature expression profile (O9, O11, O12), with higher glucose-stimulated insulin release in homozygous clusters (O13) but altered Ca2+ dynamics (O16, O17). Evidence is in vitro in hESC-derived clusters, mostly qualitative with values only in figures.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (HMOX1/SOD2/CAT antioxidant program)
edges.claim_summary: In the apoptosis-protected R138X clusters, antioxidant genes including CAT were downregulated and the authors read this as an adaptive response (O7, O6). Stacking ZnT8 loss with a CAT-based Gate4 cytoprotection program would therefore need a direct test, since this dataset does not measure oxidative stress tolerance.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2, M6 (endogenous TXNIP, MANF, BCL2 and DDIT3 stress programs in SC-islets versus primary islets)
edges.claim_summary: At 1% O2, primary and SC-beta cells had opposing endogenous TXNIP/DDIT3 programs, primary beta cells upregulated MANF, and SC-beta cells upregulated BCL2 despite pro-apoptotic signaling (O11–O16); these source-specific transcriptional associations qualify extrapolation of protective pathways and do not test TXNIP knockout or MANF/BCL2 overexpression. The frozen Blueprint already includes intrinsic stress resilience (§1.2) and a TXNIP factorial comparison (§6; ranker X5), but incorporation of this exact source-specific expression boundary is not established.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3, M7 (oxygen bridge and cluster diffusion/core hypoxia)
edges.claim_summary: A 1% O2 incubator atmosphere produced lost SC-islet glucose responsiveness at 24–48 h and qualitative core death in clusters with reported SC-islet diameter 223.5 ± 3.8 μm (O2, O17, O18), supporting the already explicit Blueprint need for oxygen management and cluster-size control (§1.2, §4.5). Intracluster oxygen was not measured, exposure ended at 48 h, and no oxygen-delivery intervention or Blueprint ≤120 μm product was tested, so this does not validate a 72-hour bridge; incorporation of the exact source/protocol-specific findings is unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (identity and glucose responsiveness during and after hypoxic stress)
edges.claim_summary: Ectopic non-beta transcripts in SC-beta cells and loss of whole-SC-islet glucose responsiveness during acute hypoxia (O2, O9, O10), together with metabolism assayed after reoxygenation (O4–O6), support checking identity and regulated secretion under the actual stress/recovery history rather than relying on baseline markers alone. Blueprint §4.5 already explicitly separates post-bridge endocrine function/recovery from survival; whether these particular 0–48-h transcriptomic/functional results are incorporated is not established, and this study does not qualify the edited product.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet functional maturity vs primary islets)
edges.claim_summary: HUES8 SC-islets secreted less insulin at high glucose than primary islets in vitro (O1), and human C-peptide at 4 weeks in NSG mice was numerically lower than with primary islets but not significantly different (O5), consistent with a residual maturity gap. Single primary donor, non-diabetic recipients and no stimulation index are reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: M3 (in vivo graft recovery and readout workflow, subcutaneous site)
edges.claim_summary: BioRep ICC IEQ standardization gave matched doses (O2) and DTZ staining made subcutaneous grafts visible for excision without interfering with IHC (O7, O8), a candidate standardized explant workflow for M3 graft studies. Validated only for terminal samples at 4 weeks in non-diabetic NSG mice; no recovery rate or viability effects of DTZ are reported.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M3 (scope of device-based transplantation without immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: Device-supported allogeneic rat survival/diabetic reversal (O3), xenogeneic mouse function (O1), and subcutaneous nonhuman-primate survival (O4) are reported without immunosuppression. The abstract does not specify an immune-isolation architecture, genetic edits, or direct T-cell, NK/macrophage, or indirect-APC readouts; these outcomes therefore do not test the Blueprint B2M/CIITA cloak or establish transfer to its genetically engineered graft. NHP evidence is survival only, and claim-specific incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (off-target enterochromaffin SC-EC cell elimination)
edges.claim_summary: Enterochromaffin-like cells persist as a smaller, unquantified fraction of the SC-islets (O4), consistent with the Gate1 need to eliminate off-target SC-EC cells rather than rely on protocol optimization alone.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet maturation, GSIS and off-target SC-EC reduction)
edges.claim_summary: Coaggregating stage 7 SC-beta cells with regenerative hPSC-derived macrophages at a 3% ratio improved glucose-stimulated C-peptide secretion (O9, O10), raised the mature SC-beta proportion about 3-fold and lowered SC-EC2 and SC-EC1 proportions 9- and 1.5-fold (O15 to O17), a candidate maturation and EC-depletion element for Gate1. Single H1 line, the scRNA-seq proportions have no stated replicates, and INS/PDX1 results conflict between qPCR and scRNA-seq (O13).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M3 (accelerated in vivo functional maturation in a mild-STZ immunodeficient model)
edges.claim_summary: SC-MReg coaggregates reached stable euglycemia four weeks faster (O1, O2) with better 1-month refeeding glucose and C-peptide (O5, O7), but all groups were similar at 2 months (O6) and SC-MUnp or SC-MInf gave no benefit (O3, O4). The effect is acceleration, not a higher plateau, in female SCID-Beige mice with mild STZ diabetes and an eye transplant site.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M3 (macrophage arm of innate immunity; macrophage phenotype as a modifier)
edges.claim_summary: Autologous hPSC-derived macrophages cocultured with SC-beta cells shifted toward a less inflammatory state (O18), persisted only transiently in the graft (O8) and did not reduce the INS-expressing cell fraction (O12), so macrophage polarization state matters when applying Gate3 macrophage assumptions. No macrophage attack on SC-beta cells, SIRPalpha/CD47 or phagocytosis of SC-beta cells was tested, and recipients lacked a human immune system.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / Gate2B / M1 (IFN-alpha-STAT2 signaling and PD-L1 in beta cells; transient RNA delivery)
edges.claim_summary: STAT2-siRNA delivered by DPP6 nanobody-targeted LNPs lowered STAT2 in IFN-alpha-stimulated human beta cells below unstimulated baseline (O5) and raised PDL1 more than 4-fold (O6), suggesting transient RNA delivery as a non-genomic route to dampen interferon signaling and raise PD-L1. The human beta cell source is not stated, there is no graft, hPSC-islet or T-cell data, and the PDL1 comparator is unspecified.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive T-cell memory against PPI; insulin signal peptide as autoantigen)
edges.claim_summary: O3 and O4: substituting the insulin signal peptide with chromogranin-A's let human beta-cell lines evade autoreactive T-cell recognition and killing without inducing ER stress (abstract-level, no numbers). Proposes antigen-level editing of PPI as an alternative or addition to HLA-based cloaking; evidence is human beta-cell lines in vitro, not SC-islets or a graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (insulin synthesis, processing and secretion in beta cells)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O2: signal peptide substitution kept insulin expression, maturation, secretion and function with physiological proinsulin/insulin ratios in insulin-null human beta-cell lines. No GSIS, perifusion or SC-islet data in the abstract.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (avascular oxygen bridge and graft vascularization)
edges.claim_summary: O1, O4 and O6: the phosphatase inhibitor NaW increased vascularized area and VEGFA expression in grafted human SC-islets and fibroblast-derived insulin-producing cells without added endothelial cells (abstract-level, no numbers). Proposes a pharmacological pro-angiogenic adjunct to speed revascularization after the avascular window; evidence is immunodeficient-mouse anterior-chamber grafts, not a hypoimmune graft or device.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M3 (peri-transplant graft survival and stress resilience)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O3: NaW increased insulin-positive tissue area and reduced apoptosis in grafted cells (abstract-level, no numbers or p). Consistent with survival gains from better graft perfusion, but the abstract names no untreated comparator and the host is an immunodeficient mouse.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (IFIH1 E627* cytoprotection candidate under cytokine/viral stress)
edges.claim_summary: O11 and O13 report lower normalized caspase-3/7 activity in E627* versus A946T SC-islets under IFNα/TNFα and high-MOI CVB3; O14 reports lower viral RNA. These support testing an IFIH1 truncation candidate, not adoption into the edited Blueprint product. One donor background, different stage-1 LATA concentrations, different cell compositions, no successful parental SC-islet comparator, and no immune-cell/long-term challenge limit transfer. O10/O12 retain their within-control significance scope; residual apoptosis and identity loss persist. Specific study-level incorporation is not established by the frozen references.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate1 / M2 (SC-islet purity and dynamic functional qualification)
edges.claim_summary: O5-O6 provide additional evidence for maintaining separate lineage-purity and glucose-function checks: both variants contained high SC-EC fractions, and neither had a statistically significant 2-to-20 mM static insulin increase. This claim is limited to requirements already explicit in frozen Blueprint §1.2 (line 61) and live-sorting contract (line 245): <1% off-target ECs plus dynamic first/second-phase GSIS and shut-off. The study does not demonstrate that ECs caused the GSIS phenotype, satisfy those gates, or adopt these exact percentages as thresholds. Frozen ranker primary-readout text at line 5808 instead says <5%; that threshold discrepancy is preserved, not silently harmonized.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M1 (IFIH1/MDA5 antiviral-safety boundary; frozen ranker Stage-0 Gate0V)
edges.claim_summary: O19 shows Arg470-antibody nondetection rather than proven protein absence; O14-O15 separate lower acute viral RNA from a nonsignificant infectious-titer contrast. These 24/48 h in-vitro data do not test the frozen ranker DEC-053 safeguard (lines 5983-6000): intact MDA5/RIG-I/MAVS activation plus 28-day immune-context viral challenge/clearance. An IFIH1 truncation candidate must be reconciled with that existing design constraint; this paper neither clears nor falsifies its full product-level antiviral criterion. No blanket Graveyard_001 STAT1/JAK1/TYK2-promoter block is inferred for IFIH1. Study-specific Blueprint incorporation remains unknown.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate3 / M1 (CD47 on the graft cell, Locus 1 CD47-IgV-GPI)
edges.claim_summary: O17 and O18: CD47 knockout in the human beta-cell line βLox5 increased apoptosis under IGRP-reactive CD8+ T cell attack, and CD47 knockout effector T cells killed βLox5 more (n = 6; values in figures only). Supports retaining CD47 on graft cells and adds a T-cell route (via SIRPγ) beyond the SIRPα macrophage axis; evidence is loss-of-function in a beta-cell line, not overexpression in SC-islets.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (autoreactive IGRP-specific CD8+ T-cell killing of the graft)
edges.claim_summary: O10, O11, O17 and O18: CD47 loss shifted T cells toward an effector phenotype and raised β-cell killing in an HLA-A*02:01 IGRP-avatar assay. Proposes testing CD47 level on SC-islets in an IGRP-avatar benchmark for Gate2B; overexpression is not tested here, the assay uses an HLA-intact line (not B2M-null cells), and the paper itself reports CD47 haplotype effects inconsistently (O6, O7).

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2B / M1 (inducible PD-L1 at Locus 3 with SERPINB9; isoform-resolved benchmark)
edges.claim_summary: IFN signaling and CVB3 were associated with an exon-3-skipped PD-L1Δ3 isoform in the reported human beta-cell/islet systems. Full-length PD-L1 showed stronger T-cell suppression; Δ3-overexpressing co-cultures retained partial/modest suppression of CD69 induction and IFN-γ despite impaired surface/PD-1-related behavior. The residual activity mechanism is not established. This qualifies use of total PD-L1 expression alone as a checkpoint-capacity readout. Transfer to the Locus 3 transgene and exact SC-islet product was not tested.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (intrinsic stress resilience of matured SC-islets)
edges.claim_summary: O2 and O4: MAFA-driven maturation is reported to give greater SC-islet resilience, and the S64F work stresses compensation to avoid intracellular stress responses (abstract-level). The stress type, readout and S64F result are not stated, so this only weakly supports a maturation-resilience link.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate4 / M2 (nutrient-deprivation, ER/oxidative stress and beta-cell identity under low glucose)
edges.claim_summary: O2 to O5: in vivo hypoglycaemia in rats and mice downregulated beta cell-enriched genes and upregulated ISR/proapoptotic UPR and oxidative stress genes, largely reversed after glucose normalisation (abstract-level, no numbers). Consistent with Gate4's nutrient-deprivation and ER/oxidative stress pressures, and suggests recipient glycaemia and glucose-dependent identity-gene shifts need to be recorded; rodent islets and in vivo fasting are far from an SC-islet graft.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate5 / M3 (prevascularization and vascular connection of SC-islet grafts)
edges.claim_summary: O3 to O6: co-culturing hPSC-derived islet organoids with blood vessel organoids gave capillary-penetrated VPIOs that survived better, connected to host vessels and restored long-term normoglycemia after subcutaneous transplant in diabetic mice (abstract-level, no numbers). Proposes organoid prevascularization as an add-on to the Blueprint's oxygen-bridge and vascularization elements; host strain, immune status, duration and the comparator are not stated.

Qualifies how far class I masking alone can be expected to protect; the abstract gives no n, no follow-up beyond the medians, and no mechanism for the eventual rejection, and antibody blockade differs from B2M knockout.

The intervention here is recipient-side, not graft-side, in mice; the abstract gives no magnitude or n.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (scope of the class I / CD8 axis alone)

edges.claim_summary: O5 and O6 show that islet allografts placed separately from the FasL myoblasts (contralateral kidney) and third-party thyroid allografts were rejected, so the protection was local and specific rather than systemic tolerance. Any ligand-based cloak should be expected to protect only cells that carry or sit next to the ligand source; the packet gives no n or magnitudes.

edges.target_gate_or_module: Gate2A / M1 (local immune-privileged cloak for allogeneic islets without systemic immunosuppression)
edges.claim_summary: O1 and O4 show that allogeneic rat islets cotransplanted with Fas ligand-expressing Sertoli-rich aggregates reversed diabetes for >95 days in 5/5 recipients without systemic immunosuppression, versus 10 days for islets alone (O2). The protective cells are unedited support cells in rats, not graft-cell edits, and the cheatsheet does not list this element.

This qualifies any assumption that partial local cloaking suffices; n and p are not given.

The abstract does not show that islet loss was Fas-mediated or at what expression level, so Fas-specific protection in the Blueprint cannot be settled from the cheatsheet.

This qualifies any expectation that graft-local ligand expression gives uniform protection or that secretion level predicts it, in a mouse biolistic model with small n.
